# RelayV4 code audit (2026-10-06)

This is the first full audit of RelayV4. It covers bugs, security, bad code, code that could be better, and overengineering, across everything except the phone app. It is final: round 1 found and verified the issues, and round 2 deduplicated them, re-checked every high-severity finding blind, filled coverage gaps and rechecked findings against the code merged since. A filterable version of the same findings is in [report.html](report.html).

- **Audited commit:** `361c6f9`. Line numbers in this report refer to the current `main` (`d04b526`). The two commits are identical outside the 19 non-phone files that PR #30 and PR #31 changed; findings in those files were remapped or rechecked (see Method).
- **Scope:** the engine (`relay-core`), the bus types (`relay-bus`), the CLI and MCP servers including the embedded Blender and Unreal Python (`relay-cli`), the phone door (`relay-remote`, `deploy/`), the GTK client (`apps/relay-native`), tests, scripts, CI, plugins and docs. The phone app (`apps/relay-mobile`) was out of scope.
- **Result:** **744 unique findings**: 0 critical, **56 high**, 236 medium and 452 low. 561 are defects or security issues (Part A) and 183 are code quality or design (Part B). Every high finding has been confirmed by at least two independent verifiers, the last of them blind.

## Executive summary

RelayV4's core design holds up. The single-store engine, the typed bus and the worktree-per-agent model are sound, and the audit found no memory-safety finding, no known-vulnerable dependency, and little overengineering (5 findings). The serious problems cluster in four places:

- **Guardrails.** They can be walked around in ordinary ways.
- **The store-lock rule.** CLAUDE.md's rule against slow work under the store lock is broken in a dozen handlers, so the whole bus can freeze.
- **The phone door.** It is exposed on the network without channel security.
- **The desktop client.** It rebuilds whole panels on every event, which resets what the user is doing, leaks widgets, and can drop its only engine connection on one large reply.

No single finding reached critical after verification. The one claimed critical, a confirmed hold landing in the wrong checkout, is real but needs uncommitted edits to the same file in the main checkout before it destroys work, so it is rated high.

### Fix first

These are ordered by harm prevented per unit of work. S, M and L are the auditors' effort estimates.

1. **Make confirmed holds replay in the agent's worktree** ([RA-009](#ra-009), S). `guardrail.confirm` replays a held agent `file.write` with no session bound, so the write lands in the user's primary checkout and the agent's worktree never gets it.
2. **Make `worktree.remove` refuse anything that is not a registered worktree of the project** ([RA-017](#ra-017), M). Today it accepts any path, even a relative one, and falls back to `remove_dir_all`.
3. **Fail closed when the guardrail hook is slow** ([RA-002](#ra-002), S). The PreToolUse adapter has no deadline of its own. When the engine is busy past the provider's 30 s hook timeout, the provider kills the hook and runs the tool unchecked.
4. **Gate Codex edits as writes** ([RA-003](#ra-003), M). Gate shell writes too: redirections, `sed -i`, `tee`, `cp` ([RA-001](#ra-001), L). At the moment no write guardrail runs for Codex, and none runs for any Bash-tool write.
5. **Validate `provider_ref`** ([RA-030](#ra-030), S). An agent can store a string that later lands in the provider's argv on resume, for example `--dangerously-bypass-approvals-and-sandbox`.
6. **Stop closing one session from deleting the hook directory** that the shared checkout's `core.hooksPath` still points at ([RA-031](#ra-031), M). Today it silently disables the commit gate for every other session.
7. **Close the phone door's network exposure** ([RA-056](#ra-056), [RA-053](#ra-053)). Stop `run.sh` from opening it on `0.0.0.0` at every launch, and add a handshake timeout and a connection cap. Channel security ([RA-052](#ra-052), L) is the larger follow-up.
8. **Move subprocesses out of the store lock and put them under deadlines.** This covers `worktree::git`/`git_mutate` ([RA-022](#ra-022)), `project.clone` ([RA-034](#ra-034)), `gh pr create` ([RA-023](#ra-023)), `avd.create`/`avd.boot` ([RA-018](#ra-018)) and `task.dispatch`'s nested prepares ([RA-032](#ra-032)). Each can freeze every session, keystrokes included.
9. **Stop one large reply from killing the client's connection** ([RA-037](#ra-037)). Any reply line over 2 MiB tears down the client's only engine connection; [RA-027](#ra-027) (mailbox history) and [RA-050](#ra-050) (Skills page) hit this in normal use.
10. **Fix the two client crashes:** the guardrail prompt queue's RefCell double borrow ([RA-042](#ra-042), S), and Replace All with zero matches in notes ([RA-044](#ra-044), S), which aborts the client and loses unsaved notes.
11. **Make `run.sh` start the engine in its own session** ([RA-055](#ra-055), S). Today Ctrl+C in the launching terminal kills every agent.
12. **Port the Blender scripts to Blender 5's layered actions** ([RA-008](#ra-008), S). This is the one failing `cargo test`.

### Themes

- **Guardrails are advisory in practice.**
  - Denied commands match one contiguous literal spelling. `rm -fr`, `git push -f`, `/bin/rm`, `sh -c` and `$( )` all pass ([RA-010](#ra-010), [RA-011](#ra-011)).
  - The `**` glob loses its backtrack point ([RA-012](#ra-012)).
  - Confirming a hook-raised hold grants nothing, so the retry is held again ([RA-025](#ra-025)).
  - At medium:
    - an agent can claim `actor: user` on the socket and answer its own guardrail ([RA-096](#ra-096));
    - `git commit --no-verify` skips the commit gate ([RA-109](#ra-109));
    - grants ignore quoted words ([RA-104](#ra-104));
    - provider settings files sit in the agent-writable worktree ([RA-273](#ra-273)).

  BUS.md calls guardrails "best effort, not a security boundary". The code is weaker than even that wording suggests, and the UI labels Codex "Guarded".
- **The store-lock invariant is convention, not structure.** Besides the subprocess handlers above:
  - `file.search` reads whole files of any size under the lock ([RA-020](#ra-020));
  - rename, move and delete re-read the file to gate it ([RA-021](#ra-021));
  - the socket serves each connection strictly in order, while the client multiplexes all UI traffic on one connection ([RA-015](#ra-015)).

  Seven separate git runners exist, and only some have deadlines. One shared runner with a mandatory timeout would remove the class.
- **Processes outlive or outrun their owners.**
  - Stopping a device run kills only the `fish -lc` wrapper, so Gradle keeps installing ([RA-019](#ra-019)).
  - Crash recovery kills any process carrying `RELAY_*` env, including an Unreal Editor the user now owns ([RA-006](#ra-006)).
  - The Unreal tools can SIGTERM the wrong checkout's editor, or quit without saving ([RA-004](#ra-004), [RA-005](#ra-005)).
- **Session and task flows dead-end.**
  - Sessions sharing a checkout are treated as one review group, which deadlocks independent agents ([RA-028](#ra-028)).
  - Exited sessions cannot be relaunched ([RA-029](#ra-029)).
  - `task.approve` fails after branch cleanup ([RA-033](#ra-033)).
  - `project.remove` fails on a foreign key once a project has labels, after it has already killed the project's agents ([RA-035](#ra-035)).
  - Codex reviewers can never bootstrap ([RA-014](#ra-014)).
  - Desktop launches ignore a plugin's default checkout ([RA-043](#ra-043)).
- **Unbounded growth.**
  - Integration worktrees and branches are never removed ([RA-026](#ra-026)).
  - Every wallpaper rotation copies an image into the audit table ([RA-049](#ra-049)).
  - Mailbox history is never pruned ([RA-027](#ra-027)).
  - Trash and soft-deleted rows are never purged, because `app.reconcile` is a stub ([RA-132](#ra-132), medium).
- **The desktop client rebuilds instead of updating.**
  - The Git panel, Guardrails page, board and sidebar are torn down on every event ([RA-036](#ra-036), [RA-038](#ra-038), [RA-045](#ra-045), [RA-046](#ra-046)). That closes menus, loses half-typed text and moves buttons under the pointer.
  - Closures hold strong references to their own widgets, so each rebuild leaks the old tree ([RA-039](#ra-039), [RA-047](#ra-047)).
  - Each refresh can page the repository's entire PR history through `gh` ([RA-024](#ra-024), [RA-040](#ra-040)).
- **The phone door was built for a trusted LAN.**
  - The token crosses the wire in clear and later frames are unauthenticated ([RA-052](#ra-052)).
  - One slow phone stalls every lane of the rendezvous ([RA-054](#ra-054)).
  - A `wss://` rendezvous panics because rustls has no CryptoProvider ([RA-051](#ra-051)).
- **Docs drift.** 36 findings, most in BUS.md, where the Codex guard, the reconcile pass and the `ui.*` executor are described as they were planned rather than as built.

### What was ruled out

- **Dependencies:** `cargo audit` found no known vulnerabilities. Two transitive warnings come through `gix`: `faster-hex` is unsound and `bisync` is yanked.
- **Lints:** the engine crates are clippy-clean.
- **Refuted in round 1:** 23 candidates. Examples:
  - stream frames racing their response (they cannot under the scheduler in use);
  - the CI trigger branch (the premise was a stale local ref);
  - nullable patch fields not round-tripping (no caller depends on it);
  - `bus.subscribe` skipping envelope checks (those ops carry no authority);
  - `blender_python` lacking a guardrail gate, as a separate issue (it is covered by the plugin-MCP finding).
- **Dropped in the completeness pass:** 13 candidates on reading the code. Examples:
  - idempotency replays (they execute nothing);
  - non-constant-time session-token comparison (same-uid boundary);
  - `/tmp` as an always-on write root (documented, D102);
  - the scrcpy forward port (adb already exposes more to local users).

## Method

**Round 1** used 475 agents at max effort, over about 19 hours (the script is [round1-workflow.js](round1-workflow.js)).
- 41 auditors each read one area in full.
- 18 more each followed one concern across the whole codebase: the CLAUDE.md invariants, SQLite use, concurrency, five security angles, data loss, GTK main-thread health, panics, dead or duplicated code, overengineering, the bus contract, performance, resource leaks and misleading docs.
- Every finding went to a verifier told to refute it, and every high or critical one to a second skeptic.
- The result was 1,126 candidates: 23 refuted and 1,103 kept.

**Round 2** used 92 agents at high effort ([round2-part1-workflow.js](round2-part1-workflow.js), [round2-part2-workflow.js](round2-part2-workflow.js)).

- **Semantic dedup.**
  - Rule: a finding is a duplicate when it shares a root cause with another, so one fix resolves both. A shared theme is not enough, and neither is a shared line.
  - Shards: 11 agents each took one shard and searched the full index for duplicates in other shards.
  - Reconciling: shard groups that shared members were merged ([reconcile.py](reconcile.py)). Two clusters chained distinct root causes and were split by hand: the Codex guard, shell writes and BUS.md drift; and the `ui.*` model and Tauri leftovers.
  - Result: 197 groups, 366 findings merged away, 737 unique. Merged findings keep their locations under "Also at" and their ids under "Merged duplicates" ([round2-dedup.json](round2-dedup.json)).
- **Blind re-check.** It covered every unique finding that any member of its group had rated high or critical: 63 findings.
  - Each went to one fresh verifier. The verifier saw the auditor's evidence and the titles of the merged reports, but no earlier verdict or severity, and was barred from reading the audit outputs.
  - It was told to refute by default and to rate severity fresh with the same rubric. Its verdict and severity are final.
  - Results: all 63 were confirmed and none refuted, so there are no disputed findings. 7 were lowered to medium and the one critical became high ([round2-blind.json](round2-blind.json)).
  - This answers the round-1 concern that the skeptic had been anchored by seeing the first verdict.
  - Medium and low findings had one adversarial verifier each and no blind re-check.
- **Completeness pass.** Two agents read every auditor's coverage notes for issues seen outside their chunk and not reported.
  - 74 such observations were already covered by a finding.
  - 21 were not. Each was written up from the code or dropped with a reason, and every write-up was verified.
  - 8 became findings (1 medium, 7 low); 13 were dropped ([round2-completeness.json](round2-completeness.json)).
- **Recheck after PR #30 and #31.** 168 findings sat in the 19 changed non-phone files, but only 13 were within 12 lines of an edit.
  - Two of those 13 had been merged into other findings.
  - One was high and went through the blind re-check, which reads the current code.
  - The other 10 were rechecked against the diff: 6 are still present, 3 changed and 1 is fixed (Appendix B).
  - Every other line in those files was remapped through the diff hunks ([linemap.py](linemap.py)).

**Severity rubric** (a single-user desktop app with a local engine, many concurrent agent sessions and an optional phone door):
- **Critical:** data loss, a hole reachable by another local user, a network peer or an escaping agent, or an engine-wide hang.
- **High:** likely wrong behaviour in a normal flow, a bus or UI freeze, unbounded growth, or a safety check that is silently bypassed.
- **Medium:** a real bug in a less common path, or a design problem with a concrete ongoing cost.
- **Low:** a minor edge case or a modest cleanup.

## Tooling results

These were run in round 1, at `361c6f9`.

- **`cargo test`:** one failure. `relay-cli` `blender::tests::the_blender_tools_work_on_a_real_rig` fails on the installed Blender 5.2.1 with `AttributeError: 'Action' object has no attribute 'fcurves'` ([RA-008](#ra-008)). `cargo test -p relay-native` passes.
- **`cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings`** (engine, bus, CLI, remote): clean.
- **`cargo clippy -p relay-native --all-targets -- -D warnings -A deprecated`:** one new Rust 1.98 lint, `chunks_exact_to_as_chunks`, in a test at `apps/relay-native/src/sounds.rs:150`. CI pins Rust 1.94, so this is toolchain drift.
- **`clippy::pedantic`:** about 1,400 warnings, mostly docs, `must_use` and cast lints. Auditors checked the cast warnings that touch lengths, offsets, timestamps and ids, and reported only real bugs.
- **`cargo audit`** (1,290 advisories, 383 crates): no vulnerabilities.
  - `faster-hex 0.10.0` is unsound (RUSTSEC-2026-0306, via `gix-hash`).
  - `bisync 0.3.0` is yanked (via `gix-protocol`).

## How to read this

- **Ids.** Part A is defects and security; Part B is code quality and design. Within each part, findings are ordered by severity, then area, and numbered `RA-nnn`.
- **Contents.** Each finding gives the problem with evidence, the concrete impact, the recommended fix, and every verifier's corrections. Where a correction disagrees with the auditor's text, trust the correction; the latest verifier's note comes last.
- **Status.**
  - "Confirmed" means a verifier established the finding from the code.
  - "Plausible" means it is probably real, but the trigger or impact could not be fully established.
  - "Blind re-check" notes come from round 2.
- **Data and tools.**
  - Raw data: [round1.json](round1.json) and the `round2-*.json` files.
  - `round2-merged.json` (round 2 folded into round 1) and `report-data.json` (this report as data) are generated rather than committed. Regenerate them with `python3 -I merge_r2.py round1.json round2-dedup.json round2-completeness.json round2-blind.json round2-linemap.json round2-merged.json`, then `python3 -I build_report.py report-config.json`.
  - The scripts are `build_report.py`, `build_html.py` and `merge_r2.py`.

| RA-001 | high | Security | `crates/relay-cli/src/main.rs:406` | Shell file-writes (Bash tool) bypass every write-path guardrail; only Write/Edit/MultiEdit and file.* are gated |
| RA-002 | high | Security | `crates/relay-cli/src/main.rs:471` | The agent guardrail hook has no deadline of its own, so a store-lock stall longer than the provider's 30 s hook timeout lets the tool run unchecked |

| RA-004 | high | Data loss | `crates/relay-cli/src/unreal.rs:589` | quit_editor sends SIGTERM without saving whenever Remote Control misses a 3 s probe, even with save=true, and the signal also hits any editor whose argv ends in the same .uproject name |

| RA-006 | high | Bug | `crates/relay-cli/src/unreal_process.rs:291` | Editor launched by ue_editor_launch / ue_build restart_editor inherits the agent's RELAY_* identity, so Relay's startup orphan reaper SIGKILLs the human's editor on the next engine start |

| RA-009 | high | Bug | `crates/relay-core/src/engine.rs:371` | guardrail.confirm replays a held agent op without the agent's session, so a confirmed agent file.write lands in the project's primary checkout |

## Part A: Defects and security

### High (56)

<a id="ra-001"></a>

#### RA-001 · Shell file-writes (Bash tool) bypass every write-path guardrail; only Write/Edit/MultiEdit and file.* are gated

`crates/relay-cli/src/main.rs:406` · **high** · Security · confirmed · effort L

**Problem.** The PreToolUse adapter maps the Bash tool to `kind:"exec"` (main.rs:406-410 for Claude; main.rs:508-512 maps Codex Bash|apply_patch|Edit|Write ALL to exec). evaluate_exec (guardrail.rs:811-847) checks only self_approval + denied_commands (+ a device lease on allow). It never evaluates protected_paths, allowed_write_roots, destructive_write or shape_gates — those live only in evaluate_write (guardrail.rs:503), reachable solely from the Write/Edit/MultiEdit tools and the file.* bus ops (file.rs:72,127 call guardrail::enforce with GateKind::Write). There is no post-hoc write detector: watch.rs emits only reconciliation events, and the `guardrail.violation` watcher described in BUS.md §9.3 is unimplemented (no `violation` emitter exists in crates/).

**Impact.** A builder session whose project sets protected_paths (e.g. `**/*.env`, `**/secrets.*`) or shape gates can modify or destroy those files with an ordinary shell command the gate waves through: `printf 'KEY=leak\n' >> config/.env`, `sed -i 's/.*/x/' src/critical.rs`, `: > important.rs`, `truncate -s0 f`, `tee`, `cp`, `python -c 'open("x","w")...'`. protected_paths / destructive_write / shape_gates / write_roots are all skipped; nothing is held, refused, or detected afterward. These are routine (non-adversarial) agent actions, so the seatbelt misses the mistakes it exists to catch. Only a later commit through the hooked git (and only if the agent does not add --no-verify, see separate finding) would catch a protected path — caps/destructive/shape are never re-checked.

**Fix.** Gate writes regardless of the tool used: in the exec gate, detect obvious file-mutating commands (redirections `>`/`>>`, sed -i, tee, cp/mv/dd/truncate/install, interpreter one-liners) and run their target paths through the write policy; and/or implement the documented post-hoc violation watcher for Claude too (re-run write policy on watched file.changed, raise guardrail.violation + file.restore_head). At minimum stop advertising write guardrails as binding when the agent holds the Bash tool.

**Verifier note.** The problem is wider than shell writes. The Codex adapter (main.rs:506-512, matcher `Bash|apply_patch|Edit|Write` in hooks.rs:517) sends every Codex tool, including its own file-editing tools (apply_patch, Edit, Write), as `kind:"exec"`. So for Codex the write rules are never checked at all. Yet providers.rs:212 now reports Codex as `guarded() = true`, and D107 and BUS §9.3 still describe a watcher that was never built (docs drift). Better fix: catch writes after they happen rather than parsing commands for redirections. A PostToolUse hook already exists for Bash and apply_patch (it feeds session.report). It could run the write policy on the paths that changed, raise a notification and offer file.restore_head. Matching redirections in the exec gate is fragile and easy to get around. At minimum, ProviderInfo.guarded and the docs should say that write rules do not bind shell writes or Codex.

**Skeptic note.** Put the Codex half first. For Codex, no write rule runs on any edit, not only on shell writes. The apply_patch envelope is structured (`*** Add File:`, `*** Update File:`, `*** Delete File:`, `*** Move to:`). The Codex adapter can parse it and send one kind:write gate per file. It can pass the hunks as `diff`, which diff_counts already counts by '+' and '-', or apply the hunks in memory to produce new_text, the way the Claude Edit adapter does. That gives Codex the same protection as Claude's Write and Edit at low cost.

I inferred that Codex's apply_patch hook input carries a `command` field from strings in the installed Codex binary, not from its documentation. If the field is missing, the adapter fails closed and blocks every patch, which would be a different bug.

The first verifier's suggestion, a PostToolUse check that offers file.restore_head, does not work as written. restore_head runs `git checkout -- path`, which restores HEAD. That cannot bring back modified or untracked content, and that content is the only thing destructive_write still guards under the default allow_if_recoverable (D114). A post-hoc check needs a snapshot taken before the command runs, to diff against and restore from. The PreToolUse adapter could take one: point GIT_INDEX_FILE at a temporary index, run `git add -A` and `git write-tree`, and copy any ignored protected files separately.

That snapshot and diff must run in the CLI hook process, not inside guardrail.gate. guardrail.gate is registered with Engine::register (handlers/guardrail.rs:304) and holds the store mutex, so a tree walk there would stall every session (CLAUDE.md invariant). In a shared-worktree group (D131), the diff cannot tell which session made a change.

Checking redirections before the command runs can only cover protected_paths and write_roots for obvious targets. It cannot measure destructive_write or shape gates. The existing shell_commands reader also treats `>` as an ordinary word character and splits commands on `&`, so `2>&1` breaks into two commands; it would need a real redirection parser.

Docs drift to fix:
- BUS.md §9.3 (lines 524-533) still says Codex is unguarded and its writes are caught post-hoc.
- D5 says the same.
- guarded() returns true for Codex.
- The UI hints promise more than the code does.

**Blind re-check note.** The more serious angle is Codex, and the claim understates it. apply_patch, Codex's normal edit tool, is sent to the gate as kind:"exec" (main.rs:508; matcher at hooks.rs:517), so every Codex file edit skips protected_paths, destructive_write and shape gates. And Codex is reported as guarded()==true (providers.rs:212), contrary to BUS.md §9.3 and D107. The commit hook still re-checks protected_paths and caps at commit time, but not destructive_write or shape_gates, and not files that are never committed. The fix for Codex should parse apply_patch file headers into kind:"write" gates with a diff, rather than relying only on shell heuristics.

<a id="ra-002"></a>

#### RA-002 · The agent guardrail hook has no deadline of its own, so a store-lock stall longer than the provider's 30 s hook timeout lets the tool run unchecked

`crates/relay-cli/src/main.rs:471` · **high** · Security · confirmed · effort S

**Problem.** The PreToolUse hook is installed with `"timeout": 30` (hooks.rs:351, Codex hooks.rs:521). claude_pre_tool awaits `client.call(&request, |_| {}).await?` with no deadline (main.rs:471; Codex main.rs:520). It fails closed (exit 2) only when the function returns an Err (main.rs:348-357, whose comment says "Claude Code only treats exit 2 as blocking"). guardrail.gate is a locked handler (`engine.register::<Gate>`, handlers/guardrail.rs:304), so it queues on the store mutex behind any long holder (see the dispatch, clone and worktree-removal findings). std::sync::Mutex also lets new arrivals barge ahead of waiters. When the provider kills the hook at 30 s, the exit-2 path is never reached. Not verifiable in this repo: that Claude Code treats a timed-out hook as non-blocking. The engine still runs the queued gate later, because a spawn_blocking dispatch cannot be cancelled. That late gate can insert holds or refusal notifications, or take a 15-minute device shell lease, for a call that already ran or was abandoned.

**Impact.** While the bus is stalled for more than 30 s (the user clones a project, or confirms a commit whose pre-commit hook runs tests), every agent's Bash, Edit and Write proceeds without guardrail evaluation. Afterwards stale holds and leases appear for actions that already happened.

**Fix.** Wrap the gate call in tokio::time::timeout (for example 20 s, under the provider's limit) and exit 2 with "guardrail unavailable" when it expires. Have the engine skip gate requests whose connection has already closed. Remove the long lock holds.

**Verifier note.** The other long lock holds are the root cause of the stall, and the ProjectClone `git clone` under the lock is one concrete instance. This finding is the fail-open that lets such a stall bypass the guardrail, and it should be fixed on its own as defense in depth. Wrap the connect and call in claude_pre_tool and codex_pre_tool in tokio::time::timeout of about 20-25 s, and return Err so the existing exit-2 path fires. The stdlib-mutex barging point is incidental and not needed for the finding.

**Skeptic note.** Upgrade the evidence. The behaviour the finding marked "not verifiable" is confirmed for the installed Claude Code 2.1.291. A command hook killed by its own timeout yields hook_cancelled/outcome "cancelled", which is non-blocking. Claude does not show it for PreToolUse, so the bypass is silent. Codex 0.154.0 most likely behaves the same; its strings fit, but the control flow was not confirmed. Cite D23, which this violates.

Stall sources: replace the vague "dispatch" holder with three concrete ones.
- project.clone (workspace.rs:234).
- guardrail.confirm of a held git.commit, which runs the user's pre-commit under the lock (engine.rs:325-342 with hooks.rs:210-213).
- worktree.remove (worktree.rs:352-368).
task.dispatch{create} is UserOnly, and the native client dispatches to existing sessions, so it is a minor path. The stdlib-mutex barging point is incidental.

Add these consequences: a late Refuse leaves a refusal notification for an action that actually ran, and a late Allow consumes once-grants.

Fix:
(1) In claude_pre_tool and codex_pre_tool, wrap connect plus call in tokio::time::timeout of about 20 s. Return Err so the existing exit-2 path fires.
(2) The engine cannot notice that a connection closed while it is awaiting dispatch, because the per-connection loop does not read during that wait. Carry a deadline in the gate request instead. After acquiring the lock, gate should return an error with no side effects (no hold, notification, lease or grant use) once the deadline has passed.
(3) Separately, remove the long lock holds.
Do not rely on raising the hook "timeout": it still fails open and does not reach existing installs.

**Blind re-check note.** The commit-with-pre-commit-hook trigger is wrong: git.commit passes --no-verify (handlers/git.rs:571). The concrete >30 s trigger is project.clone (handlers/workspace.rs:228-235), a locked register handler that runs `git clone` via Command::output() with no timeout. Worktree removal and branch switch, which have 120 s bounds, can also go past 30 s. Codex's handling of a hook timeout was not established in this repo.

<a id="ra-003"></a>

#### RA-003 · Codex apply_patch/Edit/Write are gated as kind=exec, so no write guardrail ever runs for Codex while the UI labels it Guarded

`crates/relay-cli/src/main.rs:508` · **high** · Security · confirmed · effort M

**Problem.** main.rs:506-512 builds `{session, kind: 'exec', command}` for `"Bash" | "apply_patch" | "Edit" | "Write"`. evaluate_exec (crates/relay-core/src/guardrail.rs:811-848) checks only self_approval and denied_commands; protected paths, destructive-write holds, shape gates and write roots live in evaluate_write (guardrail.rs:503), reached only for kind=write. Yet D132 (docs/engine/DECISIONS.md:650-655) says 'Shell and patch invocations reach the same guardrail.gate bus path as Claude', BUS.md §9.2 (494-498) lists those policies for `gate {kind: write}`, and the Codex driver's `fn guarded(&self) -> bool { true }` (providers.rs:212) makes the launch sheet print 'Guarded' (apps/relay-native/src/launch.rs:651-654) and Settings 'Guardrail adapter available' (tools_settings.rs:388-392).

**Impact.** A Codex builder whose apply_patch truncates a large data file, overwrites a protected path or corrupts a shape-gated JSON is never held or refused at write time: the SPEC §5 'data.ts truncation made impossible to do silently' case lands silently on disk. The pre-commit hook later checks only caps and protected paths (never destructive-write or shape gates), after the damage exists. Separately, until the user trusts the generated hook in Codex's /hooks (D132) no gate runs at all, but `guarded` is a constant true and the only 'surfacing' of the trust requirement is a description string in .codex/hooks.json (hooks.rs:500-502). Not verifiable offline: the exact tool_input Codex sends for Edit/Write; if it lacks a `command` string the adapter fails closed and blocks those tools outright. Either way no write policy is ever evaluated for Codex.

**Fix.** In codex_pre_tool, route apply_patch/Edit/Write to kind 'write': parse the patch's `*** Add/Update/Delete File:` sections (or Edit/Write path+content) into one gate call per file with new_text or diff, as claude_pre_tool does; keep kind 'exec' only for Bash. Make ProviderInfo.guarded report what actually binds (exec-only, hook trust unknown) and correct D132 and BUS.md §9.3.

**Verifier note.** I could not verify offline what tool_input Codex sends for Edit/Write. If `command` is absent, required_string fails, codex_pre_tool returns Err and the CLI exits 5, not 2. Whether Codex then blocks or proceeds is unknown, so 'fails closed' is unestablished. Context: any agent, Claude included, can write files through its shell tool without a write gate, so write guardrails are best-effort for every provider. That is a separate root cause. This finding is that Codex's primary edit tool is unguarded while the docs and UI say it is guarded. Fix as proposed: parse the apply_patch `*** Add/Update/Delete File:` sections into one kind:write gate call per file. Also make the trust state and `guarded` reflect reality, and correct D132 and BUS.md §9.3.

**Skeptic note.** 1. The first verifier is wrong about exit 5. main.rs:367-374 maps every codex_pre_tool error to Ok(2), so a missing `command` would block (fail closed). The point is moot: Codex always sends `tool_input.command` (the patch) for apply_patch.
2. Codex never sends tool_name Edit or Write; they are matcher-only aliases. The Edit/Write match arms are dead, and the fix should parse apply_patch only. Its "Edit/Write path+content" part has nothing to act on.
3. Impact wording: protected_paths and shape_gates are empty by default, and destructive-write holds fire only for untracked or modified files (D114). The default-config loss is therefore uncommitted work in a file a Codex patch truncates, and the silent "data.ts" case applies only to such files.
4. Fix details:
   - `*** Add File:` → new_text (strip the leading `+`).
   - `*** Delete File:` → new_text "", so the protected-path and destructive checks run.
   - `*** Update File:` → apply the hunks to the on-disk file to get new_text, as claude_pre_tool does for Edit. A diff alone works for destructive counts, but shape-gated paths are then always held (guardrail.rs:524-534).
   - Gate the destination of `*** Move to:` as well, and tolerate `*** Environment ID:` lines.
   - Block the whole tool call if any file is refused or held.
   - Stop running exec checks on patch text; this also removes the false self_approval and denied-command refusals.
5. `guarded` cannot simply be true, because hooks run only after a per-worktree /hooks trust. Label it accordingly, and correct D132 and BUS.md §9.3. §9.3 also documents a `guardrail.violation` notify watcher that was never implemented.

**Blind re-check note.** Docs drift goes both ways. BUS.md §9.3 (lines 524-533) and §14 (line 1131) still say Codex has "no tool hooks", that guarded is false, and that a post-hoc notify watcher catches destructive writes. That watcher does not exist anywhere in the code. D132 and providers.rs say the opposite (guarded=true). The fix should rewrite §9.3's Codex bullet, not only D132. The commit gate still enforces protected paths and caps at commit time, so the claim that write policy is "never evaluated" holds only at write time: protected paths are checked again at commit.

<a id="ra-004"></a>

#### RA-004 · quit_editor sends SIGTERM without saving whenever Remote Control misses a 3 s probe, even with save=true, and the signal also hits any editor whose argv ends in the same .uproject name

`crates/relay-cli/src/unreal.rs:589` · **high** · Data loss · confirmed · effort S

**Problem.** `match remote("GET", "/remote/info", None, Duration::from_secs(3)) { Ok(_) => { guard + save + quit } Err(_) => notes.push("the editor did not answer; asking the process to terminate instead (unsaved changes are lost)".into()) }` (577-590). The wait loop then runs `if signalled.is_none() && (notes.iter().any(|n| n.contains("terminate")) || ...) { for pid in &before { crate::unreal_process::kill(*pid); } }` (600-603). kill() runs `kill <pid>`, i.e. SIGTERM (unreal_process.rs:65-67). `before` comes from editors_for, which also matches any editor whose argument merely ends with the same file name (unreal_process.rs:57), and no guard_project runs on this path. `save` is never consulted before signalling. ue_build restart_editor=true calls quit_editor with save defaulting to true (1519). Secondary issues: the save+quit request has a 20 s reply timeout (585), yet the loop assumes 'Everything is saved by now' (598) and signals 20 s after that. The script also calls quit_editor() even when save_dirty_packages returned False (582).

**Impact.** Scenario: the human has unsaved level or asset edits, and the RC server is not answering. Causes include a failed bind after a quick relaunch (the D162 case), auto-start being off, or a game thread busy for more than 3 s loading a map or compiling. If an agent then runs ue_build {restart_editor:true} (the documented Linux C++ loop) or ue_editor_quit, the editor is terminated immediately and the edits are lost. This happens even though the tool promises 'Quit a running editor first (saving)'. If the agent works in a worktree, the editor terminated can be the human's editor on the main checkout, because it opens the same .uproject file name. A save slower than 40 s can also be signalled mid-flight.

**Fix.** When save is requested and the editor cannot be reached, refuse with instructions to start the server, or retry the probe with backoff. Only terminate when the caller passes an explicit force flag. Signal only editors whose canonical project path equals this project. In the quit script, check save_dirty_packages' result and abort the quit if it fails. Wait the full save timeout before considering a signal. Drive control flow with a bool, not `notes.contains("terminate")`.

**Verifier note.** The secondary claims are weaker than stated. (1) python_tx has a 20 s read timeout. If the save takes longer, the error is recorded as a note, and the loop sends SIGTERM about 20 s after `requested`, about 40 s in. UE's Linux SIGTERM handler only requests an engine exit, so a save already running on the game thread would most likely finish before the exit is processed. Calling that "signalled mid-flight" corruption is speculative. (2) Ignoring save_dirty_packages' False return value is real but minor. The core fix stands. When save=true and the probe fails, retry with backoff, then refuse and tell the agent to ask the human, unless an explicit force flag is passed. Match editors by canonical path only, dropping the `ends_with` fallback or restricting it to a sibling of the same root. Drive the decision with a bool rather than a substring of a note.

**Skeptic note.** 1) The "signalled mid-flight" sub-claim is wrong. The first SIGTERM only sets the exit flag. The save paths in FileHelpers.cpp never check IsEngineExitRequested, and quit_editor sends one signal per pid. A slow save therefore finishes, and the "wait the full save timeout" item adds no safety.

2) Ignoring save_dirty_packages' result is more serious than the first verifier's "minor":
- `unreal.SystemLibrary.quit_editor()` runs QUIT_EDITOR, which calls UUnrealEdEngine::CloseEditor and then RequestEngineExit. Nothing prompts to save (KismetSystemLibrary.cpp:674-677, EditorServer.cpp:5993-5996, UnrealEdEngine.cpp:943-958).
- SaveDirtyPackages runs unattended with bUseDialog=false. It silently skips packages it cannot save (FileHelpers.cpp:5912-5958, comment at 4069), such as a never-saved Untitled map or a read-only file.
- So even on the reachable path with save=true, those packages are lost. That case is narrow and secondary.

3) The fix is incomplete in four places:
- Aborting in the script on a failed save is not enough. Any python_tx error becomes a note, and the loop still sends SIGTERM 20 s later (600). The Rust side must return an error without signalling when the script reports a save failure. Only a reply timeout after the quit was issued should lead to waiting or signalling.
- Report `saved` truthfully (614).
- Do not just drop `ends_with`. It probably exists for editors launched with a relative .uproject path, and editors_for also gates builds (1518, 1521). Resolve relative arguments against /proc/<pid>/cwd, then compare canonical paths.
- Change editor_status's failed-bind advice (1657) so it tells the agent to ask the human, not to quit an unreachable editor.

**Blind re-check note.** The secondary points are overstated. python_tx waits up to 20 s for the save+quit reply. If the save runs longer, the reply errors and the note is "quit request: ...", which does not contain "terminate". A SIGTERM sent 20 s later only calls RequestEngineExit, a flag the game thread acts on after the in-progress save returns. It does not interrupt a save mid-write, so the "signalled mid-save" angle is low impact. The worktree mis-kill applies only on the unreachable path: with RC reachable, guard_project refuses first, though it leaves the editor lock held after acquire_lock. Also, since the plugin starts agents in the main checkout by default, the worktree angle is the less common case.

**Also at:** `crates/relay-cli/src/unreal.rs:577-607`, `crates/relay-cli/src/unreal.rs:1516-1520`, `crates/relay-cli/src/unreal.rs:136`, `crates/relay-cli/src/unreal_process.rs:57`, `crates/relay-cli/src/unreal_process.rs:65`, `crates/relay-cli/src/unreal.rs:600`, `crates/relay-cli/src/unreal.rs:1518`, `crates/relay-cli/src/unreal.rs:1657`, `plugins/unreal-engine/docs/mcp-tools.md:91`, `plugins/unreal-engine/skills/unreal-editor-automation/SKILL.md:270`

<a id="ra-005"></a>

#### RA-005 · editors_for matches any editor whose argument merely ends with the same .uproject file name, so quitting or building one checkout can SIGTERM another checkout's or another project's editor

`crates/relay-cli/src/unreal_process.rs:57` · **high** · Bug · confirmed · effort S

**Problem.** `.filter(|p| p.cmdline.iter().any(|a| Path::new(a).canonicalize().map(|c| c == want).unwrap_or(false) || a.ends_with(&*uproject.file_name().unwrap_or_default().to_string_lossy())))`. The fallback accepts `/proj/Game.uproject` when the agent's project is `/proj/.relay/worktrees/w1/Game.uproject`, and `TopDownShooter.uproject` when the project is `Shooter.uproject`. A relative argument is canonicalized against the MCP server's cwd, not the editor's. If `file_name()` were None, the needle would be "" and every editor would match. `is_editor` (line 44) compares `a == "-nullrhi"` case-sensitively. quit_editor (unreal.rs:575) stores these PIDs in `before` and runs `for pid in &before { kill(*pid) }` (unreal.rs:600-603).

**Impact.** Two triggers lead to the kill. (a) Remote Control does not answer within 3 s (the editor is busy or RC is off): `notes` contains "terminate" and every matched PID gets SIGTERM at once. (b) Our editor answers and quits, but the other matched editor is still running: 20 s later all of `before` gets SIGTERM. Either way, ue_editor_quit or ue_build restart_editor=true from one checkout terminates the human's editor on another checkout, or the editor of a project whose name is a suffix match, and its unsaved work is lost. The same false positive causes three more failures. ue_build refuses with "the editor is running this project" (unreal.rs:1521-1527). ue_editor_launch returns already_running for a foreign editor (unreal.rs:624-627). engine_root takes the engine from the wrong editor (lines 119-123). The engine_root unit test also fails on a dev machine with any `*Game.uproject` editor open.

**Fix.** Match on path identity only. Resolve each argument against `/proc/<pid>/cwd`, canonicalize it, compare with `want`, and remove the `ends_with(file_name)` fallback. Compare `-nullrhi` case-insensitively. In quit_editor, only signal PIDs that still match the identity check at kill time.

**Verifier note.** Reachability is narrower than the finding implies. guard_project's message says the Unreal plugin starts new agents in the main checkout by default, so path-identical matching is the common case. The false positives need a worktree agent, or two projects whose names are suffixes of one another. When RC answers with the foreign editor's project, guard_project bails before any kill. That bail also leaks the lock taken at line 573, a separate issue. Within the worktree case, the false build refusal and false already_running are deterministic, and the SIGTERM needs a busy or unresponsive editor (>3 s). The fix is right: resolve each cmdline argument against /proc/<pid>/cwd, compare canonical paths only, drop the ends_with fallback, and re-check identity before signalling.

**Skeptic note.** 1. Reachability is broader, not narrower, than the first verifier said. The desktop launch dialog always sends worktree "new" (apps/relay-native/src/launch.rs:259-262, 346, 784), so the plugin's D160 primary default (session.rs:858) never applies to agents launched from the app. Worktree Unreal agents are the default there; that is a separate bug that makes this one common. Add the README's instruction that worktree agents do C++ work, and instructions.md item 5 (restart_editor after every C++ change).

2. Trigger (a) also covers connection refused (web server not started) and non-2xx replies (passphrase mismatch). It also covers an editor busy for over 3 s with another agent's Python call; the per-checkout lock in Saved/ does not prevent that. After the kill, build relaunches the editor on the worktree copy (unreal.rs:1572).

3. Trigger (b) needs two editors running at once, with the worktree's editor holding the RC port. That is rare.

4. engine_root picking the wrong editor is harmless in the worktree case (same .uproject, same EngineAssociation). It matters only for projects whose names are suffixes of one another.

5. The file_name()==None case cannot happen: Project::find reads the path as a file first (unreal.rs:1302).

6. The case-sensitive `-nullrhi` check is a separate, low-impact issue. The tool's own headless runs pass lowercase `-nullrhi` (unreal.rs:1107).

Fix correction: do not resolve relative arguments against /proc/<pid>/cwd. UE 5.8 chdirs to Engine/Binaries/Linux at startup (LaunchEngineLoop.cpp:1801-1804), so relative launches would be missed. Instead:
- Compare absolute arguments by canonical path.
- Resolve a relative argument against PWD from /proc/<pid>/environ, or treat it as unknown.
- Pass a canonical path to launch().
- Drop the ends_with fallback.
- Before any kill, require positive identity (a canonical match, or editor_project() over Remote Control) and re-check each PID right before signalling.

Separately, even with exact matching, the terminate-when-unreachable fallback (unreal.rs:589, 600-603) still SIGTERMs the person's own main-checkout editor when a main-checkout agent restarts it while Remote Control is down or busy. The identity fix does not address that.

**Blind re-check note.** Trigger (a) needs Remote Control to be unreachable within 3 s. When the foreign editor's RC does answer, guard_project refuses before any kill, so the kill does not happen every time a worktree agent quits. D160 (Unreal agents start in the main checkout by default) makes the worktree case non-default, though still reachable. The "file_name() is None, so every editor matches" angle cannot happen, because Project::find always yields a path ending in a .uproject file name. Path (b), the 20 s timer, needs two matching editors alive at once, which is rarer than the claim suggests.

#### RA-006 · Editor launched by ue_editor_launch / ue_build restart_editor inherits the agent's RELAY_* identity, so Relay's startup orphan reaper SIGKILLs the human's editor on the next engine start

`crates/relay-cli/src/unreal_process.rs:291` · **high** · Bug · confirmed · effort S

**Problem.** launch() builds `std::process::Command::new(&binary).arg(uproject).arg("-RCWebControlEnable").args(extra)…process_group(0)` and spawns it with no env_remove/env_clear ("Its own process group: the editor outlives this MCP server and the agent", line 302). `relay unreal-mcp` runs under Claude with the session env: hooks.rs:401 says the MCP config "inherits the session/token/project environment from the Claude process", and handlers/session.rs:563-574 sets RELAY_SESSION, RELAY_TOKEN, RELAY_INSTANCE and RELAY_STORE. At engine start, recovery.rs:64-73 calls `pty::relay_children(instance, &store_path)`. That returns every live pid whose /proc environ has a matching RELAY_INSTANCE + RELAY_STORE + RELAY_SESSION (pty.rs:411-430), and each one gets kill_wait: `kill(-pid, SIGTERM)`, then SIGKILL 2 s later (recovery.rs:20-35).

**Impact.** Trigger: an agent applies a C++ change the way instructions.md rule 5 says (`ue_build restart_editor:true`, which calls launch_editor at unreal.rs:1572), or calls ue_editor_launch. The human keeps working in that editor, then Relay restarts (app update, crash, quit/relaunch). Recovery treats the editor as the agent's orphan and kills its whole process group (UnrealEditor, ShaderCompileWorkers) after 2 s; unsaved level and asset edits are lost. Second effect: the editor and its children carry agent A's RELAY_SESSION/RELAY_TOKEN. Commits from the editor's Git integration then run the pre-commit gate as agent A (hooks.rs:122-129) with agent caps. Any `relay` call made from the editor (e.g. another agent's ue_python subprocess) also acts as A.

**Fix.** In unreal_process::launch, strip Relay's identity from the child: `for (k, _) in std::env::vars_os() { if k.to_string_lossy().starts_with("RELAY_") { command.env_remove(k); } }`, or at least RELAY_SESSION, RELAY_TOKEN, RELAY_INSTANCE and RELAY_STORE. Add a test that the launch Command carries no RELAY_SESSION. The same applies to any other long-lived child the bridge starts.

**Verifier note.** This affects Claude agents. Codex clears the MCP server's environment to a short allowlist (see #12), so an editor launched from a Codex agent likely carries no RELAY_* and is not reaped. Fix as proposed: strip RELAY_* from the launch Command. The reaper could also skip processes that lead their own process group outside the session's tree, but stripping the env is the direct fix.

**Skeptic note.** Narrow the trigger to an engine restart (app.quit/relaunch, an update, a crash). Closing and reopening the desktop window does not trigger it, because the engine outlives the window (run.sh:45).

The secondary claims are minor:
- **Commits from the editor:** these are gated as agent A only when the editor's checkout has Relay's per-worktree hooksPath. That is true for the primary checkout once any agent has been launched there.
- **Bus calls "as A":** this adds no new privilege. ue_python already runs arbitrary Python as the user, and it can shed RELAY_SESSION to act as `user`, since the socket does not authenticate `user` (guardrail.rs:849-850).

After the fix, git or relay calls made from the editor run as the user, which is the right identity for the human and opens no new hole.

**Testing the fix:** factor the Command construction out of launch() and assert that get_envs() lists ("RELAY_SESSION", None) etc. Avoid mutating the process environment in a parallel test.

**Codex:** the Codex exemption is likely (Codex launches MCP servers with an allowlisted environment), but I did not verify it here.

**Optional defense in depth:** limit the env-based reaper to what SPEC §14 promises, claude/codex processes and members of recorded session process groups. Then no intentionally detached descendant can be killed this way.

**Blind re-check note.** Minor: the identity angle only lets editor children act as agent A while A's token is still valid. After that, commits from the editor fail the gate (or are misattributed) rather than gaining any privilege. The main impact is the editor being killed at engine start.

**Also at:** `crates/relay-core/src/recovery.rs:64`, `crates/relay-core/src/recovery.rs:20`, `crates/relay-core/src/pty.rs:411`, `crates/relay-core/src/handlers/session.rs:563`, `crates/relay-core/src/hooks.rs:401`, `crates/relay-core/src/hooks.rs:122`, `crates/relay-cli/src/unreal.rs:649`, `crates/relay-cli/src/unreal.rs:1572`, `crates/relay-core/src/hooks.rs:124`, `crates/relay-core/src/handlers/session.rs:565`, `crates/relay-core/src/recovery.rs:67`, `crates/relay-core/src/pty.rs:408-429`, `crates/relay-core/src/pty.rs:344-369`, `crates/relay-core/src/handlers/session.rs:564-576`, `crates/relay-core/src/recovery.rs:69`, `crates/relay-cli/src/unreal_process.rs:304`, `docs/engine/SPEC.md:354`, `crates/relay-core/tests/sessions.rs:554`

#### RA-007 · blender_export ignores view-layer visibility: excluded collections crash it, eye-hidden collections are silently left out of the FBX

`crates/relay-cli/src/blender_py/export.py:60` · **high** · Bug · confirmed · effort M

**Problem.** Lines 57-60 clear only object-level flags (`o.hide_set(False)`, `o.hide_viewport = False`), then call `o.select_set(True)` and export with `use_selection=True`. The default object list (line 7) comes from `scene.objects`, which includes objects in excluded collections. Both cases reproduced on 5.2.1. (a) With a mesh in an excluded 'Reference' collection, the default export fails with `RuntimeError: Object 'RefBox' cannot be selected because it is not in View Layer`. (b) With a mesh in a collection hidden by its eye icon (`LayerCollection.hide_viewport`), export exits 0 and reports `"objects": ["SM_Crate"], "size_cm": [100,100,100], "bytes": 4220`, but re-importing the FBX finds no objects. Control: with the collection visible, the file is 13100 bytes and contains SM_Crate.

**Impact.** An agent exports a prop, or a character whose body sits in a hidden collection, and gets a success result with an empty or incomplete FBX. blender_to_unreal then imports nothing, or a skeleton without its mesh. The mesh checks and the size were reported for objects that were never written.

**Fix.** Build the candidate set from `bpy.context.view_layer.objects`, and skip or report excluded objects explicitly. Make the chosen objects visible: un-hide their LayerCollection chain, or link them temporarily into `scene.collection`. Before exporting, assert `set(bpy.context.selected_objects) == selected` and fail with the names that could not be selected.

**Verifier note.** Take candidates from `bpy.context.view_layer.objects` and report excluded objects. Make the chosen objects selectable (un-hide their LayerCollection chain, or temporarily link them into scene.collection), and before exporting assert `set(bpy.context.selected_objects) == selected`, failing with the names that are missing. Explicitly named objects (`ARGS['objects']`) have the same problem.

**Skeptic note.** 1. The root cause is wider than claimed. On 5.2.1, three more states also silently produce the 4236-byte empty FBX with exit 0: Collection.hide_viewport (monitor icon), Collection.hide_select, and Object.hide_select. The script never clears o.hide_select.

2. "Crash" overstates case (a). Blender exits 1 and the tool returns the traceback. It also hits every Rigify file on the default path, because WGTS_rig is excluded. The Rigify recipe passes objects, which avoids it.

3. blender_to_unreal is not silent for a fully empty FBX: it returns passed:false, but blames the importer. Partial FBXs pass. The claim that it imports "a skeleton without its mesh" is unverified (no Unreal was available here); the import more likely fails.

4. The fix has three problems.
   - Un-hiding the LayerCollection chain fixes only the eye case. It did not fix the monitor icon, collection hide_select or object hide_select.
   - Linking each chosen object into scene.collection fixed the excluded, eye, monitor and collection hide_select cases. It still needs `o.hide_select = False`. Keep the assert that `set(bpy.context.selected_objects) == selected`.
   - Do not force in derived objects found through scene.objects (line 20) or children_recursive when they sit in excluded collections; report them instead. An example is an archived body that is still skinned to the rig.

5. The default filter at line 7 checks only object-level hide_render. Rigify sets hide_render on the collection, which the filter misses.

6. Update the docs that promise "every visible root": plugins/blender/skills/blender-to-unreal/SKILL.md:58-59, plugins/blender/skills/blender-to-unreal/reference/troubleshooting.md:87, and plugins/blender/skills/blender-fundamentals/reference/bpy-recipes.md:194-199.

7. On the related locations: render.py:8 shares the default-candidate cause, but the effect is only camera framing. mesh_check.py:3 neither selects nor exports anything, so this failure does not apply to it.

**Blind re-check note.** There is a third trigger that silently produces an empty FBX: Collection.hide_viewport (the monitor icon), reproduced here as well. The fix must clear it along with LayerCollection.exclude and LayerCollection.hide_viewport, or must link the selected objects temporarily into scene.collection. Line numbers are accurate: the selection loop is at lines 57-60, and the FBX call (use_selection=True) is at line 81.

#### RA-008 · Blender scripts use Action.fcurves, which Blender 5.x removed, so blender_info, skeletal export and blender_to_unreal fail on current Blender (the failing cargo test)

`crates/relay-cli/src/blender_py/info.py:45` · **high** · Bug · confirmed · effort S

**Problem.** info.py:45-46 has `groups = set(fc.data_path.split('"')[1] for fc in a.fcurves if ...)` and `"fcurves": len(a.fcurves)` for every action in bpy.data.actions. export.py:48 has `keyed = set(... for fc in act.fcurves ...)` whenever the armature has an action and kind != static. The installed Blender 5.2.1 exposes F-curves only through channelbags (`bpy_extras.anim_utils.action_get_channelbag_for_slot`, anim_utils.py:91). `cargo test` fails in blender.rs:539 (`run(PY_INFO, ...)`) with "AttributeError: 'Action' object has no attribute 'fcurves'". plugins/blender/docs/setup.md:3 promises "4.0 or newer". render.py:35 maps eevee to 'BLENDER_EEVEE', which 4.2-4.5 reject because the id there is BLENDER_EEVEE_NEXT.

**Impact.** On Blender 5.x, blender_info fails for any .blend that contains an action, and it is the documented first call. blender_export of a rig with an assigned action fails, and so does blender_to_unreal for animated characters. CLAUDE.md's `cargo test` fails on every machine with Blender 5 installed. CI runners have no Blender, so the breakage was never visible there. engine=eevee renders fail on the 4.2/4.5 LTS releases.

**Fix.** Add a `action_fcurves(action)` helper to common.py. It uses `action.fcurves` when the attribute exists and otherwise iterates `layer.strips[*].channelbags[*].fcurves`, or the assigned slot's channelbag. Use it in info.py and export.py. Pick the EEVEE id from the engine enum items. Log the Blender version in the real-Blender test, and consider a CI job with a pinned Blender.

**Verifier note.** Only info.py:45-46 and export.py:48 use the legacy API. rig_check and anim_inspect do not use fcurves. For the helper, prefer `bpy_extras.anim_utils.action_get_channelbag_for_slot(action, slot)` (or iterate layers, strips and channelbags) and fall back to `action.fcurves` when `hasattr(action, 'fcurves')`. High rather than critical: the breakage is confined to the optional Blender plugin, not the engine.

**Skeptic note.** 1) render.py:35 (eevee mapped to 'BLENDER_EEVEE') is a separate root cause and should be its own low finding. It affects only engine=eevee on 4.2-4.5; the repo's SKILL.md:241 itself documents BLENDER_EEVEE_NEXT there. Workbench, the default, is unaffected, and 5.2.1 accepts BLENDER_EEVEE. Its proposed fix, "pick the EEVEE id from the engine enum items", does not work as worded. On 5.2.1, `scene.render.bl_rna.properties['engine'].enum_items` returns only the static placeholder ['BLENDER_EEVEE'] and omits CYCLES and WORKBENCH. Use a version check (`'BLENDER_EEVEE_NEXT' if (4,2,0) <= bpy.app.version < (5,0,0) else 'BLENDER_EEVEE'`) or try/except TypeError on assignment; the TypeError lists the real ids. SKILL.md:242 gives the same misleading advice.
2) export.py should check the armature's own slot: `anim_utils.action_get_channelbag_for_slot(act, arm.animation_data.action_slot)`. This was verified on 5.2.1 (slot OBHero, 3 fcurves). Taking every channelbag would count bones from another slot when one action animates several IDs, which gives spurious "keys non-deform bones" warnings. info.py can take every channelbag, verified to give 3 fcurves. When `layers` exists (4.4+), prefer the slot or channelbag path, so that 4.4/4.5's legacy proxy, which exposes only the first slot, is not used; fall back to action.fcurves before 4.4.
3) Impact is stronger than stated. blender_export fails even with no action or animations argument whenever the armature has an action assigned (verified with {"objects":["Hero"]}). blender_to_unreal kind=animation with an action always fails. No data loss.
4) Scope: only info.py:45-46 and export.py:48 use the removed API. rig_check, anim_inspect, render (workbench), mesh_check and run.py all run correctly on 5.2.1. Not exercised: all_actions exports, fbx_options overrides, and anim_inspect partner actions.
5) setup.md:3 ("4.0 or newer") should name the tested range once fixed.

**Blind re-check note.** Two corrections to the claim:
- blender_info fails for files with any action in bpy.data.actions, not only those with an assigned action.
- The EEVEE id point (render.py:35, BLENDER_EEVEE_NEXT on 4.2-4.5) is a separate, lower-impact compatibility issue with a different root cause. It does not belong under the fcurves claim.

I did not confirm the render.py failure on 4.2-4.5, because only Blender 5.2.1 is installed here.

<a id="ra-009"></a>

#### RA-009 · guardrail.confirm replays a held agent op without the agent's session, so a confirmed agent file.write lands in the project's primary checkout

`crates/relay-core/src/engine.rs:371` · **high** · Bug · confirmed · effort S

**Problem.** `replay_registered` swaps only `actor` and `skip_policy` (`let prior_actor = std::mem::replace(&mut self.actor, actor); let prior_policy = self.skip_policy.replace(skip_policy);`). `self.session_id` stays the confirmer's, which is None for the user. `confirm` calls it at handlers/guardrail.rs:583 and only calls `ctx.set_session(hold.session_id)` afterwards, at :593. The replayed `file.write` resolves its target with `root(ctx, p.project_id, p.worktree.as_deref())` (file.rs:73), which goes through `root_choice(ctx.tx(), ctx.actor_session_id(), ..)` (file.rs:452) to `default_worktree_in`. With `session_id: None, requested: None` that returns `repo`, the primary checkout (file.rs:401-407). Agents get holds rather than refusals for `destructive_write` and `shape_gate` (guardrail.rs:1035-1036). The frozen payload has no `worktree`: fill_identity fills only required fields, and neither the MCP server nor the CLI adds it. Nested staged prepares inherit the same `session_id: self.session_id` (engine.rs:337). `evaluate_granted` also skips the agent's grants when session_id is None (guardrail.rs:484).

**Impact.** Trigger: an agent with bus writes (this user's sessions expose file_write) calls `file.write {project_id, path, text}` on a modified or untracked file, removing at least 50 lines and 40%. The write is held. The user clicks Confirm, and the text is written to `<primary checkout>/<path>` instead of the agent's worktree, with the destructive-write check skipped through skip_policy. Any uncommitted user edits to that file in the main checkout are overwritten without a check. The agent's worktree never receives the write, but the agent is told it succeeded. A second hold raised during the replay is stored with session_id NULL. The only replay test, phase8.rs `a_held_commit_still_commits_when_confirmed`, uses a user-held op, where both sessions are None.

**Fix.** Have `replay_registered` take the hold's session id (and project) and swap `self.session_id` for the duration, the same way it swaps `actor`. Have `confirm` pass `hold.session_id`. As a second guard, when a hold is created, pin the resolved worktree into the frozen payload (insert `worktree` when absent) so a replay cannot re-resolve it. Add a test: an agent file.write held by destructive_write and confirmed by the user must change the file in the agent's worktree and leave the primary checkout untouched.

**Verifier note.** Precondition: the default role allowlists (settings.rs:36-38) do not grant agents file.write/file.create/file.delete/git.commit, so this needs a customised role config. This user's sessions do expose file_write and git_commit, so it is reachable here. A confirmed user click in a normal review flow is enough to trigger it. The git.commit variant (commit or `add -A` in the primary checkout) is a second consequence worth naming. Fix as proposed: have replay_registered take and swap the hold's session_id, and pin the resolved worktree into the frozen payload when the hold is created. Add an agent-held destructive_write and confirm test that asserts the agent's worktree changed and the primary checkout did not.

**Skeptic note.** 1. The first verifier's git.commit variant is wrong. `evaluate_commit` has only the `protected_path` and `cap` policies, and `refuse_or_user_hold` refuses an agent on both rather than holding it (guardrail.rs:1035-1047). An agent's `git.commit` therefore never creates a hold, so there is no agent commit replay.
   - Agent holds raised through the bus come only from `file.write` (`destructive_write`, `shape_gate`, the 64 MiB cap) and from `file.create` (`shape_gate`, whose default list is empty).
   - `file.delete`/`rename`/`move`/`import` pass the file's own text through `guard_path_mutation`, so they never trip `destructive_write`.
   - git.rs:773 belongs in "related" only as the shared mechanism.

2. The precondition is not a customised role config. `bus_writes` is on by default in the native launch dialog (launch.rs:264-265).

3. The trigger is "more than 50 lines OR more than 40% of a file of at least 30 lines", not "50 lines and 40%". It applies only to a file git cannot restore: untracked, modified or staged in the agent's worktree.

4. Mitigations the finding omits:
   - If the agent supplied `expected_sha256`, the replay compares it against the primary's file and fails with `file.edit_conflict`, with no write (file.rs:77-90).
   - If the agent passed `worktree` explicitly, the replay hits the right tree.
   - Only the omitted-worktree, no-sha case writes to the primary checkout.
   - Actual loss of user work additionally needs uncommitted edits to that path in the primary. Otherwise it is a misplaced write plus a missing agent change.

5. "The agent is told it succeeded": more precisely, the agent sees only `guardrail.resolved{confirmed}`. The non-gate branch skips the mailbox message that §9.4 promises.

6. A secondary symptom: with `session_id` None, the agent's grants are not loaded (guardrail.rs:484). A write that relied on a `protected_path` grant is refused on replay, and the user sees "Allowed, but the action then failed".

7. Fix: swapping `session_id` in `replay_registered` is sufficient. Pinning `worktree` is optional belt-and-braces. The proposed test should omit `expected_sha256`.

**Blind re-check note.** The data-loss part is narrower than stated: it needs uncommitted edits to the same path in the primary checkout. Otherwise the main checkout gets an unexpected change that git can restore, or a new untracked file. Separately, the agent's intended write is silently dropped from its worktree. The holds that this path reaches come from `destructive_write` on modified or untracked files, or from `shape_gate`; committed or ignored files are allowed through by `allow_if_recoverable`. The pinned-worktree guard must be applied only to ops whose payload schema has a `worktree` field.

**Also at:** `crates/relay-core/src/handlers/guardrail.rs:583`, `crates/relay-core/src/handlers/guardrail.rs:593`, `crates/relay-core/src/handlers/file.rs:401`, `crates/relay-core/src/handlers/file.rs:452`, `crates/relay-core/src/guardrail.rs:1035`, `crates/relay-core/src/guardrail.rs:484`, `crates/relay-core/src/engine.rs:337`, `crates/relay-core/src/handlers/git.rs:773`, `crates/relay-core/src/engine.rs:364-377`, `crates/relay-core/src/engine.rs:330-341`, `crates/relay-core/src/handlers/file.rs:401-408`, `crates/relay-core/src/handlers/file.rs:73-102`, `crates/relay-core/src/handlers/guardrail.rs:690-699`, `crates/relay-core/src/engine.rs:364`, `crates/relay-core/src/handlers/file.rs:398`, `crates/relay-core/src/handlers/file.rs:93`, `crates/relay-core/src/handlers/guardrail.rs:691`, `apps/relay-native/src/guardrail_pages.rs:299`, `docs/engine/BUS.md:541`

<a id="ra-010"></a>

#### RA-010 · Guardrail denied-command matching misses commands in ( ), $( ) and backticks, which the device-lease parser in the same gate call already splits on

`crates/relay-core/src/guardrail.rs:939` · **high** · Security · confirmed · effort M

**Problem.** guardrail::shell_commands splits commands only on `';' | '\n' | '|' | '&' =>` (939). Every other character falls to the default arm, so `(`, `)`, `` ` `` and `$(` stick to words. For `(git reset --hard)` the bare words are ["(git","reset","--hard)"], and the word-window match in denied_matches (969-1001) never hits. device_lease::split_commands (device_lease.rs:365-389) is a second shell splitter in the same crate. It splits on `(None, ';' | '\n' | '|' | '&' | '(' | ')' | '`')` and on `$(`, and it unquotes tokens. guardrail.gate runs both on the same command: evaluate_granted first, then device_lease::gate_command (handlers/guardrail.rs:510-532). I ported shell_commands and denied_matches to Python and used a neutral pattern. `zap --all` matched. `(zap --all)`, `cd src && (zap --all)`, `echo $(zap --all)`, `` `zap --all` ``, `"zap" --all` and `echo "\"" ; zap --all ; echo "\""` were all NOT matched (the last one because a backslash-escaped quote inside double quotes flips the quote state).

**Impact.** An agent whose Bash call runs `(cd sub && git reset --hard)` or `git clean -fd` inside a subshell or command substitution executes a denied command without any hold or refusal. This is a common, non-adversarial shell idiom. self_approval (857) uses the same tokenizer: `(relay --actor user …)` produces the word "(relay", which fails the `starts_with("relay")` stem check. D103 covers quoted data, not subshells.

**Fix.** Give relay-core one shell tokenizer. It should split on `(`, `)`, backtick, `$(`, `{` and `}`, honour backslash escapes inside double quotes, and treat a quoted first word as the program. Use it in both guardrail and device_lease, and add tests for subshell and command-substitution forms.

**Verifier note.** Line refs are accurate: tokenizer at guardrail.rs:894-952, separator arm at 937, matcher at 969-998, self_approval at 857. The denied list was never a hard boundary even against a deliberately evasive agent: `bash -c 'git reset --hard'` is a quoted word and goes unmatched by design (D103). High is still right because the subshell and `$( )` misses occur in non-adversarial use. Besides sharing one tokenizer, strip leading `(`/`{` and trailing `)`/`}` from words when they are not quoted.

**Skeptic note.** 1. The impact is overstated. A trailing `)` does not defeat the match when an argument follows the pattern. These are still DENIED:
- `(cd frontend && rm -rf node_modules)`
- `(cd sub && git reset --hard origin/main)`
- `(cd sub && git clean -fd .)`

The reliable misses are:
- the program glued to `(`, `$(` or a backtick;
- the pattern's last word followed directly by `)`;
- an escaped `\"` inside double quotes earlier in the line, which can hide every later command on that line.

The escaped-quote case should be stated as a co-equal trigger, not an aside.

2. The fix is necessary but not sufficient. The contiguous-window matcher (guardrail.rs:985-988) separately lets all of these through today:
- `git -C <dir> reset --hard` and `git -C sub clean -fd`
- `git push origin main --force` and `git push -f`
- `git clean -fdx` and `git clean -df`
- `rm -fr`, `rm -r -f` and `rm --recursive --force`

`git -C` is arguably the most frequent miss, because Claude Code agents are told to avoid `cd`. That is a separate root cause: the matcher compares a contiguous run of words, where it should match the program plus its required subcommand and flags in any position, with flag bundling allowed. If no other finding reports it, it should be its own finding. A tokenizer-only fix will leave the denied list unreliable.

3. Implementation notes for the fix:
- Inside double quotes, apply the POSIX rule: a backslash escapes only `$`, backtick, `"`, `\` and newline. Inside single quotes it escapes nothing.
- Splitting on `{` and `}` is harmless for matching. `find -exec rm -rf {} \;` still matches before the `{`.
- Grant values are re-tokenized at check time by the same function (guardrail/grants.rs:143), so grant comparison stays consistent after the change.
- The device_lease splitter special-cases `&>` (device_lease.rs:376) and re-splits quoted text on whitespace with `unquote` (321, 392-394). Moving it to the shared tokenizer actually fits the "one quoted word" comment at 431. Its tests need re-running.
- Prefer splitting over the first verifier's idea of stripping `(` and `)` from words. Stripping misses `$(` and backticks unless those are also stripped.
- The `self_approval` sub-point is low impact on its own: its comment at guardrail.rs:849-850 says it "closes the obvious door, not every door", and invoking relay as the user is a deliberate act.
- There are no tests for subshells, command substitution or escaped quotes. Add them together with the fix.

**Blind re-check note.** Not every subshell form is missed. A miss needs the pattern's first word right after `(`, `$(` or a backtick, or its last word right before `)` or a backtick. `(cd x && rm -rf build)` and `(cd sub && git reset --hard HEAD)` still match, because the paren is attached to a word outside the pattern. The line numbers are roughly right: the separator arm is around 939, denied_matches around 969-1001, and self_approval around 857. Separately, the denylist can already be bypassed through a fully quoted `bash -c '...'`, since D103 treats quoted text as data. That is why this is high rather than critical: it is a best-effort guard against accidents, not a security boundary.

<a id="ra-011"></a>

#### RA-011 · Denied-command matching requires the pattern's exact words contiguously, so everyday spellings of the default denied commands run unchallenged

`crates/relay-core/src/guardrail.rs:988` · **high** · Security · confirmed · effort L

**Problem.** `denied_matches` drops every fully quoted word (`.filter(|word| !word.quoted)`, 977) and then needs the pattern as one contiguous window: `bare.windows(wanted.len()).any(|window| window == wanted.as_slice())` (988). `shell_commands` (894-956) understands only quotes, backslash and `; \n | &`; `$(`, backticks, `(`, `sh -c '..'` and `eval` are treated as plain characters or quoted data. A Python port of these functions, which reproduces every case the repo's tests assert, shows that with the default list ["rm -rf","git reset --hard","git clean -fd","git push --force"] 26 of 29 real executions are NOT matched. Examples: `git push -f origin main`, `git push origin main --force`, `git push origin +main`, `git clean -fdx`, `git clean -xfd`, `git clean -f -d`, `git reset HEAD~1 --hard`, `git -C ../app reset --hard`, `rm -fr build`, `rm -r -f build`, `rm -rfv build`, `rm --recursive --force build`, `/bin/rm -rf build`, `"rm" -rf build`, `rm '-rf' build`, `sh -c 'rm -rf build'`, `echo $(rm -rf build)`, `(rm -rf build)`. The dry-run exemption (1012-1019) exempts a whole command, so `relay q guardrail.check $(rm -rf ~)` passes.

**Impact.** An agent that types `git push origin main --force`, `git clean -fdx` or `git reset HEAD~1 --hard` (all common LLM spellings) overwrites the remote or destroys uncommitted and untracked work with no refusal, even though the user configured exactly these rules. For shell commands from Claude's Bash tool and from Codex, this matcher is the only check.

**Fix.** Match each command on normalized argv instead of a literal window. Take the basename of argv[0]. Skip wrappers (sudo, env, command, exec, nice, time, xargs) and `VAR=val` prefixes. Keep quoted words as words, so a quoted argv[0] is still the program. Expand clustered short flags (`-fdx` contains -f and -d). Accept required flags anywhere after the subcommand, in any order, with known equivalents (-f/--force, -r/-R/--recursive), and count `+ref` refspecs as a force push. Recurse into `sh|bash|zsh -c <arg>`, `eval`, `$(..)`, backticks and subshells. Add a regression table with the variants above.

**Verifier note.** Severity: high rather than critical. This is a denylist tripwire that is silently bypassed by common spellings, which the rubric rates high. It is not a sandbox escape, and the provider's own permission layer sits beside it, but it can let `git push origin main --force` or `git clean -fdx` destroy work with no refusal. On the dry-run exemption: `relay q guardrail.check $(rm -rf ~)` does pass, but it would pass without the exemption too, because `$(rm` is never equal to `rm`. The root cause is the matcher, not the exemption. The proposed fix (normalize argv[0] to its basename, skip wrappers and VAR= prefixes, keep a quoted argv[0], expand flag clusters, match flags in any order, recurse into sh -c/eval/$()) is sound. The regression table is the important part.

**Skeptic note.** Severity: high, not critical (BUS.md §0.6, "seatbelts, not sandboxes"; the rubric rates a silently bypassed safety check as high).

Scope: the title says everyday spellings run unchallenged, which overstates it. The canonical spellings are refused: `git push --force <remote> <branch>`, `git reset --hard <ref>`, `git clean -fd`, `rm -rf` and `rm -Rf`. So are forms wrapped in sudo, env, timeout or find -exec, because the window is not anchored to the first word. The gap is variant spellings. Add `git clean -df` to the list of misses: it is a very common spelling and is not refused. I could not check the "26 of 29" count because the finding does not list its cases, but the result itself reproduces.

Dry-run exemption: it is not the root cause. `relay q guardrail.check $(rm -rf ~)` would pass without it, since `$(rm` never equals `rm`.

"Only check": this is the only check on the Relay side. Claude's own permission prompts may still apply, depending on the user's settings. Codex hands approvals to an automatic reviewer (D135).

Fix: do not anchor on argv[0] with a fixed wrapper list; that regresses timeout, find -exec, nohup, xargs with options and sudo with options. Instead:
- Treat any word whose basename equals the pattern's program as the start of a candidate.
- Require the pattern's subcommand words in order after it, skipping git global options (`-C <dir>`, `-c k=v`, `--git-dir=`, `--work-tree=`).
- Require the pattern's flags as a set, anywhere later in the same simple command. Expand single-dash clusters and apply equivalents per program (-f/--force; -r/-R/--recursive). Treat `+ref` refspecs as a force push.
- Keep quoted single tokens as words, so `rm '-rf'` and `"rm"` count. Quoted multi-word data must still never match, which keeps the D103 tests passing.
- Track single versus double quotes, so `$(..)` and backticks inside double quotes are inspected.
- Narrow the dry-run exemption to the relay command itself, or recursion into `$()` would be exempted wholesale.
- Keep `DeniedMatch.bare` for `grants.covers_command`.
- Update D103, BUS.md §9.2 and the "matched word by word" hint at apps/relay-native/src/guardrail_settings.rs:70. Native code cannot be compiled headless.

Cheap stopgap: add `git push -f`, `git clean -df`, `git clean -fdx`, `git clean -xfd` and `rm -fr` to the defaults. It cannot cover a trailing `--force` or `+ref` without over-blocking.

**Blind re-check note.** The claim says the matcher is the only check for commands from Claude's Bash tool. That holds only within Relay. Claude is launched without a permission-bypass flag, so Claude Code's own permission system may still prompt, depending on the user's mode. For Codex (`--approve-for-me`) the claim holds. The `$(rm -rf ~)` case inside `guardrail.check` would also not match without the dry-run exemption, because `$(rm` is a single word to this reader. Line numbers (977, 988, 1012-1019, settings.rs:33) are accurate.

**Also at:** `crates/relay-core/src/guardrail.rs:977`, `crates/relay-core/src/guardrail.rs:920-953`, `crates/relay-core/src/guardrail.rs:1012-1019`, `crates/relay-core/src/handlers/settings.rs:33`, `crates/relay-core/src/guardrail.rs:894`, `crates/relay-core/src/guardrail.rs:1001`, `crates/relay-core/src/device_lease.rs:365`, `crates/relay-cli/src/main.rs:405`, `crates/relay-core/src/guardrail/grants.rs:141`, `crates/relay-core/src/guardrail.rs:975`, `crates/relay-core/tests/guardrails.rs:339`, `crates/relay-core/tests/guardrails.rs:590`, `crates/relay-core/tests/guardrails.rs:645`, `crates/relay-core/src/guardrail.rs:969`, `crates/relay-core/src/guardrail.rs:1012`, `crates/relay-core/src/guardrail.rs:857`, `crates/relay-core/tests/agent_surface.rs:229`
