#### RA-026 · Integration worktrees, branches and build output are never removed: unbounded disk growth from the normal 'Test together' flow

`crates/relay-core/src/handlers/integration.rs:101` · **high** · Resource leak · confirmed · effort M

**Problem.** Every request creates `<repo>/.relay/integrations/<id>` on branch `relay/integration-<id>` (lines 86-101) and run() returns after Passed/Failed/Conflict leaving both; the only cleanup is UserOnly integration.discard and the discarded-before-merge path (119-122). The native Code page always sends `"build":true` (code_git.rs:738) and lists integrations as plain labels with no discard action (code_git.rs:752-770); recovery.rs, branch_cleanup and worktree GC never touch .relay/integrations. Each request also spawns an unbounded std::thread (line 40). SPEC §8 specifies '→ discard' and 'The 73GB problem, closed'; the module doc calls them throwaway. app.resources measures only session worktrees, so this disk is invisible in the resources panel.

**Impact.** Each integration leaves a full checkout (plus LFS content) and its build tree (often GBs) on disk and a relay/integration-N branch in the user's repo and branch picker, forever. A builder agent (integration.request is in its default allowlist, settings.rs:36) can loop requests, each spawning a thread, a checkout and a concurrent build with no cap; the `queued` state is never actually used.

**Fix.** Purge build dirs and remove the worktree when a run ends failed/conflict, and after a short retention for passed ones (keep the latest N per project); cap concurrent integrations per project and really queue the rest; add a discard action in the Code page; have recovery GC directories under .relay/integrations with no live row.

**Verifier note.** Additional related defects worth folding in: (1) nothing resets integrations left in queued/merging/building/deploying after an engine restart (recovery.rs:114 and engine.rs:645 reset device_runs only), and workspace.rs:166/304 integrations_live() then refuses project.remove / workspace.remove forever for that project unless the user finds integration.discard outside the native UI. (2) IntegrationDiscard is registered with Engine::register and calls worktree::remove(..., purge=true), which walks and rm -rf's the build dirs and runs dir_size over the whole checkout while holding the store mutex (CLAUDE.md invariant: slow tree walk in a locked handler) — once a discard UI exists, discarding a multi-GB build freezes the bus. Fix should register discard with register_staged and do the removal outside the lock, plus a restart sweep that marks stale live integrations failed and GCs orphan directories.

**Skeptic note.** Corrections to the finding:
- "The 73GB problem, closed" (SPEC.md:216-219) belongs to the session worktree-lifecycle bullet, not the integration one. The integration bullet (212-216) only ends "→ discard". The finding should cite D38 (DECISIONS.md:138-141), which makes keep-until-explicit-discard the design. So the defect is the missing discard affordance plus the missing retention policy, not the fact that the tree is kept.
- Build output accrues only when project.build_cmd is set (NULL by default) and the merge passed. Otherwise each run costs a checkout (plus LFS files) and a branch.
- The builder-agent loop is speculative. The realistic case is repeated clicks, each starting another concurrent build.

Fix caveats:
1. integration.discard runs under the store mutex (registered with `register` at integration.rs:58). worktree::remove does dir_size walks and remove_dir_all, and runs `git worktree remove --force`, `git worktree prune` and `git branch -D` with no timeout. Wiring a Code-page button to the handler as it stands turns a multi-GB discard into a one-click bus freeze. Move it to register_staged, as session.close does (session.rs:1547-1582), or to after_commit. git.rs:129 (worktree.remove) has the same pattern; that is a separate invariant finding.
2. Removing failed or conflict trees immediately contradicts D38's inspection intent. Prefer purging build output on failure plus retention by age or count.
3. A retention GC must:
   - skip trees that a live device_run uses (device_runs.worktree). device.run and device.build with integration_id run Gradle inside a passed tree (device.rs:983-1016).
   - delete the `relay/integration-<id>` branch too, because worktree::remove keeps branches.
4. A startup GC must do its disk work outside the recovery transaction, which holds the store lock across steps 2-7.

On the first verifier's extra items:
- Item (1) is real but has a different root cause: nothing reconciles integrations after a restart. Rows stuck live permanently block project.remove and workspace.remove even with force (workspace.rs:166-169, 303-307). Report it separately as medium and cross-reference the shared startup sweep.
- Item (2) is a separate invariant finding, but fixing it is required before adding the discard button (caveat 1).

A rare extra consequence: worktree::create (worktree.rs:204-211) checks out an existing branch instead of branching from base. With a fresh store against the same repo (ids restart at 1), a leaked `relay/integration-1` either fails the new run (the path or branch is already checked out) or, if its directory was pruned, gets merged onto a stale integration commit.

**Blind re-check note.** "Forever" overstates it slightly: the user can still discard one by hand with `relay cmd integration.discard {"integration_id":N}` (the CLI's generic op call), which removes the worktree and deletes the branch. What is missing is any GUI path or automatic cleanup. `worktree.disk` would show these worktrees, because it lists every git worktree, but no UI calls it. Two related gaps: project removal (workspace.rs:370) deletes the integration rows but leaves their directories and branches behind as orphans, and an engine restart mid-run leaves a row in merging/building with nothing to reconcile it. The thread-per-request point is minor next to the disk growth. Fix nuance: passed integrations must be kept while they may still be used by device.run (it requires state 'passed'), and conflict worktrees may be worth keeping briefly for inspection, so purge their build directories rather than deleting them outright.

#### RA-027 · mailbox.list returns a project's entire message history, which is never pruned; the GUI re-fetches it on every event and drops its whole control connection once the reply passes 2 MiB

`crates/relay-core/src/handlers/notes.rs:684` · **high** · Performance · confirmed · effort M

**Problem.** MailboxList (notes.rs:660-689) builds `SELECT m.*, CASE ... (correlated NOT EXISTS / MAX subqueries per row) FROM messages m LEFT JOIN message_recipients ... WHERE m.project_id=?1 ... ORDER BY m.sent_at, m.id` with no LIMIT. For the user (session None) there is no recipient filter, so it returns every message ever sent in the project. It runs inside the locked transaction (`e.register`). Messages are deleted only by project.remove (workspace.rs:355-356). The engine itself appends broadcast ('*') messages to every live peer: when an agent turn ends without session.done and the previous notification was read (notify_completion, session.rs:285-292, with the text set to the agent's last assistant message), on every session.done (1212-1219) and on every blocked report (1408-1411). The GUI's Mailbox page calls `mailbox.list {project_id}` (pages.rs:44, 51-58). Every event without special handling falls through to ui.refresh_page() (app.rs:1263-1264), so the query re-runs on task.changed, mailbox.new, notify.*, overlap.changed and others. The control connection rejects any line longer than MAX_LINE = 2 MiB (client.rs:48, 200-205); that error ends the connection, and app.rs:1267-1275 then shows 'Engine disconnected'.

**Impact.** Lock hold time and reply size grow linearly with history. With agent summaries of several hundred bytes to a few KB, roughly 1,000-2,000 messages exceed 2 MiB. From then on, opening the Mailbox page disconnects the whole GUI: the terminals' control plane, events and every request. Each reconnect while that page is open fails the same way. task.list has the same shape: full body and changelog plus about 9 queries per task (task.rs:236-337) for every non-deleted task, re-fetched by the board on every event (pages.rs:43). A long-lived board reaches the same limit.

**Fix.** Paginate. Give mailbox.list and task.list a limit/before cursor with a default (for example 200), have the GUI request pages, and refresh the mailbox page only on mailbox events. Prune or archive acknowledged system broadcasts after N days. Cap the stored text of system broadcasts, since the full summary already lives in the notification. Separately, the client should fail only the oversized request instead of dropping the whole connection.

**Verifier note.** Only the Mailbox page (and the Board, through task.list) triggers this. Other pages do not call mailbox.list. The mirror connection uses a 32 MiB limit (mirror.rs:41); the control connection uses 2 MiB. Fixes, in priority order: (1) bound the reply with a default limit and a before/since cursor, like mailbox.outbox, which already takes a LIMIT (notes.rs:641); (2) cap the stored text of system broadcasts, since the notification already carries the full summary; (3) make an oversized response fail only that request instead of tearing down the control connection.

**Skeptic note.** Corrections to the impact:
- Terminals are not disconnected. Each pane opens its own socket (terminal.rs:476 Client::connect in attach_and_render). Panes are torn down and re-attached only when the user clicks Reconnect (app.rs connect(), 1139-1142).
- The lock-hold growth is minor. message_recipients has PRIMARY KEY (message_id, session_id), so the correlated subqueries are index lookups, and at the 2-5k rows where 2 MiB bites the query takes milliseconds. The real costs are the reply size and the full GTK rebuild per event.
- "1,000-2,000 messages" assumes a 1-2 KB average text. A mixed average gives about 2,500-5,000 messages.

Extra trigger: mailbox.new events carry the full message text (notes.rs:625, session.rs:293, 1217, 1411) on the same 2 MiB connection. A single message over about 2 MiB would drop the GUI on any page. There is no text cap (notes.rs:220-226). This is rare, since model output limits make such a message unlikely.

task.list (related): it is unbounded (task.rs:836-863, every non-deleted task including done ones, with body and changelog). The Board also refreshes after every refresh() (app.rs:1441), so past 2 MiB it would drop the GUI right after each reconnect. Reaching that takes about 800 or more tasks with multi-KB bodies and changelogs, so it is less likely.

Fix refinements:
1. A plain LIMIT on the current ascending order would show the oldest 200 messages and hide new mail. Return the newest N for the user view (ORDER BY sent_at DESC, id DESC LIMIT n+1, then reverse) with a before cursor and a next value, as task.activity already does (task.rs:788-827). Keep agents' oldest-first unread_only behavior. Update MailboxListIn and BUS.md §10.7.
2. In the GUI, request one page at a time, refresh only on mailbox.new and mailbox.changed, and append rows instead of rebuilding.
3. In client.rs, recover the response id from the line prefix (Response serializes v and then id first, which shape() at client.rs:34-45 already relies on). Discard the rest of an oversized line and fail only that request, instead of returning Err from the reader loop.
4. Capping stored broadcast text (the notification keeps the full summary) and mailbox.send text is sound. Pruning conflicts with D26 and with task.activity's task-linked messages, so it is a product decision, not part of the fix.

**Blind re-check note.** refresh_page coalesces events (the page_pending/page_dirty loop), so the query runs at most once per burst, not once per event. It only runs while the Mailbox page is the current page. Broadcasts are added only when another non-closed session exists, and for turn-end summaries only when the previous identical notification was read. The added lock-hold time is a linear SQL scan and is minor next to the 2 MiB disconnect, which is the real impact. Line numbers for the session.rs broadcast sites are about 280-298, 1212-1218 and 1407-1411.

#### RA-028 · Review-group logic treats every session on the same worktree as one group, which deadlocks independent agents that share the primary checkout (the default for Unreal-plugin projects, D160)

`crates/relay-core/src/handlers/session.rs:100` · **high** · Bug · confirmed · effort M

**Problem.** `builders_left` counts `... WHERE ts.task_id=?1 AND s.worktree=?2 AND s.role='builder' AND s.state!='closed' AND ts.completed_at IS NULL` (100-102). `ids` (105) and `reviewers_left` (116-118) use the same rule. task.dispatch queues each task for `SELECT id FROM sessions WHERE worktree=?1 AND state!='closed'` (task.rs:572) and makes it current for any session there that has no live task. D160 / plugins::default_checkout (plugins.rs:210-215) puts every session of an Unreal-plugin project on the primary checkout, and session.create accepts "primary" or an existing path without any PAIR relationship.

**Impact.** Launch builder A with T1 and builder B with T2 on the primary checkout. Dispatch also queues T1 for B and T2 for A. A's session.done(T1) finds B's unfinished T1 row and returns before moving T1 to review; B's done(T2) is blocked the same way by A. Neither task reaches in_review and neither agent advances. Any idle agent there without a task is made current on someone else's task and prompted to start it, which duplicates work in one checkout. validate_pair's worktree-wide counts (764-767) also refuse to form a real review group on a shared checkout, and Close returns 'session.pair_live' for unrelated sessions (1553-1557).

**Fix.** Store group membership explicitly (pair_with links or a group id) and use it in complete_group_assignment, assign_session, validate_pair and Close instead of `worktree=?`.

**Verifier note.** In the native launch sheet the worktree field defaults to 'new' (launch.rs:259-260). The shared-primary case therefore needs the user to type 'primary', or a session.create without a worktree from CLI/MCP in a project with a plugin turned on. For Unreal users that is the normal path. Deadlock versus duplicated work depends on whether the sessions exist before the dispatches; in the native launch flow they do. The Close refusal only costs remove_worktree:false. Suggested fix as proposed: an explicit group id or pair links instead of `worktree=?`.

**Skeptic note.** 1) Trigger. The native launch sheet defaults the worktree to "new" (launch.rs:259-260), so in the GUI the user must type "primary" or a path. A bus or CLI create with no worktree on an Unreal-plugin project lands on primary by default. A second live agent is not required: a leftover non-closed session on the same checkout is enough. That covers restorable sessions after any engine restart, plus exited and parked ones. 2) The "prompted to start it" part only happens on `start:true` dispatches. The native launch uses `start:false`, so there the session's current task changes without any prompt. 3) Fix: do not switch Close's `others` count (session.rs:1553-1559) to group membership. That count also decides whether `run_teardown` runs (352-361), which uninstalls the checkout's git, Claude and Codex hooks. Grouping it would strip the guardrail hooks from a live, unrelated agent on the same checkout. The count also stops a pooled worktree from being removed under another session. Keep Close keyed on the worktree, and only skip the `session.pair_live` refusal when the checkout is not pooled; line 1569 never removes those anyway. A group id needs an appended migration and a SCHEMA_VERSION bump, backfilled from pair_with. pair_with alone forms a chain (builder2 -> reviewer -> builder1) and Close sets it to NULL. Stale cross-queued task_sessions rows already in users' stores still feed next_queued_task and guardrail task ownership, so they need cleaning up too.

**Blind re-check note.** "The default for Unreal-plugin projects" is only partly true. The D160 default applies when the caller omits worktree (CLI, MCP, phone, task.dispatch create). The desktop launch dialog always sends its Worktree field, which defaults to "new" (launch.rs:259-262, 346), so desktop users reach this by typing "primary", as D160 encourages for Unreal. In the claimed scenario, B is not "queued and made current" on T1 while it holds T2: B keeps T2 current, because assign_session only replaces a current task that is null or done. The deadlock still follows from the cross-inserted task_sessions rows. Lines verified: complete_group_assignment 91-128 (builders_left 100-102, ids 105, reviewers_left 116-118), validate_pair 764-767, Close 1552-1557, task.rs assign_session 562-604 (the query is at 572).

#### RA-029 · An exited session can never be relaunched: every launch op refuses 'exited', and the UI's Resume button for exited sessions always fails

`crates/relay-core/src/handlers/session.rs:945` · **high** · Bug · confirmed · effort S

**Problem.** Resume: `if row.session.state != SessionState::Restorable { ... "only restorable sessions resume" }` (945-953). Wake accepts only Parked (1001), ClearRestorable only Restorable (961), and Spawn only Created; for any other non-live state Spawn replies "use session.resume or session.wake" (924-931). Nothing moves `exited` to `restorable`: recovery converts only live states (recovery.rs:80-98), and so does Engine::shutdown. The native UI maps `"restorable" | "exited"` to a Resume button that calls session.resume (apps/relay-native/src/shell.rs:687-689).

**Impact.** After any provider exit (crash, OOM, `/exit`, auth expiry) the session is permanently stuck. Resume fails with session.state every time, and Spawn's error points to two ops that also refuse. The only way out is closing the session, which loses its provider conversation, PAIR membership and place in the queue.

**Fix.** Accept Exited in Resume and ClearRestorable, saving the dead PTY's scrollback first, or have the exit callback mark the row restorable. Correct Spawn's message.

**Verifier note.** Any provider exit (/exit, crash, auth expiry) leaves the session with no way to relaunch it in place; closing loses its provider_ref conversation and its PAIR link. Fix: accept Exited in Resume and ClearRestorable, saving the dead PTY's scrollback first (finish_launch already kills and replaces the old Pty through set_pty), and correct Spawn's error message. Also add Exited -> session.resume in task.rs's launch_op mapping.

**Skeptic note.** 1. Scrollback detail. While the engine runs, an exited session has no fresh session_scrollback row: the exit callback saves none. Only Engine::shutdown saves scrollback for every PTY, dead ones included (mark_restorable inserts scrollback for all of them and changes state only for live ones). So a Resume that relies on plan_launch's load_scrollback would open blank or with stale history. Take initial_scrollback from the dead Pty still in the registry (`engine.pty(sid)` then `.scrollback(None)`) in the unlocked phase, or save it before planning.

2. Prefer accepting Exited in Resume and ClearRestorable over the alternative of having the exit callback write `restorable`. Rows with that state:
   - feed the launch-time session.restorable list, where a NULL restore_reason is reported as "app_restart" (session.rs:1496), so the pane would say "Relay was closed";
   - lose the "exited with code N" display (session_context.rs:196-199).

3. Also map Exited to session.resume in task.rs:693-696, and fix Spawn's message at 927.

4. Offering "Clear context" for exited sessions also needs native changes at shell.rs:726 and agent_menu.rs:573. Per CLAUDE.md those cannot be compiled in CI or an agent session, and the PR must say so.

5. Impact wording. Closing does not destroy the conversation: the provider's transcript stays on disk. What is lost is Relay's provider_ref handle and in-place resume, plus:
   - the session name;
   - the PAIR link;
   - its claims;
   - its saved scrollback;
   - its task queue.
   The worktree and branch are kept, because Discard uses remove_worktree:false.

**Blind re-check note.** Two corrections to the impact. Closing the session from the UI keeps the worktree and branch (remove_worktree=false), and the worktree can be reattached with session.create worktree=<path>. What is actually lost is the provider conversation handle, the session identity and PAIR membership, and the task link. A builder's task has already been set to 'failed' by the exit callback (session.rs:662). There is a further angle the claim misses: task.dispatch (task.rs:693-705) also refuses an exited session, so the fix should extend its launch_op mapping to Exited as well.

#### RA-030 · Agent-reported provider_ref goes unvalidated into the provider CLI's argv on resume, letting an agent inject CLI flags

`crates/relay-core/src/handlers/session.rs:1358` · **high** · Security · confirmed · effort S

**Problem.** `let provider_ref = data.get("session_id").or_else(|| data.get("provider_ref")).and_then(Value::as_str);` is stored by `UPDATE sessions SET ... provider_ref=COALESCE(?2, provider_ref)` (1371-1373). There is no format check. `session.report` is AgentOnly with `data: Option<Value>` (relay-bus ops/session.rs:149-151). It is in the default builder, reviewer and docs allowlists (handlers/settings.rs:36-38) and only needs the caller's own session (`assert_own`, 1351). Agents also get it as the `session_report` MCP tool. On resume or wake the stored string becomes an argv element: Claude gets `args.extend(["--resume".into(), reference.to_string()])` (providers.rs:185), and Codex gets `args.push(reference.to_string())` as the trailing positional after `--config developer_instructions=…` (providers.rs:229). The PTY spawn uses no shell, so a value starting with `--` is parsed by the provider CLI as an option. Resume and wake happen in normal use: `session.resume` and `session.wake` (session.rs:944, 1000), and `task.dispatch` starts `session.wake`/`session.resume` on its own for a parked or restorable session (task.rs:695-696).

**Impact.** A prompt-injected agent calls `session.report {kind:"session_start", data:{provider_ref:"--config=sandbox_mode=\"danger-full-access\""}}`. Relay already passes `--config` to `codex resume`, so clap accepts the `--config=` form. Other values work too, such as `--dangerously-skip-permissions`, or Claude's `--settings=/tmp/x.json` pointing at a file with `{"disableAllHooks":true}` (/tmp is always an allowed write root, guardrail.rs:617). The next resume, wake or dispatch then starts the provider without Codex's workspace-write sandbox (which D135 relies on), or without Relay's PreToolUse guardrail and Claude's permission prompts. A confused-deputy variant sets another session's id, so the resume opens that session's conversation.

**Fix.** Validate provider_ref when it is written. Provider session ids are UUID-like, so accept only `[0-9A-Za-z-]` with no leading `-`, and refuse anything else in session.report. Pass the value in a form that cannot be read as an option (`--resume=<id>`; put `--` before Codex's positional). Prefer taking provider_ref only from the provider-hook payload shape (claude-report/codex-report), not from arbitrary `data.provider_ref`.

**Verifier note.** Severity is high rather than critical. It needs an already compromised agent and waits for a park/wake or resume, and the system already accepts that same-uid agents have other imperfect escape routes (BUS.md §14; guardrail.rs:849). Still, this is a clean argv injection through a typed op, and it defeats the provider sandbox and Relay's hooks for that session, so it should be fixed. I could not run the provider CLIs to confirm how each flag is parsed; that relies on commander's and clap's documented behaviour. Fix as proposed: reject provider_ref values that are not `[0-9A-Za-z_-]` or that start with '-' in session.report, emit `--resume=<id>` for Claude, and put `--` before Codex's positional.

**Skeptic note.** Severity: high, not critical. Trigger: there is no automatic idle parking, because parking.idle_minutes is never read by the engine. Resume happens after an app restart (Resume or task.dispatch) or after a manual Park and Wake. Exploitation is harder than described: every later Claude PostToolUse/Stop hook report (and probably Codex's) overwrites provider_ref with the real session_id. A planted value only lasts if it is written after the last hook or if the session is killed before the next one. The impact is mostly the Codex sandbox, since Relay already leaves the Claude settings/hook file in the worktree unprotected and documents guardrails as seatbelts (BUS.md §0.6).

Fix corrections:
(1) Validate in two places. Reject in session.report anything empty, overlong, starting with '-', or outside a conservative id charset. Also check again at launch, in prepare_launch or Driver::args, because rows written before the fix may already hold a bad value. When the value is bad, fall back to --continue / --last, or refuse.
(2) For Claude, emit `--resume=<id>`.
(3) For Codex, putting `--` before the positional inside Driver::args, as proposed, would break every Codex resume. prepare_launch appends `--config` notify, plugin MCP `--config`s and `--add-dir` after Driver::args returns (session.rs:541-558), and after a `--` clap would read those as extra positionals. The `--` and the id must come last, after all options, or rely on strict validation alone.
(4) Taking provider_ref only from the hook payload shape does not help. At the bus, hook calls and agent calls look the same: same session token, the hook forwards stdin JSON unchanged, and the MCP server forwards any arguments.
(5) Update the argv tests in providers.rs:402-410.

**Blind re-check note.** Corrections to the fix:
1. For Codex, putting `--` before the positional as proposed would break the launch. In handlers/session.rs (~541-558), spawn appends `--config <notify>`, the plugin MCP `--config` pairs and `--add-dir <root>` after the args from the driver. After a `--` those would be read as positionals. Either move provider_ref to the very end behind `--`, or rely on validation alone.
2. "Take provider_ref only from the provider-hook payload shape" does not help. The provider hooks and the agent's MCP tool call the same session.report op, and an agent can just send data.session_id. Only validating the value closes the hole.
3. Impact nuance: an injected flag replaces the id, so both CLIs most likely show the session picker instead of resuming silently.
4. On the Claude side, Relay's PreToolUse guardrail survives `--dangerously-skip-permissions`, because the hook lives in .claude/settings.local.json. Only a `--settings` file with disableAllHooks would remove it.
The Codex sandbox bypass is the strongest angle.

#### RA-031 · Closing one session on a shared checkout deletes the hook directory that the checkout's core.hooksPath still points at, silently disabling the commit guardrail for the remaining sessions

`crates/relay-core/src/handlers/session.rs:1596` · **high** · Security · confirmed · effort M

**Problem.** Close computes `let teardown = if others == 0 { Some(read_teardown(..)) } else { None };` (1559) but then unconditionally runs `crate::hooks::remove_hook_dir(&repo, &s.name);` (1596). install_git points the worktree's `core.hooksPath` at `.relay/hooks/<name>` of whichever session was created or launched last (hooks.rs:93-157). The doc on remove_hook_dir claims a still-wired dir "is left alone by uninstall_git before this runs" (hooks.rs:283-284), but with others>0 uninstall never runs. Verified in a scratch repo: after the hooksPath directory disappears, `git commit` runs no pre-commit hook, and `git rev-parse --git-path hooks` still returns the dead dir. install_git's fallback (hooks.rs:96) then records that dead dir as the 'previous' hook on the next launch, so the user's original hook drops out of the chain.

**Impact.** Trigger: two sessions share a checkout (a review group, or any sessions on the primary checkout, which is the default for every session when the Unreal plugin is on, D160), and the user closes the most recently launched one. The UI passes remove_worktree:false for this. From then on, raw `git commit` from the surviving agents skips Relay's commit gate (protected paths and file/line caps, guardrail.rs:757-808) and the user's own pre-commit hook, with no warning. Related paths: a refused non-PAIR create on a shared checkout (900-910) runs uninstall_git for the new name, which restores the pre-Relay hooksPath underneath the other live sessions. A refused PAIR create skips cleanup (`p.pair_with.is_none()`), leaving hooksPath on a dir for a name that never got a row; the startup sweep (recovery.rs:136-138) then deletes that dir, with the same result.

**Fix.** Track hook ownership per worktree, not per session. Remove or uninstall only when no other non-closed session uses the worktree; otherwise first re-point core.hooksPath at a surviving session's directory (install_git for a live member), then delete. Apply the same rule to the refused-create cleanup.

**Verifier note.** An agent can already skip a pre-commit hook with `git commit --no-verify`; nothing in the guardrails denies it (no match for `no-verify` in crates). So this bug silently disables the gate for cooperative agents and for the user's own hook, rather than opening a new escape. High is still right under 'a safety check that can be silently bypassed'. Fix: in Close prepare, when others>0, first re-point core.hooksPath at a surviving session's dir (install_git for that live name, under hooks::writes()) or skip remove_hook_dir while the dir is the active hooksPath, and only delete it after that. Apply the same ownership check to the refused-create cleanup.

**Skeptic note.** 1. Line references. The fallback that adopts the dead dir as "previous" is hooks.rs:98 (`or_else(rev-parse --git-path hooks)`), not :96. The hooksPath write is hooks.rs:150-154.

2. A second concrete consequence. If a checkout's sessions are closed newest-first, the final teardown cannot read the dead dir's PREVIOUS file. It then unsets the worktree hooksPath (hooks.rs:256-276) instead of restoring a user-set worktree-level core.hooksPath. Reversing the close loop in sessions.rs:1365-1367 would fail its `assert_eq!(hooks(&f.repo), "user-hooks")`.

3. A git.commit during the window repairs the gate but not the chain. Its refresh_git (git.rs:548) recreates the dir under the closed session's name, with a PREVIOUS file that points at itself.

4. Fix:
- In Close prepare, under hooks::writes(): when others>0 and the active worktree hooksPath is the closing session's dir, call install_git for one surviving session first, then remove the dir. install_git still reads the intact PREVIOUS file, so the user's chain survives. Do the same in DiscardRestorable (session.rs:1505-1541).
- Skipping the delete alone is not enough. The startup sweep (recovery.rs:123-142) removes every dir whose name has no non-closed row, and DiscardRestorable already leaves such an active dir behind.
- For a refused create (session.rs:900-910), PAIR creates included, re-point to a live session instead of calling uninstall_git. That cleanup currently runs git subprocesses inside the transaction with the store held, so move it to the unlocked side.
- Harden install_git: a configured Relay dir with no PREVIOUS file should not fall back to `rev-parse --git-path hooks`, which returns that same dead dir.
- Add the newest-first close order to the existing test.

**Blind re-check note.** The claim is accurate. Two additions: the startup sweep (sweep_hook_dirs) deletes the dir as well, so the fix must re-point hooksPath rather than only skip remove_hook_dir; and the surviving session's next bus git.commit (refresh_git) re-creates the closed session's dir, restoring the gate for bus commits, while raw commits stay ungated until a survivor relaunches.

<a id="ra-032"></a>

#### RA-032 · task.dispatch runs session.create/spawn's unlocked phases (git fetch, worktree add, PTY start) inside its own transaction, under the store mutex

`crates/relay-core/src/handlers/task.rs:683` · **high** · Invariant · confirmed · effort L

**Problem.** Dispatch is registered with plain `e.register::<Dispatch>`, yet dispatch_task calls `ctx.invoke_registered("session.create", ...)` (683) and `ctx.invoke_registered(op, json!({"session":name}))` for session.spawn/wake/resume (712). Engine::invoke_registered (engine.rs:325-351) runs a staged op's `prepare` with `held: Some(self.tx)`, which keeps the lock and the open transaction. Its comment claims this happens 'only on this path' (guardrail.confirm). session.create's prepare says 'Fetch, checkout... None of it belongs under the global store mutex' (session.rs:854-856). That prepare runs `git fetch --all` (git.rs:938-945, 20 s timeout) and `git worktree add` (worktree.rs:214, 120 s timeout). spawn's prepare runs git config subprocesses (hooks.rs:75) and copies skills. finish_launch then starts the PTY inside the transaction (session.rs:646). Fanout repeats all of this for every descendant (1068-1075).

**Impact.** `task.dispatch {create}` (a documented API that fanout requires) holds the global store mutex for a network fetch plus a full checkout. That can last up to about 140 s per session, multiplied by the number of fanned children. During that time every other request blocks, including every agent's guardrail.gate hook and every UI read. The native task page's Dispatch button to a Created, Parked or Restorable session also runs spawn/wake/resume's git subprocesses and file writes under the lock. The external side effects are outside the transaction. If a later step fails (for example child k's create in a fanout), the session rows roll back, but the earlier worktrees, hooks and running agent PTYs remain. Those PTYs stay in Engine::ptys with no matching row.

**Fix.** Split task.dispatch so the slow work happens outside the transaction. Options: register it as staged and create the sessions in the unlocked phase, or require existing sessions (as launch.rs already does) and start them after commit through separate session.spawn requests. Only the task and assignment writes should stay in the transaction. Correct the invoke_registered comment.

**Verifier note.** The native multi-agent launcher (launch.rs:805-810) avoids the problem by calling session.create separately and then dispatching with start:false. The main live triggers are therefore the phone door's dispatch-with-create and the native Dispatch button. Fix: make task.dispatch staged, doing the session create/launch in the unlocked phase, or have callers create and spawn the session as separate requests and keep only the task and assignment writes in the transaction.

**Skeptic note.** Corrections to the finding:
- The title lists "PTY start" as one of the unlocked phases. It is not. Pty::spawn runs in finish_launch, which holds the lock on every spawn by design (D149: "only the PTY start and the row update hold it"). What the nested path wrongly moves under the lock is the prepare work: the fetch, worktree add, install_git, the skill copy, and the adapter and brief writes.
- The live heavy trigger is the phone door: both the "New request" sheet and Board dispatch send create with start:true. Fanout has no UI caller anywhere. The native Dispatch button triggers only the lighter spawn, wake or resume prepare.
- History: session.create became staged in 6e7b044 (2026-09-09). The "only on this path" comment was written earlier, in fcbdbce (09-04). So the nested path quietly kept the old cost of running everything inside the transaction.

Caveats on the fix:
1. Do not move the spawn into a staged task.dispatch prepare. plan_launch builds the brief from the store (awareness::brief), and the brief has to see the assignment, which is written inside the transaction. Launch through a separate top-level session.spawn, wake or resume after commit, as launch.rs does. Ideally the engine runs that launch before it replies, so the phone's immediate Terminal attach does not race into session.not_spawned.
2. Keep the provider.not_installed refusal (board.rs:45) by checking providers::executable in the prepare.
3. Define what happens to checkouts already created in the prepare when a later step fails, especially for fanout's N checkouts.
4. Update D149 and the invoke_registered comment. Add a debug_assert in invoke_registered so that only the guardrail.confirm replay may run a staged prepare nested. Other nested callers exist at lower cost: project.remove{force} and workspace.remove call session.close, whose prepare runs the hook-teardown git subprocesses (workspace.rs:173 and 328).

Separate issue noticed while checking, with a different root cause: project.clone (workspace.rs:228-238) is a plain `register` handler. It runs `git clone` with `Command::output()`, which bypasses output_with_timeout and has no time limit, while holding the store mutex. The native client allows it 1800 s (client.rs:67).

**Blind re-check note.** The path that fetches and checks out under the lock is the phone's DispatchSheet and any `create` payload. The native Dispatch button sends `session`, so it hits only the spawn, wake or resume prepare (hook, skill and brief writes), not git fetch or worktree add. The fetch runs only when the requested branch does not already exist (`refresh_new_worktree`), and git.rs:969-974 is where that is decided. The orphaned PTY and worktree after a failure in a later fanout child is a consequence of reading the code; I did not exercise it.

#### RA-033 · task.approve fails hard once the assigned session's branch is gone, which automatic branch cleanup causes after a merged session is closed

`crates/relay-core/src/handlers/task.rs:1113` · **high** · Bug · confirmed · effort S

**Problem.** With no sha, Approve resolves `repo.rev_parse_single(format!("refs/heads/{}", session.session.branch))` and returns `BusError::unavailable("git.head", ...)` when it fails. Its comment (1105-1108) says 'session.close deliberately keeps its branch'. That is no longer true: session.close calls `crate::branch_cleanup::after_close(engine, project_id, branch)` (session.rs:1630-1635), and branch_cleanup deletes a closed session's `relay/<name>` branch once its work is merged (branch_cleanup.rs:1-22). The sha that session.done already linked (task_commits, session.rs:97-99) is ignored. Sessions in a detached primary checkout record branch 'HEAD' (worktree.rs:122), which never resolves as refs/heads/HEAD. Neither native caller can pass a sha: board_view.rs:841 `self.act("task.approve", json!({"task_id":task["id"]}))` and task_pages.rs:625.

**Impact.** Normal flow: the agent finishes, the user merges its PR, closes the session, and the cleanup thread deletes the branch. From then on, dragging the card to Done or clicking 'Approve task' fails with unavailable/git.head, and the app gives no way to supply a sha, so the task cannot be approved from the UI. Tests never hit this because Instance::Test skips cleanup.

**Fix.** When the recorded branch does not resolve, fall back to the newest task_commits row for the task, then to the project HEAD. Fail only when nothing is known. Remove the stale comment.

**Verifier note.** Severity stays high: a core flow (approving a finished, merged task) fails, and the user has no workaround. Fix as proposed: if refs/heads/<branch> does not resolve, fall back to the newest task_commits sha for the task, then to the project HEAD (or the base branch tip), and fail only when none exist. Update the stale comment at 1105-1108.

**Skeptic note.** "The user has no workaround" overstates it. The GUI has none, but `relay cmd task.approve '{"task_id":N,"sha":"<sha>"}'` works through the CLI's generic Cmd (relay-cli main.rs:36/388), and so does re-creating the branch by hand.

The trigger is wider than "a merged session": a closed session whose branch has no commits of its own is also judged "merged into main" and deleted. The periodic sweeper also reaches sessions closed by discard_restorable and sessions closed before the upgrade.

The detached-HEAD case ('HEAD' from worktree.rs:122) is a separate, rare, pre-existing cause with the same symptom. It only affects sessions in the primary checkout. The same fix covers it.

Fix order: recorded branch, then the newest task_commits sha for the task (the session.done commit), then the tip of the project's base branch (which contains the merged work) or HEAD. Fail only when the repo itself cannot be read.

Same root cause, also to update:
- the stale comment at task.rs:1105-1106;
- BUS.md:733 ("branch is kept");
- the GUI texts that promise the branch is kept: agent_menu.rs:590 and 609, and shell.rs:724 ("its worktree and branch are kept"). Cleanup can now delete both the branch and a clean pooled worktree.

Two follow-ups:
- Add a test that runs branch_cleanup::run before approving.
- Optionally, record the deleted tip in the cleanup's audit summary. It currently records branch, outcome, reason and pr, but not the sha.

**Blind re-check note.** The handler starts at task.rs:1086; the rev_parse_single and error mapping are at 1112-1114. The "HEAD" angle is a separate, rarer path. A session in a detached primary checkout records the branch "HEAD" (worktree.rs:121-122 head_of), and refs/heads/HEAD never resolves, so approval fails there even without any cleanup. Branch cleanup excludes branches equal to the project's base_branch, but not "HEAD".

#### RA-034 · project.clone runs `git clone` synchronously inside a locked handler with no timeout

`crates/relay-core/src/handlers/workspace.rs:234` · **high** · Invariant · confirmed · effort M

**Problem.** `e.register::<ProjectClone>` runs `Command::new("git").current_dir(&workspace.path).arg("clone").arg("--").arg(&p.url).arg(&destination).output()` inside the request transaction with the store mutex held. It does not go through proc::output_with_timeout, sets no GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0 and does not null stdin. The registry describes the op as "(async; project.changed when done)" (relay-bus ops/workspace.rs:37-38), and the native client allows it 1800 s (client.rs:65-67). By contrast git.rs fetch_remote (L937-952) uses a timeout, a null stdin and runs outside the transaction.

**Impact.** Every clone freezes the whole bus (UI queries, agent MCP calls, every lock-taking op) for its full duration: seconds to tens of minutes for large or LFS-heavy repositories. A clone that waits on a credential prompt or helper blocks it indefinitely.

**Fix.** Make it register_staged: clone in the prepare phase via proc::output_with_timeout with GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0 and stdin null, then run project.add in the short finish phase. Alternatively run it as a background job that emits project.changed, as the op description already claims.

**Verifier note.** One claim is wrong: Rust's `Command::output()` already defaults stdin to null, so "does not null stdin" is not accurate. The hang risk comes instead from the missing GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0 and the missing deadline. git prompts on /dev/tty when the engine has a controlling terminal, and it may run a GUI askpass or credential helper that waits for input. session.input does not touch SQLite (D148), so raw keystrokes may still flow, but everything else that takes the lock freezes. Fix: register_staged. Clone in prepare via proc::output_with_timeout (long deadline) with GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0 (and GIT_ASKPASS unset or `true`). Then invoke project.add in the short finish phase and delete the destination on finish failure. Alternatively make it truly async, with a worker thread and a project.changed emit, as the op description already claims.

**Skeptic note.** 1. "does not null stdin" is wrong. Command::output() already defaults stdin to Stdio::null, and git reads credentials from /dev/tty, not stdin. The hang comes from prompts being left enabled plus the missing deadline.

2. "freezes the whole bus" needs two qualifications. PTY output and keystrokes keep flowing. Unlocked queries from other user connections (the CLI, the phone) still run. The desktop UI, however, is frozen even apart from the mutex, because it sends project.clone on its main connection, which the engine serves serially.

3. "blocks indefinitely" is conditional. It needs git to reach a prompt that waits: an engine with a controlling tty, or a GUI askpass or credential helper. A systemd-launched engine fails fast instead.

4. The fix is incomplete, in four ways.
   (i) register_staged alone does not unfreeze the UI. Either also route project.clone over a dedicated connection on the client (add it to is_lifecycle_request at client.rs:50-62, as session.create already is), or make the op truly async: return at once, clone on a worker via after_commit, emit project.changed, and write the project.clone.completed audit row that BUS.md §5.1 (:247) and the registry text at relay-bus ops/workspace.rs:38 already promise. Async also removes that docs drift.
   (ii) Prompt suppression: GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0 alone still lets askpass helpers and ssh prompt. Also set GIT_ASKPASS to an empty string (this skips core.askPass and SSH_ASKPASS) and use ssh -o BatchMode=yes when the user has no GIT_SSH_COMMAND. Add -c http.lowSpeedLimit/lowSpeedTime so a stalled transfer fails, and run it through proc::output_with_timeout with a long deadline; its process-group kill also reaps git-remote-https and git-lfs.
   (iii) Once the existence check moves outside the lock, it can race a concurrent clone, and the failure cleanup `fs::remove_dir_all(&destination)` could delete the other clone. Clone into a unique temp directory inside the workspace, rename it into place in the short finish phase, and only ever delete the temp directory.
   (iv) Sibling to fix in the same change: crates/relay-core/src/github.rs:105-110 (skill.install's `git clone --depth 1`) is also a raw .output() with no deadline and no prompt suppression. It is staged and unlocked, so it does not hold the mutex, but it can hang its request forever.

Related additions: apps/relay-native/src/app.rs:1111; apps/relay-native/src/client.rs:50; crates/relay-core/src/socket.rs:332; docs/engine/BUS.md:247; crates/relay-core/src/github.rs:105.

**Blind re-check note.** The handler is registered at line 228. The decisive Command call is at line 234. An endless hang needs a credential helper or askpass that blocks. A plain git terminal prompt probably fails at once when the engine has no controlling TTY. Even so, every clone freezes the bus for as long as it takes.

#### RA-035 · project.remove / workspace.remove always fail with FOREIGN KEY error once a project has a task label, after already SIGKILLing the project's agents

`crates/relay-core/src/handlers/workspace.rs:380` · **high** · Bug · confirmed · effort S

**Problem.** The delete list at workspace.rs:354-374 covers message_recipients … plugin_projects but never `labels`. Migration v16 defines `labels(... project_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES projects(id) ...)` with no ON DELETE CASCADE (store.rs:315-319), foreign_keys=ON (store.rs:397), and nothing in the crate ever deletes a label row (`label_id()` task.rs:124-142 only inserts; no `DELETE FROM labels` anywhere). So `DELETE FROM projects WHERE id = ?1` (workspace.rs:380) raises `FOREIGN KEY constraint failed`. I reproduced this by building the v20 schema from MIGRATIONS and replaying the handler's exact DELETE list against a project with one label. Before that statement runs, with `force` (the native dialog always sets `payload["force"] = json!(true)`, shell/registry.rs:626), the handler invokes `session.close {remove_worktree:false}` for every open session (workspace.rs:327-329). Close's prepare phase runs the hook teardown on the filesystem (core.hooksPath restored, adapters removed, hook dir deleted), and its finish phase calls `take_pty` and leaves the kill in `after_commit` (session.rs:1602-1607). When the request fails, the transaction rolls back and the after_commit closures are dropped. Each closure held the last `Arc<Pty>`: socket attach streams hold only a broadcast receiver, and reader and waiter threads hold `Arc<Shared>`. So `Drop for Pty` SIGKILLs the agent's process group (pty.rs:381-390), and the un-silenced exit callback then marks the session `exited` and its builder task `failed`.

**Impact.** Trigger: tag any task (task.label.add, or the board's labels field on create), then later remove the project, or the workspace that contains it. Consequence: removal always fails with an internal FOREIGN KEY error, and the project can never be removed. Each attempt also SIGKILLs every running agent of that project. Those sessions end `exited`, not `restorable`, so the conversations are lost. Their Relay commit hooks are uninstalled and their builder tasks are marked failed, while the project stays.

**Fix.** Add `"DELETE FROM labels WHERE project_id=?1"` after the task deletes (task_labels cascades), and add a project.remove regression test that uses a labelled task. Also stop nested session.close from detaching PTYs before commit: move `take_pty` into the after_commit closure, so a rolled-back request leaves the PTY registered.

**Verifier note.** Fix: add `DELETE FROM labels WHERE project_id=?1` after the tasks delete (task_labels cascades), and add a regression test that removes a project with a labelled task. Separately, keep a nested close from detaching the PTY before commit: call take_pty inside the after_commit closure, or restore it on rollback. The hook teardown done in prepare also cannot be rolled back.

One caveat on impact: the claim that the conversations are "lost" depends on the provider. Many CLIs keep their own transcripts on disk. What is lost for certain is Relay's restorable state.

**Skeptic note.** Impact: drop the claim "conversations are lost" as harm caused by the bug. The dialog (registry.rs:554) tells the user the agents "will be stopped and closed", and a successful close would also leave them non-resumable. The real harm is twofold.
1. The project, and any workspace containing it, can permanently never be removed in the app. No op deletes a `labels` row, and removing the label from every task does not help (verified).
2. Each failed forced attempt leaves an inconsistent state. Agents are SIGKILLed with no grace period, and their git, Claude and Codex guardrail hooks are uninstalled. Sessions end `exited` instead of `closed`, and active builder tasks become `failed`. Live device runs are stopped in memory (device.rs:265-270). Meanwhile the bus reports failure and the project stays.

Fix: adding `DELETE FROM labels WHERE project_id=?1` anywhere before the projects delete is correct (task_labels cascades on both of its foreign keys). It is also complete: `labels` is the only gap in the foreign-key graph. Add regression tests for project.remove and workspace.remove with a labelled task, including a forced removal with a live session.

The proposed take_pty change is incomplete and unsafe alone. The nested close's prepare phase has already run `run_teardown` (session.rs:1575: pre-commit hook plus the PreToolUse `guardrail.gate` adapters) and `remove_hook_dir` (session.rs:1596). Keeping the PTY alive after a rollback would therefore leave an agent running without its guardrails. A real atomicity fix must, when the op runs nested (`held` is Some), also defer that teardown, and `device.run.stop`'s in-memory stop, into after_commit along with the kill.

**Blind re-check note.** The PTY Drop is at pty.rs:400-409, not 381-390 (381-390 is inside Pty::kill). The exit callback is at session.rs:646-662. The proposed secondary fix (deferring take_pty) does not undo the filesystem hook teardown that session.close's prepare phase performs inline. On a rolled-back project.remove the agents' hooks stay uninstalled even with that change. The labels DELETE is the fix that matters; also test that project.remove succeeds after a label was added and then removed from every task.

**Also at:** `crates/relay-core/src/store.rs:315`, `crates/relay-core/src/handlers/workspace.rs:327`, `crates/relay-core/src/handlers/workspace.rs:380`, `crates/relay-core/src/handlers/workspace.rs:173`, `crates/relay-core/src/handlers/session.rs:1602`, `crates/relay-core/src/pty.rs:381`, `apps/relay-native/src/shell/registry.rs:626`, `crates/relay-core/src/handlers/task.rs:124`, `crates/relay-core/src/handlers/task.rs:137`, `crates/relay-core/src/handlers/task.rs:136`, `crates/relay-core/src/handlers/workspace.rs:172`, `apps/relay-native/src/shell/registry.rs:624`, `crates/relay-core/src/handlers/task.rs:1219`, `crates/relay-core/src/handlers/session.rs:1573`, `crates/relay-core/tests/registry_remove.rs:52`, `crates/relay-core/tests/bus.rs:958`

#### RA-036 · Each refresh closes an open card menu or peek picker and resets the peek's scroll and focus

`apps/relay-native/src/board_view.rs:1247` · **high** · Bug · confirmed · effort M

**Problem.** render() always ends with `self.render_peek();` (1247). That does `clear(&self.peek);` (2289) and appends a brand-new `crate::app::scrolled(&body)` (2457-2459) whose adjustment is never pushed to `self.scrolls`, so its position is never restored. The card context menu is parented to the card (`pop.set_parent(anchor);`, 2095), and render() destroys every card (`clear(&self.content)`, 1188). The peek's Status/Priority/Type/Size pickers are MenuButtons inside the cleared peek (2350-2381), and the strip is cleared too (1281). Focus is restored only when it was inside `self.content` (1182-1186). The peek close button and the peek task links rebuild the peek under the focused widget and never restore focus (2318-2323, 2477-2482). show() renders even when no task changed (502-503), and app.rs:1264 refreshes the page on every unclassified event.

**Impact.** While agents work, any event for the project (an agent's task.update, notify.new, mailbox.new, guardrail.held...) has these effects: a right-click menu or a peek picker vanishes under the pointer; a long description being read in the peek jumps back to the top; text selected in the peek is dropped; and keyboard focus on a strip chip or a peek control is lost.

**Fix.** Skip render when the task list is unchanged (compare ids and updated_at). In render_peek, rebuild only when the peeked task's updated_at has changed; otherwise keep the panel, or keep the scroller and save/restore its vadjustment. Defer re-render while a card menu or a peek picker popover is open, and re-render on its `closed` signal. Restore focus (focus_board) after the peek close and task-link handlers.

**Verifier note.** The most frequent trigger is usage.changed (provider.rs:83), which falls through to refresh_page in app.rs even though the board shows nothing from it; device.changed and run.changed fall through the same way. The cheapest first fix is in app.rs: route usage.changed, device.changed and run.changed away from refresh_page, as is already done for settings.changed. Then skip Board::render when the task list's ids and updated_at values are unchanged, and rebuild the peek only when the peeked task changed. Defer a re-render while a card menu or picker popover is open. The auditor's line numbers are close: render_peek starts at 2288 and the pickers are at about 2330-2370. Note that apps/relay-native cannot be compiled in this environment.

**Skeptic note.** Trigger: replace usage.changed with session.changed from any project, which goes through apply_session_event (agent_menu.rs:133-135) because the project filter at app.rs:1213-1216 exempts session.* events. Add the notify.changed / notify.new / mailbox.new events emitted at each agent turn end in the current project (session.rs:1415-1423, 261-299), and task.changed from agents. These fall to app.rs:1264. usage.report is not called by any hook: the statusLine script only writes relay-usage.json (hooks.rs:576-577). The audit.rs:16 and D151 comments saying it is called on every window refresh are stale.

Lines: render starts at 1181, not 1180. The auditor's picker lines (2350-2381) are right; the verifier's "about 2330-2370" is not.

Fix:
1. Skip render when the whole decorated task list (Vec<Value>) is equal to the last one, not just ids and updated_at, because derived fields (sessions, commits, labels, rollup, relations, _module_name) change without bumping updated_at.
2. Build a key for the peek from the peeked task and the tasks it links to (parent, sub-tasks, blocked-by/blocks), and rebuild the peek only when that key changes. Otherwise keep the scroller, or save and restore its vadjustment the way the lanes do (1222-1234).
3. Defer the render while a board popover is open, and run it on the popover's `closed` signal.
4. Call focus_board after the peek close button and the task-link handlers.
5. Routing: limiting the board refresh in apply_session_event to the current project's sessions is a bigger win than moving usage/device/run.changed out of the fallback refresh, since session.changed is the busiest trigger. Keep the refresh for the current project, because task assignment reaches the board only through session.changed.

apps/relay-native cannot be compiled here, so this is verified by reading the code only.

**Blind re-check note.** The proposed fix, skipping the render when task ids and updated_at match, is too narrow. task.list rows carry derived fields such as state, sessions and _module_name, and these can change without updated_at changing, so that check could hide real updates. Compare the whole new Vec<Value> with the stored one, which is cheap, before rendering. Apply the same test in render_peek to the peeked task's Value. Separately, app.rs should not refresh the board for events that cannot change it, such as usage.changed, notify.* and mailbox.*. usage.changed is the most frequent of these, so it matters more than the task.update example the audit gives. The other parts of the fix are sound: defer the render while a card menu or picker popover is open and re-render on `closed`, save and restore the peek's vadjustment when it must be rebuilt, and call focus_board after the peek close and task-link handlers. The cited lines are accurate to within a line or two (render_peek starts at 2288).

#### RA-037 · Any single response line over 2 MiB tears down the whole UI control connection (git.diff.file of a large or binary file; notes.list of a large notes corpus)

`apps/relay-native/src/client.rs:200` · **high** · Bug · confirmed · effort M

**Problem.** The reader does `if line.len() + n > max_line { return Err(Error::Protocol(format!("frame exceeds {} MiB", …))) }` (client.rs:200-205), which ends the reader task. `outcome.unwrap_err()` then fails every pending request and sends Notice::Disconnected (259-265). app.rs:1267-1275 drops the client, shows "Engine disconnected" and requires Reconnect, and reconnecting stops and recreates every terminal pane (app.rs:1139-1144). MAX_LINE is 2 MiB (client.rs:48). Two engine responses exceed it in normal use. (1) git.diff.file returns `old`, `new` and the full unified diff in one response with no cap (git.rs:235-254), reading whole files and lossy-decoding binaries (git.rs:802-848). The Git panel requests it for any changed non-image file (code_git.rs:896-898 → 1338) and only checks `old.len() + new.len() > 1048576` after the response has arrived (code_git.rs:1350). A lossy-decoded random binary grows ×2.37 when JSON-escaped (measured in the scratchpad), so a substantially changed ~250 KB .uasset/.fbx/.wav (about four copies: old, new and both sides of the diff) or a ~1 MB text file (lockfile, generated code) exceeds 2 MiB. (2) notes.list returns every note with its full body and no limit (notes.rs:339-349), and agent-callable notes.append grows notes without a cap. The client calls notes.list on every Ui::refresh (app.rs:1440 → notes_window.rs:208), including the first refresh after each connect.

**Impact.** Clicking a large changed file in the Git panel disconnects the whole UI. In-flight requests such as a save fail with "Invalid engine response: frame exceeds 2 MiB" even though the engine may have applied them. Reconnecting re-attaches every terminal, and reopening the diff repeats the failure. Once a project's notes exceed about 2 MiB, every connect is followed by a notes.list that kills it again, so the client can no longer stay connected.

**Fix.** Make an oversized line a per-request failure. Skip to the next newline without buffering, take the id from the `{"v":1,"id":"…"` prefix, fail only that pending request with a typed too-large error, and keep the connection open; add a test for this path. Also cap on the engine side: git.diff.file should refuse or truncate above the editor's 1 MiB limit and skip binaries, and notes.list should return summaries with bodies fetched through notes.get.

**Verifier note.** The notes.list trigger needs about 2 MiB of note bodies in one project, which is unusual. The git.diff.file trigger is the one that matters. Fix both sides. On the client, fail only the oversized request: skip to the next newline and recover the id from the prefix. On the engine, give git.diff.file a size limit and binary detection that refuses before building the response.

**Skeptic note.** Thresholds, using measured factors: lossy-decoded and escaped binary grows 2.35-2.5x for mesh-like data and up to 4.5x for zero-heavy Blueprint data. Text grows about 1.1x. The line exceeds 2 MiB for:
- an untracked or LFS-modified binary of about 230-450 KB;
- a fully changed non-LFS binary of about 120-210 KB;
- a small edit to a text file of about 1 MB or more, or a full rewrite of about 500 KB or more.

The "in-flight save" example is weak, because open_diff refuses when the editor is dirty (code_git.rs:1320). The real collateral damage is lost event delivery (guardrail.held prompts included) until a manual Reconnect, plus any unrelated concurrent request.

The notes trigger is rarer (about 2 MiB of note text in one project), but it is worse than stated. notes.changed events carry the full note body (notes.rs:63-66). The notes window exists from startup (notes_window.rs:153-166), so notes.list runs after every connect. One oversized note therefore kills every subscribed client on each save, and keeps killing it on every reconnect.

Additional related locations: crates/relay-core/src/handlers/notes.rs:65 (event payload) and crates/relay-core/src/socket.rs:744 (unbounded writer).

Fix refinements:
1. Client: also skip oversized Event lines and trigger a refresh instead of disconnecting.
2. Engine: in git.diff.file, check the blob or file size before reading. Detect binaries and LFS pointers, reusing git.diff's `binary` heuristic at git.rs:224. Return a typed BusError rather than changing DiffFileOut, which lives in schema/bus.v1.json.
3. Optionally, have socket.rs replace any response over the wire limit with a typed bus error, which fixes every op at once.
4. If notes.list moves to summaries, the native notes page must fetch bodies through notes.get.

**Blind re-check note.** The size check is at client.rs:200-205, inside the loop that starts around line 196. The Reconnect teardown is at app.rs:1137-1142, reached from the button at app.rs:970-973. The notes.list angle needs an unusually large notes corpus (over 2 MiB) and is a secondary, less likely trigger. The main real-world trigger is git.diff.file on a changed binary file or a file over about 1 MiB. One extra point for the fix: git.diff.file already has the information to flag binary content cheaply (old or new contains '\0', as git.diff checks), so the engine can refuse before it computes TextDiff on huge inputs.

#### RA-038 · The Git panel is destroyed and rebuilt on every file/git event, dropping focus, open popovers and view state

`apps/relay-native/src/code_git.rs:170` · **high** · Bug · confirmed · effort L

**Problem.** refresh_git does `clear(&e.git);` (170) and then rebuilds everything: the header and the branch-picker MenuButton, a Paned with a recomputed `panes.set_position(...)` (250), and the commit form, re-parenting the persistent commit TextView through `detach(&message)` (297/311). It also rebuilds every section, the history (`graph_key.set_active(true)`, 552) and the merge-test check buttons. It is triggered from editor.rs invalidate(), which app.rs:1232-1240 calls for every file.changed/git.changed/worktree.changed/integration.* event in the project, debounced to 1 s. It runs without checking `self.git.is_visible()` and without looking at which worktree the event came from (invalidate takes no payload). Removing the focused TextView's ancestor makes GTK unset the window focus, and removing the MenuButton disposes its popover. The function is about 700 lines (clippy too_many_lines 696/100). Because nothing survives a refresh, state lives in widget names and CSS classes (`widget_name() != "commit-message"`, the `has-staged` class).

**Impact.** While an agent edits files in the project, someone typing a commit message loses keyboard focus on every refresh and the following keystrokes are dropped. The branch picker or commit-options popover closes under the pointer, the History split jumps back to its computed position, the Graph toggle turns back on, merge-test ticks clear and scroll positions reset, about once a second. All of this work (5 bus requests and hundreds of widgets) is also done while the panel is hidden.

**Fix.** Build the panel skeleton once and update its parts in place: labels, counts, and row lists keyed by path. That keeps focus, popovers and user state. Skip refresh_git while the panel is hidden and refresh when toggle_git or apply_layout shows it. Ignore file.changed events whose payload worktree is not the shown checkout. Split refresh_git into per-section builders.

**Verifier note.** The refresh is not once a second without pause. It happens at most once per second, and only while project events keep arriving, which is common with active agents (refs updates, git.changed, integration events). Agent file edits inside .relay/worktrees are filtered for the primary checkout's watcher. Fix as proposed: build once and update in place, or at minimum save and restore focus and popover state, and skip the work while the panel is hidden. Category bug (UX). The 700-line function is a secondary maintainability point.

**Skeptic note.** Corrections to the finding:
- The rebuild is not unconditional once a second. It happens at most once per second, and only while events arrive.
- "Events in the project" understates the trigger. Watcher file.changed events and system worktree.changed events carry no envelope project_id, so app.rs:1213 lets them through from every watched root in every project, for the life of the engine.

Gaps in the proposed fix:
1. The git.status fetched in refresh_git also feeds note_changes (code_git.rs:172 calls project_files.rs:549-586), which tints Explorer folders. Skipping refresh_git while the panel is hidden would leave those tints stale. Keep fetching status and calling note_changes, and skip only the rebuild and the other four requests. toggle_git and apply_layout take &self and get no ui, so they need some other way to start a refresh when the panel is shown.
2. Filtering file.changed by the payload's worktree needs care:
   - Compare canonical paths: watch.rs canonicalizes the root, while Editor.worktree is "" for the primary checkout.
   - Keep events from the primary root even when a linked worktree is shown. A commit there changes only the shared .git/refs under the primary root.
   - Also filter on payload project_id, or set the event's project with .in_project() in watch.rs.
3. A cheap first step removes most spurious rebuilds: skip the clear and rebuild when the fetched payloads match the last render. Otherwise, save and restore focus and cursor, the Paned position, the Graph state, the merge selections and the scroll positions. Or defer the rebuild while the commit field has focus or a popover is open.
4. Cache or throttle git.pr.list, and stop making git.log wait on it in the join. Then History will not blank on every refresh.

Related, worth checking as a separate finding: with live sessions, each rebuild probably leaks the merge-test widgets. The Test button's clicked closure owns the CheckButtons (719-727), and each CheckButton's toggled closure holds a strong clone of the Test button (698-714). This is a gtk-rs reference cycle that dispose never breaks.

**Blind re-check note.** The commit message text is not lost, because the same TextView is reused and only focus and keystrokes are dropped. The refresh rate is about once per second plus the time the five bus calls take, not exactly 1 Hz. When filtering events by worktree, keep refreshing on git.changed and integration.* from other worktrees, because they can change the shown checkout's branch and ahead/behind data. Only file.changed is safe to filter by worktree.

#### RA-039 · Signal closures hold strong refs into their own widget trees, so each Git refresh and sidebar rebuild leaks the old branch picker, merge-test rows and project/workspace menus

`apps/relay-native/src/code_git.rs:999` · **high** · Resource leak · confirmed · effort M

**Problem.** render_branch_picker builds a cycle between two widgets. 997 `let query = search.clone();` feeds 999 `create_key.connect_clicked(move |_| { ... reveal(form) ... query ... })`. 1195 `let create = create_key.clone();` feeds 1196 `search.connect_activate(move |_| { first(entries)... create.emit_clicked() })`. So search ↔ create_key reference each other, and `entries` keeps every branch row and key alive. The merge-test section has a second cycle: each `pick.connect_toggled` holds `test` (700-701), and `test.connect_clicked` owns `picks` (719). refresh_git runs `clear(&e.git)` (170) and builds a fresh picker (779) on every call. GTK only unparents removed children and never disposes an object whose refcount stays above zero, so the closures are never freed. The same mistake appears in shell/registry.rs:506: each menu key captures `popover.clone()`, and the MenuButton's dispose only unparents its popover. The sidebar is cleared and rebuilt (registry.rs:133-137) whenever its signature changes; the signature includes every session's state (127-132) and the filter text. Other sites: agent_menu.rs 451, 541, 578 and 608 (the popover is captured by its own keys and is only unparented on close, 371-374); agent_menu.rs:835 (revealer ↔ cancel); task_pages.rs:490-497 (`create` owns its ancestor `form` and the Rc<Panel>, whose guard holds more of the form).

**Impact.** refresh_git runs on every navigation to Agents (app.rs:1350-1351 → project_files.rs:63-67), after every save or git action, and up to once a second from Editor::invalidate while agents change files. Each run strands one search entry, the create form, one row per local and remote branch (about 8-10 widgets each; about 200+ widgets for this repo's 21 local branches), and one CheckButton group per live session. Each sidebar rebuild (every agent running↔idle↔blocked flip, every filter keystroke) strands one popover of about 15 widgets per workspace header and visible project row. Agent-settings and New-task panels leak once per open. Memory grows without bound for the life of the window (sizes estimated, not measured).

**Fix.** Capture weak references, as the same files already do elsewhere (code_git.rs:1021 `popover.downgrade()`, project_files.rs:135). Use `search.downgrade()` (or `create_key.downgrade()`) in one of the two handlers, `test.downgrade()` in the pick toggles, `popover.downgrade()` in registry_menu and agent_settings_body, `revealer.downgrade()` in confirm_strip, and `form.downgrade()` / `Rc::downgrade(&panel)` in the task composer. glib::clone!(#[weak] ...) makes this systematic.

**Verifier note.** The leak rate is driven by refresh_git running even while the Git panel is hidden (see #3) and by sidebar rebuilds on every session state flip. Growth is unbounded for the life of the window in normal multi-agent use. The widget counts are estimates. Fix as proposed (weak captures / glib::clone! #[weak]).

**Skeptic note.** Corrections to the details:
- **Widget counts.** A registry_menu strands about 22-26 widgets, not about 15. That is the popover, its body, 2 labels, 2 separators, and 4-5 keys of button, box, image and label each. A local branch row is about 5-8 widgets, not 8-10. Both figures are estimates.
- **Merge-test cycle.** It forms only when there is at least one non-closed session.
- **What carries the high rating.** It rests on refresh_git (navigation to the default agents page, plus file, git, worktree and integration events, debounced to once a second) and on the sidebar rebuild after every session state flip. The agent-settings and New-task leaks are once per user-opened panel.
- **confirm_strip revealer cycle (agent_menu.rs:835).** It sits inside the settings popover that already leaks, so it only matters once the popover captures are made weak. It still has to be fixed.
- **Task composer.** A weak `form` alone frees everything after Panel::close clears the body. Weak Rc<Panel> captures in both cancel (479) and create (489) are still the safer change.
- **Related sites.** registry_drag (shell.rs:38) and scope_picker already capture weakly and do not leak.

**Blind re-check note.** The claim's widget counts and memory sizes are estimates and were not measured. The branch rows themselves already capture the popover weakly. They leak only because search's closures, through `entries`, keep them reachable from the search↔create_key cycle. Breaking that one edge frees all of them. Invalidate-driven refreshes happen only while the Code or Agents page is shown.
