#### RA-040 · Every file/git/worktree event re-fetches and rebuilds the hidden Files tree and Git panel, including a paginated `gh api` call, up to once a second while agents work

`apps/relay-native/src/editor.rs:509` · **high** · Performance · confirmed · effort M

**Problem.** `if matches!(ui.page.borrow().as_str(), "code" | "agents") && !self.invalidate_pending.replace(true)` arms a 1000 ms timer (514). The timer runs load_tree or run_search, then refresh_git and refresh_scopes (519-525), with no check of `file_sidebar.is_visible()` or `git.is_visible()`, although both start hidden (299-300). navigate() never stores "code" (app.rs:1314-1315), so the gate reduces to 'the default Agents page'. Routing is at app.rs:1232-1240. Each refresh_git sends git.status (code_git.rs:159), then git.branches, git.log, integration.list and git.pr.list together (578-583). The engine serves git.pr.list with `gh api --paginate --slurp repos/{owner}/{repo}/pulls?state=all&per_page=100` and no cache (crates/relay-core/src/handlers/git.rs:625-628, 1083-1094). load_tree re-requests file.tree for the current directory and for every expanded folder (editor.rs:575-582, 866-867 → 841-842). Each of those runs `git status --porcelain=v1 -z --untracked-files=all` (file.rs:30-31 → worktree.rs:86-89). The watcher emits file.changed for a watched root at most every 125 ms while files change (watch.rs:113-129).

**Impact.** With panels hidden, sustained activity in a watched root of the current project (main checkout, the user's own saves, any worktree once listed/read through the bus, git.changed/worktree.changed) triggers about one refresh per 1-2 s. Each refresh costs: (a) 2+N full git status scans in the engine; (b) one GitHub REST call per page of PRs, roughly 1,800-3,600 calls/hour/page against the 5,000/hour token budget that agents' own `gh` use shares; (c) a main-thread rebuild of the whole tree (about 8 widgets + 3-5 controllers per entry; list_dir is uncapped) and the Git panel (one change_row per file at code_git.rs:488; untracked=all lists every untracked file). That is hundreds of ms per refresh for a few thousand entries, plus a finding-2 leak each time. With the Git panel open, each refresh destroys it (clear at 170): scroll resets, an open branch picker or commit menu closes, and the commit-message TextView is unparented and re-parented (297-311) without grab_focus. A user typing a commit message while agents work loses keyboard focus.

**Fix.** Refresh only what is shown. Reload the tree only if `file_sidebar.is_visible()` and git only if `git.is_visible()`; otherwise set dirty flags that toggle_files/toggle_git/show_files consume. Ignore events whose `payload.worktree` is not the editor's scope. Take git.pr.list out of the automatic refresh (fetch it on panel open or explicit Refresh, or add an engine-side TTL cache). Cap rendered rows (e.g. the first 500 plus 'N more') or use a virtualized ListView. Keep the panel's persistent widgets (scroller, commit box, pickers) across refreshes, or restore focus and scroll.

**Verifier note.** The GitHub rate-limit figures assume continuous activity and are upper-bound estimates. Every one of these refreshes also adds to the #2 leak, which compounds both. Fix as proposed: refresh only visible panels (or set dirty flags), and move git.pr.list out of the automatic refresh or give it an engine-side TTL cache.

**Skeptic note.** 1. The trigger is broader than "a watched root of the current project". Watcher file.changed has no envelope project_id (crates/relay-core/src/engine.rs:567) and watchers are never removed. A watched root in any project therefore refreshes the current project's tree, Git panel and PR list. invalidate also ignores payload.worktree.

2. For agents in pooled worktrees the typical rate is lower than "up to once a second while agents work", because .relay is excluded from the primary watcher (watch.rs:166-170). About one refresh a second needs a watched root that keeps changing. Examples: a worktree the user has browsed, one the phone has read, or one an agent has queried through relay tools; a "primary" session; or untracked churn such as __pycache__ or .venv. The GitHub rate-limit figures are upper bounds. Running out needs sustained churn and a repo with more than about 150 PRs, since state=all pages through every PR the repo has ever had.

3. Focus loss is not established. No GTK source was available to show where focus goes when an ancestor of the focused widget is removed and the widget is re-added in the same main-loop iteration. Certain: the scroll position resets and the popovers close.

4. The finding misses an impact. Each refresh's git.pr.list and status scans block every other UI request on the single, strictly in-order UI socket (crates/relay-core/src/socket.rs:334; apps/relay-native/src/app.rs:1111-1116; apps/relay-native/src/client.rs:136). The result is app-wide sluggishness while agents work; terminals are not affected.

5. Related symptom: the "Files changed on disk" error (editor.rs:530-532) appears on every such event while an open document is modified, including events from unrelated projects or worktrees.

Additional references:
- docs/engine/DECISIONS.md:427-434 (D97) and :635-640 (D130).
- The expanded-folder re-fetch is at editor.rs:826-842.

**Blind re-check note.** Corrections and caveats:

1. The trigger is wider than "the current project". Watcher file.changed events are sent through emit_system with envelope project_id None (engine.rs:567). The app.rs:1211 filter checks only e.project_id, so file activity in any project's watched root drives the refresh. The fix should also filter on payload.project_id for system events.
2. The GitHub call figures are upper bounds that depend on sustained activity and on gh round-trip latency. Refreshes run back to back through GitRefreshGuard's dirty flag, at about one per max(1 s, latency).
3. The git status scans run in register_unlocked handlers, so they do not hold the store mutex and do not freeze the bus.
4. Gaps in the fix:
   - The dirty flags must also be consumed by show_files, toggle_files and toggle_git, and by layout restore that sets visibility.
   - Scope filtering on payload.worktree can apply only to file.changed. worktree.changed and integration.* carry no worktree, and git.changed for shared refs affects every worktree.
   - refresh_git also feeds the tree's CHANGED badges (project_files.rs:549), so when only the tree is visible it still needs a git.status call, though not the pr.list.

apps/relay-native cannot be compiled in this environment; this was established by reading code only.

#### RA-041 · A query left in the explorer search box makes every file event re-run a full-worktree content search, with no coalescing

`apps/relay-native/src/editor.rs:522` · **high** · Performance · confirmed · effort S

**Problem.** invalidate: `if e.search.text().trim().is_empty() { e.load_tree(&ui, Some(directory)); } else { e.run_search(&ui); }` (519-523). Unlike load_tree's tree_load_pending, run_search has no pending or queued guard. It bumps tree_revision and spawns a new `file.search` each time (1106-1114); older results are discarded only when they arrive. The engine search walks the whole worktree and `read_to_end`s every file before its UTF-8 check. It skips only .git/.relay/node_modules/target (file.rs:316-341, 629-635) and runs until 100 hits.

**Impact.** Users normally search once and leave the text in the box. After that, each file event starts another full read of the repository on the UI's sequential connection, about once a second during agent work and from any project (see invalidate), even when the explorer is hidden. On a large checkout (e.g. an Unreal project with multi-GB Content/Binaries/DerivedDataCache) each run takes seconds to minutes. Runs queue behind each other and block every other UI request until they time out. The results list is rebuilt each time, losing hover and focus.

**Fix.** Do not re-run searches on file events: mark the results stale and offer a refresh. If they must re-run, coalesce run_search like load_tree (pending flag plus one queued rerun) and only while the explorer is visible. Engine: skip generated directories (is_generated_path) and binary files before reading them fully.

**Verifier note.** The search is register_unlocked, so the store mutex and other connections are not blocked; the freeze is confined to the native UI's connection. That still matches 'freeze of the UI'. Worst on Unreal/game repositories: .uasset content is read in full and then rejected as non-UTF-8. The fix should also apply is_generated_path-style skips and a binary sniff (read the first few KB before the whole file) in the engine search.

**Skeptic note.** 1. The cross-project leak is not in `invalidate`. It comes from two places together:
   - the filter at app.rs:1213 checks only the envelope `project_id`;
   - watcher events are emitted without one (watch.rs:128 through `emit_system`).
   Events from handlers that call `changed()` (file.rs:588-594) do carry a `project_id` and are filtered.

2. Severity depends on the size of the checkout. On typical repositories the cost is background churn and rebuilding the results list, about 0.05 s per run measured on RelayV4's own root. The freeze needs multiple GB that the search does not skip.

3. The freeze affects only the native client's main connection. The bus, the store mutex and the terminals are not blocked.

4. The fix needs four more parts:
   - **Share the guard with `load_tree`.** Give search and tree loads one pending/next slot. Both bump `tree_revision` and rebuild the same tree box, and `TreeLoadGuard`'s queued `load_tree` already throws away an in-flight search's results.
   - **Use a separate connection for `file.search`.** Coalescing alone does not help when a single search runs longer than 30 s. Send it on its own connection, as `image_read` and `lifecycle_request` already do.
   - **Cap files in the engine, not just directories.** Add a per-file size cap and a NUL check on the first few KB. `is_generated_path` alone would still read every Content/*.uasset in full. It would also hide tracked build/ or dist/ sources. A gitignore-aware listing through gix, which is already a dependency, is better.
   - **Skip anything that is not a regular file.** The walk opens every entry that is not a directory. A FIFO in the tree blocks `open()` forever. A symlink to /dev/zero grows the buffer until the engine runs out of memory. This is a separate hazard in the same code and is worth its own finding.

**Blind re-check note.** Keystrokes and terminal I/O are not blocked: they use separate connections. Only requests on the desktop UI's main connection queue behind the searches. "Even when the explorer is hidden" holds because invalidate fires on the default "agents" page. The rerun rate is capped at about once per second by invalidate_pending, so the growth is a backlog only when a search takes over ~1 s. The engine's file.search is register_unlocked, so it does not hold the store mutex or block other connections.

#### RA-042 · close_prompt panics on a RefCell double borrow whenever a waiting prompt should be promoted (crash or dead event loop with 4+ open requests)

`apps/relay-native/src/guardrail_pages.rs:666` · **high** · Bug · confirmed · effort S

**Problem.** `if let Some(next) = WAITING.with(|w| (!w.borrow().is_empty()).then(|| w.borrow_mut().remove(0))) {`. The workspace is edition 2021 (Cargo.toml:9). The `Ref` temporary from `w.borrow()` is not in any shorter temporary scope, so it lives until the closure body ends. It is therefore still held when `bool::then` runs `w.borrow_mut()`, which panics with `already borrowed: BorrowMutError`. WAITING is non-empty as soon as more than TRAY_LIMIT (3) requests are open: show_prompt pushes the 4th and later ones there (573-579). `removed` is true whenever the closed id is one of the visible prompts. Consequences, verified in the crate sources: (a) gtk4-0.11.4 `clicked_trampoline` is a plain `unsafe extern "C" fn`, so a panic in a click handler aborts the process. (b) glib-0.22.9 `TaskSource::poll` wraps `spawn_future_local` futures in `catch_unwind` and then ends the task.

**Impact.** With 4 or more open exception requests, closing any visible prompt panics. (1) The "Answer later" X (459) runs close_prompt inside a click handler, which aborts the whole desktop client. (2) An answer from the Guardrails page, the phone, the CLI, or session expiry arrives as `guardrail.resolved`. guardrail_event (691) then runs close_prompt inside the long-lived event-loop task (app.rs:1147-1202). That task dies, so the client silently stops applying engine events (sessions, notifications, prompts, page updates). Its dropped receiver then makes the reader task close the connection without a Disconnected notice: the status bar still looks connected while later calls fail with "Connection closed". (3) Approve or Deny in the prompt kills either that action's task or the event loop, whichever reaches close_prompt first. (4) restore_prompts (711) on reconnect or session-close expiry dies the same way. The queue the tray exists to drain can never drain.

**Fix.** Use one mutable borrow: `let next = WAITING.with(|w| { let mut w = w.borrow_mut(); (!w.is_empty()).then(|| w.remove(0)) }); if let Some(next) = next { show_prompt(ui, &next); }`. Move the WAITING/DISMISSED/tray-count bookkeeping into a small GTK-free struct, with a unit test for "4 requests, close one, the 4th is promoted".

**Verifier note.** The proposed fix is right: take a single `borrow_mut` and bind the result before calling show_prompt. Severity stays high, not critical, because this is a client crash or freeze, not an engine failure, and it needs 4 or more open exception requests at once.

**Skeptic note.** Impact (2) is slightly wrong about session expiry. The session-close expiry event carries no hold_id (handlers/session.rs:1620-1624), so guardrail_event calls restore_prompts (a separate spawned future) instead of close_prompt. In that case only the restore task dies, as item (4) already says, not the event loop. The phone and CLI answers are the paths that kill the event loop for certain. The Guardrails-page answers race like (3). A further consequence the finding understates: after the first panic, WAITING is never drained by promotion. A reconnect's restore_prompts can then put the queued request into the tray while it also stays in WAITING, so every later close of a visible prompt panics again until that request is resolved. The fix needs one caveat, per CLAUDE.md: relay-native cannot be compiled in CI or in an agent session. The suggested GTK-free unit test would therefore run only on a GTK 4.22 developer machine (`cargo test -p relay-native`), and the change must be described as not compiled.

**Blind re-check note.** Approve or Deny with a 4th request waiting kills exactly one of the two close_prompt callers, the action task or the event loop, whichever runs first. The other finds the slot already renamed LEAVING and does not panic. The "Disconnected" path in client.rs is at about lines 235-237 (the reader's send to the dropped notice receiver). This is not compile-verified, because relay-native cannot be built here.

**Also at:** `apps/relay-native/src/guardrail_pages.rs:459`, `apps/relay-native/src/guardrail_pages.rs:479`, `apps/relay-native/src/guardrail_pages.rs:382`, `apps/relay-native/src/guardrail_pages.rs:691`, `apps/relay-native/src/guardrail_pages.rs:711`, `apps/relay-native/src/guardrail_pages.rs:573`, `apps/relay-native/src/app.rs:1147`, `apps/relay-native/src/app.rs:1202`, `apps/relay-native/src/client.rs:235`

#### RA-043 · Desktop launch dialog always sends worktree:"new", so a plugin's default_checkout (D160) never applies to desktop launches

`apps/relay-native/src/launch.rs:260` · **high** · Bug · confirmed · effort S

**Problem.** The Worktree entry is built with .text("new") (launch.rs:259-262); the payload always includes "worktree":self.worktree.text().trim() (346); launch refuses an empty value (784 'Set a worktree for every agent.'). The engine applies the plugin default only when the request omits worktree: p.worktree.as_deref().or(pair_worktree.as_deref()).unwrap_or(prepared.default_checkout) (session.rs:858), default_checkout being "primary" when an enabled plugin asks (plugins.rs:210-215; plugins/unreal-engine/plugin.json:18 "default_checkout": "primary"). D160 (DECISIONS.md:930-935): 'session.create without an explicit worktree then uses the primary checkout ... An explicit worktree still wins.'

**Impact.** In a project with the Unreal Engine plugin on, every agent launched from the desktop (launch sheet, board 'New agents / pair') gets a new pooled worktree instead of the main checkout the editor has open; its C++ lands in the worktree while editor edits land in the main checkout, and the unreal-mcp live tools refuse to act on an editor with a different copy of the project open. Phone-launched agents (no worktree) behave differently from desktop ones.

**Fix.** Default the field to empty ('Default') and omit `worktree` from the session.create payload unless the user typed one (drop the empty refusal at 784), or prefill it from plugin.list for the current project.

**Verifier note.** The plugin default is at plugins.rs:208-214, not 210-215. The desktop launch sheet is the main way to start agents, so this defeats D160 for the primary client; the workaround (typing 'primary' in the collapsed Advanced field) is undiscoverable. Fix: default the entry to empty with a 'Project default' placeholder, omit worktree from the payload when it is empty, and drop the refusal at launch.rs:784. Or prefill the entry from plugin.get/list for the current project.

**Skeptic note.** 1. Drop the phone-app comparison from the impact; apps/relay-mobile is out of scope.
2. The default lives at plugins.rs:208-215 (doc comment 208-209, fn 210). The engine line is session.rs:858 as cited.
3. Remove the "or prefill it from plugin.list" alternative. plugin.list/plugin.get do not expose default_checkout (relay-bus/src/types.rs:662-678), so it would need a bus type change and would copy engine logic into the client. Recommended fix: an empty Worktree entry with a "Project default" placeholder, worktree omitted or null when blank, and no refusal at launch.rs:784.
4. Also update the placeholder at launch.rs:261 and the hint at launch.rs:590 ("Each solo agent has its own worktree"), which is wrong for plugin projects.
5. Caveat for the fix: review groups in an Unreal project would then also land in the primary checkout. validate_pair (session.rs:764-772) counts builders and reviewers by `worktree=?1`, so solo sessions already in the primary checkout make the second builder of a two-builder group fail with session.review_group_full, or session.pair_exists if another reviewer is there. This is an existing engine issue already reachable with an explicit "primary". Either keep groups on an explicit "new" unless the user chooses otherwise, or count group membership by pair links.
6. Add as evidence: the bridge's refusal text at crates/relay-cli/src/unreal.rs:484 claims "the Unreal plugin does that by default for new agents", which is false for desktop launches.

**Blind re-check note.** No line corrections; the cited lines are accurate. One addition: the fix must omit the `worktree` key rather than send an empty string, because session.create treats "" as an explicit path and refuses it. Group follower agents inherit agent 1's checkout through pair_with, so they are affected the same way and are fixed the same way.

#### RA-044 · Replace all with zero matches panics in the sourceview5 binding and aborts the whole client, losing every unsaved note

`apps/relay-native/src/note_pages/doc.rs:899` · **high** · Bug · confirmed · effort S

**Problem.** `let note = match self.search.replace_all(&self.find.replacement.text()) {`. The locked sourceview5 0.11.2 implements this by hand (src/search_context.rs): `let is_ok = ffi::gtk_source_search_context_replace_all(...); assert_eq!(is_ok == 0, !error.is_null());`. But the C function returns `guint`, the number of replacements (sourceview5-sys: `-> c_uint`). So 0 replacements with no GError becomes `assert_eq!(true, false)`, a panic in every build profile. The "Replace all" button is always sensitive (doc.rs:204, 436-437: `replace_all.connect_clicked(move |_| all())`). The handler runs inside gtk4 0.11.4's `unsafe extern "C" fn clicked_trampoline`, and unwinding out of extern "C" aborts under Rust 1.98. The app has no panic hook and no catch_unwind.

**Impact.** Trigger: Ctrl+H, type something not in the note (or leave the query empty, or type an invalid regex), click Replace all. Clicking Replace all a second time after a successful run does the same. The native client aborts. Unsaved note text is lost (autosave is off by default, D72), and so are unsaved code-editor buffers. The code editor's "All" button (editor.rs:1075) crashes the same way when its non-empty query has no match. A smaller problem: when occurrences_count() is still -1 (scan unfinished), the result reads "Replaced 0" after N replacements.

**Fix.** Never call the binding when there may be no match. Guard with `self.search.forward(&self.buffer.start_iter()).is_some()`, which is synchronous and works while the count is -1. Better: call `sourceview5::ffi::gtk_source_search_context_replace_all` directly and use the guint it returns for "Replaced N". Apply the same guard in editor.rs. Add a zero-match case to verify_tools: note_pages.rs:1201 only tests a single match. replace() has a similar debug_assert_eq! (search_context auto binding) that fires if GtkSourceView declines a replacement without an error. That is rare (regex lookbehind), but the same guard approach applies.

**Verifier note.** I rate this high, not critical. The engine is a separate process, so agent sessions survive and only the desktop client aborts. What is lost is unsaved buffer text, not stored data. It is still a guaranteed crash from a routine action, and that is enough for high. The fix is right: guard with `search.forward(&buffer.start_iter()).is_some()`, or better, call the ffi function directly and use the guint it returns to report "Replaced N". This also fixes the wrong "Replaced 0" message while occurrences_count() is still -1.

**Skeptic note.** Severity: critical becomes high. Only the GTK client aborts. The engine and every agent session survive (README: "Closing the window keeps the engine, sessions and worktrees alive"), and no stored data is lost. The loss is unsaved note and editor text, plus a first Replace all's unsaved replacements when the crash is a second click.

The trigger and mechanism are as stated, and I checked them against the real GtkSourceView 5.20.0. replace_all returns 0 with no GError for a query with no match, an empty query, an invalid regex, and a second call after a successful one. The process aborts because rustc 1.98 aborts when a panic unwinds out of an `extern "C"` function, and nothing on the signal path catches it.

Fix: prefer the direct FFI call over the forward() guard. Call `sourceview5::ffi::gtk_source_search_context_replace_all`, treat only a set GError as failure, and use the returned count. The forward() guard misses the rare case where regex_replace stops on the first match without setting a GError. Put this in one shared helper for doc.rs:899 and editor.rs:1075; their messages have already diverged ("Replaced N" vs "Replaced all matches"). The zero-match regression test must call that helper, because calling `SearchContext::replace_all` directly in verify_tools would itself panic. Per CLAUDE.md, the change cannot be compiled in an agent session; it must be built and tested on a machine with GTK 4.22.

The secondary `replace()` debug_assert_eq! is live in run.sh's dev build, but both callers guard it with occurrence_position > 0, so it is low severity at most.

**Blind re-check note.** Everything checks out against the code. Two small clarifications. First, the engine and agent sessions are not affected: only the GTK client process aborts. Second, in editor.rs the empty-query case returns early, so only a non-empty query with no match crashes there. The fix should go through the FFI and check the count, rather than rely only on a forward() pre-check.

#### RA-045 · Every engine event clears and rebuilds the Guardrails page: review state and half-typed denial reasons are lost, and Approve keys shift under the pointer

`apps/relay-native/src/pages.rs:124` · **high** · Bug · confirmed · effort M

**Problem.** For "guardrails", refresh runs `let body = page.last_child()...; clear(&body);` and then rebuilds every card through `guardrail_pages::page(...)` (157). refresh_page fires from app.rs:1263-1264 (`} else { ui.refresh_page(); }`) for every current-project event that is not project, session, file, layout, ui or settings: task.*, mailbox.*, guardrail.*, notify.*, overlap.changed, module.*, run.*, usage.changed. The "Keep forms mounted" owner check (91-93) only protects what sits above the list, but on this page the interactive state lives inside the list: the denial Entry (guardrail_pages.rs:288, 351-403), the exact-action pane that gates "Allow once" (276-278, 316-346), and the Details expanders. The rebuild also awaits twice mid-way (guardrail_pages.rs:774, pages.rs:161), so partial content is drawn and the scroll position clamps. Holds are listed newest first (`ORDER BY id DESC`, handlers/guardrail.rs:320), and exception cards' Approve keys are enabled immediately.

**Impact.** While agents are active, the user's typed denial reason vanishes, and the reviewed payload collapses with "Allow once" going insensitive again before it can be clicked. Expanders close and the scroll jumps. Answering one card emits guardrail.resolved and mailbox.new for the same project, which resets every other card. A new request is inserted at the top and pushes the others down by about one card height. That can put a different agent's always-enabled "Approve once" or "Approve for this session" key under the pointer at click time. With many open holds (up to 1000 listed), each event also recreates thousands of widgets on the main thread.

**Fix.** Reconcile instead of rebuilding. Key cards by hold id (the widget name already carries it), insert new cards, remove resolved ones, and update the "ago" labels in place, leaving existing cards and their form state untouched. Refresh this page only for guardrail.* and overlap.* events. List open requests oldest first (append at the bottom) so that arrivals never move existing keys.

**Verifier note.** The most frequent trigger is usage.changed from the statusline hook, not only task and mailbox events. The approve-under-pointer harm depends on timing; the certain harm is losing typed reasons and completed reviews during a normal flow. The fix is right: reconcile cards by hold id, and limit this page's refreshes to guardrail.* and overlap.* events, or at least drop usage.changed, run.* and device.changed.

**Skeptic note.** The first verifier's "most frequent trigger is usage.changed from the statusline hook" is wrong. At HEAD the Claude statusline script (crates/relay-core/src/hooks.rs:576-578) only writes ~/.claude/relay-usage.json, and no hook or CLI path calls usage.report: D64 makes stored usage.report rows only a fallback, and the comments at audit.rs:16-17 and in D151 are stale. usage.changed fires only if an agent calls the usage.report tool itself. device.changed from the adb watcher runs only while the Devices page is open (app.rs:1338-1346), so it does not reach this page. The real frequent triggers are the session.report lifecycle events (notify.new/changed, mailbox.new, task.changed when a session goes running↔blocked), guardrail.held/resolved together with their notify.new and mailbox.new, and agent mailbox, task and overlap traffic.

Smaller corrections:
- Only exception cards carry the hold id in their widget name (guardrail_pages.rs:417). hold_row cards have no name, so they need one for reconciling.
- The awaits at guardrail_pages.rs:774 and pages.rs:161 run after all request and hold cards are appended. Only the ACTIVE EXCEPTIONS and overlap tail is briefly missing, and scroll clamps only when the viewport reaches it.
- "Up to 1000 holds" is not a realistic case, because open holds expire when their session closes (session.rs:1612-1625).

Fix completeness:
- If refresh is limited to guardrail.* and overlap.*, also subscribe to guardrail.grant_used (emitted at guardrail.rs:763, not in app.rs:1154). Otherwise the grant's "used N times" count, which today updates only as a side effect of other events, goes stale.
- Sort oldest first on the client. Do not change `ORDER BY id DESC LIMIT 1000`, which would change which 1000 rows come back and the order every other consumer sees.
- Keep each card's review state and open denial form, keyed by hold id.
- Oldest first stops new arrivals from moving keys, but a resolution above (answered from the tray prompt, from the phone, or expired) still shifts cards up. To close the misclick risk, briefly desensitize Approve keys after the layout moves.

**Blind re-check note.** The usage.changed trigger is mostly moot: the Claude statusline script (hooks.rs:576) writes relay-usage.json and never calls usage.report. The frequent triggers are task.changed, mailbox.new, overlap.changed, notify.* and guardrail.* in the current project, plus device, run and avd events, which carry no project_id. The second await that leaves partial content drawn is pages.rs:161 (overlap.list) and the guardrail.requests.list call in guardrail_pages::page (around line 774), as cited.

#### RA-046 · Switching project with an explicit page (Files and Git, dashboard rows, notifications) is undone by the per-project layout restore

`apps/relay-native/src/shell.rs:402` · **high** · Bug · confirmed · effort M

**Problem.** open_project (24-36) sets restored_project=0, spawns refresh(), and then calls navigate(page). navigate's save_layout bumps layout_revision (app.rs:1358 → shell.rs:287-288). The refresh future only runs later, and captures the revision at that point (app.rs:1371). So restore_layout's guard `if self.layout_revision.get() != revision` (327, 338) never sees that explicit navigation. After session.list and settings.get, apply_layout ends with `self.navigate(page)` to the saved page (398-402). The saved page cannot express Files: self.page is "agents" for both views, and editor.layout_state (project_files.rs:38-41) stores only pane visibility and widths. navigate("agents") always calls editor.show_agents() (app.rs:1350-1356), and navigate also runs dismiss_panels().

**Impact.** In project A, choosing "Files and Git" from project B's ⋯ menu (registry.rs:481) shows Files, then flips back to B's agent wall a couple of round trips later. These all land on the project's last saved page instead of the requested one: dashboard hold rows (tools.rs:373, "guardrails"), review rows (tools.rs:412, "board" + open_task), and notification clicks (notification_center.rs:310). A task panel opened in that window is either closed by dismiss_panels or ends up over the wrong page. The editor tree and git status are also loaded twice. This is exactly what the comment at 337 says must not happen. No test covers it: roadmap_smoke.rs:239 passes "files", which navigate silently ignores.

**Fix.** Make an explicit destination win over the restore. One option: read the revision in open_project before calling navigate and store it as the restore baseline, so restore_layout applies `page` only if nothing navigated since the switch. Another: pass the requested page into restore_layout/apply_layout and apply only mode, columns, order, split and project_tools. Also persist Files vs Agents in the layout, so restoring "agents" does not force show_agents().

**Verifier note.** Mechanism as stated. The fix should make the requested destination survive. One option: in open_project, after navigate, set a 'restore baseline' that makes restore_layout skip the saved page. Another: pass the requested page through and apply only mode, columns, order, split, sidebar and project_tools. In both cases, persist Files vs Agents in the layout. Finding #5 is the opposite race: when a refresh is already in flight during the switch, the explicit page wins but B's layout is overwritten. Both should be fixed together around one 'restore pending for project X, baseline revision R' state.

**Skeptic note.** Add the board's project picker (board_view.rs:513 -> pages.rs:238) to the triggers. It is the most frequent one. Also add the facets from (c): the notification focus mode is lost, and the engine's page state diverges from what the window shows.

Fix option 1 is wrong as written. If open_project captures a pre-navigate baseline, the existing guard at shell.rs:327-329 returns before anything is applied and calls save_layout(). That would overwrite B's saved mode, columns, order and split with A's on every switch, because open_project always navigates. The baseline must gate only the page field. In practice that makes option 2 the correct shape: restore mode, columns, focused, order, split and project_tools, and skip the page when an explicit destination was requested.

Two further points for the fix:
- editor.apply_layout can hide the file sidebar that show_files just revealed (project_files.rs:43-45 vs 21). For an explicit "code", call show_files again after applying, or keep the tree visible.
- The sidebar rows and "Open agents" also pass "agents" explicitly (registry.rs:283, 416, 480). The API needs an Option<page>, so that a plain switch can still restore the saved page.

Persisting Files vs Agents is an optional improvement, not needed to fix this bug. Fix it together with #5 through one "restore pending for project X" state.

**Blind re-check note.** The mechanism is as claimed. Two additions. First, the revision guard works only when a refresh iteration is already running at the time of the switch, because that iteration captured the older revision. Even then it takes the save_layout() branch, which saves the previous project's mode, columns, split and order under the new project's key. So fix option 1 (skip the restore when navigation happened) would add that clobber to the normal path. The fix should apply every non-page field and keep the requested page (option 2), and should persist "code" vs "agents". Second, more callers are affected than listed: tools.rs:534/640 and pages.rs:238 also pass non-default pages through open_project.

#### RA-047 · Every sidebar row's ⋯ menu leaks: its buttons hold the popover strongly, and the whole tree is rebuilt on every agent state change

`apps/relay-native/src/shell/registry.rs:506` · **high** · Resource leak · confirmed · effort S

**Problem.** registry.rs:505-512: `let pop = popover.clone(); key.connect_clicked(move |_| { pop.popdown(); if let Some(ui) = weak.upgrade() { action(&ui); } });`. `key` is a child of `body` (504), and `body` is the popover's child (514). That makes a cycle: popover → body → key → clicked closure → popover. When a row is removed, GtkMenuButton's dispose only unparents its popover. The popover then stays referenced by its own buttons' closures, so it is never disposed. The leak includes the popover, body, title/path labels, separators, 4-5 buttons (each a Box, Image and Label), and the Action closures holding three clones of the project/workspace JSON (470, 478). One menu is built per workspace header (366) and per visible project row (439). render_projects rebuilds every row whenever its signature changes (133-137), and the signature includes every session's state in every project. Each running/idle/blocked transition emits session.changed (crates/relay-core/src/handlers/session.rs:1424-1426), which calls render_projects through apply_session_event (agent_menu.rs:131). The codebase already uses the safe pattern elsewhere (pages.rs:229 `let pop = popover.downgrade();`). registry_editor repeats the mistake: `check` holds `save` strongly (828), save's clicked closure holds name/branch/build/run/pinned strongly (912), and their changed/notify handlers hold `check` (871-888). So save and the inputs form a cycle that survives Panel::close's clear(body).

**Impact.** Memory grows for as long as the app runs, in proportion to agent activity times the number of sidebar rows. Every agent turn boundary in any project rebuilds the tree and leaks one popover subtree per visible row. For example, 20 rows and a few hundred agent state transitions an hour leak thousands of widget subtrees per hour (rough estimate, not measured). Each open/close of Project or Workspace settings leaks about 10 more widgets.

**Fix.** Capture the popover weakly (`let pop = popover.downgrade();` and upgrade it inside the handler, as pages.rs:229 does), or use `glib::clone!(#[weak] popover, ...)`. Better still, build the menu lazily with MenuButton::set_create_popup_func, so rows that are never opened allocate nothing. In registry_editor, capture `save` and the labels weakly inside `check` (the inputs are already weak there), or capture the inputs weakly in the save closure.

**Verifier note.** The rate is not measured. The per-popover cost is probably modest because the leaked popovers are never realized or measured, but the growth is unbounded and scales with (rows x agent state transitions), which fits the 'unbounded growth in normal use' rule for high. Fix: capture `popover.downgrade()` in the entry closures, as pages.rs:229 does, or build the popover lazily with MenuButton::set_create_popup_func. In registry_editor, capture `save` weakly inside `check`, or capture the inputs weakly in save's clicked closure. Not compiled or run: the leak follows from reading the code and from GTK4 dispose semantics.

**Skeptic note.** Details:
- The safe example is at pages.rs:228, not 229.
- The workspace menu holds 3 JSON clones (470) and the project menu 2 (478).
- Another source of session.changed: engine.rs:1317-1343, where input to an idle agent marks it running.

Impact, measured rather than guessed: in a C reproduction on GTK 4.22.5, each leaked menu subtree costs about 76 KiB of heap. Each rebuild loses about 75 KiB × (workspace headers + visible project rows); the Rust closures and JSON clones come on top of that. This is still a model of the app, not a measurement of the app.

Fix: `set_create_popup_func` is an optimisation, not a substitute for the weak capture. GTK calls it on every activation, so it must build only when `menu.popover().is_none()`, and the popover it builds still needs weak captures in its entry closures.

Related sites with the same root cause, not listed in the finding: agent_menu.rs agent_settings_body captures `popover.clone()` strongly in closures on its own children. These are brief (451), save (541), start-fresh confirm (578) and close confirm (608). The closed handler (370-373) unparents that popover, but the cycle keeps the whole subtree alive, so every open and close of an agent's settings leaks it. That happens once per user click, which is less often, and the same fix applies.

Separate issue, not counted here: the rebuild disposes the MenuButton of an open ⋯ menu, so the menu disappears under the user whenever any agent changes state. Building the menu lazily does not fix this; only avoiding the full rebuild does.

**Blind re-check note.** Line numbers check out within ±1 (save.connect_clicked is at line 913, the check closure starts at 825, and the strong save clone is at 827). The per-hour size of the leak is an estimate, not a measurement. The registry_editor cycle is a separate, much smaller leak (one per settings open), not one tied to agent activity.

**Also at:** `apps/relay-native/src/shell/registry.rs:828`, `apps/relay-native/src/shell/registry.rs:912`, `apps/relay-native/src/shell/registry.rs:136`, `apps/relay-native/src/agent_menu.rs:131`, `crates/relay-core/src/handlers/session.rs:1424`, `apps/relay-native/src/pages.rs:229`

#### RA-048 · A task in a completed module opens as unsaved: close, navigation and every action are blocked, and Save silently unassigns the module

`apps/relay-native/src/task_pages.rs:518` · **high** · Bug · confirmed · effort S

**Problem.** open() calls `module.list` without `include_archived` (517-520). The engine then returns only modules with `completed_at IS NULL` (crates/relay-core/src/handlers/module.rs:145). detail() fills the combo from that list and calls `module.set_active_id(Some(&task["module_id"]...to_string()))` (571-576). For a completed module no row matches, so the combo stays unselected. The snapshot's `"module_id":chosen(&module).parse::<i64>().ok()` (596) is then null while `base["module_id"]` is N. `dirty()` compares the snapshot with the raw row (`self.base.borrow()[k] != *v`, 174-179), so it is true before the user touches anything. Completing a module does not touch its tasks (module.rs:159-175). Those tasks still appear on the board and in the module editor's task list (note_pages.rs:1365-1380). Because of `.unwrap_or(Value::Null)` (520), the same thing happens for every task with a module whenever module.list fails.

**Impact.** Open a done task that belongs to a completed module. Back and the scrim refuse ("Save your changes or choose Discard and close."), and page navigation refuses (dismiss_panels). Move, Approve, Dispatch, labels, relations, Delete and "New agents / pair" all refuse with "Save task changes…". If the user clicks Save as the message tells them to, the update sends module_id:null (the expected module_id:N still matches). The task is silently removed from its module, so module stats and patch-notes drafts lose it.

**Fix.** Fetch modules with `include_archived: true` and label completed ones, or always add the task's current module to the combo. Measure dirtiness against the form's own initial snapshot, not the raw row, so a value the widgets can't show never looks like an edit. Keep `base` only for `expected`. Show module.list/task.list errors instead of rendering with `unwrap_or(Null)`.

**Verifier note.** The trigger is opening any task of a completed module from the board or from the archived module's editor. The module.list-failure path (unwrap_or(Null) at 520) is a secondary trigger. Fix: request include_archived:true, or always add the task's current module_id to the combo. Compute dirty() against the form's initial snapshot rather than the raw row.

**Skeptic note.** The proposed fix needs one correction. Measuring dirty() against the form's initial snapshot hides the false dirty state, but on its own it does not stop the data change. Save still sends the whole snapshot (`next`), which includes module_id:null. So if the user edits any other field (the title, say) and saves, the task is still silently detached from its module. If dirtiness switches to an initial snapshot, Save must also send only the fields that differ from that snapshot, with `expected` limited to those fields. The baseline must also be reset after a successful save and on Discard, because today both update `base`.

Draft is shared with the module and note editors, so changing what dirty() compares against changes their behavior too.

The essential fix is to keep the task's current module in the combo: request include_archived:true and label completed modules, or add the current id when it is not listed. On a module.list error, show the error instead of rendering an editor with an empty module list.

The finding's line references are correct.

**Blind re-check note.** Line numbers have drifted slightly. The module.list call is at about lines 517-520 of task_pages.rs, the combo set_active_id at about 571-576, the snapshot at about 596, and dirty() at about 174-178. One addition: "Discard and close" still works as an exit, so the user is not trapped, but every action on the task stays blocked unless they save, and saving unassigns the module.

**Also at:** `apps/relay-native/src/task_pages.rs:571`, `apps/relay-native/src/task_pages.rs:596`, `apps/relay-native/src/task_pages.rs:174`, `crates/relay-core/src/handlers/module.rs:145`, `apps/relay-native/src/note_pages.rs:1376`

#### RA-049 · Wallpaper images live in audited settings, so every rotation tick (and every library Save) copies the previous image into the audit table and keeps it for 180 days

`apps/relay-native/src/tools_settings.rs:136` · **high** · Performance · confirmed · effort M

**Problem.** Uploaded wallpapers become data URLs stored in the settings tree: tools_settings.rs:1009-1011 `let image=format!("data:image/jpeg;base64,{}",...); library.push(json!({..."image":image,"preview":image}))`, and Save persists them with `settings.push(("settings.set", json!({"path":format!("appearance.{field}"),"value":wallpaper_snapshot[field]})))` (132-139). The 'Rotate wallpapers randomly' checkbox (338-353) drives wallpaper_rotation.rs:176, which calls `settings.set {"path":"appearance.wallpaper","value":candidates[index]}` every 1-1440 minutes (default 15). In the engine, settings.set is Audit::Always + Undo::Inverse (relay-bus ops/notify.rs:23). The handler records the old value: handlers/settings.rs:218-220 `let before = get(...)?; ... ctx.set_undo("settings.set", json!({ "path": p.path, "value": before }), None)`. audit.rs:88-97 caps payload and result at 64 KB, but audit.rs:123 writes `e.undo_op.map(|u| serde_json::to_string(u)...)` with no cap. recovery.rs:18/193-202 prunes only rows older than 180 days.

**Impact.** With rotation on, each tick adds one audit row holding the previous full image. I re-encoded the system wallpapers the way the app does (1280-px JPEG at q80): the data URLs came out at 25-166 KB, and photographs are larger. At the default 15 minutes that is ~2.4-16 MB a day; at the 1-minute minimum it is ~36-240 MB a day. Rows are kept 180 days, so the single SQLite store grows to gigabytes. The engine copies that store under its mutex for backups and runs VACUUM after pruning. Each Save that changes the library also stores the previous library (up to 1.5 MB, with previews duplicated). Unfiltered audit.list pages also carry these images.

**Fix.** Keep image bytes out of the settings tree. Write uploaded and bundled wallpapers to files under the store or cache directory, and keep only ids/paths in appearance.wallpapers and appearance.wallpaper. If that is too large a change, rotate through a dedicated op with Audit::Never, and cap or hash undo_op the way payload already is.

**Verifier note.** Each row's cost is not just the undo_op. Payload and result_summary also hold the new image whenever it is 64 KB or less (always true for the bundled presets), so capping undo_op alone does not fix it. The real fix is the one proposed: keep image bytes out of the settings tree and store ids or paths. As a stopgap, rotation could go through an op with Audit::Never, and undo_op could get the same size cap as the payload.

**Skeptic note.** Anchor: the main driver is the rotation tick, so anchor at apps/relay-native/src/wallpaper_rotation.rs:175 (trigger) and crates/relay-core/src/audit.rs:123 (the uncapped write). tools_settings.rs:136 is the rarer Save path.

Cost per row:
- Over 64 KB, only undo_op holds a full image (the previous one). Payload and result become {truncated,bytes} markers.
- At 64 KB or less, the row holds three copies. This covers the bundled presets (about 36 KB per row), and images just under 64 KB cost up to about 190 KB per row.
- The finding's per-day figures assume the app is open 24/7. Ticks only happen while the window is open.
- At the default retention the size levels off at the 180-day window. It is only truly unbounded with audit.retention_days=0.
- Prune and VACUUM run only at engine launch (recovery.rs:183-221), not periodically.
- Measured on the system wallpapers: median 131 KB, range 36-406 KB.

Fix:
- Files plus ids/paths: also needs a one-time conversion of the data URLs already stored in appearance.wallpapers and appearance.wallpaper, and the client must load images from files. The rows already written age out over 180 days, unless a one-off scrub and VACUUM removes them sooner.
- The smallest targeted fix for the main source: rotate by writing a small selected-id key that the client resolves against the library, or through an Audit::Never op. This also stops settings.changed (handlers/settings.rs:222) broadcasting the full image on every tick.
- A generic undo_op cap does not help images of 64 KB or less, because payload and result still hold the new image. It also changes behaviour elsewhere: task.update's inverse carries the old body (handlers/task.rs:890), so large-body edits would stop being undoable. If a cap is used, scope it, and store NULL above the limit so audit.undo reports the row as not undoable.
- Any change under apps/relay-native cannot be compiled in an agent session and must be reported as uncompiled (CLAUDE.md).

**Blind re-check note.** The impact is larger than stated for small images. When the image is 64 KB or less, each tick also stores the new image in payload and again in result_summary, not just the previous image in undo_op. With the default bundled PNGs that is about 36 KB per tick. Pruning runs only at engine start, so rows can outlive 180 days until the next restart. The fix's "cap or hash undo_op" option would break audit.undo for settings.set unless the row is also marked as not undoable. Prefer storing images as files, or an unaudited rotation op.

**Also at:** `apps/relay-native/src/wallpaper_rotation.rs:176`, `apps/relay-native/src/tools_settings.rs:338`, `apps/relay-native/src/tools_settings.rs:1011`, `crates/relay-core/src/handlers/settings.rs:218`, `crates/relay-core/src/audit.rs:123`, `crates/relay-core/src/recovery.rs:193`

#### RA-050 · Skills page fetches every skill's full body; past 2 MiB the reply exceeds the client's line cap and the whole engine connection is torn down

`apps/relay-native/src/tools_skills.rs:25` · **high** · Bug · confirmed · effort M

**Problem.** `list_op: "skill.list"` is called with `json!({})` by market::refresh (tools_market.rs:96) on every refresh_page while Skills is visible. The engine (handlers/provider.rs:86-107) returns `SELECT * FROM skills` rows, and the bus `Skill` type includes `body: String`. Each body may be up to 256 KiB (provider.rs:583-591), with no limit on the number of skills. client.rs:48 sets `MAX_LINE: usize = 2 * 1024 * 1024`. At client.rs:200-204 the reader returns `Err(Error::Protocol("frame exceeds 2 MiB"))` from its loop; that fails every pending request and sends Notice::Disconnected (259-265). app.rs:1267-1275 then drops the client. The page needs bodies only for `description()` (tools_skills.rs:54) and the detail view (240). skill.install's reply (provider.rs:244 `SkillInstallOut { skills }`) also echoes every body it installed.

**Impact.** Once installed skills total more than about 2 MiB, opening Skills disconnects the native app from the engine. That takes roughly 80 skills of 25 KB, or 9 at the 256 KiB cap, and the installer imports every SKILL.md in a pasted repository, so one large collection repo is enough. Installing such a repo disconnects in the middle of the install, although the install has already committed. After Reconnect, the next engine event while Skills is open does it again. Below the cap, the page still re-downloads and re-parses the whole library on every task, mailbox or notify event, and the engine builds that reply under the store mutex. 'Open on GitHub' goes through ui.mutate, so it also triggers a full re-fetch.

**Fix.** Make skill.list return a summary without bodies (id, name, description, source, enabled_in, dates), or add a summary flag. Load the body with skill.get when the detail opens, as plugins already do with plugin.get. Have skill.install return ids and names only. In client.rs, fail only the oversized response by discarding that line, instead of dropping the connection.

**Verifier note.** The line numbers check out. The 'roughly 80 x 25 KB' estimate is high because JSON escaping inflates bodies, so fewer are needed. The fix is right: a bodyless summary list (it could carry a server-computed description, which also deals with native-tools#14), a body fetched only for the detail view, and a skill.install reply that does not echo bodies. Discarding only the oversized response line in client.rs would also stop the failure from taking down the whole connection.

**Skeptic note.** Add apps/relay-native/src/shell.rs:832 to `related`. It is the Agent skills sheet, which calls skill.list with only project_id and gets every body back. The "one large collection repo is enough" claim needs a qualifier: real multi-plugin repos usually fail at the root with skill.duplicate_name and install nothing, so several installs adding up is the reliable trigger. The first verifier said JSON escaping noticeably lowers the count needed; it does not, the measured overhead is about 6%.

What the fix needs to cover:
1. No skill.get op exists. It has to be added as a bus op with a handler.
2. A summary list must carry a server-computed description. description() parses the body and is used for search, the card and the detail (tools_skills.rs:34, 106, 144).
3. Besides the detail view at line 240, the Edit dialog (tools_skills.rs:187-190, 410-417) fills its editor from the list row's `body`. A bodyless list would open an empty editor, and saving it would overwrite the real instructions. That is a data-loss trap for a careless fix, so Edit must fetch the body first.
4. Keep the full form available behind an opt-in `summary` flag or a separate op, because agents reach skill.list through MCP.
5. skill.install should return ids and names only. The installer reads only the count (tools_skills.rs:372).
6. To drop only the oversized line on the client, the reader must skip to the newline and read the request id from the line prefix (`{"v":1,"id":"..."`). Otherwise the request waits out its 30 s timeout. A cap in the engine that turns an oversize reply into a typed error would protect every client.

**Blind re-check note.** There is no skill.get op on the bus today. The fix has to add one, or put a description/excerpt in the list summary, because the page's description() parses the frontmatter out of the body. Live terminal sessions are not affected (terminals use their own connections); what is lost is the UI's single control/event connection. Line anchors are approximately right: client.rs 48/200, app.rs ~1267, provider.rs ~86 and ~244.

#### RA-051 · wss:// rendezvous dial panics: rustls is built with no CryptoProvider, so the tunnel task dies on its first connect

`crates/relay-remote/Cargo.toml:21` · **high** · Bug · confirmed · effort S

**Problem.** relay-remote enables `tokio-tungstenite = { version = "0.30", features = ["rustls-tls-native-roots"] }`. tokio-tungstenite and tungstenite both depend on rustls with `default-features = false` (+`std`), and nothing else in the graph turns on a provider. Cargo.lock's rustls 0.23.45 entry lists only once_cell, rustls-pki-types, rustls-webpki, subtle and zeroize; the built fingerprints (target/debug/.fingerprint/rustls-*/lib-rustls.json) show features ["std"]. For a wss:// URL with no explicit connector, tokio-tungstenite 0.30 src/tls.rs:126 calls `ClientConfig::builder()`. In rustls 0.23.45 (src/crypto/mod.rs:248-253) that runs `Self::from_crate_features().expect("Could not automatically determine the process-level CryptoProvider from Rustls crate features...")`. There is no `install_default` anywhere in crates/ or apps/. tunnel.rs:57 `tokio_tungstenite::connect_async(url.as_str())` runs inside the task spawned at tunnel.rs:30, whose reconnect loop has no panic guard. The integration test only dials `ws://` (tests/remote.rs:230), so CI never reaches TLS. Established from the lockfile, compiled features and library source; no wss dial was executed.

**Impact.** `relay remote via wss://relay.example.org` is the configuration MOBILE.md §4 and the `via` warning tell users to use. Follow it with `relay serve --remote` or `relay remote serve`, and the first dial (right after the TCP connect) panics inside the tunnel task. The backoff loop dies with it and the PC never registers in its room. The CLI has already printed 'dialing rendezvous …', and phones are told `host.offline` forever. The only trace is a panic line in the engine log. With TLS the away-from-home route fails every time; only the insecure ws:// setup works.

**Fix.** Give rustls exactly one provider. Either add `rustls = { version = "0.23", default-features = false, features = ["ring", "std", "tls12", "logging"] }` (or `aws_lc_rs`) to relay-remote so feature unification enables it, or build an explicit `Connector::Rustls` from `ClientConfig::builder_with_provider(Arc::new(rustls::crypto::ring::default_provider()))` and dial with `connect_async_tls_with_config`. Add a test that dials a wss:// endpoint (a local rustls acceptor with a test CA, through a custom connector) so CI exercises TLS.

**Verifier note.** Severity is high, not critical. The engine, the desktop client and the LAN door keep working, and only the panicking tokio task dies. What fails every time is the optional away-from-home route over wss://, the secure configuration the docs recommend. That is a hard failure of an optional feature, not a crash or data loss. The fix is as proposed: enable exactly one rustls provider feature (e.g. a direct `rustls = { version = "0.23", default-features = false, features = ["ring", "std", "tls12"] }` dep in relay-remote), or pass an explicit `Connector::Rustls` built with `builder_with_provider`. Also consider wrapping the tunnel loop so that a future panic is logged as fatal and not silently ended.

**Skeptic note.** Severity should be high, not critical. Tokio catches the task panic, so only the optional wss:// rendezvous route dies. The engine, the desktop client and the LAN/Tailscale door are unaffected.

Precision on the trigger: the panic needs a successful TCP connect, and on top of that a non-empty native CA bundle (tokio-tungstenite tls.rs:96-126). On a host with no CA bundle, the dial instead returns "no native root CA certificates found" and retries forever. That route is still dead, but it does not panic. On a normal Linux desktop the panic path is the one taken.

Where the panic text appears depends on how the door was started:
- `relay remote serve`: printed in the terminal.
- `relay serve --remote` from run.sh: written to target/engine-<instance>.log.
- The systemd unit: written to the journal.
So it is not only in "the engine log".

Fix: the second option (an explicit `Connector::Rustls` built from `builder_with_provider(rustls::crypto::ring::default_provider())`) is not independent of the first. `rustls::crypto::ring` only exists when rustls's `ring` feature is enabled, so that option still needs the direct dependency. It would also have to copy the native-roots loading. The direct dependency alone is enough: `rustls = { version = "0.23", default-features = false, features = ["ring", "std", "tls12"] }` in relay-remote. Enable exactly one provider, because turning on both ring and aws_lc_rs makes `from_crate_features()` return None and the panic comes back.

For the regression test, a unit test that calls `rustls::ClientConfig::builder()` is reliable. A test that dials `wss://127.0.0.1:<port>` against a listener that accepts and drops would pass without exercising TLS on a CI image with no CA bundle.

Optionally, run each attempt as `tokio::spawn(connect_once(..)).await` inside the loop, so a future panic becomes a logged, retried error and does not quietly end the tunnel.

**Blind re-check note.** Small details: the panic fires inside tokio-tungstenite's wrap_stream, after the native roots are loaded and before the TLS handshake starts. If the native CA store is empty, the dial returns an Err instead and is retried; that case is rare. A panic only kills the tunnel task, not the engine, because the workspace profiles do not set panic=abort. Explicit provider selection (builder_with_provider) is the sturdier of the two fixes, because feature unification would become ambiguous again if anything later enables aws_lc_rs as well as ring.

**Also at:** `crates/relay-remote/src/tunnel.rs:57`, `crates/relay-remote/src/tunnel.rs:30`, `crates/relay-remote/tests/remote.rs:230`, `Cargo.lock:2798`

#### RA-052 · Phone protocol has no channel security: token sent in clear at pairing, bus lines unauthenticated, PC never authenticated

`crates/relay-remote/src/bridge.rs:79` · **high** · Security · confirmed · effort L

**Problem.** On a pairing hello, `admit` answers `Welcome::paired(&device.id, &device.token)` (bridge.rs:79), so the long-lived 256-bit token is sent in the clear. The direct door is a plain `accept_async` on a TcpStream (direct.rs:89, ws:// only) and is the route the phone tries first (MOBILE.md:140). After the one-time proof, `run` forwards every frame with `writer.write_all(line.as_bytes())` (bridge.rs:177-181): no encryption, no MAC, and nothing ties later frames to the proven connection. Greeting and Welcome (wire.rs:17-53) carry only public fields; `host_id` is also served by /info. So the phone has nothing to verify the PC with and will hand a fresh proof to whoever answers at a stored address. Through the rendezvous, TLS terminates at the server, which sees the pairing code, the token and every line, and can write into any lane. The docs say otherwise. lib.rs:9 and MOBILE.md:12 say 'the server copies lines and reads none of them'. wire.rs:68 says 'Passive listening on the LAN learns the proof, not the credential'. BUS.md:1121 still says 'No RPC over the network … Remote access is an SSH problem', the premise for giving `user` no credential at all.

**Impact.** A phone credential is full `user` (session.spawn, file.write, guardrail.confirm, …), which means code execution on the PC. (1) Anyone who can sniff the phone's WiFi during the one pairing exchange keeps a permanent credential: open or shared-PSK WiFi, or a housemate with the PSK. (2) An active LAN attacker (ARP spoofing plus a transparent WebSocket proxy) can inject bus requests into an already-authenticated connection at any time, or relay a phone's proof from a spoofed or stale address to the real door. (3) Whoever runs or compromises the rendezvous, or anyone on the path of a ws:// rendezvous, can do the same remotely. All terminal output, diffs and file contents also cross the LAN in plaintext.

**Fix.** Authenticate the channel end to end. Simplest for the direct door: TLS with a per-host self-signed certificate whose SHA-256 fingerprint goes in the pairing QR and is pinned by the phone. For both routes, derive a session key after the proof (e.g. HKDF(token, challenge || phone_nonce)) and seal every line with an AEAD and a counter nonce. That also authenticates the PC (only it knows the token) and gives replay protection. Stop sending the token: derive it from an X25519 exchange with a PC public key carried in the QR, or from a PAKE keyed by the pairing code. Correct lib.rs, MOBILE.md and BUS.md §14 in the same change. Needs a matching phone-side change.

**Verifier note.** The docs are not uniformly wrong. MOBILE.md §6 ('Security model, honestly') already says the pairing reply carries the token, that the server can read lines ('readable by whoever runs the server. Run it yourself.'), and wire.rs:68-70 says the same. `relay remote via` warns on ws:// (relay-cli remote.rs:283-285). These are the real drift: lib.rs:9-10 and MOBILE.md:12 ('copies lines and reads none of them'), BUS.md §14 line 1121 ('No RPC over the network … Remote access is an SSH problem'), and the fact that MOBILE.md §6 never mentions active MITM. Its line 'Listening on the LAN yields proofs that are only good for that connection' covers passive listening only. The undisclosed part is the active-attacker gap: proof relay, injection into an admitted connection, and no PC authentication. Fix: pin a PC key or certificate fingerprint carried in the pairing QR, use TLS or an AEAD-sealed channel keyed from the token and challenge after the proof, and correct the docs. This needs a phone-side change.

**Skeptic note.** Mechanism: "nothing ties later frames to the proven connection" is not literally true, because the TCP/WebSocket connection does tie them. What is missing is a cryptographic binding, so only an on-path attacker can inject, not any LAN peer. The "stale address" relay is mostly impractical: an attacker on another network who answers the phone's stale home address still needs a route to the real door, which normally sits behind NAT. The realistic vectors are an on-path LAN man-in-the-middle, the rendezvous host, and capture at pairing.

Docs: as the first verifier noted, MOBILE.md §6 (186-192) and wire.rs:68-70 already disclose that the token crosses at pairing and that the server can read lines. Two more lines belong in "related":
- MOBILE.md:95-96, "wss:// keeps that between the phone and the PC", is plainly false. TLS ends at the proxy in front of the rendezvous, and the rendezvous process sees the token.
- rendezvous.rs:3-4, "every credential check still happens on the PC", hides that the server can inject after the check.

Fix defects:
1. "A session key … sealed with an AEAD and a counter nonce": if both ends use one key with counters starting at 0, nonces repeat, which breaks AES-GCM and ChaCha20-Poly1305 completely. Derive one key per direction.
2. Deriving the key as HKDF(token, nonces) gives no forward secrecy: a later leak of remote.json or of the phone's token decrypts recorded sessions. Use a vetted handshake with an ephemeral Diffie-Hellman instead of hand-rolled HKDF plus AEAD. For example, Noise via the `snow` crate, with the token as the pre-shared key on reconnect, the PC's static key carried in the QR for pairing, and CPace or SPAKE2 keyed by the code when the link is typed.
3. Once one end-to-end layer covers both routes, TLS with a pinned certificate on the direct door is redundant. One mechanism over the existing WebSocket text frames is simpler and keeps the rendezvous blind.
4. Bind the handshake transcript (host_id, challenge, phone nonce), and make the phone refuse to send bus lines until the PC has proven it holds the key.
5. Bump WIRE_V and stop accepting v1, at least for a device that has spoken v2. Otherwise an active attacker simply forces v1. Existing tokens can serve as pre-shared keys, so phones already paired need not pair again for the channel part.

Interim, PC side only: state in MOBILE.md §6 that an active LAN attacker or the rendezvous host can act as the phone. Until the phone change lands, recommend Tailscale (`relay serve --remote --remote-bind <tailnet ip>:7420`) as the only route that resists this.

**Blind re-check note.** Correction to how the claim is framed: the pairing-sniff angle and the rendezvous-operator-reads-lines angle are not undocumented. MOBILE.md §6 (around lines 197-212) explicitly accepts both: the token travels as a plain LAN packet on your own WiFi, and the server is readable by whoever runs it, so "run it yourself". The contradiction is internal to the docs: MOBILE.md:12 and lib.rs:9-10 ("reads none of them") and BUS.md §14 ("No RPC over the network") are stale. What is truly unaddressed, in code and in docs, is that the PC is never authenticated and that nothing ties frames after the handshake to the proven peer. An active LAN MITM can therefore inject `user` bus requests into an admitted connection, or relay a phone's proof, with no warning anywhere. Severity is high: exploitation needs an on-LAN or on-path position, or presence during the one pairing exchange. It is not critical-by-default.

**Also at:** `crates/relay-remote/src/direct.rs:89`, `crates/relay-remote/src/bridge.rs:177`, `crates/relay-remote/src/wire.rs:68`, `crates/relay-remote/src/lib.rs:9`, `crates/relay-remote/src/rendezvous.rs:3`, `docs/MOBILE.md:12`, `docs/engine/BUS.md:1121`, `crates/relay-cli/src/remote.rs:284`, `crates/relay-remote/src/bridge.rs:98`, `crates/relay-remote/src/bridge.rs:172`, `crates/relay-remote/src/wire.rs:67`, `crates/relay-remote/src/rendezvous.rs:200`, `crates/relay-remote/src/rendezvous.rs:275`, `crates/relay-remote/src/tunnel.rs:139`, `docs/MOBILE.md:95`, `docs/MOBILE.md:191`

<a id="ra-053"></a>

#### RA-053 · In-engine LAN door has no handshake timeout or connection cap: any LAN peer can exhaust the engine's file descriptors

`crates/relay-remote/src/direct.rs:76` · **high** · Security · confirmed · effort M

**Problem.** `DirectServer::bind` spawns one task per accepted socket with no limit (direct.rs:37-46). `handle` first does `let n = stream.peek(&mut head).await?;` (76) and then `tokio_tungstenite::accept_async(stream)` (89). Neither has a timeout. HELLO_TIMEOUT (bridge.rs:39) only starts after the greeting is sent, so its comment 'A TCP connection that never speaks holds nothing but a task' is wrong: such a connection also holds an fd forever. The door is always on and runs inside the engine: run.sh:32 starts `serve --remote`, deploy/relay-remote.service:9 runs `relay serve --remote`, and `--remote-bind` defaults to `0.0.0.0:7420` (relay-cli main.rs:68). `systemctl --user show` on this machine reports DefaultLimitNOFILESoft=1024, and the unit sets no LimitNOFILE. No `accept_async_with_config` is used, so tungstenite's default 64 MiB max_message_size applies. Every unauthenticated handshake also does two blocking reads of remote.json on the engine's runtime (bridge.rs:117, :72).

**Impact.** Trigger: any host on the same network opens ~1000 TCP connections to :7420 and sends nothing, or half an HTTP request. Each one parks in `peek` or the handshake forever until the engine hits EMFILE; its Unix socket door then only logs 'accept failed' and retries every 50 ms (relay-core socket.rs:120). Every agent's `relay hook claude-pre-tool` / `codex-pre-tool` either fails to connect and exits 2, blocking the tool call (relay-cli main.rs:348-356), or connects into the listen backlog and waits with no timeout (socket.rs Client::call) until the provider kills it after 30 s (hooks.rs:351). What the provider then does with the tool call was not verified. The desktop cannot open terminal or status connections, and PTY spawns and git subprocesses fail. No pairing is needed: users who never use the phone are exposed because run.sh always opens the door. A peer can also pin up to 64 MiB of partial-message buffer per connection for 30 s windows. Severity depends on the fd soft limit of the launch environment, which is 1024 under the shipped systemd unit and typical terminals.

**Fix.** Put peek, the WebSocket handshake and the hello under one `tokio::time::timeout` (e.g. 10 s). Cap concurrent unauthenticated connections with a `Semaphore` (16-32) and cap total connections. Use `accept_async_with_config` with `max_message_size`/`max_frame_size` around 1-4 MiB. Enable TCP keepalive. Consider binding only private or tailnet interfaces by default, or opening the door only when remote.json has a device or a pending code. Set LimitNOFILE in relay-remote.service.

**Verifier note.** Calibrate the fd limit. `systemctl --user show` reports DefaultLimitNOFILESoft=1024, so the shipped unit is exposed to about 1000 idle connections. On this machine an interactive shell's soft limit is 1048576 (`ulimit -Sn`), so an engine launched by run.sh from a terminal needs far more connections than one source IP's ports can give; there the realistic attacks are memory and task exhaustion plus the pre-hello 64 MiB message buffer within the 30 s window. Fix: one `tokio::time::timeout` around peek, handshake and hello; a Semaphore on pre-auth connections; `accept_async_with_config` with small max_message_size and max_frame_size; TCP keepalive; LimitNOFILE in the unit; and consider opening the door only when remote.json has devices or a pending code.

**Skeptic note.** 1. The fd calibration is wrong. The live engine's soft limit is 1024 (/proc/2269869/limits), so about 990 connections are enough. The first verifier's 1048576 came from the agent's own shell, which inherits Claude Code's raised limit. It is not the limit of the user's Konsole, from which run.sh started the engine.

2. The memory claim is overstated. tungstenite 0.30 reserves the frame length the header declares, but read_in only zero-fills and keeps bytes that actually arrive, and HELLO_TIMEOUT drops a connection that has not said hello after 30 s. So pinned memory is roughly the attacker's bandwidth times 30 s (about 3.5 GB at 1 Gbit/s), not 64 MiB per connection. The blocking reads of remote.json (bridge.rs:117 and :72) are real but negligible.

3. Fix adjustments:
   - Put a timeout of about 10 s on peek plus accept_async only, in direct.rs. bridge::run already bounds the hello, and wrapping all of handle() would cut off admitted sessions.
   - Cap connections with Semaphore::try_acquire_owned and drop the socket at once when no permit is free. Awaiting a permit still holds the fd. Keep the cap far below the fd headroom, ideally per source IP as well.
   - LimitNOFILE in the systemd unit does not cover run.sh, which is how the user actually launches the engine. Raise the soft limit to the hard limit with setrlimit at engine start.
   - Set max_message_size above the largest legitimate phone request, or limit only the phase before the hello.
   - Opening the door only when remote.json has a device or a pending code would remove the exposure for users without a phone. But `relay remote pair` runs as a separate process and only writes remote.json, so the engine needs a way to notice: a file watch or a bus op.

4. Report the following separately as its own root cause. The PreToolUse adapter (main.rs:348-375) has no deadline shorter than the provider's 30 s timeout. So any engine stall of 30 s or more, this attack included, lets Claude Code go ahead with the tool call. Give connect plus call a timeout of 10-20 s that exits 2.

**Blind re-check note.** The bridge.rs:117/:72 blocking registry reads are minor and are not part of the decisive mechanism. The 64 MiB angle is bounded by HELLO_TIMEOUT and bandwidth once a connection completes the upgrade. The decisive defect is the untimed peek/accept_async at direct.rs:76/89 together with the uncapped spawn at :42. When the engine hits EMFILE, Unix-socket clients connect into the kernel backlog and then hang. They do not get a connect failure.

**Also at:** `crates/relay-remote/src/direct.rs:89`, `crates/relay-remote/src/direct.rs:37`, `crates/relay-remote/src/bridge.rs:37`, `crates/relay-remote/src/direct.rs:126`, `crates/relay-cli/src/main.rs:68`, `run.sh:32`, `deploy/relay-remote.service:9`, `crates/relay-core/src/socket.rs:120`, `crates/relay-cli/src/main.rs:355`, `crates/relay-remote/src/direct.rs:42`, `crates/relay-remote/src/rendezvous.rs:127`, `crates/relay-remote/src/rendezvous.rs:159`, `crates/relay-cli/src/remote.rs:107`, `crates/relay-remote/src/direct.rs:108`, `crates/relay-remote/src/bridge.rs:125`, `crates/relay-remote/src/direct.rs:93`, `crates/relay-remote/src/bridge.rs:39`, `crates/relay-remote/src/bridge.rs:117`, `crates/relay-remote/src/bridge.rs:130`, `crates/relay-core/src/socket.rs:119`, `crates/relay-cli/src/main.rs:348`
