<a id="ra-118"></a>

#### RA-118 · Startup recovery kills whatever process now holds a stale sessions.pid, plus its process group

`crates/relay-core/src/recovery.rs:86` · **medium** · Bug · confirmed · effort S

**Problem.** Step 2 does `Some(p) if pty::pid_alive(p as u32) => { kill_wait(p as u32); ...` for every row still in spawning/running/idle/blocked. `pid_alive` is only `libc::kill(pid as i32, 0) == 0` (pty.rs:394-396). `kill_wait` sends SIGTERM, then SIGKILL after 2 s, to both `-(pid)` and `pid` (recovery.rs:20-34). Nothing checks that the pid still belongs to a Relay child. Step 1 has already reaped every process carrying this instance's RELAY_SESSION/RELAY_STORE (recovery.rs:67-74, via pty::relay_children), so step 2 can only ever hit processes that are not Relay's.

**Impact.** After an unclean stop the session rows keep state `running` and their pids. Causes: power loss, kernel panic, or the engine being OOM-killed or SIGKILLed; only `Engine::shutdown` marks rows restorable. On the next start, usually after a reboot when pids are handed out from low numbers again, any same-user process that now has one of those pids gets SIGTERM and then SIGKILL, together with its whole process group: an editor, browser, terminal or desktop component. Unsaved work in it is lost, and the report calls it 'reaped'. pid reuse without a reboot is also realistic: this machine has pid_max 4194304, is already at about 4.08M after 11.5 days, and is about to wrap.

**Fix.** Never signal by bare pid in step 2. Step 1 already reaped every env-tagged orphan, so step 2 should only mark the row restorable. If a kill is still wanted, first confirm identity: `pty::proc_env(p)` must contain RELAY_SESSION == name and RELAY_STORE == store path. Comparing /proc/<p>/stat starttime with spawned_at also works.

**Verifier note.** Severity high, not critical: it needs an unclean stop plus a pid collision with a same-user process (other users' processes return EPERM, so pid_alive is false). The fix is right: in step 2 drop the kill and just mark the row restorable, or signal only after confirming that proc_env(p) has RELAY_SESSION == name and RELAY_STORE == store path (or comparing /proc/<p>/stat starttime against the row). Separately, kill_wait sends SIGKILL without waiting afterwards, so step 2 can see a step-1 victim still alive and signal it again. That is harmless only while the pid has not been reused.

**Skeptic note.** Severity medium, not high. The finding's "pid reuse without a reboot is realistic ... about to wrap" is wrong. A wrap restarts allocation at 300, and a given stale pid is reused only when the counter climbs back to it, about one full cycle after the session was spawned. Also, I read last pid 3,097,640 at 11.6 days uptime (/proc/loadavg), not ~4.08M. "Usually after a reboot" is also too strong: it needs the stale pid to be below the new boot's pid counter when Relay starts. And "step 2 can only ever hit processes that are not Relay's" is slightly too strong: it can also hit a step-1 victim that is not yet dead, or an orphan whose environment step 1 could not read.

Fix: drop the kill in step 2. The finding's other option, "compare /proc/<p>/stat starttime with spawned_at", is unsound. spawned_at is only ever written as COALESCE(spawned_at, now) (handlers/session.rs:681), so it keeps the first spawn's time. A resumed session's current pid always started later: an equality check never matches, and a >= check matches any process that reused the pid. A start-time check would need a per-spawn start time (and boot id) stored with the pid, which means a new column, a migration and a SCHEMA_VERSION bump. Caveat, not verified: step 1 sees only processes whose /proc/<pid>/environ it can read, so without step 2's kill a non-dumpable orphan would no longer be reaped. Such an orphan has lost its PTY and normally exits on SIGHUP.

Related, same root cause:
- tests/sessions.rs:576 seeds pid 999999 as a "dead" pid. Under pid_max 4194304 that is a valid pid. If a process of the same user holds it during `cargo test`, the test SIGKILLs it and its group, then fails at line 591.
- crates/relay-core/examples/perf.rs:581-585 store_copy nulls every pid before running recovery on the copy, which works around this same hazard. Its comment at lines 1092-1093 credits the copy for the protection, but on a copy step 1 matches nothing; the nulled pids are what keep step 2 away from the fixture's two live sessions.

#### RA-119 · A large `audit.retention_days` panics recovery at every launch, so the engine can never start again

`crates/relay-core/src/recovery.rs:194` · **medium** · Bug · confirmed · effort S

**Problem.** `let days: i64 = ...serde_json::from_str::<i64>(&value)...unwrap_or(180); if days > 0 { let cutoff = crate::time::days_ago(days); ... }`. time.rs:16 computes `Timestamp::now() - SignedDuration::from_hours(days.saturating_mul(24))`. jiff 0.2.35 implements `Sub<SignedDuration> for Timestamp` with `.expect("subtracting signed duration from timestamp overflowed")` (timestamp.rs:2500-2506), and `from_hours` panics on overflow. Anything above about 4.39 million days (past jiff's year -9999 limit) panics. settings.set does no range check ("unknown paths are allowed", settings.rs:9-11). serve::start calls recovery with no catch_unwind (serve.rs:23), and there is none anywhere in the workspace.

**Impact.** Trigger: `relay q settings.set '{"path":"audit.retention_days","value":9999999}'`, a natural "keep forever" value (0 is the documented one). From then on every `relay serve` panics inside recovery and exits. The setting can only be changed through the engine, so the user must hand-edit store.db. Each attempt also runs steps 1-2 (process kills) before the panic rolls the transaction back, so stale pids are signalled again on every try.

**Fix.** Clamp in recovery (`days.min(36_500)`). Make days_ago use `checked_sub` and return an Option, and skip pruning on overflow. Validate `audit.retention_days` as an integer in 0..=36500 in settings.set.

**Verifier note.** The trigger is narrower than claimed. settings.set is user-only (guardrail.rs:852 lists it among ops agents cannot call). No native UI exposes audit.retention_days, and the documented "keep forever" value is 0 (BUS.md:281, DECISIONS.md:840). The value has to be typed into the CLI and be above about 4.4 million, so this is medium rather than high: the consequence is severe but the trigger is rare. Fix as proposed: use checked_sub (or clamp days), and validate the range in settings.set.

#### RA-120 · Recovery VACUUMs the entire store on practically every launch once the audit log is older than the retention window

`crates/relay-core/src/recovery.rs:218` · **medium** · Performance · confirmed · effort S

**Problem.** `if pruned > 0 { if let Err(error) = conn.execute_batch("VACUUM") {...} }` runs after deleting rows where `ts < now - retention`. Once the store is older than 180 days, each launch prunes the rows that crossed the cutoff since the previous launch, so `pruned > 0` on almost every start. store.rs:539 sets `temp_store=MEMORY`; VACUUM attaches an empty-name temp DB, which becomes an in-memory DB under that setting (sqlite3.c: `isTempDb && sqlite3TempInMemory(db)`). In WAL mode the rewrite goes through the WAL, and no journal_size_limit is set, so the WAL is never truncated.

**Impact.** Every engine start after the first 180 days of use rewrites the whole store while the doors are closed. That costs seconds for a few hundred MB, plus a RAM spike about the size of the store. The -wal file stays about the size of the store for the engine's lifetime. This undoes the PERF §1.5 work that deferred the dirty scan to save ~160 ms of startup.

**Fix.** VACUUM only when free pages are a large fraction of the file (`PRAGMA freelist_count` against `page_count`, e.g. above 25%). Alternatively switch to `auto_vacuum=INCREMENTAL` and run `PRAGMA incremental_vacuum(N)`. Set `journal_size_limit`, or run `wal_checkpoint(TRUNCATE)` after compaction.

**Verifier note.** The cost scales with the store's size. For the tens-of-MB store that tune() assumes it is roughly 100-500 ms per launch, and seconds only for a much larger store. Calling it 'seconds' is the upper end of the range. The suggested freelist_count/page_count threshold is the right fix. A wal_checkpoint(TRUNCATE) after the VACUUM fixes the WAL size.

#### RA-121 · adopt() replaces the skill library folder inside the install transaction; a rollback leaves an orphan that the next skill reusing the rolled-back id materializes

`crates/relay-core/src/skills.rs:51` · **medium** · Bug · confirmed · effort M

**Problem.** `adopt` does `fs::remove_dir_all(to)` and `fs::rename(from, to)` on `<store>/skills/<id>`. It is called from install_downloaded_skill inside skill.install's finish transaction (provider.rs:504-508). When a later item in the same install fails (`skill.name_exists`, provider.rs:228-240), the transaction rolls back but the folder move stays. The skills id is `INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT` (store.rs:259), and the sqlite_sequence bump rolls back too. Verified: after a rolled-back insert the next INSERT receives the same id.

**Impact.** Installing a repository whose second skill conflicts by name leaves `<store>/skills/N` holding skill #1's folder. The next `skill.create` gets id N, and because fill prefers a copied SKILL.md (see the related finding), that new skill materializes into every checkout and home with skill #1's instructions and assets. For an existing id, the library now holds the new files while the row keeps the old body, revision and stamp, so checkouts disagree.

**Fix.** Adopt after commit: stage to `<id>.pending` inside the transaction and rename it in `after_commit`, or adopt entirely in `after_commit`. Also remove any pre-existing library dir when a row is created fresh (skill.create / INSERT).

**Verifier note.** Fix as proposed: either collect the (assets, id) pairs and adopt them in ctx.after_commit, or stage under `<id>.pending` and rename after commit. Defensively, also have skill.create's INSERT path remove any existing library_dir for the new id. Medium is right: real wrong content in an install-with-conflict path, and no data loss.

Every engine start runs `refresh_all` (serve.rs:29-33), and run.sh defaults to the dev instance. Likewise `sweep_hook_dirs` (hooks.rs:291) deletes every `.relay/hooks/<name>` not open in this instance's store (recovery.rs:124-139).

**Impact.** Starting a dev engine whose store has different skills removes or rewrites the stable instance's user-scope skill folders, and the stable instance does the same on each of its launches. Codex sessions of the other instance lose their skills. When both instances list the same repository, each fsck deletes the other's live hook directories, leaving dangling core.hooksPath values: commits go ungated and the user's hooks are skipped.

**Fix.** Namespace by instance: record the instance in the marker and prune only your own folders, and use `.relay/hooks/<instance>/<session>` (or pass every instance's live set to the sweep).

**Verifier note.** The trigger needs both instances in use at once with overlapping projects or different skill sets, which is why this stays medium even though the hook half is a silent bypass of the commit gate. The hook sweep only runs at engine start (recovery), not on every launch. Fix: put the instance in the skill marker and in the hook path (`.relay/hooks/<instance>/<session>`, or prune/sweep only entries whose marker or script names this instance). Codex-home pruning should likewise skip folders stamped by another instance.

#### RA-125 · Skill materializer prefers the library's original SKILL.md over the stored body, so skill.update edits never reach agents' skill folders

`crates/relay-core/src/skills.rs:341` · **medium** · Bug · confirmed · effort S

**Problem.** For library skills, `copy_bounded(&library_dir(store, *id), dest)?` copies the folder that skill.install staged from the clone, and that folder includes its SKILL.md (github.rs:180-182 copies `path.parent()`). Then `if !instructions.is_file() { fs::write(&instructions, &row.body) }`, so `row.body` is written only when no SKILL.md was copied. `skill.update` (provider.rs:155-173), exposed by the skill editor (tools_skills.rs:468-471), changes only the DB body and `updated_at`, which changes the stamp and forces a re-copy of the stale file.

**Impact.** A user edits an installed GitHub skill's instructions in the skill editor. `.relay/session-skills.md` shows the new text, but `.claude/skills/<dir>/SKILL.md`, `.agents/skills/...` and the machine-wide homes keep the original. Those folders are the delivery path D147 points agents at, so agents keep following the old instructions. The same happens when skill.create reclaims a soft-deleted name whose old library folder still exists.

**Fix.** For `Source::Library`, always write `row.body` to SKILL.md after copying (the row is the source of truth), or skip SKILL.md when copying the library folder.

**Verifier note.** Downgraded to medium: only installed GitHub skills with a library folder are affected; skills made in the editor have no library dir and are written from `row.body`. The agent also sees the new text in `.relay/session-skills.md`, so it gets contradictory instructions rather than only the old ones. Fix: for `Source::Library`, always write `row.body` to SKILL.md after the copy, or skip SKILL.md in the copy. Optionally remove the library dir on skill.delete, or on a reclaiming skill.create.

#### RA-126 · Every `?` in handle_conn skips the cleanup block, leaving a half-open connection that keeps streaming output but never reads another request

`crates/relay-core/src/socket.rs:387` · **medium** · Error handling · confirmed · effort M · rechecked after PR #30/#31: still present

**Problem.** `while let Some(line) = lines.next_line().await? {` returns early on a non-UTF-8 line or a read error. `tokio::task::spawn_blocking(...).await?` (lines 361, 419, 459, 511, 524, 652, 726, 742) returns early on a handler panic, since there is no catch_unwind anywhere. The cleanup (`forwarder.abort()`, `attached.drain() ... abort()`, `attached_runs ... abort()`, lines 746-759) runs only on a clean EOF. Dropping a tokio JoinHandle detaches the task rather than aborting it. The forwarder, PTY and logcat tasks keep their `out_tx` clones, so the writer task keeps the write half open. The request that panicked gets no `internal` response.

**Impact.** Trigger: one panic in any handler reached from the native app's control or terminal connection (e.g. a poisoned std::Mutex `.unwrap()`), or a stray non-UTF-8 byte from a raw client. Consequence: the window keeps receiving events and PTY frames, but every action or keystroke on that connection times out after 30 s (client.rs:65-72). The socket never closes, so the client never reconnects.

**Fix.** Own the per-connection tasks in a struct whose Drop aborts them (or a JoinSet, or AbortOnDrop handles), so every exit path cleans up. Map a JoinError to `Response::err(req.id, BusError::internal(..))` and keep serving. Read lines as bytes (`read_until(b'\n')`) and answer invalid UTF-8 with a `bus.parse` response instead of dropping the connection.

**Verifier note.** Small correction: `attached_mirrors` holds MirrorAttachment values whose Drop aborts the task, so mirror tasks are cleaned up even on early return. Only the forwarder, PTY and run tasks (and the writer) leak. If no forwarder or attachment exists, the writer ends and the client does see EOF. The trigger needs a handler panic (e.g. a poisoned std::Mutex unwrap) or a raw client sending non-UTF-8 bytes, which keeps this at medium.

<a id="ra-127"></a>

#### RA-127 · bus.wait subscribes only when it is called, so an event that fires between a refusal and the agent's wait is lost; only exception requests are special-cased

`crates/relay-core/src/socket.rs:463` · **medium** · Concurrency · confirmed · effort M

**Problem.** `let mut rx = engine.subscribe();` runs when the wait request arrives, so events emitted before that are gone. The fix for this exact race exists only for `guardrail.request_resolved` (exception_waited, socket.rs:198-205, commit a7aa654). Elsewhere agents are told to use the racy pattern: the device.busy hint says `wait for it with bus.wait {"events":["device.lease.released"]} and retry` (device_lease.rs:149), and the brief repeats it (providers.rs:48-49). A lagged waiter also drops the event it was waiting for, only logging it (socket.rs:432-434).

**Impact.** An agent's `adb install` is refused with device.busy. While the LLM composes its next call, which takes seconds, the peer releases the lease. The agent's bus.wait then sleeps until it times out (60 s by default, up to 1 h if the agent asked) even though the device is free. With several agents contending, this repeats on each contention.

**Fix.** Stamp each event with a monotonic sequence number under the lock, return the current sequence number in refusals that recommend bus.wait, and accept an `after_seq` cursor in WaitIn, replaying from a small ring of recent events. For state-based waits, check the current state first, as exception_waited does: for device.lease.released, return at once if the device named in `matching` has no lease.

**Verifier note.** The impact is bounded. Unless the agent passed a longer timeout_ms (the clamp allows 1 s to 1 h), the wait ends after the default 60 s with timed_out:true, and the agent can retry. The result is a stall of up to a minute per contention, not a hang, so medium is right and nothing higher. The Lagged branch (socket.rs:432-434) only matters if more than 4096 events arrive during one wait, which is rare; treat it as a footnote, not part of the root cause. The cheapest fix follows the exception_waited pattern: when the filter matches device.lease.released, check the current lease table after subscribing and return at once if the device (or any device, when no matching is given) is free. Alternatively, change the hint to 'bus.wait with a short timeout, then device.leases'. A general seq/after_seq replay ring would also work but is a larger change.

<a id="ra-128"></a>

#### RA-128 · `app.backup.now` copies the whole database inside a locked handler, and `backup_with` spins forever if called after a write

`crates/relay-core/src/store.rs:563` · **medium** · Invariant · confirmed · effort M

**Problem.** handlers/app.rs:47-48 registers BackupNow with `e.register` and calls `store.backup_with(ctx.tx(), "manual")`. backup_to runs `bk.run_to_completion(256, Duration::from_millis(0), None)`. The store mutex is held for the full copy, so the 256-page steps buy nothing. SQLite's backup_step returns SQLITE_BUSY immediately while the source btree is in a write transaction (bundled sqlite3.c:85056-85063). rusqlite 0.40's run_to_completion treats Busy as sleep(0) and retry (backup.rs:301-310).

**Impact.** Trigger: the user clicks "Back up now". Consequence: every bus request except keystrokes is blocked for a full DB copy (CLAUDE.md §5.1 invariant), which takes seconds once the store holds several 8 MiB scrollback snapshots. Latent hazard: any future handler that calls backup_with after writing in its transaction (e.g. "back up before X") spins at 100% CPU while holding the store mutex, freezing the engine.

**Fix.** Register the op as staged or unlocked and copy step-wise, re-taking the store mutex for each `step(n)`. SQLite's backup follows same-connection writes made between steps. In backup_to, replace run_to_completion with an explicit loop that returns an error on repeated Busy/Locked instead of spinning. Assert that the source connection has no open write transaction.

**Verifier note.** The spin is not reachable today. The handler transaction is a DEFERRED BEGIN (`conn.transaction()`), BackupNow writes nothing before calling backup_with, and the audit row is appended after the handler returns (engine.rs:996+). It is a hazard only for a future caller that writes first. The present cost is a stall of the bus on a rare, user-initiated action: roughly hundreds of milliseconds to a few seconds depending on store size. Unlocked registration on its own is not enough. Because the engine connection uses locking_mode=EXCLUSIVE, a second connection cannot read the store, so the backup has to stay on the engine connection and copy in steps, taking the store mutex for each step(n). Same-connection writes made between steps are carried into the backup automatically. Replace run_to_completion with an explicit loop that gives up after repeated Busy or Locked results.

<a id="ra-129"></a>

#### RA-129 · Recursive watch registration covers every session worktree and build tree under the root, follows symlinks, and on failure silently re-walks on every request

`crates/relay-core/src/watch.rs:133` · **medium** · Performance · confirmed · effort M

**Problem.** `watcher.watch(&root, RecursiveMode::Recursive)` registers an inotify watch for every directory; `is_generated_path` filters events only. Session worktrees live inside the primary root (`.relay/worktrees`). Here the primary checkout has 24,602 directories, 19,878 of them under .relay/worktrees (5 worktrees). notify 8.2's recursive add walks with `follow_links` (Config::default `follow_symlinks: true`), and its `?` aborts the whole watch on the first directory that vanishes mid-walk (PathNotFound) or on ENOSPC (inotify.rs:400-415). `ensure` drops the error without logging and clears the registration key, so the next file.tree, file.read, file.search or git.status starts another full walk.

**Impact.** About 80% of the primary checkout's inotify watches sit on trees whose events are discarded, and each worktree's build dirs are watched twice. While agents build, target/ directories churn: registering the primary checkout can keep failing, the Code view gets no live refresh, and every request spawns another ~25k-directory walk. When max_user_watches is lower, the limit is exhausted silently.

**Fix.** Watch the root non-recursively and each top-level entry recursively unless it is generated, `.relay` or `.git` (adding new top-level directories on Create). Set `Config::default().with_follow_symlinks(false)`, log registration errors, and back off retries per root.

**Verifier note.** The claim that registration 'can keep failing' while agents build is overstated. filter_dir already drops entries whose stat fails, so a directory that vanishes only aborts the walk if it disappears in the tiny window between that stat and inotify_add_watch, or right after the add. That can happen with cargo incremental session dirs, but rarely. The confirmed, ongoing cost is about 20k redundant watches with pinned inodes plus duplicated OPEN/MODIFY event traffic during worktree builds, all off the bus, together with silent, unlogged failures and an immediate re-walk with no backoff. ENOSPC is unlikely in practice: this machine's max_user_watches is 524288. Fix as proposed: do not descend into `.relay`, `.git` or generated dirs (e.g. watch the root non-recursively and its non-generated top-level entries recursively), turn off follow_symlinks, log the error, and back off retries per root.

<a id="ra-130"></a>

#### RA-130 · Worktree file watchers are never dropped: one inotify instance, one thread and a recursive watch set per worktree ever opened, for the engine's whole lifetime

`crates/relay-core/src/watch.rs:138` · **medium** · Resource leak · confirmed · effort M

**Problem.** file.tree, file.read and file.search (handlers/file.rs:21,41,301) and git.status (handlers/git.rs:164) all call ensure_after_commit for the worktree the caller names. Agents default to their own session worktree. ensure() builds notify::recommended_watcher, calls watcher.watch(&root, RecursiveMode::Recursive) (watch.rs:133) and keeps it with `watchers.insert(key.clone(), watcher)` (watch.rs:138). Engine::watchers is a Mutex<HashMap<String, RecommendedWatcher>> (engine.rs:420). A grep finds only contains_key and insert on it, never a remove: not in session.close (session.rs:1547-1638), git.worktree.remove, integration.discard or project.remove. In notify 8.2 each INotifyWatcher owns an inotify fd, a mio epoll fd and an eventfd waker, plus a 'notify-rs inotify loop' thread that exits only on the Shutdown message sent from Drop (notify inotify.rs:128-150, 177-182, 606-611). Recursive mode walks the tree with WalkDir and adds one inotify watch for every directory, including target/, node_modules/ and .git/objects. The project-root watcher also covers every nested .relay/worktrees/<name>/ checkout. is_generated_path (watch.rs:158) only filters events inside the callback; it does not stop the watches that D57 says are ignored.

**Impact.** Each session worktree that an agent (via MCP file_read/git_status) or the Code view touches adds a permanent watcher. When a session closes and its checkout is removed, the watcher's thread and 3 fds stay. When the checkout is kept, all of its directory watches stay too; the shell's discard action passes remove_worktree:false (shell.rs:734). Kept watchers go on emitting file.changed for dead sessions. On this machine the project root alone has 24,634 directories and one worktree has 15,075, so a few dozen kept worktrees approach fs.inotify.max_user_watches (524,288 here). Each watch costs roughly 1 KiB of unswappable kernel memory. With the kernel-default max_user_instances of 128, a long-running engine can use up inotify instances for the whole user session. IDEs and other tools then fail to watch files, and Relay's own later registrations fail silently (registered = false at watch.rs:132-146).

**Fix.** Release watchers when their worktree stops mattering. Remove the map entry in session.close and discard (when no other open session uses that checkout), worktree.remove, integration.discard and project.remove. Also schedule removal when the watched root itself is deleted (a remove or IN_IGNORED event for the root). Optionally cap the map with an LRU, or use one shared watcher with per-root watch/unwatch instead of one inotify instance per root. To match D57, stop recursing into generated directories: watch non-recursively and add subdirectories yourself, skipping target/, node_modules/, .relay/ and .git/objects.

**Verifier note.** On this host max_user_instances is 1024, so instance exhaustion takes far longer than the finding's 128 suggests. The practical limit is max_user_watches (524288), consumed by recursive watches on kept worktrees with build trees, which also starves other tools. The fix is as proposed: remove the map entry in session.close/discard, git.worktree.remove, integration.discard and project.remove, and stop recursing into generated directories.

**Skeptic note.** Severity is medium, not high. The impact is overstated. The live engine (about 20 h, 4 sessions) holds 3 watchers, all on project roots, and none on a session worktree. branch_cleanup removes merged checkouts, so kept watch sets do not grow without limit. "Kept watchers go on emitting file.changed for dead sessions" happens only if something writes into a closed checkout. The 128 instance limit and the 1 KiB-per-watch starvation figures do not apply to this host (1024 instances, 84 in use across the whole user session).

What the finding missed: (1) a stale map key blocks re-registration when a removed root's path is reused, through a reused session name or a project directory re-cloned in place, so that checkout gets no live refresh until the engine restarts; (2) branch_cleanup.rs:307 worktree::remove is another removal path the fix list omits.

Report separately: the project-root watcher's recursion into nested .relay/worktrees and build directories is a different root cause and the main watch cost. The RelayV4 root watcher alone holds 24,540 watches, about 19.9k of them under .relay/worktrees, which is 98% of the user's 39,165 inotify watches. Dropping per-worktree watchers does not change it. In pooled worktrees .git is a file, and the main .git/objects has only 4 directories, so .git/objects is negligible.

Fix: drop the watcher when its root is deleted (DELETE_SELF or IN_IGNORED on the root). Also drop it explicitly in session.close when no other session uses the checkout, and in git.worktree.remove, branch_cleanup, integration.discard and project.remove. Match keys by the canonical path computed before deletion, or by prefix. Avoid an LRU cap, which could stop refresh for a checkout that is on screen.

#### RA-131 · Background git status runs with GIT_OPTIONAL_LOCKS=1, so Relay's polling makes concurrent git commands in the same checkout fail on index.lock

`crates/relay-core/src/worktree.rs:90` · **medium** · Concurrency · confirmed · effort S

**Problem.** status_files runs `git status --porcelain=v1 -z --untracked-files=all` with `.env("GIT_OPTIONAL_LOCKS","1")`. This is deliberate (comment 83-85): it persists refreshed stat data. The cost is that git status holds index.lock through its collect phase (untracked scan, submodule status). Verified: while such a status was running (slowed via a submodule), a concurrent `git add` failed immediately with "Unable to create '.git/index.lock': File exists". Relay runs this status for git.status, every file.tree listing (status_badges, file.rs:31), dirty flags, git.diff, suggest_message, branch switch and commit prepare. The desktop re-runs git.status and file.tree on every file.changed / git.changed event (app.rs:1232-1240 -> editor.rs:508-524, 1 s debounce).

**Impact.** While an agent edits files, the panel keeps re-running status on the checkout it is showing. The agent's or the user's own git add / commit / switch in that checkout then fails intermittently with 'Another git process seems to be running'. The window grows with status time (large trees, many untracked files, submodules), which are exactly the repos the setting was meant to help.

**Fix.** Use GIT_OPTIONAL_LOCKS=0 on polling paths (panel refresh, badges, dirty flags). Persist stat data separately with an occasional `git update-index -q --refresh`, run when no session is live in the checkout or on an explicit refresh.

**Verifier note.** GIT_OPTIONAL_LOCKS=1 is git's own default, so the explicit env is not what introduces the lock. What does is running background polling with the default lock behaviour; VS Code sets GIT_OPTIONAL_LOCKS=0 for exactly this reason. The explicit "1" also overrides a user or agent environment that set 0. The fix stands: use 0 on the polling paths (badges, panel refresh, dirty flags) and keep 1, or an occasional `git update-index -q --refresh`, for explicit or idle refreshes so the LFS-rehash concern stays addressed.

**Also at:** `crates/relay-core/src/handlers/git.rs:733`, `crates/relay-core/src/handlers/file.rs:31`, `apps/relay-native/src/app.rs:1232`, `apps/relay-native/src/editor.rs:508`

#### RA-132 · app.reconcile and app.log.tail are success-returning stubs: the documented purge never runs, so notifications, trash and soft-deleted rows grow forever

`crates/relay-core/src/handlers/app.rs:137` · **medium** · Resource leak · confirmed · effort M

**Problem.** `e.register::<Reconcile>(|_ctx, _| { // ... Phase 1 has nothing to verify yet ... Ok(ReconcileOut { actions: Vec::new() }) });` BUS.md §5.4 (lines 288-291) says soft-deleted task/module/note/file rows are 'hard-deleted by the reconcile pass' after undo.grace_days, and SPEC:35 calls reconcile the only clock-driven work. The unfiltered dashboard query uses LIMIT 8, so a full scan and sort of a few thousand small rows is negligible. The real ongoing cost is that `.relay/trash/<id>/payload` files in a primary checkout are never reclaimed (pooled worktrees lose theirs when the worktree is removed), plus slow row growth and docs drift. Fix: add the purge at launch beside audit retention (trash and soft-deleted rows older than undo.grace_days, read notifications past an age cap), or correct BUS.md §5.4. Either implement log.tail or leave it unregistered so it reports not_implemented.

#### RA-133 · audit.undo's staleness check fails in both directions: workspace.update and session.update can never be undone, and ops recorded without `expect` overwrite later edits

`crates/relay-core/src/handlers/audit.rs:11` · **medium** · Bug · confirmed · effort S

**Problem.** target_updated_at maps only the task., module. and notes. prefixes, project.update, and skill.; anything else returns Ok(None). Undo then tests `actual.as_deref() != Some(expected)` (line 61) whenever the inverse carries expect.updated_at. workspace.update (workspace.rs:144-146, expect set, key workspace_id) and session.update (session.rs:1474-1477, expect set, key `session` name) are both `Undo::Inverse`, so they always fail with audit.stale. In the other direction, settings.set (settings.rs:220, 230), guardrail.config.set (handlers/guardrail.rs:99), notify.settings.set, ui.*, plugin.enable, skill.create and the notes.create→delete inverse (notes.rs:372, 577) record `expect: None`, so their undo runs unconditionally. BUS.md §5.5 promises that an undo never silently clobbers a later edit.

**Impact.** `audit.undo` of a workspace rename or a session.update always returns audit.stale unless force:true is passed. Undoing an older settings.set or guardrail.config.set restores the old subtree over any later changes without warning, for example re-loosening guardrail config the user has since tightened.

**Fix.** Drive the check from a per-op table giving the table and the id field (or a lookup by name for sessions). When an inverse has no way to verify freshness, refuse with audit.stale or a new code unless force is set. Record an expect value for settings and config ops, such as the subtree's latest updated_at or a hash of the current value.

**Verifier note.** For guardrail.config.set, the inverse is inverse_patch(before, merged), which touches only the changed keys. Clobbering therefore happens only if the same keys were edited later, but that is still a silent clobber (e.g. re-loosening a key the user tightened again). Even with a correct lookup, session.update undo would often be stale, because session state transitions bump sessions.updated_at. A per-entity freshness token (or refusing undo without force when freshness cannot be checked) is the right fix.

**Also at:** `crates/relay-core/src/handlers/workspace.rs:144`, `crates/relay-core/src/handlers/session.rs:1474`, `crates/relay-core/src/handlers/settings.rs:220`, `crates/relay-core/src/handlers/notes.rs:372`, `crates/relay-core/src/handlers/audit.rs:61`, `crates/relay-core/src/handlers/audit.rs:10`, `crates/relay-core/src/handlers/session.rs:1436`, `crates/relay-core/src/handlers/task.rs:905`, `crates/relay-core/src/handlers/task.rs:897`, `crates/relay-core/src/handlers/notify.rs:150`, `apps/relay-native/src/board_view.rs:890`, `crates/relay-core/src/handlers/audit.rs:22`

#### RA-134 · device.run holds the store mutex across `adb devices -l` (up to 2 s) and other I/O instead of using register_staged

`crates/relay-core/src/handlers/device.rs:152` · **medium** · Invariant · confirmed · effort M

**Problem.** RunOp is registered with `e.register` (line 140). Inside the transaction it calls `require_device(&adb, &p.device)?` (line 152), which goes to `list_with_adb` and `output_with_timeout(adb devices -l, ADB_LIST_TIMEOUT = 2s)` (lines 579-590). It also does `run_source` -> `gix::open(root)` (line 971), several canonicalize calls, a tempfile write (`gradle_init_script`) and `worktree::contains`. The same `adb devices` call was moved off the lock for device.list (comment at lines 29-31, D144) and for device.mirror.start (lines 70-72, D149). CLAUDE.md requires `register_staged` for a mutation with a slow read phase.

**Impact.** Every Run press blocks all other bus traffic for the adb round trip. That routinely exceeds the 16 ms LOCK_BUDGET even with a warm adb server, and reaches 2 s when the server is cold, which is the case the code's own comment at line 29 describes.

**Fix.** Convert to `register_staged`. In prepare, read the project and settings via `ctx.read`, do the early lease `check`, `require_device`, root resolution, wrapper and init-script creation, and `run_source`. In finish, re-read the project, acquire the lease, insert the row and schedule the worker.

**Verifier note.** The worst case is bounded at about 2 s by ADB_LIST_TIMEOUT. session.input has its own lock-free fast path, so typing into terminals keeps working during the stall, but every other bus op waits. The proposed register_staged split (prepare does the adb, gix and tempfile work; finish re-reads the project, acquires the lease, inserts the row) is the right fix. The early lease check can stay in prepare as long as acquire in finish remains authoritative.

#### RA-135 · In-memory engine state is mutated inside handlers and not rolled back when the transaction fails, so device.run's phantom run can hold the device forever

`crates/relay-core/src/handlers/device.rs:176` · **medium** · Bug · confirmed · effort M

**Problem.** RunOp inserts the runtime into device_runs and acquires a Kind::Run(id) lease (handlers/device.rs:176-177) before the pipeline appends the audit row and commits (engine.rs:999-1024). If that fails, the row is rolled back and the worker (an after_commit action) never starts, but the map entry and the lease stay. prune treats any id still in device_runs as live (handlers/device_lease.rs:94-96). device.release refuses Run leases, and device.run.stop fails with run_not_found. The same pattern appears in the gate's shell lease (handlers/guardrail.rs:532) and in set_pty during finish_launch (session.rs:685).

**Impact.** After a commit failure (for example disk full), the device stays "in use by device run N" until the engine restarts.

**Fix.** Register these in-memory side effects as after_commit actions, or record compensations that run on rollback.

**Verifier note.** Re-anchor the finding on the composite-rollback trigger (session.rs:685 under task.rs:712 + task.rs:1073), not on a commit failure. The consequence there is an orphaned live agent PTY, its worktree and its hooks, with no session row. For device.run the impact is as described but needs a commit failure. guardrail.rs:532 (gate_command lease) has the same shape. Fix: move in-memory registrations (set_pty, device_runs insert, lease acquire) into after_commit, or record rollback compensations that kill the PTY or release the lease when the pipeline's Err branch runs.

**Also at:** `crates/relay-core/src/handlers/device_lease.rs:94`, `crates/relay-core/src/handlers/guardrail.rs:532`, `crates/relay-core/src/handlers/session.rs:685`

#### RA-136 · A broken or half-created Relay signing profile blocks every release build and can be neither disabled nor recreated

`crates/relay-core/src/handlers/device.rs:210` · **medium** · Error handling · confirmed · effort S

**Problem.** Build calls `load_signing_profile(ctx.engine(), &project.path)?.filter(|profile| profile.enabled)` (line 210), so the `?` fails the build before `enabled` is even looked at. `load_signing_profile_disk` returns an error when profile.json is unreadable or invalid, or when `!keystore.is_file()` (lines 1226-1243). `set_signing_enabled` uses the same loader (line 1323), so disabling fails with the same error. `create_signing_profile` refuses with `device.signing_exists` whenever the directory exists (lines 1285-1291), but a directory without profile.json reads as 'not configured' (line 1223). The cleanup (lines 1316-1318) only runs when the closure returns Err, not when the engine dies during the keytool step (up to 90 s) or the Secret Service step (up to 30 s). There is no delete op (relay-bus ops/device.rs).

**Impact.** If release.p12 is moved or deleted (for example the user backs it up elsewhere, or restores the data directory only partly), every `device.build` for that project fails with device.signing_keystore_missing, even with Relay signing disabled, and the user cannot disable it from the UI. That contradicts D158, which says a disabled profile falls back to the project's normal Gradle release signing. If Relay is killed while creating a profile, signing.get says 'not configured' while signing.create answers 'already has a profile' forever. Both cases need manual deletion of a directory named by a sha256 hash.

**Fix.** Read profile.json first and validate the keystore only when the profile is enabled. Let `set_signing_enabled(false)` rewrite the JSON without requiring the keystore. Treat a profile directory with no profile.json as an incomplete creation that create may clean up, and write profile.json last (via `write_private_replace`) so it acts as the commit marker. This keeps D157's rule of no delete or replace for a real profile.

**Verifier note.** There is a third half-created state. profile.json is written before store_signing_secret runs (Secret Service), so a crash between those two steps leaves a profile that loads as configured and enabled but has no stored password. Builds then fail at secret lookup until the user disables the profile, and disabling only works while the keystore is present. The triggers are uncommon (a keystore removed by hand, the engine killed mid-create), which is why this is medium. Writing profile.json last as the commit marker, after the secret is stored, fixes both partial-create cases.

#### RA-137 · The device watch reads `adb track-devices` line by line, but the stream is %04x-framed, so unplugging the last device emits no device.changed

`crates/relay-core/src/handlers/device.rs:396` · **medium** · Bug · confirmed · effort S

**Problem.** The worker runs `adb track-devices -l` (line 367) and emits one `device.changed` per successful `reader.read_line(&mut line)` (lines 373-378). I checked upstream adb source. `read_and_dump` copies the server stream to stdout byte for byte. The server's `device_tracker_send` writes each update as `snprintf("%04x", len)` followed by the device list, where each device line ends in '\n' and an empty list is the empty string. So 'all devices gone' arrives as a bare `0000` with no newline. `read_line` blocks until the next update and then merges the two into one line. The fake adb in tests/bus.rs:148-151 prints unframed lines, so this framing is never tested.

**Impact.** After unplugging the only (or last) phone, the status bar still says '1 device' and the Devices page still lists it until an unrelated event refreshes them; in an idle app they stay wrong. The opposite problem also occurs: an update listing N devices emits N events. The native client answers each one with `device.list` plus a page refresh (`device.list` and `avd.list`, app.rs:1190 and tools_devices.rs:11/92), so plugging in a device with 3 attached triggers about 3 times the adb and emulator subprocesses.

**Fix.** Parse the protocol: read 4 bytes, parse the hex length, `read_exact` the payload, and emit exactly one `device.changed` per frame, including `0000`. Make the fake adb emit framed output and add a test for the empty frame.

**Verifier note.** The status bar can also be corrected by unrelated usage.changed or run.changed events, so 'stays wrong' applies mainly to an idle Devices page. The extra events from multi-device frames cost a few redundant device.list calls (adb subprocesses run unlocked under D144), not a functional failure. Fix as proposed: read the 4 hex bytes, read_exact the payload, emit one event per frame, and make the fake adb emit framed output including a 0000 frame.

**Also at:** `crates/relay-core/src/handlers/device.rs:367`, `crates/relay-core/tests/bus.rs:148`, `apps/relay-native/src/app.rs:1190`, `crates/relay-core/src/device.rs:17`

#### RA-138 · The device watch stops permanently when the adb server restarts and is not respawned while clients still hold watch leases

`crates/relay-core/src/handlers/device.rs:402` · **medium** · Bug · confirmed · effort S

**Problem.** When `adb track-devices` exits (EOF or error, lines 375-376), the worker calls `runtime.finish()` and then `clear_device_watch` (lines 380-381). That drops `watch.runtime` (line 386) but leaves `watch.clients` above zero. The Watch handler only spawns a worker when a client increments the count while `runtime.is_none()` (lines 48-57). The engine also turns a repeated `{"on":true}` from a connection that is already watching into a no-op before the handler runs (engine.rs:882). Note that `read_line` returns Err, and so breaks the loop, on a non-UTF-8 byte as well.

**Impact.** `adb kill-server`, an adb crash, or the common version fight between a distro adb and Android Studio's SDK adb ('server version doesn't match this client; killing...') closes track-devices. From then on no `device.changed` events reach any window that was already watching, so the Devices page and mirror windows stop noticing plug and unplug until the user leaves the page and comes back.

**Fix.** In the worker, when the child exits and `runtime.stopped()` is false, respawn `adb track-devices` with backoff and emit one `device.changed` so clients re-list, instead of clearing the runtime. Clear it only on `stop()`.

**Verifier note.** A non-UTF-8 byte from read_line would also end the loop, but adb output is ASCII, so this is mostly theoretical. Respawn with backoff while !runtime.stopped(), and emit one device.changed after each respawn so clients re-list. Clear the runtime only in stop().

#### RA-139 · adb is only looked up in settings and on PATH, never in the discovered Android SDK as emulator and avdmanager are

`crates/relay-core/src/handlers/device.rs:590` · **medium** · Bug · confirmed · effort S

**Problem.** `adb_path` returns the configured path or `which::which("adb")`, and otherwise fails with 'adb is not installed or not on PATH' (lines 550-572). `sdk_tool` resolves emulator and avdmanager from settings, then PATH, then `android_sdk_root` (`emulator/emulator`, cmdline-tools) (lines 397-414). `android_sdk_root` finds `$ANDROID_SDK_ROOT`, `$ANDROID_HOME` and `~/Android/Sdk` (lines 416-436), but `platform-tools/adb` is never tried. The two lookups have also drifted on an empty configured value: `sdk_tool` and `android_sdk_root` skip `""`, while `adb_path` turns it into 'configured adb does not exist: '. The Settings page promises 'Standard SDK paths are discovered automatically' (tools_settings.rs:440).

**Impact.** With Android Studio's default SDK in ~/Android/Sdk and platform-tools not on the desktop session's PATH (fish `fish_add_path` does not reach an engine launched from the desktop), device.list, device.watch, mirroring and runs all fail with device.adb_missing. Meanwhile avd.list and avd.catalog work, and Settings says discovery is automatic. A client that stores `""` for a cleared field breaks adb instead of falling back.

**Fix.** Make adb one more `sdk_tool` case (`"adb" => sdk.join("platform-tools/adb")`) and skip empty configured values. Break the `android_sdk_root -> adb_path` cycle by having the SDK-root inference use only the configured or PATH adb.

**Verifier note.** The empty-string drift is real in the engine: `sdk_tool` and `android_sdk_root` filter out `""` and `adb_path` does not. The native client cannot trigger it, though: tools_settings.rs:643-644 stores `Value::Null` for an empty entry. Only a CLI/MCP `settings.set` with `""` reaches it, so it is a minor side note. Fix: in `adb_path`, after PATH, try `android_sdk_root`'s env/home candidates joined with `platform-tools/adb`, and filter empty configured values. To avoid recursion, do not call `android_sdk_root` as-is, because it calls `adb_path`. Factor the env/home discovery into a helper that both functions use.

#### RA-140 · Run and build workers and the AVD queries run git, adb shell and SDK tools with no deadline; a hang leaves the run in 'building' holding its device lease

`crates/relay-core/src/handlers/device.rs:1596` · **medium** · Error handling · confirmed · effort M

**Problem.** `sync_primary_checkout` fetches through `worktree::git_mutate`, which is a plain `Command::new("git")...output()` (worktree.rs:26-27). It has no timeout and does not set `GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0`, unlike `worktree::create` (worktree.rs:213-214). `git_capture`, `git_optional` and `git_is_ancestor` (lines 1500-1543) use bare `output()`/`status()`. In the run worker, `adb ... logcat -c` (1687-1689), `cmd package resolve-activity` (2033-2049), `am start -W` (2061-2064) and every `pidof` poll (2092-2095) are bare `.output()` calls; the 10 s pid deadline is only checked between calls. `apksigner verify` and `jarsigner -verify` (1937, 1944) are the same. So are the unlocked queries: `emulator -list-avds` (478), `adb emu avd name` (505) and `avdmanager list device -c` (315). None of these children is registered with the runtime, so Stop cannot kill them.

**Impact.** `am start -W` blocks while the app waits for a debugger (the 'Wait for debugger' developer option) or never finishes launching, and a fetch can stall on the network or an askpass prompt. The run then stays in 'building' indefinitely, holding its device lease so other sessions get device.busy, and its worker thread never exits; Stop only releases the lease. A wedged emulator console makes every Devices-page refresh (`avd.list`) hang, leaving one more blocked thread and adb process per refresh.

**Fix.** Run each call through `proc::output_with_timeout` with its own budget: about 60 s for the fetch (with `GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0`), 20 s for `am start -W`, 5 s for resolve-activity, pidof and `logcat -c`, 60 s for the signers, 10 s for -list-avds, 3 s for `emu avd name` and 30 s for avdmanager. Check `runtime.stopped()` between steps so Stop takes effect.

**Verifier note.** The impact is overstated in one respect. `RunStop` (device.rs:263-284) removes the runtime, releases the run's leases and sets the state to 'stopped', so Stop does unblock other sessions and fix the run's state. What remains is that the run sits in 'building' holding the lease until someone presses Stop, and the worker thread plus its orphaned git/adb child leak after Stop. Fix as proposed: route each call through `proc::output_with_timeout` with per-step budgets, set GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0 on the fetch, and check `runtime.stopped()` between steps. The handler-side AVD queries are the clear CLAUDE.md invariant violation.

#### RA-141 · A run's logcat is tied to the one pid found after launch: the run never ends when the app dies, and a startup crash is reported as pid_missing without its stack

`crates/relay-core/src/handlers/device.rs:1769` · **medium** · Bug · confirmed · effort M

**Problem.** After launch the worker resolves a single pid with `wait_for_app_pid` (line 1724, 10 s) and streams `adb logcat ... --pid={pid}` (line 1748). The loop ends only at EOF (lines 1775-1791). `logcat --pid` keeps running after that process exits, so EOF only comes from a device disconnect or Stop. A crash only triggers `report_crash` (lines 1780-1783) and the run stays 'running'. If the app dies before `pidof` sees it, the run fails with 'device.pid_missing: the installed app did not expose a process after launch' (lines 1724-1732). The FATAL EXCEPTION in the device log is never read, even though `logcat -c` (line 1687) had just trimmed that log to this launch.

**Impact.** After the app crashes or the user closes it, the run keeps its Kind::Run lease indefinitely. Every other session's `device.run` or `adb install` gets device.busy ('holds the device until it stops'), and agents wait for a `device.lease.released` that only arrives when a person presses Stop. The most common development failure, a crash on startup, produces a generic error with no stack trace in the run log.

**Fix.** Start logcat at launch without the pid filter but with `-T <launch time>` (or `--uid` where the device supports it), and filter by pid on the client once it is known. Poll `pidof`, or watch for ActivityManager's 'Process ... has died' line, and when the process is gone end the run ('finished' or 'crashed') and release the lease. On pid_missing, dump the crash buffer (`logcat -b crash -d`) into the run log.

**Verifier note.** Runs are open-ended by design (they last until Stop), so this is a missed liveness check rather than a run that should 'end' at some point. The defects are two: the run does not notice the app has died, and a startup crash loses its stack. Related gaps: an app relaunched under a new pid is not followed, and wait_for_app_pid does not check runtime.stopped() during its 10 s wait. Fix: on pid_missing, dump `logcat -d -b crash` into the run log. While streaming, poll pidof (or match ActivityManager's 'Process <pkg> (pid N) has died'), and when the app is gone mark the run finished or crashed and call release_run.

**Also at:** `crates/relay-core/src/handlers/device.rs:1724`, `crates/relay-core/src/handlers/device.rs:1780`, `crates/relay-core/src/handlers/device.rs:1687`, `docs/engine/DECISIONS.md:390`

#### RA-142 · One non-UTF-8 output line ends a run's logcat stream (the run is then marked finished or hangs) and truncates build logs

`crates/relay-core/src/handlers/device.rs:1800` · **medium** · Bug · confirmed · effort S

**Problem.** Both readers use `BufReader::lines()`, which yields `Err(InvalidData)` for any line that is not valid UTF-8. The logcat loop does `let Ok(line) = line else { break };` (line 1779), then `child.wait()`, and unless the run was stopped it calls `advance_run(..., "finished", true)` and `release_run` (lines 1786-1793). `stream_command` pushes `output: {error}` and breaks (lines 1848-1851), which drops the pipe while the command keeps running.

**Impact.** If an app or a native library logs a byte sequence that is not valid UTF-8 (raw bytes, Latin-1 text), its logcat stream ends. The read end closes, `adb logcat` dies on its next write, and the run is marked 'finished' with its device lease released while the app is still running. If the app goes quiet instead, the run sits in 'running' with a frozen log until someone stops it. For builds, everything after the bad line is missing from the run log, including Gradle's error messages.

**Fix.** Read raw lines with `read_until(b'\n', &mut buf)` and convert them with `String::from_utf8_lossy` (trimming `\r\n`). Never treat a decode error as end of stream; break only on real I/O errors or EOF.

**Verifier note.** Note the extra consequence: once the child has been taken, Stop cannot kill a lingering adb logcat. Fix as proposed: read_until(b'\n') plus String::from_utf8_lossy, and break only on EOF or a real I/O error.

#### RA-143 · A device.run.stop that arrives before the worker registers its child is lost; the worker still builds and installs, then rewrites the stopped row

`crates/relay-core/src/handlers/device.rs:1862` · **medium** · Concurrency · confirmed · effort M

**Problem.** RunStop (lines 263-283) calls `runtime.stop()`, releases the run's lease and writes state='stopped'. `RunRuntime::stop` (device.rs:403-408) can only kill a child that is already in the slot, and `RunRuntime::set_child` (device.rs:373-375) stores a child without checking `stopped()`. By contrast, `DeviceWatchRuntime::install` (device.rs:33-41) kills a late child. run_worker never checks `runtime.stopped()` between phases. It runs `sync_primary_checkout(&root)` (line 1665: git status, a network `git fetch`, then `merge --ff-only`). Then `stream_command` spawns the build and calls `runtime.set_child(child)` (line 1841), and its loop returns `Streamed::Stopped` on the first line (line 1844) without killing anything. After a successful build the worker runs `logcat -c`, `am start -W` and up to 10 s of pid polling, then `advance_run(..., "running", false)` (line 1734). That function's SQL is `UPDATE device_runs SET state=?1 ... WHERE id=?4` (line 2194) with no state guard, and `fail_run` (2157) and `finish_build` (2171) are just as unconditional.

**Impact.** Pressing Stop in the first seconds of a primary-checkout run (during the sync and fetch) does not stop it. The checkout is still fast-forwarded, then Gradle `installDebug` starts and nothing ever kills it. It installs onto a device whose lease RunStop already released, so another session can be installing at the same time, which is exactly the clobbering that leases exist to prevent. Pressing Stop during launch or the pid wait still launches the app and flips the row back to 'running' with no runtime behind it. The run list then shows a live run that cannot be attached (`device.run_not_live`), `project.remove` keeps refusing without force, and an `adb logcat` child is left running and unreaped.

**Fix.** Make `RunRuntime::set_child` kill the child and return false when `stopped()` is already set (as `DeviceWatchRuntime::install` does), and have callers bail out on false. Check `runtime.stopped()` before the sync, before spawning, before the launch and before each `advance_run`. Guard every worker write with `AND state IN ('building','running')` and skip the event when no row changed.

**Verifier note.** The relevant RunStop lines are handlers/device.rs:253-274, not 263-283. A related issue that widens the window (plausible, not fully established): stream_command spawns `fish -lc "<cmd> 2>&1"` without process_group, and stop() kills only that shell PID. A Gradle wrapper or java child launched by the shell is not signalled, so Stop in the middle of the build may also leave installDebug running. A fix should kill the whole process group, e.g. process_group(0) at spawn and kill(-pgid) in stop(). The rest of the proposed fix is right: set_child kills the child and returns false once stopped() is set, the worker checks stopped() between phases, and every worker write is guarded with `AND state IN ('building','running')`, with no event emitted when no row changed.

**Skeptic note.** 1. Line numbers: RunStop is handlers/device.rs:263-285. The finding's 263-283 was right; the first verifier's 253-274 is wrong, because line 253 is the end of the SigningCreate registration.

2. Drop the claim that the run "cannot be attached (device.run_not_live)". The only attach happens inside the device.run / device.build response (socket.rs:660). No op attaches to an existing run.

3. The first verifier's process-group point is now established, not just plausible:
- A scratch experiment showed fish 4.9.3 `-c 'sleep 7.31 2>&1'` forks the command instead of exec'ing it, and the child survived a SIGKILL to the fish PID.
- fish runs no job control under -c, and stream_command (1822-1831) sets no process_group, so the whole tree shares the engine's process group.
- So stop() during a build kills only fish. The gradlew/java child keeps the pipe open, the worker returns Stopped on the next line, and Gradle very likely completes installDebug or the Play publish. The JVM ignores SIGPIPE; that the Gradle client keeps going after its stdout breaks is my inference, not tested.
- Tests cannot see any of this. Instance::Test uses sh (1821), and the tests assert only the row state. The hold test (bus.rs:614-630) even waits for the "$ ./gradlew assembleHold" line, which is pushed before the spawn (1817), so its own Stop can land in this race.

4. Add to related: handlers/device.rs:1880 (secret lookup before 1902, publish path), 1776-1777 and 1843-1844 (early returns that neither kill nor reap the child), 1821-1841 (spawn with no process group).

5. Completing the fix:
- Spawn both the run command and logcat with process_group(0), and send kill(-pid) in stop() and in set_child when stop has already been called. proc.rs:32/55/65 already uses this pattern.
- On every Stopped or early return, take_child, kill and wait.
- Check stopped() after the sync, before the spawn, before the launch, between pidof polls, and after load_signing_secret.
- Make the worker writes conditional (`AND state IN ('building','running')`) and have them report whether a row changed. When none changed, emit nothing and tear down instead of streaming logcat.

**Blind re-check note.** Line numbers in the current tree: advance_run("running") is at handlers/device.rs:1755 (not 1734), the logcat set_child at 1794, the unguarded UPDATE at 2215 (not 2194), and fail_run/finish_build at 2176/2185. In the sync or spawn window the row stays 'stopped', because stream_command returns Stopped and the worker exits. Only the post-build launch window flips it back to 'running'. A second device.run.stop clears the phantom 'running' row, and engine restart recovery closes it too, so 'project.remove keeps refusing' lasts only until either happens. Whether the unkilled build actually completes the install depends on Gradle tolerating EPIPE on stdout after the reader is dropped. That is likely but not established. Severity is medium rather than high.

#### RA-144 · Shell leases shrink to the 90 s grace on the first PostToolUse, though background or parallel device commands are still running

`crates/relay-core/src/handlers/device_lease.rs:137` · **medium** · Bug · confirmed · effort M

**Problem.** `command_finished` shortens leases when `turn_ended || command.is_some_and(|command| device_command(command).is_some())`. `shell_finished` then sets every Kind::Shell lease of the session to `min(expires, now + SHELL_GRACE)` (device_lease.rs:253-261). It is driven by `session.report kind=tool_use`, which comes from the PostToolUse hook (hooks.rs:357), and by `kind=stop` (session.rs:1379-1383). It never looks at `tool_input.run_in_background` or a trailing `&`. There is one lease per device per holder and no count of in-flight commands.

**Impact.** Trigger: an agent runs `./gradlew installDebug` with Bash `run_in_background: true`, or `adb install x.apk &`. The tool returns as soon as the command is launched, PostToolUse arrives, and the lease lapses 90 s later while the build and install run for minutes. Another session's install is then accepted onto the same phone, which is exactly the clobber the lease exists to prevent. The same happens with two parallel device commands (the first to finish shortens the shared lease) and when the turn's Stop hook fires while a background install continues.

**Fix.** Do not shorten the lease for background launches: if `data.tool_input.run_in_background` is true or the command ends in `&`, keep SHELL_RUNNING. Count in-flight device commands per (session, device) and shorten only when the count reaches zero.

**Verifier note.** For a background launch, keep SHELL_RUNNING; the 15-minute cap still bounds it. Parallel commands need a per-(session, device) in-flight count. A trailing `&` is already a command separator in split_commands, so detect it separately from tool_input.run_in_background.

#### RA-145 · Line counts use an unbounded Myers diff (no deadline, binary checked afterwards), including inside the locked file.write

`crates/relay-core/src/handlers/file.rs:103` · **medium** · Performance · confirmed · effort S

**Problem.** file.write is `e.register::<Write>` (file.rs:72) and calls `let (removed, added) = line_counts(&old, &p.text);` (103) → `TextDiff::from_lines(old, new).iter_all_changes()` (599-610), right after guardrail::enforce computed counts for the same pair with `changed_line_counts`, whose doc says it is a 'Linear multiset line comparison ... This deliberately avoids quadratic LCS work on large generated files (SPEC §15's performance doctrine)' (guardrail.rs:1096-1099, used at 575). similar 2.7's TextDiff::from_lines uses Myers with no deadline (TextDiffConfig::default: `deadline: None`); its docs: time O((N+M)D), 'two large and completely distinct sequences ... spin'. The same unguarded diff runs per changed file in git.diff (git.rs:203-213 → counts 850-860), in git.commit's prepare via staged_numstat (861-873), in git.show/tree_diff_files (1239), and as the unified diff of git.diff.file (248-251); `binary: old.contains('\0') || new.contains('\0')` is computed after diffing (224, 1246).

**Impact.** Saving (editor) or file_write-ing (agents via MCP) a large file whose content changed substantially — a reformatted or regenerated 20k-line file — costs on the order of (N+M)·D ≈ 10^9 line comparisons: seconds with the store mutex held, stalling every session. In the unlocked git paths, a regenerated lockfile or a binary asset kept in git (.blend/.uasset without LFS) pins a core and the requesting connection (UI head-of-line) for seconds to minutes.

**Fix.** file.write: return the counts guardrail::enforce already computed (or call the linear changed_line_counts); everywhere else build diffs with `TextDiff::configure().timeout(Duration::from_millis(200))`, and skip blobs that contain NUL or exceed a size cap before reading them into strings.

**Verifier note.** The strongest trigger is binary files, not text rewrites. A modified binary asset in git (a .uasset, .umap or PNG without LFS) is split on '\n' into tens to hundreds of thousands of mostly distinct pseudo-lines. With LFS, HEAD holds a 3-line pointer while the working file is the real binary, which is the worst case: d runs to about m/2 with about d iterations each. Either way, committing or viewing such a file in the Code panel can pin a core for seconds to minutes, and the whole asset is read into a String first. Under the lock in file.write, the trigger needs a near-total rewrite of a large file: about 1-3 s at 20k lines, about 0.1 s at 5k. That is real but less common. Fixes: file.write should reuse the linear changed_line_counts, since only counts are needed. Elsewhere, detect binary (NUL in the first 8 KiB of the raw bytes) and cap size before converting or diffing, and build diffs with `TextDiff::configure().timeout(..)`.

**Skeptic note.** Corrections to the finding:
1. **Lead with the binary/LFS trigger in the unlocked git paths, not the store-mutex stall.**
   - LFS makes working-tree diffs (git.diff, git.diff.file) the worst case: 3-line pointer vs the full smudged binary.
   - Staged and commit numstat compare pointer to pointer, so they are fast with LFS. They are slow only for non-LFS binaries.
   - '\r' also splits lines in similar, which doubles a binary's pseudo-line count and makes it about 4x slower.
   - Regenerated lockfiles rarely hit the bad case, because most of their lines are unchanged.
2. **The cost figures are overstated.** A fully rewritten 20k-line file is about 4e8 Myers iterations (about n² for distinct n=m), roughly 0.5-1.5 s, not about 1e9 and "seconds". The file.write case is also not limited to near-total rewrites: a small file overwritten with large distinct content costs about 0.34·m², and the destructive_write gate allows it.
3. **"Stalling every session" is wrong for keystrokes.** User session.input and session.resize skip the store (D148). What stalls is store-backed requests: agents' hook and MCP calls, and UI queries.
4. **The git cost blocks only the requesting connection,** but the native UI uses one control connection, so all its engine calls queue behind it with 30 s timeouts.

Related, but a separate root cause: git.diff.file returns the whole lossy-decoded binary as `new`, and again in `hunks`. The native client caps the control channel at 2 MiB (client.rs:47, 192-197). Opening the diff of almost any non-image binary therefore tears down the UI's engine connection ("frame exceeds 2 MiB"; app.rs:1267-1275). The binary/size guard fixes both problems.

Fix caveats:
- **file.write:** call `changed_line_counts` (make it `pub(crate)`). Getting the counts back out of `enforce` would need plumbing, because enforce returns `()` and `evaluate_granted` may evaluate twice. Multiset semantics stop counting moved lines as changed, so document that for `WriteOut`.
- **Binary detection:** test raw bytes (a NUL in the first 8 KiB) before `from_utf8_lossy`.
- **LFS:** treat an LFS pointer on the old side, or an oversized blob, as binary.
- **git.diff.file:** give DiffFileOut a binary/too-large flag and send no content for those files.
- **Time budget:** a 200 ms per-file deadline still adds up across many files in git.diff, so use a total budget too.

**Blind re-check note.** The git paths (git.diff, git.diff.file, git.show, and git.commit's staged_numstat, which runs in the unlocked prepare phase) do not hold the store mutex. Their cost is head-of-line blocking of the UI's single socket connection, because socket.rs awaits each spawn_blocking dispatch in turn. It is not a bus-wide stall. file.write cannot hit the binary case, because read_to_string fails on non-UTF-8 and leaves `old` empty, so the diff is cheap. The 10^9-comparison estimate for a fully rewritten 20k-line file is about right (roughly 8e8 cheap u32 steps, about 1-2 s). The 'seconds to minutes' figure applies only to multi-MB distinct binaries in the git paths, and regenerated lockfiles usually change too few lines to be expensive.

#### RA-146 · file.write replaces a symlink with a regular file; file.create and file.import follow a dangling symlink out of the worktree

`crates/relay-core/src/handlers/file.rs:115` · **medium** · Bug · confirmed · effort S

**Problem.** safe_join (file.rs:489-506) validates `fs::canonicalize(path)` but returns the unresolved `root.join(rel)`. Write reads through the link with `fs::read_to_string(&path)` (so expected_sha256 matches), then calls `fs::rename(&temp, &path)` (115), which replaces the link itself. For a dangling link, `path.exists()` is false, so safe_join only canonicalizes the parent. Create's `fs::write(&path, text)` (154) and Import's `fs::copy` (624) then open the link target wherever it points. The guardrail's write_target treats any relative path as InWorktree without resolving links (guardrail.rs:628-630). The Code tree treats symlinks as files and opens them in the editor (editor.rs:748).

**Impact.** Editing a symlinked file such as CLAUDE.md -> AGENTS.md in the editor and saving turns CLAUDE.md into an independent copy. AGENTS.md keeps the old text, so Codex agents read stale instructions, and git shows a typechange the user may commit. Separately, an agent (file.create is on its MCP surface) can plant a dangling link and make Relay write a file outside every write root.

**Fix.** Use symlink_metadata in safe_join. Either refuse symlinks for write/create/import, or operate on the canonical target (temp file in the target's directory, renamed onto the target). Open new files with create_new(true) and O_NOFOLLOW.

**Verifier note.** The escape only creates new files: an existing outside target canonicalizes outside root and is rejected, and Create refuses existing paths. Import is Actors::UserOnly, so only file.create is agent-reachable. An agent that can run `ln -s` can usually write outside the worktree through its shell directly, and the same unresolved-symlink gap applies to the provider's native Write tool through the hook guardrail. The escape is therefore a secondary guardrail weakness, and the symlink-clobber on save is the main user-visible bug. Medium is correct.

#### RA-147 · Directory-level rename/move/delete bypass protected paths of the files inside the directory

`crates/relay-core/src/handlers/file.rs:180` · **medium** · Security · confirmed · effort M

**Problem.** Rename checks only `from_rel` and `into_rel` (L180-181), Move does the same (L209-210), Delete checks only the named path (L224), and Import only the top-level `dest_rel` (L286). path_matches matches a path inside a protected pattern but never an ancestor of one (guardrail.rs:1164). **Fix.** When the operand is a directory, refuse if any protected pattern could match beneath it (pattern starts with `<dir>/`, or a glob whose literal prefix overlaps), or walk the directory and check each descendant.

#### RA-148 · Agents can aim file.* mutations at any project and any worktree of it; nothing confines them to their own checkout

`crates/relay-core/src/handlers/file.rs:420` · **medium** · Security · confirmed · effort M

**Problem.** root_choice does `let project = get_project(conn, project_id)?; let chosen = default_worktree_in(conn, session_id, &project, requested)?;` with no check that `project_id` is the actor session's project, and default_worktree_in accepts `Some(PROJECT_ROOT) => Ok(repo)` and `Some(path) => Ok(PathBuf::from(path))` (L399-400). guardrail::enforce is then called with that caller-chosen `root` (L93-96), so evaluate_write treats every relative path as in-worktree. guardrail::authorize checks only `session`/`task_id` payload fields (guardrail.rs:328-349). Other handlers do enforce ownership: overlap.rs:76-77 `not_own("project")`, notes.rs assert_actor_project, session.rs assert_same_project. The hook path (handlers/guardrail.rs:516,608) always judges the session's own worktree. rel() also never refuses `.git`/`.relay` components and the default protected_paths list is empty (settings.rs:31).

**Impact.** A session with bus_writes can write, rename, move or trash files in the project's primary checkout, in peer agents' worktrees, and in any other registered project (the target project's guardrail config is the one applied). For a provider that runs sandboxed, the engine performs those writes outside the sandbox. Repository metadata and Relay-generated files under `.git/` and `.relay/` are reachable the same way, so other guardrail layers can be undermined.

**Fix.** For agent actors, require payload project_id == own session's project (one shared assert like assert_actor_project) and, for mutations, require the resolved root to be the session's own worktree unless a user grant covers it. In rel() (mutation callers) refuse any `.git` or `.relay` component.

**Verifier note.** This requires the opt-in per-session `bus_writes` (off by default, BUS.md §9.1), which is why it is high rather than critical. file.restore (L237-251) is also unscoped: it trusts the trash row's worktree and checks only project_id. Fix: for agent actors, require payload project_id to equal the session's project. For mutations, require the resolved root to equal the session's own worktree unless a user grant covers it. Refuse `.git` and `.relay` components in rel() for mutations.

**Skeptic note.** Severity: medium, not high.

1. The first verifier's "off by default" is only true of the engine (store.rs:90, session.rs:809). The native launch dialog defaults bus_writes on (launch.rs:264-265).
2. Applying the target project's guardrail config is the correct config for the target files. The only check that does not run is the own-tree / write-root boundary. Protected paths, shape gates and destructive-write holds all still run.
3. The `.git` code-execution and sandbox points add nothing under BUS.md §0.6, §4.2 and §14. The agent's Bash, and every Codex edit, are already unchecked for write targets, and Relay launches no provider sandboxed. A new `.git/hooks` file written via file.write is also not executable (permissions are copied only from an existing file, L111-114), but `.git/config` is writable.
4. Related locations to add: git.rs:491, 508, 543 (git.stage, git.unstage, git.commit via resolve_root at 751-777), and file.rs:238-251 (file.restore trusts the trash row's worktree and checks only project_id).

Fix:
- Put the check on the mutation path, not in root_choice, because queries also use root_choice and agent_surface.rs:177 pins `@project` for git.status.
- For agent actors, require project_id to equal the session's project, mirroring notes.rs assert_actor_project.
- Require the canonical resolved root to equal the canonical session.worktree. This is safe for PAIR and shared-worktree groups, which reuse one worktree (session.rs:778-800), and for sessions launched on the primary checkout. Use an explicit grant for exceptions.
- Apply the same check to git.stage, git.unstage and git.commit.
- Refuse `.git` and `.relay` components for agent mutations only, so a user's edit of `.git/info/exclude` is not blocked.
- Update D111 and BUS.md:816, which advertise `@project` "throughout git.* and file.*", and the stale BUS.md:839.
- Say plainly that this restores consistency, not containment, per §0.6.

#### RA-149 · safe_join requires the parent to exist, so nested creates, writes and restores fail and the create_dir_all calls are dead

`crates/relay-core/src/handlers/file.rs:494` · **medium** · Bug · confirmed · effort M

**Problem.** For a path that does not exist, `fs::canonicalize(path.parent().unwrap_or(root))` (L494) returns ENOENT whenever the parent is also missing, which becomes `file.not_found`. So `fs::create_dir_all(parent)` in Write (L105), Create (L151) and Restore (L247) never creates anything, and Create kind=dir only works one level deep. The UI's create dialog suggests `relative/path.rs` (editor.rs:1203). For existing paths, canonicalize(path) follows the final symlink (L492, L496), so links that point outside the worktree, or dangle, cannot be deleted, renamed or moved.

**Impact.** Common flows fail: creating `newdir/file.rs` from the UI, an agent writing a file in a new module directory, restoring a trashed file whose folder was trashed too. The user also cannot remove an outward or broken symlink from the Code page.

**Fix.** Canonicalize the deepest existing ancestor and check containment there. Treat the final component with symlink_metadata, so ops act on the link itself rather than its target.

**Verifier note.** Restore only fails when the file's parent directory is itself gone, for example when a file is trashed and then its folder is trashed separately. Trashing a folder moves its children with it, so that case is narrower than the finding suggests. Agents mostly write through their own harness tools, so the main exposure is the Code-page create dialog and MCP file_write/file_create. Fix: walk up to the deepest existing ancestor, canonicalize it and check starts_with(root). Every remaining component is a plain Normal component, guaranteed by rel(). For Delete, Rename and Move, canonicalize only the parent and use symlink_metadata on the final component.

#### RA-150 · git.log walks breadth-first, so a parent can come before its child and the history graph grows phantom lanes

`crates/relay-core/src/handlers/git.rs:263` · **medium** · Bug · confirmed · effort S

**Problem.** `repo.rev_walk([tip.detach()]).all()` uses gix's default Sorting::BreadthFirst: a FIFO queue with a seen-set (gix-traverse 0.60 simple.rs:44, 597-602, 669-670). That is neither date order (like git log) nor topological order. Example: M merges A (main, parent X) and F2<-F1 (feature, parent X). The walk yields M, A, F2, X, F1, so X comes before its child F1. The desktop graph (code_git.rs:1822-1897) reserves a lane for each parent 'until the corresponding commit arrives'. F1 reserves a lane for X after X has already been emitted, so that lane never closes. LogIn.graph is accepted but ignored.

**Impact.** In any history where merged branches have different lengths, which is routine with agent branches, the history pane draws a lane that never ends, and commits appear in a different order from git log.

**Fix.** Use `.sorting(Sorting::ByCommitTime(CommitTimeOrder::NewestFirst))` for the list, and gix's topological walk when graph is requested.

**Verifier note.** Use `.sorting(Sorting::ByCommitTime(CommitTimeOrder::NewestFirst))` to match git log's default. Note that commit-time order alone still breaks under clock skew, so the graph view ideally needs a topological order (gix_traverse's topo walk) or a client-side topo sort before `commit_graph`.
