#### RA-151 · git.branches still runs a merge-base walk per branch with no object cache; the PERF §1.3 fix went only into the duplicate branches_for

`crates/relay-core/src/handlers/git.rs:326` · **medium** · Performance · confirmed · effort S

**Problem.** The git.branches handler computes merged per branch with `head.as_ref().and_then(|h| repo.merge_base(*h, id.detach()).ok())` (324-328), on a repo opened without object_cache_size_if_unset. branches_for (1445-1513) builds the same Branch rows with a single merged_tips walk and a 16 MiB object cache. Commit f2789df changed only branches_for: the handler is identical in f2789df~1 and f2789df. Yet FIXES-2026-09-20.md:24 credits git.branches with '§1.3: one walk decides merged for every branch; object cache on'. The owners SQL is also duplicated: worktree_owners_by_branch (18-32) vs an inline copy (1463-1474).

**Impact.** git.branches runs on every git-panel refresh, i.e. continuously while agents work. PERF §1.3 measured this algorithm at 520 ms CPU and 545 MB allocated for about 150 branches and 65 commits. That cost repeats on every refresh in a busy repo, and the two copies will keep drifting apart.

**Fix.** Keep one function that builds Branch rows (merged_tips, object cache, owners map). Call it from git.branches and from the delete/clean paths, running it unlocked. Correct the FIXES table.

**Verifier note.** Calibrate the impact. The handler runs unlocked, so it never blocks the bus. The cost is CPU, allocation and Code-page latency, scaling as branches × distance to the base. The 520 ms / 545 MB figure was measured on clean_merged, not on git.branches, whose baseline was 10 ms on the perf fixture; on a large real repo with old branches it can reach hundreds of ms or more. The primary category is performance (an unapplied perf fix), with duplication and docs drift (the FIXES table row) as secondary. Fix: build the Branch rows in one helper that takes the owners map as a parameter, so it runs unlocked for git.branches and from ctx.tx() for the delete and clean paths. Have git.branches call it and add remote_branches. Correct FIXES-2026-09-20.md:24.

#### RA-152 · git.branch.create checks out the new branch in a live session's checkout, bypassing the guard that git.branch.switch enforces

`crates/relay-core/src/handlers/git.rs:366` · **medium** · Bug · confirmed · effort S

**Problem.** checkout defaults to true, and the handler runs `git switch -c <name> [start]` (366-374) in whatever root resolve_root returns, with no session-ownership check. BranchSwitch refuses the same move with git.checkout_session_owned ('This checkout belongs to the live session ..; its agent decides its branch', 389-401). The desktop branch picker always offers 'Create and switch' and sends checkout:true with the selected checkout (code_git.rs:974-1037), including an agent's worktree.

**Impact.** Creating a branch while viewing an agent's checkout moves that agent onto the new branch mid-task. Its later commits land on a branch that no session row records (sessions.branch goes stale), so branch-ownership checks and closed-session cleanup reason about the wrong branch.

**Fix.** When checkout is true, apply BranchSwitch's live-session owner check. Alternatively, offer only checkout:false for checkouts owned by a session.

**Verifier note.** The user explicitly chose 'Create and switch', so this is an inconsistency between the two guards rather than a silent action. Impact is a stale sessions.branch and an agent whose branch changes mid-task. Severity is medium at most. Separately, BranchCreate is registered with Engine::register, so the `git switch` (worktree::git_mutate, a plain Command::output() with no timeout) and the `git worktree list` inside root_verify both run while the store mutex is held. The same applies to Stage and Unstage. That breaks the CLAUDE.md invariants and is worth its own finding if no other auditor reported it.

#### RA-153 · Paths are passed to git as pathspecs, so a bracketed filename also stages (or, via file.restore_head, discards) its glob matches

`crates/relay-core/src/handlers/git.rs:502` · **medium** · Data loss · confirmed · effort S

**Problem.** Stage builds `vec!["add","--"]` plus the caller's paths (501-503). Unstage uses `reset HEAD --` or `rm --cached --` (521-527). file.restore_head runs `git_mutate(&root, &["checkout","--",&p.path])` (file.rs:256). A `--` separator does not disable pathspec magic. Verified: `git add -- "src/[id].tsx"` also staged src/i.tsx and src/d.tsx. validate_path only rejects `..` and absolute paths.

**Impact.** Bracketed names are routine in Next.js, SvelteKit and Nuxt (pages/[id].tsx, [slug]/page.tsx). Staging or unstaging one such file also stages or unstages any sibling whose name matches the character class. file.restore_head on such a file throws away uncommitted edits in those siblings. Names containing * or ? behave the same way.

**Fix.** Pass --literal-pathspecs (a global option placed before the subcommand), or set GIT_LITERAL_PATHSPECS=1, for these commands.

**Verifier note.** The trigger is rarer than the finding implies. The bracket class must match a real sibling, e.g. `[id].tsx` against `i.tsx` or `d.tsx`, or `app/[slug]/page.tsx` against `app/s/page.tsx`. Ordinary Next.js trees seldom have such siblings, and names containing `*` or `?` are rare. The consequence on file.restore_head is silent loss of uncommitted edits, so this is rated medium as data-loss in an uncommon edge case. Fix: pass `--literal-pathspecs` before the subcommand, or set GIT_LITERAL_PATHSPECS=1, in these three call sites. The simplest place is git_mutate's callers for path-taking ops.

**Also at:** `crates/relay-core/src/handlers/git.rs:526`, `crates/relay-core/src/handlers/file.rs:256`, `crates/relay-core/src/worktree.rs:36`

#### RA-154 · The commit gate judges a numstat taken before the lock, then `git commit` commits whatever the index holds at that later moment

`crates/relay-core/src/handlers/git.rs:557` · **medium** · Security · confirmed · effort M

**Problem.** prepare computes staged_numstat(&root) (557) with nothing locked. finish later passes it to `guardrail::enforce(.. Some(&numstat) ..)` and runs `git commit --no-verify` (561-572). That commits the index as it stands at that moment and skips the per-session pre-commit gate hook. Nothing ties the commit to the tree that was evaluated.

**Impact.** Anything staged between prepare and finish is committed without being checked against protected paths or caps: the agent's own `git add` in its shell, or another tool. An agent can simply retry until the race lands. Separately, outside this chunk: the default denied_commands (settings.rs:33) do not include `git commit --no-verify`, so an agent with a shell can skip the hook-based gate entirely.

**Fix.** Gate a snapshot. In prepare, run `git write-tree` and compute the numstat for that tree. In finish, commit exactly that tree: `git commit-tree <tree> -p HEAD -m ..`, then `git update-ref HEAD <new> <old>` as a compare-and-swap. Alternatively, recompute the numstat inside finish and refuse if it changed.

**Verifier note.** Calibration: the race on the bus path is the weaker part of this. Agents can call git.commit only with session.bus_writes (guardrail.rs:363-366; agent_surface.rs:111 asserts that a builder cannot by default). Every agent has a shell, and from there `git commit --no-verify` (or `-c core.hooksPath=...`) skips the commit gate outright, so the race adds little for an adversarial agent. On its own the race is low: the window is short and it needs concurrent staging, e.g. an agent staging in a checkout the user is committing from the desktop. The --no-verify shell bypass is the real guardrail escape (medium to high). It is arguably its own root cause and should be reported separately if no other auditor has. Fix the race by gating a snapshot: `git write-tree` in prepare, then commit-tree plus update-ref compare-and-swap in finish, or recompute the numstat in finish and refuse if it changed.

#### RA-155 · A submodule bump or a nested repository makes git.commit and git.diff fail outright

`crates/relay-core/src/handlers/git.rs:822` · **medium** · Bug · confirmed · effort S

**Problem.** revision_text does `let object = entry.object().map_err(gix_err("git.object"))?;` and index_text does `repo.find_object(entry.id).map_err(gix_err("git.object"))?` (836). Neither checks the entry mode. For a gitlink (mode 160000) the id is a commit in the submodule's repository, not in the superproject's object store (verified: `git cat-file -t <gitlink oid>` reports 'could not get object info'), so both return Err. staged_numstat (861-872) calls both for every staged path. The Diff handler (203-213) calls revision_text and working_text for every status path. Verified porcelain output: a staged submodule bump is `M  lib`, an untracked nested repository is `?? nested/`. working_text(root, "nested/") calls fs::read on a directory; the IsADirectory error is not NotFound, so it returns git.read_failed (844-847). tree_diff_files survives the same input only because it uses .ok().

**Impact.** Any commit through Relay that includes a submodule pointer update is refused in prepare with a cryptic git.object error. The desktop smart commit (all:true runs `git add -A`) in a worktree where an agent cloned a reference repo stages it as an embedded gitlink and then fails the same way. git.diff fails for the whole worktree whenever a submodule is modified or a nested repository is untracked.

**Fix.** Check the entry mode before loading. For gitlinks, return git's own text (`Subproject commit <oid>\n`) built from the entry id. Treat a missing object as empty via .ok(). In working_text, return empty for directories and other non-regular files.

**Verifier note.** Lowered to medium. Submodules and embedded clones are less common in this user's flows. The desktop does not call git.diff (only git.diff.file), so the visible failure is git.commit refusing a commit with a cryptic git.object error, plus agents' and the phone's git.diff. Fix: in revision_text and index_text, treat EntryKind::Commit as the text `Subproject commit <oid>\n` and map a missing object to empty. In working_text, use symlink_metadata and return empty, or the link target, for anything that is not a regular file. That overlaps with core-git#2's fix.

#### RA-156 · git.diff / git.diff.file follow symlinks out of the worktree and read without bound; a symlink to /dev/zero OOMs the engine

`crates/relay-core/src/handlers/git.rs:844` · **medium** · Bug · confirmed · effort S

**Problem.** working_text is `validate_path(path)?; match std::fs::read(root.join(path))`. validate_path only rejects `..` and absolute paths. fs::read follows symlinks and reads to EOF with no cap. file.rs guards this case for file.read with safe_join (file.rs:489-505: canonicalize, then refuse 'path escapes the worktree through a symlink'); git.rs has no equivalent. `git status --porcelain=v1 -z --untracked-files=all` lists untracked symlinks (verified: links to /etc/hostname and /dev/zero appear as `?? host`, `?? zero`). The Diff handler reads every listed path (211), and DiffFileOp reads the requested path (239) and returns its full text in `new`. Who can trigger it: both ops are queries any agent may call (MCP git_diff, git_diff_file); the desktop calls git.diff.file when a changed file is clicked (code_git.rs:1338); and the phone door can call them.

**Impact.** An agent, or a checked-in fixture, creates `ln -s /dev/zero z` in a worktree. The next git.diff, or a click on `z` in the git panel, makes the engine read /dev/zero until allocation fails, which kills the engine and every session. A symlink to ~/.ssh/id_ed25519 or a credentials file returns its contents through git.diff.file, where file.read would refuse. Because the engine is not sandboxed, this works even when the agent's own sandbox denies that read. Ordinary symlinks also diff wrongly: git stores a link as its target path, so a tracked symlink always shows as modified against the target file's contents.

**Fix.** Use symlink_metadata. For a symlink, return read_link as text (this is what git compares). For anything that is not a regular file, return empty. Cap the read (e.g. 8 MiB; mark larger files binary), and reuse file.rs's canonicalize-and-contain check for regular files.

**Verifier note.** The rating stays high rather than critical. The crash needs an agent (misbehaving or prompt-injected) or a checked-out fixture to plant a symlink to a device. Secret disclosure matters only where the agent's own shell reads are otherwise restricted, though the engine is unsandboxed and file.read shows containment is meant to be a boundary. Fix: use symlink_metadata. For a symlink, return read_link as text (git's view). For non-regular files, return empty. Cap regular-file reads (e.g. 8 MiB, flagged binary/truncated). Apply the same treatment to the directory/EISDIR case noted in core-git#6.

**Skeptic note.** Severity medium, category bug (robustness and correctness). Under BUS.md §4.2, §9.5 and §14, neither the read outside the worktree nor an agent-triggered crash crosses a trust boundary.

Two claims are imprecise:
1. "reads /dev/zero until allocation fails, which kills the engine": the engine dies from the kernel OOM killer or systemd-oomd once RAM and swap are full; with default heuristic overcommit, no allocation is refused first. In current std, read_to_end grows its buffer with try_reserve, so a refused allocation would return an io error and the engine would survive.
2. "a tracked symlink always shows as modified" is true only for git.diff.file. git.diff lists a link only when git reports it changed, and then counts it against the target's contents.

Fix:
- Call symlink_metadata first.
- For a symlink, return the read_link bytes; that is git's blob for mode 120000.
- For a FIFO, device, socket or directory, return empty. This also removes the FIFO hang and the EISDIR failure in core-git#6.
- Read regular files with File::open(..).take(cap+1), as file.read does, and mark a truncated file as binary.
- For git.diff.file, still canonicalize and check containment, because symlink_metadata sees only the last path component (e.g. `linkdir/id_ed25519` where linkdir -> ~/.ssh).

The same special-file read exists in two more places, which should use the same helper:
- overlap.rs:246: `std::fs::read(worktree.join(path)).unwrap_or_default()` reads the whole file before the 2 MiB check in symbols(). It is reached by overlap.scan and overlap.flag for changed .rs/.ts/.tsx/.svelte/.kt files.
- guardrail.rs:562-572 and 695-701: the 64 MiB guard uses metadata().len(), which follows the link and is 0 for a character device or FIFO. guardrail.gate is a locked Engine::register handler (handlers/guardrail.rs:304), so there the endless read would hold the store mutex.

<a id="ra-157"></a>

#### RA-157 · git.diff, git.show and the commit gate reopen the repo and reload the index per file, then run an unbounded Myers diff on whole file contents, binaries included

`crates/relay-core/src/handlers/git.rs:850` · **medium** · Performance · confirmed · effort M

**Problem.** counts is `TextDiff::from_lines(old,new)`. similar's default config has no deadline, and its own docs (algorithms/myers.rs:12-18) say large distinct inputs 'will make it spin without making reasonable progress'. It runs on whole files before any binary check: `binary: old.contains('\0')||...` is computed afterwards (224, 1246). The inputs are `String::from_utf8_lossy(..).to_string()` copies, which expand each invalid byte to a 3-byte U+FFFD. Each revision_text call does gix::open + rev-parse + tree peel (803-815). Each index_text call does gix::open + index_or_empty() (831-832), i.e. a full index decode per file. staged_numstat (861-872) and the Diff loop (203-231, which also does an O(n*m) `files.iter_mut().find`) call these for every changed path. tree_diff_files diffs every blob of a commit (1239). The desktop guards only images, by extension, before calling git.diff.file (code_git.rs:1325).

**Impact.** Committing modified non-LFS binary assets (.uasset/.umap/.blend, MBs to hundreds of MBs) via git.commit spins a worker in prepare for minutes or longer before the gate even runs. The client gives up after 30 s while the engine keeps working. Clicking such a file in the git panel, or opening a commit that changed one, does the same and allocates several times the file size. For LFS files the comparison is pointer vs smudged binary, so every modified LFS asset shows as a huge bogus diff. Staging thousands of files in a repo with a large index re-decodes that index thousands of times.

**Fix.** Open the repository and the index once per request and pass them down. Check size and binary-ness (NUL in the first 8 KiB) before reading whole files, and skip the text diff for binaries. Set a timeout with `TextDiff::configure().timeout(..)`. For the commit gate, run `git diff --cached --numstat -z -M` once; it handles binaries, renames and filters, and evaluate_commit already falls back to it.

**Verifier note.** Three corrections. (1) Severity is medium, not high. Every affected handler is register_unlocked or register_staged, so the store mutex is not held and the bus does not freeze. One blocking-pool thread burns a core and the calling client times out. (2) The LFS claim is wrong for the commit gate: HEAD and the index both hold LFS pointers, so staged_numstat compares pointer to pointer, which is cheap. It holds only for unstaged git.diff and git.diff.file, where working_text reads the smudged binary and compares it with the HEAD pointer. (3) The desktop never calls the list-form git.diff; only MCP agents do. The fix is right: open the repo and index once per request, check for NUL in the first 8 KiB and for size before decoding and diffing, and set `TextDiff::configure().timeout(..)`. For the gate, use `git diff --cached --numstat -z -M` through proc::output_with_timeout.

#### RA-158 · Commit gate ignores the source path of a staged rename: protected files can be moved out unchallenged, and renames count as whole-file additions

`crates/relay-core/src/handlers/git.rs:867` · **medium** · Security · confirmed · effort S

**Problem.** parse_status records renamed_from (worktree.rs:109-111). staged_numstat ignores it: per entry it does `let old = revision_text(root, "HEAD", &s.path)?; let new = index_text(root, &s.path)?; ... push_str(format!("{a}\t{r}\t{}\n", s.path))`. Verified: `git mv secrets/config.yml moved.yml` gives porcelain `R  moved.yml\0secrets/config.yml`, so the numstat line is `50\t0\tmoved.yml`. The old path never appears, and because HEAD has nothing at the new path, the whole file counts as added. evaluate_commit (guardrail.rs:765-781) matches protected_paths only against the paths in this numstat. The Diff handler looks up the old side by the new path in the same way (207).

**Impact.** When protected paths are configured, an agent refactor that moves a protected file elsewhere commits through git.commit with no protected-path refusal or hold. A deliberate `git mv protected/x x` does the same. The file leaves its protected location without a grant. Conversely, moving any file longer than the line cap (default 2000) counts as that many added lines and triggers a false guardrail.cap hold. git.diff shows renamed files as entirely new.

**Fix.** Treat a rename as touching both paths: add renamed_from to the touched list and read the old text from renamed_from. Simpler: feed the gate from `git diff --cached --numstat -z -M`, which reports both paths and handles binaries.

**Verifier note.** The bypass is specific to the in-process git.commit op (MCP git_commit and the desktop Commit button). A shell `git commit` goes through the pre-commit hook, where `request.diff` is None and evaluate_commit falls back to `git diff --cached --numstat`. That output reports a rename as `old => new`, so prefix or `**` patterns still match the old path. Fix: add `renamed_from` to the touched paths and read the old side from `renamed_from` (in staged_numstat and in Diff at 207). Alternatively, have both paths use `git diff --cached --numstat -z -M`, parse its separate old and new path fields, and feed both to the protected-path check.

**Skeptic note.** 1. Severity: medium, not high (see reason).

2. Agents can reach git.commit only when the session has `bus_writes` (off by default). The finding's impact statement leaves this out. From the desktop Commit button, the user loses only a confirmation prompt.

3. The first verifier said the shell `git commit` route still catches renames with prefix or `**` patterns. That is only partly true. With default git config, `git diff --cached --numstat` (guardrail.rs:760) compacts paths. Verified outputs:
- `0 0 secrets/config.yml => moved.yml`
- `0 0 {secrets => lib}/config.yml`
- `0 0 config/{secrets => }/prod.yml`

A port of `path_matches` gives these results:
- `secrets` and `secrets/**` match only the first form.
- An exact-file pattern such as `secrets/config.yml` never matches.
- The brace forms match neither. They are the usual output when a file moves to another directory under the same name, so `migrations/**` misses `{migrations => db/migrations}/x.sql`.

So the default agent route, the pre-commit hook, has the same blind spot for most renames. The root cause is `evaluate_commit`'s input in both routes. The broader reach is still bounded by protected_paths being opt-in.

4. The cap symptom is a refusal for an agent: `refused` with code `guardrail.cap` and an exception hint. Only the user gets a hold (`guardrail.user_bypass`). It also fires for directory moves whose files total more than 2000 lines, not only for one large file.

5. Fix caveats:
- Do not add the rename source to staged_numstat as an extra numstat line. `evaluate_commit` counts files per line, so every rename would count twice against caps.files: a 25-file directory move would count as 50, over the default 40. The source path must be matched against protected patterns but counted once.
- Preferred fix: produce both inputs, staged_numstat's replacement and the `None` fallback at guardrail.rs:760, from `git diff --cached --numstat -z -M`. Give `evaluate_commit` a `-z` parser. Verified format: `a\tr\tpath\0`, and for renames `a\tr\t\0old\0new\0`. `-M` forces rename detection whatever `diff.renames` says. Match protected patterns against both old and new paths. This also yields real counts (0/0 for a pure rename), which removes the false cap.
- In git.diff (git.rs:207), read the old side from `renamed_from` when it is present.
- Add a regression test covering an exact-file pattern, a directory pattern, a same-name move out of the protected directory, and both commit routes.

**Also at:** `crates/relay-core/src/worktree.rs:109`, `crates/relay-core/src/guardrail.rs:765`, `crates/relay-core/src/handlers/git.rs:207`

#### RA-159 · tree_diff_files reports directories as changed files in git.show and git.diff {base}

`crates/relay-core/src/handlers/git.rs:1238` · **medium** · Bug · confirmed · effort S

**Problem.** The callback matches Addition, Deletion, Modification and Rewrite and pushes a DiffFile for every non-empty location; it never checks entry_mode. gix-diff 0.66 emits changes for tree entries: a (tree, tree) pair with different ids is visited as Change::Modification before it recurses (gix-diff tree/function.rs:301-320); whole subtrees are visited as Addition/Deletion (131-191); and the rewrite tracker passes tree modifications straight through (rewrites/tracker.rs:171-184). <a id="ra-160"></a>

#### RA-160 · Timed-out git switch / worktree add / status are SIGKILLed, leaving a stale index.lock that blocks every later git command

`crates/relay-core/src/handlers/git.rs:1350` · **medium** · Error handling · confirmed · effort S

**Problem.** Budgets: run_switch bounds git switch with output_with_timeout(.., 120s); worktree::create does the same for git worktree add (worktree.rs:214); status_files uses 10 s (worktree.rs:91); fetch uses 20 s (945). At the deadline, proc.rs:55 sends SIGKILL to the process group, and git cannot remove its lock files on SIGKILL. Verified: a git switch killed during a slow smudge left .git/index.lock behind, and the next `git switch` failed "Unable to create '.../index.lock': File exists". With SIGTERM instead, git removed the lock. run_switch's doc comment ('every refusal leaves the checkout as it was', 1345-1346) is false on this path. The client gives these ops 30 s (client.rs:65-70). Its table entry `git.worktree.create` names no op (the op is `worktree.create`). So the UI reports failure while the engine keeps switching for up to 120 s, and a retry collides with the first run's lock.

**Impact.** A switch or worktree creation that overruns its budget leaves the checkout half-updated and locked; this is plausible with LFS smudge of large Unreal assets. Every later git command there fails, for the user and for agents, until someone deletes index.lock by hand. A killed `git worktree add` also leaves a registered half-checkout plus the new branch, so the retry fails with worktree.exists.

**Fix.** In output_with_timeout, send SIGTERM to the group, wait a short grace period (1-2 s), then SIGKILL. When a mutating git command times out, say so and check for a leftover lock. Align the client's per-op timeouts with the engine's budgets and fix the op name in the client table.

**Verifier note.** session.create already gets 180 s on the client, which covers the 20 s fetch plus the 120 s add. The client-mismatch part applies only to git.branch.switch and worktree.create. status_files is a real trigger too, because of GIT_OPTIONAL_LOCKS=1. Fix: in output_with_timeout, send SIGTERM to the group, wait 1-2 s, then send SIGKILL (pty.rs:342-349 already does this). Fix the client op name and give git.branch.switch more than 120 s.

#### RA-161 · v3 import copies attachments to dest_dir.join(original_name) and reads v3 `path` unchecked: path traversal, arbitrary file write/read, silent overwrite

`crates/relay-core/src/handlers/import_v3.rs:262` · **medium** · Security · confirmed · effort S

**Problem.** Lines 243-266: `let candidates = if Path::new(&path).is_absolute() { vec![PathBuf::from(&path)] } else { vec![dir.join(&path), repo.join(&path)] }; ... let dest_dir = attach_root.join(new_id.to_string()); std::fs::create_dir_all(&dest_dir).bus()?; let dest = dest_dir.join(&name); std::fs::copy(&src, &dest).bus()?;` where `name` = v3 `attachments.original_name` and `path` = v3 `attachments.path`, both straight from the untrusted relay.db. Path::join with an absolute `name` replaces the base and `../` climbs out of `<store dir>/attachments/<id>/`. v4's own attach path (task.rs:490 `safe_name` keeps only file_name() and rejects ./..; task.rs:523 writes `{id}-{name}`) does neither of these things for the importer.

**Impact.** Importing a crafted v3 store (a repo that committed `.relay/relay.db`, or one an agent wrote into a checkout the user then types into the onboarding import field) with original_name `../../../../.local/bin/git` copies attacker bytes, exec bits preserved by fs::copy, to an arbitrary path (PATH dir, ~/.bashrc, or `<store dir>/store.db`, corrupting the live store); an absolute `path` such as ~/.ssh/id_rsa is copied into Relay's attachment store and served by task views. Benign data breaks too: two attachments of one task named `image.png` (clipboard pastes) land on one file, so the second silently overwrites the first while both rows point at it; a name containing '/' or equal to '' / '..' makes fs::copy fail and `?` aborts the whole import.

**Fix.** Reuse task.rs `safe_name` and the `{attachment_id}-{name}` naming (insert the row first, as attach_bytes does); canonicalize each source candidate and require it to stay under the v3 .relay dir/repo; downgrade per-attachment failures to warnings instead of aborting the import.

**Verifier note.** Downgraded from high. app.import.v3 is `Actors::UserOnly` (relay-bus ops/app.rs), so no agent can call it with a crafted source. The exploit needs the user to type the path of an attacker-crafted v3 store into onboarding or the CLI. The importer exists to migrate the user's own v3 data, so that is unlikely. The duplicate-name overwrite is the more realistic harm. The fix stands: insert the row first and write to `{attachment_id}-{safe_name(name)}`, require each canonicalized source to stay under the v3 .relay dir or repo, and turn per-attachment failures into warnings.

**Also at:** `crates/relay-core/src/handlers/task.rs:490`, `crates/relay-core/src/handlers/task.rs:523`, `apps/relay-native/src/onboarding.rs:532`, `crates/relay-core/src/handlers/import_v3.rs:283`, `crates/relay-core/src/handlers/import_v3.rs:246`, `crates/relay-core/tests/store.rs:108`

#### RA-162 · v3 import writes guardrail caps without validation; 0, negative or >u32 values break every agent mutation in the project

`crates/relay-core/src/handlers/import_v3.rs:317` · **medium** · Bug · confirmed · effort S

**Problem.** `let files = s.get("max_files").and_then(Value::as_i64); ... crate::handlers::settings::set(tx, &path, &json!({ "files": files, "lines": lines }), &now)?;` with path guardrails.projects.<id>.caps, committed without re-reading the config. GuardrailCaps fields are u32 (crates/relay-bus/src/types.rs:175-176), validate_config rejects 0 (guardrail.rs:293-295), and guardrail::config -> typed() deserializes+validates on every read; authorize calls it for every agent mutation (guardrail.rs:358). guardrail.config.set validates the merged result before committing (handlers/guardrail.rs:97-98). The import also emits no settings.changed / guardrail.config_changed.

**Impact.** A v3 sessions.json entry with max_files 0 (a common 'no limit' convention), a negative number or one above u32::MAX commits a project layer that fails typed(); from then on every agent mutation in that project (session.report, task.move, guardrail.gate...) is refused with 'invalid guardrail config' until the user repairs the layer.

**Fix.** Skip non-positive/out-of-range caps with a warning, and after writing call guardrail::config_for(tx, ConfigScope::Project(project.id))? so an invalid layer rolls the import back; emit guardrail.config_changed.

**Verifier note.** The mechanism is certain. I could not establish whether v3 ever wrote 0 or negative caps (no v3 source in the repo), so how often this triggers is unknown. The user can recover with guardrail.config.set or settings.reset on the project caps path. Fix: skip non-positive or out-of-range values with a warning, call guardrail::config_for(tx, ConfigScope::Project(id))? after writing so an invalid layer rolls the import back, and emit guardrail.config_changed.

#### RA-163 · integration.request lets an agent act on any project_id, unlike handlers that refuse not_own("project")

`crates/relay-core/src/handlers/integration.rs:17` · **medium** · Security · confirmed · effort S

**Problem.** `let project = get_project(ctx.tx(), p.project_id)?;` and nothing compares it with the caller's session. guardrail::authorize only scopes payload fields named `session`/`task_id` (guardrail.rs:328-349) and fill_identity fills project_id only when omitted (engine.rs:1150-1165). notes::assert_actor_project (notes.rs:47-55), overlap.rs:68-79 and session.rs:195-204 all refuse a foreign project for agents; BUS.md §9.1 draws the agent boundary at the caller's own project.

**Impact.** A builder agent in project A passing project B's id creates worktrees and relay/integration-N branches in B's repository, runs B's build_cmd on B's branches and, with deploy, installs on a device, all audited as A's agent. integration.get/list return other projects' build log tails to agents, and ui.layout.save/delete (allow_ui) accept any project_id the same way.

Agents usually also have a shell as the same OS user, so this mainly gives cross-project build/deploy and log reads through the bus with mis-attributed audit, not a new code-execution primitive. Fix: enforce project_id scope for agent callers once in guardrail::authorize (compare payload project_id with session.project_id), or apply assert_actor_project in integration.request/get/list and ui.layout.*.

#### RA-164 · Integrations interrupted by quit or crash stay merging/building/deploying forever and permanently block project and workspace removal

`crates/relay-core/src/handlers/integration.rs:40` · **medium** · Bug · confirmed · effort S

**Problem.** The run is a detached `std::thread::spawn(move || run(engine, id, parent))` with no registry. recovery::run_with (recovery.rs:53-213) resets sessions and device_runs but never integrations; Engine::shutdown ignores them; app.quit checks only `live_pty_count()` (app.rs:39-41). project.remove refuses 'force or not' while any row is in ('queued','merging','building','deploying') (workspace.rs:304-307, integrations_live at 387-391) with hint 'wait for the integration to finish'; registry_remove.rs:150 inserts exactly such a 'merging' row.

**Verifier note.** Downgraded from high to medium. The trigger is quitting or crashing during an integration run, which is a less common path. An escape exists, though not in the UI: a generic bus or CLI call of integration.discard. Fix: in recovery, mark queued/merging/building/deploying rows failed with finished_at and an 'interrupted by restart' log line, have app.quit without force report running integrations, and keep the child handle so shutdown can kill it.

#### RA-165 · integration.discard removes the worktree (tree walks, rm -rf, untimed git) inside a locked `register` handler

`crates/relay-core/src/handlers/integration.rs:62` · **medium** · Invariant · confirmed · effort M

**Problem.** `e.register::<IntegrationDiscard>(...)` runs in the request transaction with the store mutex held and calls `worktree::remove(Path::new(&project.path), Path::new(path), true)` then `worktree::git_mutate(..., &["branch", "-D", ...])`. worktree::remove (worktree.rs:352-370) does purge_build (dir_size walk + remove_dir_all per build dir), a second dir_size over the whole checkout whose result this handler discards, then `git worktree remove --force` and `git worktree prune` via worktree::git, a bare `Command::output()` with no timeout (worktree.rs:26-33). D149 converted session.close/discard_restorable to register_staged for exactly this work (session.rs:1505, 1547); this op was missed. integration.request likewise runs gix::open + rev_parse_single per branch under the lock (lines 28-29), the gix work D149 moved out of transactions.

**Impact.** Discarding an integration that built (a Rust/Gradle/Unreal target tree of several GB, 100k+ files) holds the global store mutex for seconds to minutes; every other request queues behind it, including agents' guardrail.gate hooks on each tool call, session.report and the UI's ctx.read bursts. A git that hangs (hook, LFS, index lock) holds it forever. Breaks the CLAUDE.md rule that every subprocess forked from a handler goes through proc::output_with_timeout.

**Fix.** Register with register_staged: prepare reads the row via ctx.read and removes worktree + branch unlocked (git through output_with_timeout); finish only sets state='discarded'. Skip the size walk when the freed bytes are unused. Move integration.request's gix validation into a staged prepare as well. git.rs:129 worktree.remove needs the same change.

**Verifier note.** Downgraded from high to medium. Both integration.discard and worktree.remove are Actors::UserOnly, and neither has a caller in apps/relay-native, so they are reached only through a generic bus or CLI call. A real stall can happen but rarely does in normal use. The gix::open + rev_parse_single in integration.request (lines 28-29) costs milliseconds and is minor. Fix: register_staged, with prepare reading the row and doing the removal and branch delete unlocked (git through output_with_timeout) and finish setting state='discarded'. Skip the second dir_size when the freed byte count is not used.

#### RA-166 · Every merge failure is reported as a 'conflict' between the first two alphabetically sorted branches

`crates/relay-core/src/handlers/integration.rs:128` · **medium** · Bug · confirmed · effort M

**Problem.** `branches.sort(); branches.dedup();` (line 26) discards the caller's order; then `if let Err(error) = worktree::git_mutate(&path, &merge_args) { let pair = integration.branches.first().cloned().zip(integration.branches.get(1).cloned()); fail(..., IntegrationState::Conflict, &format!("merge: {error}"), pair) }` (128-141). Octopus refusal, a branch deleted after validation, a failing pre-merge-commit hook and unrelated histories all become Conflict, and the pair is whatever sorts first. SPEC §8: 'Conflicts abort with the pair named.'

**Impact.** With three or more agents selected, the Code page (`#id · conflict · a, b`, code_git.rs:752-766) tells the user two agents conflict when the conflict is between others; non-conflict failures send the user to resolve a conflict that does not exist.

**Fix.** Keep the caller's order; distinguish conflicts (unmerged paths / CONFLICT in output) from other failures (state failed); to name the pair, merge the branches one at a time with --no-commit and record which branch failed against which, or test pairwise after an octopus failure.

**Verifier note.** Sorting itself is harmless for octopus correctness; the defect is that the pair is fabricated. Fix: detect real conflicts (unmerged paths / CONFLICT lines) vs other errors (state failed), and find the pair by merging sequentially (or pairwise after an octopus failure) and recording which branch failed against which; show log_tail in the UI.

#### RA-167 · integration.request lets any builder agent have the engine run its branch's build outside any sandbox, with user-level bus rights

`crates/relay-core/src/handlers/integration.rs:165` · **medium** · Security · confirmed · effort M

**Problem.** `integration.request` is in the default builder allowlist (handlers/settings.rs:36; BUS.md:464). It accepts any two refs the agent names (lines 18-30) and `build` defaults to true (`p.build.unwrap_or(true)`, line 32). After commit, `run()` merges the branches into `.relay/integrations/<id>` and executes `shell(&path, command, None)` (165), which is `Command::new("fish")…args(["-lc", command])` … `cmd.output()` (229-234). That process inherits the engine's environment, with no RELAY_SESSION or RELAY_TOKEN and no timeout. `deploy` (207) runs the user's `run_cmd` with an agent-chosen `RELAY_DEVICE`, without the device lease that the user-only `device.*` ops take. The CLI falls back to actor `user` when RELAY_SESSION is absent (crates/relay-cli/src/main.rs:129), and BUS.md §4.2 says `user` needs no token.

**Impact.** An agent (prompt-injected, or a Codex agent inside its workspace-write sandbox) commits a malicious build step on its branch, such as Cargo build.rs, an npm prebuild or a Gradle task. It then calls `integration.request {branches:["main","relay/<self>"]}`. Relay runs that code as the user, with network and full filesystem, outside the provider sandbox and without any Claude permission prompt or exec gate. Any `relay cmd …` the build runs is actor `user`, so it can approve its own guardrail requests, change settings, or type into other sessions. A build that hangs pins the thread forever, and the hard-coded `fish` fails on machines without it.

**Fix.** Require user confirmation (a hold) before building or deploying an agent-requested integration, or make build and deploy user-only. Run the build with the requesting session's RELAY_SESSION/RELAY_TOKEN so its bus calls stay agent-scoped. Use proc::output_with_timeout and `sh -c` (or $SHELL) instead of `fish -lc`. Take the device lease for deploy.

**Verifier note.** Severity is medium, not high. Building agent code is the op's documented purpose (BUS.md builder row; D38), and the command is the user's own build_cmd. For Claude agents there is little extra power: they can already run `cargo build` themselves, and Relay's guardrail only inspects command lines, not what build.rs does. The real extra power is escaping the Codex OS sandbox and the agent-chosen deploy device with no lease. The claim that 'bus calls run as user' is the documented same-uid trade-off (BUS.md §4.2, §14: 'Tokens prevent misattribution, not determined impersonation'; guardrail.rs:849-850 calls the identity-shedding check best effort), so it adds no new capability. The missing timeout runs on a detached thread, not under the store lock: a hung build leaves the integration stuck in Building and leaks the process, but the bus stays responsive. Fix: put the agent-requested build/deploy behind a user hold (or make build/deploy user-confirmed), export the requester's RELAY_SESSION/RELAY_TOKEN, use proc::output_with_timeout, take the device lease for deploy, and do not hard-code fish.

**Also at:** `crates/relay-core/src/handlers/integration.rs:32`, `crates/relay-core/src/handlers/integration.rs:207`, `crates/relay-core/src/handlers/integration.rs:229`, `crates/relay-core/src/handlers/settings.rs:36`, `crates/relay-cli/src/main.rs:129`, `docs/engine/BUS.md:464`

#### RA-168 · Integration deploy re-implements device.run without the device lease, ANDROID_SERIAL or the default Gradle install

`crates/relay-core/src/handlers/integration.rs:232` · **medium** · Bug · confirmed · effort M

**Problem.** Deploy runs `shell(&path, command, Some(&device))` whose only device plumbing is `cmd.env("RELAY_DEVICE", device)` (lines 185-215, 228-234), and requires project.run_cmd (186-195: 'Deploy requested but no run command is configured.'). device.run first does `device_lease::check(ctx, &p.device, &holder)` and `device_lease::acquire(...)` (device.rs:150, 177), checks the device is ready, sets both RELAY_DEVICE and ANDROID_SERIAL (device.rs:1673) plus ANDROID_HOME, and with an empty run_cmd falls back to `./gradlew install<Variant>` (device.rs:1037-1055; the native project form labels an empty run command 'Gradle wrapper install task'). Without ANDROID_SERIAL a configured `./gradlew installDebug` installs on every connected device (device_lease.rs:28 says exactly this) and adb fails with more than one device; projects relying on the default Gradle install can never deploy an integration.

The run_cmd "" case is only reachable via a raw bus call: the native project form sends null for an empty field (registry.rs:926-931). Fix as proposed: after a passed build, start device.run with integration_id (resolve_run_root at device.rs:975 already accepts a passed integration) and the requesting session as lease holder.

#### RA-169 · Integration merge/build/deploy children are untimed, uncancellable, fully buffered, and survive discard

`crates/relay-core/src/handlers/integration.rs:234` · **medium** · Resource leak · confirmed · effort M

**Problem.** `let out = cmd.output().map_err(|e| e.to_string())?;` for `fish -lc <cmd>` (229-234); the merge goes through worktree::git_mutate, also a bare `.output()` (worktree.rs:27). No deadline, no process group, no handle kept; integration.discard has nothing to kill, and after a discard set_state returns Ok(()) silently (266-270) so run() proceeds to the next step. output() buffers the child's whole stdout+stderr before tail() keeps 12 KB.

**Impact.** A build or hook that hangs (waiting on a lock, device or prompt) leaves the integration building/deploying and its thread parked forever. Discarding a running build deletes the directory under cargo/gradle, which keep writing and recreate `.relay/integrations/<id>/target/...` outside any registered worktree, where nothing will ever remove it. A chatty long-running command grows engine memory without bound.

**Fix.** Model integrations like device runs: keep the Child (own process group) in a runtime map, stream output into a bounded ring buffer, enforce a configurable deadline, and have discard/shutdown kill the group before removing the worktree; make set_state signal 'discarded' so run() stops.

**Verifier note.** Calibrate the mechanism: Command::output() gives the child a null stdin, so an interactive prompt does not hang it; hangs come from locks/daemons/network. These threads are not bus handlers and hold no store lock, so this is not the CLAUDE.md output_with_timeout invariant in the strict sense; the cost is a stuck integration, a stuck thread and a blocked project.remove. Full buffering of build output is real but rarely large in practice. The 'cargo/gradle recreates target/ after discard' consequence is plausible (both create_dir_all their output dirs) but was not verified.

#### RA-170 · Mailbox and task-session lookups use the session name, which is recycled after close, so a new session inherits a dead namesake's inbox and outbox

`crates/relay-core/src/handlers/notes.rs:672` · **medium** · Bug · confirmed · effort M

**Problem.** Session names are drawn from 36x36=1296 adjective-animal pairs and are unique only among non-closed sessions (sessions.rs:73-89; store.rs:96 `CREATE UNIQUE INDEX sessions_live_name ... WHERE state != 'closed'`). MailboxList joins `LEFT JOIN message_recipients mr ON mr.message_id=m.id AND mr.session=?2` (672) on the name. MailboxOutbox filters `m.from_session = ?2` by name (640), as does the priority-pending check (293), and task.list's session filter uses `s.name=?` (task.rs:851). MailboxAck matches `session_id = ?3` (694).

**Impact.** Once a few hundred sessions have been closed, new sessions often get a recycled name. In the same project, the new agent's `mailbox.list {unread_only:true}` returns the old namesake's unacked mail, including system 'Your current assignment is Task #N' messages about someone else's task. Agents are told to read and ack unread mail, but every `mailbox.ack` on these fails with 'message N is not addressed to this session', so they stay unread forever. `mailbox.outbox` shows the namesake's sends, the namesake's unacked priority mail can block new priority sends, and task.list {session} plus the board's agent filter attribute the old session's cards to the new one.

**Fix.** Resolve the requested or actor session to its live id and filter `mr.session_id = ?`. Store the sender's session id on messages (migration) for the outbox and priority checks, or at minimum bound them by `sent_at >= session.created_at`. Filter task.list's session by the live session id.

**Verifier note.** How often this hits scales with N/1296 for N closed names in the same project, so it is common for long-lived projects and rare early on. The decisive harm is the un-ackable stale unread mail. The outbox and priority mix-ups are minor. The fix is as proposed: filter MailboxList by `mr.session_id` resolved from the live session (the column and index already exist), and key task.list's session filter on the live session id. For the outbox and priority checks, store the sender's session_id (migration) or bound by the session's created_at.

`crates/relay-core/src/handlers/notify.rs:71` · **medium** · Performance · confirmed · effort M

**Problem.** perf.rs:844-845 says 'A refusal leaves a notification and a hold leaves a row; neither can be deleted', and :755 says 'Messages have no delete'. The only DELETEs are on project removal (workspace.rs:356, 367); recovery prunes only the audit table. notify.list is registered with engine.register (86) and builds `SELECT * FROM notifications WHERE 1=1 [AND read=0] ORDER BY created_at DESC,id DESC LIMIT ?` (58-71). Both indexes lead with project_id or category (store.rs:138-139). EXPLAIN QUERY PLAN on that schema (scratch test, SQLite 3.53) gives 'SCAN notifications' plus 'USE TEMP B-TREE FOR ORDER BY' for the shell's `{"unread_only":true,"limit":100}` (shell.rs:756, re-run on every notify.* event per app.rs:1197-1199) and for the notification center's `{"limit":100}` (notification_center.rs:134). The committed baseline measured 780 us with 203 rows against 28 us with 2.

**Impact.** Every guardrail refusal or hold, provider update and session report adds a row that is kept forever. The unread-count refresh that follows each notification scans and sorts the whole table while holding the mutex. Its cost, and the stall it puts on every other locked request, grows linearly over the life of the install.

**Fix.** Append a migration that adds an index on (read, created_at) and one on created_at, and bump SCHEMA_VERSION. Add a retention pass next to the audit retention in recovery, for example deleting read notifications and read mail older than N days.

**Verifier note.** The impact is slower than the finding implies. Rows are small and grow at roughly tens per day, and session.input does not touch SQLite (D148), so keystrokes do not stall. What slows is every other locked request during the refresh, by a few milliseconds per tens of thousands of rows. That is medium, not high. A single index on (read, created_at) serves both the unread_only and the plain listing, because SQLite can walk created_at in order with read=0 as a prefix, or skip-scan it. Retention for read notifications and acknowledged messages fits beside the audit retention in recovery.rs. I did not check the messages/mailbox query plan separately.

**Also at:** `crates/relay-core/src/store.rs:138`, `apps/relay-native/src/shell.rs:756`, `apps/relay-native/src/notification_center.rs:134`, `crates/relay-core/src/handlers/workspace.rs:367`, `crates/relay-core/examples/perf.rs:844`

#### RA-172 · notify.settings.set stores `before` as a merge patch, so audit.undo cannot remove keys the change added

`crates/relay-core/src/handlers/notify.rs:150` · **medium** · Bug · confirmed · effort S

**Problem.** `let before = settings::get(ctx.tx(), Some("notifications"))?; ... merge_value(&mut next, &payload.patch); settings::set(ctx.tx(), "notifications", &next, &ctx.now)?; ctx.set_undo("notify.settings.set", json!({"patch":before}), None);` audit.undo replays that envelope through the same handler (audit.rs:68), i.e. merge_value(current, before), which only touches keys present in the patch. guardrail.config.set computes guardrail::inverse_patch(&before, &merged) for exactly this reason (handlers/guardrail.rs:103, guardrail.rs:242). Reproduced in a Python model: after patch {categories:{integration:false}} and its undo, categories.integration is still false.

**Impact.** The native Settings save always patches notifications.categories.<cat> (tools_settings.rs:664), adding keys to the default-empty `categories`. Undoing that change via audit.undo (CLI/MCP/phone) reports success and marks the audit row undone, so it cannot be retried, while the category settings stay changed.

**Fix.** Record `json!({"patch": guardrail::inverse_patch(&before, &next)})`, or record the undo as settings.set {path:"notifications", value: before} (a full replacement).

**Verifier note.** Lines are notify.rs:146-150 (set_undo at 150). The impact is narrow: only keys that were absent before are not reverted, and in practice those are notification category toggles. sound/volume do revert, because `before` carries them, defaults included. Fix: record `json!({"patch": crate::guardrail::inverse_patch(&before, &next)})`. Alternatively record the undo as `settings.set {path:"notifications", value: before}`, as settings.set itself does.

#### RA-173 · Symbol overlaps key symbols by bare name, so same-named items in a file overwrite each other

`crates/relay-core/src/handlers/overlap.rs:214` · **medium** · Bug · confirmed · effort S

**Problem.** node_name returns a bare identifier (L180-195). impl_item has no `name` field, so the first type identifier is used, which is the trait for `impl Trait for X`. symbols() does `out.insert(name, hash_hex(bytes))` into a BTreeMap (L214), so every `fn new`, every `impl Display for ...` and so on share one key, and the last inserted (first in file) wins.

**Impact.** An edit to one same-named method can be masked by another's unchanged hash (false negative), and edits to different items with the same name are reported as one shared symbol (false positive). Symbol-level detection, the precision D28 promises, is unreliable.

**Fix.** Key symbols by a qualified path (enclosing symbol names plus kind), or append an ordinal for duplicates.

**Verifier note.** Mechanism detail: the false negative only affects symbol granularity, because the file-level finding is always recorded alongside it, and an edit inside an impl usually also changes the enclosing impl_item's hash. Fix: key symbols by a qualified path (enclosing impl/mod/class names plus kind, using the impl's `type` field and, where present, its `trait` field) rather than the bare identifier. Fall back to an ordinal suffix for remaining duplicates.

**Also at:** `crates/relay-core/src/handlers/overlap.rs:180`

#### RA-174 · Sessions sharing one worktree (PAIR/review) are scanned separately and reported as overlapping on every changed file

Claim-vs-claim between partners can stay if wanted, since that one is explicit intent.

#### RA-175 · File/symbol overlap scans only run when an agent calls overlap.flag, so overlap.list is empty or stale in practice

`crates/relay-core/src/handlers/overlap.rs:475` · **medium** · Bug · confirmed · effort M

**Problem.** apply_scan is reached only from Flag (L455-482) and Scan (L531-545). `overlap.scan` has no caller outside tests and perf examples. Role instructions tell agents to declare files with session.claim (providers.rs:42), which inserts claims but writes no overlaps rows and triggers no scan (session.rs:1296-1306). The UI's "Shared file activity" list reads overlap.list (pages.rs:161-175). SPEC §15 describes a debounced overlap scan.

**Impact.** Two agents editing the same file or symbol are never flagged in normal use. Rows produced by an occasional flag stay `active=1` until the next flag, so the list can also be stale.

**Fix.** Trigger a debounced staged scan after file.changed or session.claim events, or have session.claim reuse the Flag scan.

**Verifier note.** The staleness part is overstated. Closing a session deactivates every overlap row that names it (session.rs:251-255), and recovery.rs:169 does the same, so rows do not survive their sessions. They only go stale while both sessions stay open. The impact is partly reduced because session.claim still returns `collisions` for claim-vs-claim conflicts directly to the agent. What is missing is detection of actual edits and the UI view. Related UI bug: pages.rs:173 prints `text(&overlap, "note")`, but the Overlap type has no `note` field (overlap_row builds id/project_id/sessions/path/symbol/kind/acked_by/first_seen/last_seen), so the second line of every entry is always empty. Fix as proposed: run a debounced register_staged-style scan after commit on file.changed or session.claim, off the store lock (collect_changes already runs unlocked).

#### RA-176 · provider.refresh runs provider subprocess probes inside the locked request transaction (D149 / CLAUDE.md invariant)

`crates/relay-core/src/handlers/provider.rs:19` · **medium** · Invariant · confirmed · effort M

**Problem.** `e.register::<Refresh>(|ctx: &mut Ctx, _| { let discovered = crate::providers::refresh(ctx.tx(), &ctx.now)?;`. refresh forks `<binary> --version` and `claude auth status` / `codex login status` for both providers through command_output, with PROBE_TIMEOUT = 3 s (providers.rs:320-331, 360). The comment there cites D144's timeout only. D149 says slow work runs outside the transaction, 'not merely with a timeout', and provider.list was converted to unlocked but refresh was not. provider_updates.rs:61-62 also calls `crate::providers::refresh(tx, now)` inside engine.system_write, which holds the store mutex.

**Impact.** Each 'Refresh providers' click, and every completed provider update, holds the global store mutex for as long as the slowest of four Node/Bun cold starts: typically hundreds of ms, up to 3 s at the timeout. Every other op queues behind it, including agents' PreToolUse guardrail checks and session.report hooks. Only keystrokes and resizes escape, via the fast path.

**Fix.** Register provider.refresh with register_staged. Prepare reads the cached rows and resolved paths in a short ctx.read and runs the probes unlocked; finish only upserts provider_cache and inserts the notifications. In provider_updates, probe before system_write and pass the results in. With the probes off the lock, the nested thread::scope fan-out can also go.

**Verifier note.** The worst case is bounded at about 3 s per click (the parallel probes each time out at 3 s), so this is a stall, not a hang. Medium is right. The fix is as proposed: register_staged, with prepare doing a short ctx.read of the cached rows and executable paths and then the probes, and finish doing the upserts and notifications. In provider_updates, probe before system_write.

The materializer copies library_dir(id), which includes the downloaded SKILL.md, and writes the row body only `if !instructions.is_file()` (skills.rs:328, 340-344).

**Impact.** Example: the user removes GitHub skill 'pdf', then writes their own 'pdf' in the skill editor. The new skill reuses the old id and still carries source_url. The Skills page therefore shows it as a GitHub skill with 'Update from GitHub' and no Edit button (tools_skills.rs:163-185). Every checkout's .claude/skills/pdf/ and .agents/skills/pdf/ get the old upstream SKILL.md and scripts, not the text the user just wrote. Clicking 'Update from GitHub', the only action offered besides Remove, matches the row by source (`Some(named) if Some(named.id) == source_id`) and overwrites the user's body. skill.install has no undo.

**Fix.** When skill.create revives a tombstone, clear source_url/source_path/revision and remove library_dir(id). Give skill.delete's undo its own restore path (clear deleted_at) instead of routing it through skill.create, so undo can still bring the source back.

The fix must therefore split the two paths as proposed: skill.delete's undo needs its own restore (clear deleted_at only), and a user-initiated skill.create that revives a tombstone clears source_url/source_path/revision and removes library_dir(id). The SKILL.md precedence in fill is the shared root with #24.

#### RA-178 · GitHub ops registered here fork gh/git with no timeout (CLAUDE.md: every handler subprocess goes through proc::output_with_timeout)

`crates/relay-core/src/handlers/provider.rs:247` · **medium** · Invariant · confirmed · effort M

**Problem.** github.status calls github::status(), which runs `gh api user` with plain `.output()` (github.rs:45). github.repo.list runs `gh api --paginate` the same way (github.rs:68-70). skill.install's prepare phase calls download_skills, which runs `git clone --depth 1 ...` via `.output()` (github.rs:106-109) and `git rev-parse` (github.rs:155-156). github.connect's thread runs `gh auth login --web` via `.status()` with no bound and no single-flight guard (github.rs:56-63).

**Impact.** These run unlocked, so they do not freeze the bus. But a stalled network call, or a credential helper waiting on a dialog, leaves the request hanging indefinitely and leaks a blocking-pool thread and a child process per attempt; onboarding retries pile them up. Each click on Connect starts another concurrent browser login.

**Fix.** Route these calls through proc::output_with_timeout with network-sized deadlines (30-120 s), and keep at most one github.connect in flight.

**Verifier note.** Stronger mechanism: requests on a socket connection are served serially (socket.rs:741), so a hung gh or git call blocks the native client's shared connection (app.rs:1111), not only a pool thread. The github.connect part is weak. `gh auth login --web` runs after_commit on its own thread, it is bounded by device-code expiry, and onboarding.rs:444 disables the Connect button until the flow fails. The 'concurrent browser logins pile up' claim is therefore mostly unfounded. git rev-parse is local and low risk. Fix: route `gh api` and `git clone` through proc::output_with_timeout with network-sized deadlines, and set GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0 on the clone.

#### RA-179 · Every skill/plugin mutation spawns its own unsynchronized refresh_all, so a stale plan can win the race

`crates/relay-core/src/handlers/provider.rs:532` · **medium** · Concurrency · confirmed · effort M

**Problem.** `ctx.after_commit(|engine| { std::thread::Builder::new().name("skill-materialize".into()).spawn(move || crate::skills::refresh_all(&engine)).ok(); });`. refresh_all reads its plan under the store lock, then prunes and writes folders with no lock held (skills.rs:267-305). Unlike prepare_launch's apply, it does not take hooks::writes(). write_skill returns early for folders whose marker already matches the stamp (skills.rs:313-315).

**Impact.** Two mutations in quick succession run two materializers at once: toggling two skills in the top-bar popover (D142), or an install followed by an enable. The newer thread skips folders the older one already stamped, so it can overtake it. If it prunes a just-disabled skill S in a checkout before the older thread reaches that checkout, the older thread then rewrites S from its stale plan. The disabled skill stays materialized and agents keep loading it until some later refresh. The reverse ordering can leave a newly enabled skill missing.

**Fix.** Funnel materialization through one worker with a dirty flag: coalesce bursts and re-plan after each pass. Alternatively, hold a dedicated mutex around plan+apply in refresh_all and around prepare_launch's apply.

**Verifier note.** Other unsynchronized writers: serve.rs:32, workspace.rs:215 and session.rs:480/493 (session launch takes hooks::writes; refresh_all and workspace do not). Fix: run one materializer worker behind a dirty flag (coalesce bursts and re-plan after each pass), or use a dedicated mutex that every caller of skills::apply takes around both plan and apply.

#### RA-180 · An assignment is typed into the terminal only if the session is idle at that moment; a busy or blocked session is never prompted later

`crates/relay-core/src/handlers/session.rs:73` · **medium** · Bug · confirmed · effort M

**Problem.** The after_commit returns early with `if !pty.claim_idle_edge() { return; }` (73). The only later delivery is in Report stop, which requires done_pending_stop: `if let (Some(completed), Some(current)) = (pending_stop, s.task_id) { if completed != current { deliver_assignment(...) } }` (1384-1388). done_pending_stop is set only for the session that itself called done.

**Impact.** task.dispatch makes a task current for a session that is mid-turn or waiting on a permission prompt (task.rs:714-718), or a group advances while a builder is busy with something else. The terminal write is skipped. That session's next Stop delivers nothing either, because it did not call done. The agent ends its turn idle, on a new current task it was never told about. The only record is a non-priority mailbox message, which produces no mail hint.

**Fix.** Record which task was last delivered, and deliver on stop/idle whenever the current task differs from it, instead of keying on done_pending_stop.

**Verifier note.** Narrower trigger: dispatch makes a task current only for a session whose task is NULL, done or deleted (task.rs:607-611), so 'busy' here means a task-less session that is running or blocked, or a reviewer that is mid-turn when its builders finish. Normal group advances mostly reach idle builders, or the session that called done, which is delivered at its Stop. Suggested fix: keep a last_delivered_task_id, compare it to task_id on every stop/idle report, and deliver when they differ.

#### RA-181 · Launch files are written inside the agent-writable worktree with symlink-following writes, so an agent can make Relay overwrite files outside its sandbox

`crates/relay-core/src/handlers/session.rs:321` · **medium** · Security · confirmed · effort S

**Problem.** write_session_file runs `fs::create_dir_all(parent)` and then `fs::write(&path, text)` (318-323) for `.relay/sessions/<name>/session-brief.md`, `.relay/session-skills.md` and `.relay/sessions/<name>/role-instructions.md` inside the worktree (507-526). Both calls follow symlinks. The guardrail treats `.relay/` like any other worktree path, and `ln -s` is not a denied command, so an agent can replace any of these files with a symlink.

**Impact.** On the next spawn, wake or resume, the unsandboxed engine overwrites the symlink's target outside the worktree (e.g. ~/.bashrc or ~/.ssh/authorized_keys) with brief text that includes agent-controlled claim strings. This only matters where the agent itself is confined (a Codex sandbox with --add-dir write roots); a Claude agent's Bash is not confined anyway. install_claude's statusline temp file has the same pattern: a write plus chmod 755 that would follow a planted symlink.

**Fix.** Write to a temp file in the same directory and rename it over the target (rename replaces a symlink instead of following it), or open with O_NOFOLLOW. Refuse to write when `.relay` or `.relay/sessions/<name>` is a symlink.

**Verifier note.** Severity is high, not medium. This is a confined agent escaping its sandbox, limited by needing a relaunch and Codex as the provider, and it can destroy user files even with no malicious payload. The fix stands: write to a temp file opened with O_CREAT|O_EXCL|O_NOFOLLOW in the same directory and rename it over the target, and refuse to proceed if `.relay`, `.relay/sessions` or `.relay/sessions/<name>` is a symlink (symlink_metadata). Apply the same fix to the `.relay-tmp` files in hooks::install_claude, which already rename but first write through a predictable temp path.

**Skeptic note.** Severity should be medium, not high. The trigger needs a deliberately hostile, Relay-aware Codex agent and then a user-initiated spawn, wake or resume. Claude sessions are unaffected. What is bypassed is Codex's own sandbox (D135), not Relay's guardrails, which BUS.md:29-31 already describes as seatbelts rather than a security boundary.

Related locations:
- The Codex-relevant hooks.rs location is install_codex's `.codex/hooks.json.relay-tmp` (hooks.rs:544-547). It writes to a predictable temp path before renaming. Whether Codex itself stops its agent writing `.codex/` cannot be established from this repo.
- install_claude's temp files (hooks.rs:378-381, 388-393 including the 0755 chmod, 395-399, 409-411) and add_claude_mcp_servers (hooks.rs:440-442) matter only when a confined agent earlier had write access to the same worktree. Worktrees can be reused across sessions and providers (read_teardown, session.rs:333-335).
- skills::apply (skills.rs:326-346) writes into `.claude/skills` and `.agents/skills` through create_dir_all, which follows a symlinked parent. This is the same class with lower impact (fixed file names); I did not trace it fully.

Fix:
- Create any temp file with create_new (O_CREAT|O_EXCL, which refuses an existing path, including a symlink) under an unpredictable name, then rename it over the target.
- A symlink_metadata pre-check on `.relay` and `.relay/sessions/<name>` alone is racy. Either resolve every component beneath the worktree with directory fds (openat2 with RESOLVE_BENEATH|RESOLVE_NO_SYMLINKS, or an equivalent crate), or, simpler and more complete, move these engine-written launch files out of the agent's write roots (for example, into the engine's data directory) and pass absolute paths through RELAY_BRIEF and --append-system-prompt-file.
- Apply the same treatment to the hooks.rs `.relay-tmp` writes.

**Also at:** `crates/relay-core/src/handlers/session.rs:507-526`, `crates/relay-core/src/hooks.rs:388-392`

#### RA-182 · The session brief walks git commit history while holding the store lock, on every launch and every session.brief

`crates/relay-core/src/handlers/session.rs:451` · **medium** · Invariant · confirmed · effort M

**Problem.** plan_launch runs inside `ctx.read` (604-609) and calls `crate::awareness::brief(conn, ...)` (451). The Brief op is `e.register::<Brief>` (1124-1129) and calls the same function. brief() calls `crate::handlers::git::briefing_state` (awareness.rs:211), which does `gix::open` plus up to three ahead/behind computations. Each is two unbounded `rev_walk(..).with_hidden(..)` counts (git.rs:922-935, 1018-1033), so the cost grows with how far the branch, its upstream and the base have diverged.

**Impact.** Every spawn, wake, resume and clear, and every session.brief call (the agent menu uses it), walks the commit graph with the global store lock held. On a large repository where the branch is thousands of commits behind base, this can stall every request for hundreds of milliseconds or more. I did not measure the actual cost.

**Fix.** Compute briefing_state outside the lock (in prepare_launch, and make Brief a register_unlocked op) and pass the result into brief(), or cache it keyed by (branch tip, base tip).

**Verifier note.** The mechanism and lines are correct. A simpler fix than threading results through: make briefing_state a separate input to brief(). Compute it in prepare_launch, which already runs unlocked, and in a register_unlocked or register_staged variant of session.brief. Also cap the counts (for example stop at 1000 and report '1000+') so a huge divergence cannot cost unbounded time anywhere.

#### RA-183 · A task.dispatch that fails after a nested launch rolls back the session row but leaves the spawned agent process registered under an id that will be reused

`crates/relay-core/src/handlers/session.rs:685` · **medium** · Bug · confirmed · effort M

**Problem.** When task.dispatch invokes session.create and session.spawn nested (task.rs:683, 712), finish_launch starts the child and registers it in memory: `let pty = Pty::spawn(spec, …)` and `ctx.engine().set_pty(sid, &name, pty)` (session.rs:646, 685). A later step of the same dispatch can still fail, for example the next fanout child's `dispatch_task(ctx, id, None, template.clone(), start)?` hitting git.fetch_failed (task.rs:1073). dispatch_inner then rolls the transaction back (engine.rs:1074), but nothing undoes set_pty or kills the child. The worktree, branch and hooks created by the nested session.create prepare (session.rs:874, 892) also stay on disk. sessions.id is AUTOINCREMENT (store.rs:86), and a rolled-back insert's id is handed out again. I checked this with sqlite3: the rolled-back insert got id 2 and the next insert also got id 2.

**Impact.** The orphaned claude/codex process keeps running with no session row; its own bus calls fail authentication. The next session.create receives the same id, so `engine.pty(id)` returns the orphan for the new session. Attaching shows the orphan's output, and the session.input fallback handler (session.rs:1660-1675) writes the user's keystrokes into the orphaned agent. At shutdown, mark_restorable writes the orphan's scrollback and state over the new session's row (engine.rs:661-679).

**Fix.** Do not start PTYs inside a transaction that can still fail. Either have finish_launch queue the spawn/set_pty in after_commit, or record PTYs spawned in the request on Ctx and take/kill them on rollback in dispatch_inner. Alternatively, make task.dispatch commit each child dispatch separately.

**Verifier note.** The finding misses a worse consequence when the reused id is later spawned. set_pty returns the orphan and finish_launch calls kill_detached(old) (session.rs:685-686), which does not silence_exit. The orphan's exit callback then runs `UPDATE sessions SET state='exited' WHERE id=N AND epoch=1 AND state IN live` (session.rs:651-655). The new session's first launch also uses epoch 1 (row.epoch+1, session.rs:580), so the freshly started session is marked exited, and its task is marked failed if it is a builder. Reachability is narrower than the finding implies. task.dispatch is UserOnly, and no client (native, CLI or remote) sends `fanout`, so the trigger needs a raw bus/CLI call. Without fanout, the steps after the launch almost never fail. Fix: on failure, record PTYs spawned during the request on Ctx and kill them with silence_exit in the rollback branch, or defer spawn/set_pty to after_commit.

**Also at:** `crates/relay-core/src/handlers/session.rs:646`, `crates/relay-core/src/handlers/task.rs:1073`, `crates/relay-core/src/handlers/task.rs:712`, `crates/relay-core/src/engine.rs:1074`, `crates/relay-core/src/store.rs:86`, `crates/relay-core/src/handlers/session.rs:1662`, `crates/relay-core/src/engine.rs:661`

#### RA-184 · A new session silently reattaches a closed namesake's leftover relay/<name> branch instead of branching from base

`crates/relay-core/src/handlers/session.rs:867` · **medium** · Bug · confirmed · effort S

**Problem.** Names come from 36×36 = 1296 adjective-animal pairs and are unique only among non-closed sessions (`SELECT 1 FROM sessions WHERE name = ?1 AND state != 'closed'`, sessions.rs:74-89). The reservation loop skips only names whose pooled worktree directory still exists (session.rs:839-841). For the default `new` checkout, `let branch = p.branch.clone().unwrap_or_else(|| worktree::branch_for(&prepared.name))` gives `relay/<name>` (867). If that branch exists, `from = None` (869-873), and `worktree::create` runs `git worktree add <path> <branch>` on the existing branch (worktree.rs:204-206). session.close removes the worktree but keeps the branch (worktree.rs:350 "The branch is kept"), and branch_cleanup deletes only branches it can prove merged. The native launcher never sends `branch` (launch.rs:346).

**Impact.** Trigger: a session closes with unmerged work (abandoned, or squash-merged without gh evidence), and a later session draws the same name. With k leftover branches, each new session hits one with probability k/1296. Consequence: the new agent starts on the old session's unmerged commits instead of a fresh branch from base, with no warning, so its diff, commits and PR mix in unrelated history.

**Fix.** Also skip names whose `refs/heads/relay/<name>` exists in the reservation loop (a cheap gix ref lookup), or make generated branches unique (for example suffix the session id). Reattach an existing branch only when the caller passed `branch` explicitly.

**Verifier note.** The new agent starts on the old branch's tip, which may also be far behind base, not only carrying unrelated commits. The fix is as proposed: in the reservation loop, also skip a name when refs/heads/relay/<name> exists (existing_worktree_branch is already available). Only reattach when p.branch was given explicitly.

#### RA-185 · Calling session.done a second time in the same turn completes the next queued task, which the agent never worked on

`crates/relay-core/src/handlers/session.rs:1166` · **medium** · Bug · confirmed · effort S

**Problem.** Done always acts on `s.task_id` (1161, 1165-1166). The first completion has already advanced task_id to the next queued task (122), and nothing checks `done_pending_stop` (set at 1163 and still set until the turn's Stop) before completing again. The tests record this as the contract (tests/sessions.rs:1264, tests/agent_features.rs:257), and DISCOVERY_HINT tells agents to omit the task id (providers.rs:31), so they cannot name the task they mean.

**Impact.** An agent calls session.done again in the same turn: to add a forgotten `sha`, to fix the summary, or to retry after an MCP timeout (a new request id, so replay idempotency does not apply). For a builder with no waiting partner, the second call moves the untouched next task to in_review, broadcasts '<name> finished' for it and advances again. That task's work is silently skipped.

**Fix.** While done_pending_stop is set, refuse a second `completed` done, or treat it as an update to the pending completion. Alternatively accept an optional task_id that must match the current task.

**Verifier note.** Two details are wrong in the finding. First, the second call usually does not broadcast a fresh '<name> finished': record_agent_notification (261-278) dedups on an unread notification with the same title and link, and then only updates its body. Second, it misses one consequence: a `sha` passed on the retry (the 'add a forgotten sha' case) is inserted into task_commits for the wrong task (line 95). The behaviour is deliberate, but its harm is not documented anywhere. Fix: refuse, or treat as an update, a `completed` done while done_pending_stop equals a different task than the current one. Alternatively, accept an optional expected task_id. The two tests that assert the current behaviour need updating.

**Also at:** `crates/relay-core/src/handlers/session.rs:120-129`, `crates/relay-core/tests/sessions.rs:1264`, `crates/relay-core/src/providers.rs:31-32`

#### RA-186 · Deleting a task an agent is working on makes that agent's session.done, Stop reports and permission-prompt reports fail with task.not_found

`crates/relay-core/src/handlers/session.rs:1214` · **medium** · Bug · confirmed · effort S

**Problem.** All three paths pass the session's current task as the mail's re_task: `send_system(ctx.tx(), s.project_id, "*", ..., s.task_id, &ctx.now)?` (1214-1216, 285-292, 1408-1410). notes::send fails with `not_found("task.not_found")` when `SELECT project_id FROM tasks WHERE id=?1 AND deleted_at IS NULL` finds nothing (notes.rs:227-241). task.delete only sets deleted_at (task.rs:909-916), so sessions.task_id keeps pointing at the deleted task.

**Impact.** The user deletes a board task while its agent works on it. From then on, whenever no unread card already exists: session.done fails with "no task N in project P", so the agent can report neither completion nor blocked. Every Stop-hook report rolls back, so the session stays 'running' and no completion notice appears. A permission-prompt notification also fails, so the user is never told the agent is waiting. Because `?` rolls back the whole report each time, the failure repeats on every later report.

**Fix.** Pass re_task only if the task still exists, or have send_system drop a dangling re_task instead of failing. Also clear or advance sessions.task_id when its task is deleted.

**Verifier note.** The failure is gated: it happens only when record_agent_notification inserts a fresh notification, meaning no unread '<name> finished' or '<name> needs attention' card exists. Restoring the task, or clearing task_id with session.update, recovers. Deleting an in-progress task is a less common path, so medium rather than high. Fix: have send_system drop a dangling re_task instead of failing (the message is still useful), and clear sessions.task_id (or advance the queue) when the task is deleted.
