#### RA-187 · session.report sets state unconditionally: the Stop hook overwrites 'blocked' from session.done, and a late hook revives parked or exited rows

`crates/relay-core/src/handlers/session.rs:1361` · **medium** · Bug · confirmed · effort S

**Problem.** `"stop" | "idle" => "idle"` (1361), then `UPDATE sessions SET state=?1 ... WHERE id=?4` (1371-1374), with no condition on the current state. session.done with blocked/partial sets `state='blocked'` (1186-1191) from inside the agent's turn, and that same turn ends with the Stop hook, which reports kind=stop. Agent tokens authenticate for any non-closed session (engine.rs:1377-1384), so a report still in flight when park kills the child is accepted (e.g. an orphaned `relay hook claude-report`, or a Codex notify).

**Impact.** (a) Every done(blocked|partial) shows as 'idle' within about a second, so the session never appears to need attention. (b) A late report turns a parked, exited or restorable row back into idle or running. Then Wake refuses (not parked), Spawn refuses (already_spawned) and Park refuses (no PTY), so the session is stuck until it is closed.

**Fix.** Add `AND state IN ('spawning','running','idle','blocked')` to the update. Do not let a stop demote 'blocked' when the turn ended with done(blocked), e.g. by recording the done status next to done_pending_stop.

**Verifier note.** The main, frequent impact is (a): blocked is overwritten to idle. (b) is a real but narrow race. A provider killed by park usually does not fire a Stop hook, so (b) mainly applies to a Codex notify process that is already in flight or an orphaned hook process. Fix both at once: guard the UPDATE with `AND state IN ('spawning','running','idle','blocked')`, and when the current state is 'blocked', do not let kind=stop demote it unless a newer session_start or tool_use has happened (for example, record the done status next to done_pending_stop).

#### RA-188 · task.activity scans and JSON-parses the project's whole audit history under the store lock every time a task is opened

`crates/relay-core/src/handlers/task.rs:766` · **medium** · Performance · confirmed · effort M

**Problem.** The WHERE clause ORs `(op LIKE 'task.%' AND json_extract(payload,'$.task_id') = ?2)`, `(op = 'task.create' AND json_extract(result_summary,'$.id') = ?2)` and `json_extract(result_summary,'$.task.id') = ?2` (763-767). The last branch applies to every op, so no audit index ((project_id, ts), (op, ts), ...) can serve it, and result_summary (up to 64 KB) is parsed for every non-matching project row. A task with fewer than limit+1 matches therefore scans back to the start of the retention window (180 days by default, settings.rs:43). That window includes every agent's audited guardrail.gate and session.report rows, which are project-tagged. The native task page runs this query on open (task_pages.rs:1134 `refresh.emit_clicked()`, call at 1056).

**Impact.** Cost grows with the project's entire audit history, not the task's, so the perf baseline note that it 'scales with the task's audit rows' is wrong. That baseline measured about 1.7 µs per row (2.6 ms at 1,500 rows). After months of hook traffic (hundreds of thousands of rows), opening a task holds the store mutex for hundreds of milliseconds to seconds, stalling the UI and every agent's guardrail gate.

**Fix.** Index the task id. Either add an `audit.task_id` column filled in audit::append from payload.task_id or the result id (migration plus index), or keep a task_audit(task_id, audit_id) link table, and page by that index.

**Verifier note.** The finding overstates the size of the stall. In a synthetic test (300k rows) the scan cost about 0.09 µs per row with '{}' result summaries and about 0.27 µs per row with ~1 KB summaries: roughly 25-80 ms at 300k rows. Hundreds of milliseconds needs on the order of a million or more project audit rows, and 'seconds' needs several million. The 1.7 µs/row baseline includes audit::get and JSON decoding of the returned rows, not only the scan. The issue is still real: cost grows with the project's whole audit history, not with the task's, and the bus is blocked while it runs. The proposed fix is right: index a task_id column or a link table. A cheaper partial fix is to register the query with register_unlocked.

**Also at:** `apps/relay-native/src/task_pages.rs:1056`, `apps/relay-native/src/task_pages.rs:1134`, `docs/perf/BASELINE-2026-09-19.md:224-227`, `crates/relay-core/src/audit.rs:94-101`, `crates/relay-core/src/handlers/task.rs:763`, `crates/relay-core/src/store.rs:28`, `crates/relay-core/src/audit.rs:208`, `apps/relay-native/src/board_view.rs:881`, `crates/relay-core/src/store.rs:32`, `crates/relay-core/src/recovery.rs:18`, `docs/engine/DECISIONS.md:832`

#### RA-189 · Undoing a move out of Done is always refused, which also jams the board's Ctrl+Z

`crates/relay-core/src/handlers/task.rs:905` · **medium** · Bug · confirmed · effort S

**Problem.** Move records the inverse `task.move {"column":column_str(before.column),"position":index}` (905) for every move, including Done -> In Review, a move it explicitly supports (902 sets AwaitingReview). The same handler then refuses `if p.column==Column::Done { return Err(conflict("task.column_transition","move to done through task.approve")) }` (897) with no exception for undo. audit.undo replays the inverse through invoke_registered (audit.rs:68). The native board's undo_last (board_view.rs:879-890) always undoes the newest user `task.*` row that has an undo_op and no undone_by.

**Impact.** Dragging a Done card back to In Review and pressing Ctrl+Z fails with task.column_transition. The failed row stays newest, so every later Ctrl+Z on the board picks it again and fails. Nothing older can be undone until the user makes another undoable board change.

**Fix.** When before.column is Done, record the inverse as `task.approve {task_id, sha: <latest linked sha>}`. Approve re-links the same sha (INSERT OR IGNORE) and restores Done with state none. Alternatively, let task.move accept done when it runs as an undo.

**Verifier note.** Moving a card out of Done to any column, not only In Review, creates a 'done' inverse that cannot be replayed. The fix should record task.approve (or a dedicated restore) as the inverse whenever before.column is Done. undo_last could also skip a row whose undo has already failed.

#### RA-190 · task.attach, file.import and file.rename/move do unbounded file reads and copies inside the transaction

`crates/relay-core/src/handlers/task.rs:993` · **medium** · Performance · confirmed · effort M

**Problem.** - task.attach with a path (plain register, task.rs:982) runs `let bytes = std::fs::read(&src).bus()?;` with no size check. attach_bytes then writes the bytes back with `std::fs::write(&path, bytes)` (task.rs:505-538). All of it happens in the transaction.
- file.import (plain, file.rs:262-298) recursively copies arbitrary absolute source trees with `copy(source, &dest)` (file.rs:293, 612-627).
- file.rename and file.move call guard_path_mutation. It reads the entire source file into memory with `fs::read_to_string(content).unwrap_or_default()` (file.rs:578), before enforce, which itself caps reads at 64 MiB.
Related one-shot cases:
- app.backup.now copies the whole database inside the transaction (app.rs:48, store.rs:556-564).
- skill.install's finish may copy up to 64 MiB in skills::adopt's copy fallback (provider.rs:505, skills.rs:51-66).
- app.import.v3 copies attachments (import_v3.rs:263).

**Impact.** Three user actions hold the global lock for a full read or copy and load the whole file into memory: attaching a large file to a task ("Attach image" takes a typed path, task_pages.rs:880), importing a directory, and renaming a multi-GB asset. Every agent hook and UI request waits meanwhile.

**Fix.** - Attachments: cap the size and stream the copy (fs::copy) outside the lock. As a staged op, copy to a temp name in prepare, then insert the row and rename in finish.
- file.import: stage it the same way.
- guard_path_mutation: use a capped read (the gate's 64 MiB rule) instead of read_to_string of the whole file.

**Verifier note.** Also file.delete (file.rs:224) calls guard_path_mutation and reads the whole file. A side observation worth its own look: for a directory source, guard_path_mutation's read_to_string fails to "", so file.import gates only the top-level dest path and never the files copied beneath it. The app.backup.now case is arguably intentional, because a consistent snapshot needs the lock. Fix: before enforce, use a metadata-capped read (the gate's 64 MiB rule) or skip content for binaries; cap attachment size; stage the copies.

#### RA-191 · Soft-deleting a parent leaves live sub-tasks attached to it; every parent.set on them then fails, and hidden subtrees escape the depth and children caps

`crates/relay-core/src/handlers/task.rs:1171` · **medium** · Bug · confirmed · effort M

**Problem.** Delete (909-916) only stamps deleted_at, so children keep parent_id pointing at the deleted task. ParentSet re-emits `for parent in [before.parent_id, task.parent_id].into_iter().flatten() { let parent = get_task(ctx.tx(), parent, false)?; ...}` (1170-1172). get_task with include_deleted=false returns task.not_found for a deleted old parent, and the whole request rolls back. assert_parent's cycle walk `cursor = get_task(tx, id, false)?.parent_id` (400) fails the same way on any soft-deleted ancestor. child_ids and subtree_height (164-197) skip deleted rows, so live descendants of a deleted child are invisible to the depth check. Restore (929-951) re-attaches a task without re-running any of assert_parent's checks.

**Impact.** After deleting a parent card, its children still appear on the board with a parent badge. 'Detach from parent' (board_view.rs:2211-2214) and dropping them onto another card always fail with 'no task <deleted id>'. The only workaround is to restore the parent, re-home the children, and delete it again. Dropping any card onto a task whose grandparent is deleted fails with an id the user never chose. Moving a node whose deleted child hides live grandchildren pushes them past TASK_DEPTH_MAX (Task.depth is documented as never above 2). Restore can push a parent past TASK_CHILDREN_MAX.

**Fix.** In ParentSet, re-emit with include_deleted=true or skip parents that are not found. Walk ancestors with a cached `SELECT parent_id` as depth_of does. Then either detach live children on delete (recording them for undo) or make the depth and children checks and restore count subtrees under deleted nodes.

**Verifier note.** The main user-visible effect is that the children of a deleted parent cannot be detached or re-parented until the parent is restored. Escaping the depth and children caps is a secondary, rarer effect. Minimal fix: in ParentSet, re-emit with include_deleted=true or skip a parent that is not found, and walk ancestors with a plain SELECT parent_id as depth_of does. Then pick one model, either detaching children on delete (recorded for undo) or counting subtrees under deleted nodes in the caps.

#### RA-192 · workspace.discover walks the filesystem while holding the store mutex although it never touches the store

`crates/relay-core/src/handlers/workspace.rs:114` · **medium** · Invariant · confirmed · effort S

**Problem.** `e.register::<WsDiscover>(|_, p| {` ignores ctx, yet `register` holds the store lock for the whole handler. discover_repositories (L393-413) does read_dir up to four levels deep. The op is a query (relay-bus ops/workspace.rs:12-13), and onboarding calls it with a user-chosen folder such as $HOME (onboarding.rs:336).

**Impact.** A tree walk under the global lock, which CLAUDE.md names explicitly. On a big home directory or a network mount, every agent and UI request stalls for the duration.

A second bug in the same walk: `for entry in fs::read_dir(path)?` and `entry.file_type()?` propagate the first EACCES or ENOENT from any subdirectory. One unreadable directory under the chosen root (for example a root-owned docker or lost+found dir in $HOME) makes the whole discovery fail with workspace.discover_failed instead of skipping that entry. The walk should skip unreadable subdirectories and fail only on the root.

#### RA-193 · Project/workspace ids are recycled while removal leaves id-keyed state that the next project or workspace inherits

`crates/relay-core/src/handlers/workspace.rs:178` · **medium** · Bug · confirmed · effort M

**Problem.** workspaces and projects use `id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY` without AUTOINCREMENT (store.rs:46-57), although the v2 comment cites D85: "a bare rowid recycles a deleted id" (store.rs:60-62). A SQLite run confirmed the max id is reused. WsRemove deletes only the workspaces row (L178) and never `guardrails.workspaces.{id}.*`, which guardrail::layers reads by id (guardrail.rs:107,129-131). ProjectRemove deletes exactly `layout.current.{id}` (L378-379), but settings are stored as flattened leaves (settings.rs:68-78) and the client writes `native.layout.current.{id}` (shell.rs:308). Open holds and audit rows keep the old id.

**Impact.** A newly added workspace silently inherits the removed one's guardrail layer, which may be looser. A new project inherits pending holds, layout state and audit/undo history that belong to a different repository.

**Fix.** Migrate both tables to AUTOINCREMENT (table rebuild). On workspace.remove, delete settings under `guardrails.workspaces.{id}`. On project.remove, delete `native.layout.current.{id}%` and resolve or delete open holds.

**Verifier note.** The holds and audit part is weak. Audit rows are kept on purpose (comment at workspace.rs ~L349). Open holds of the project's sessions are expired by session.close, which project.remove invokes for every open session. Only session-less holds could survive, and I did not establish that any exist. The real consequences are the workspace guardrail layer (main issue) and layout state carried over to an unrelated project (cosmetic). Trigger needs the removed workspace/project to have the highest id, which is common when a just-added wrong folder is removed and the right one added. Fix: in WsRemove, delete `guardrails.workspaces.{id}` and `guardrails.workspaces.{id}.%`. In ProjectRemove, use `path = 'layout.current.{id}' OR path LIKE 'layout.current.{id}.%' OR path LIKE 'native.layout.current.{id}%'`. Optionally migrate both tables to AUTOINCREMENT via a table-rebuild migration appended to MIGRATIONS.

#### RA-194 · project.remove/workspace.remove force-close sessions with their teardown subprocesses running under the held lock

`crates/relay-core/src/handlers/workspace.rs:328` · **medium** · Invariant · confirmed · effort M

**Problem.** `ctx.invoke_registered("session.close", ...)` runs once per open session. invoke_registered runs a staged op's prepare with `held: Some(self.tx)` (engine.rs:325-351). session.close's prepare (session.rs:1547-1596) runs run_teardown, which is documented as "Subprocesses and file rewrites, so it runs with the store unlocked" (session.rs:350-362) and spawns git config calls with 10 s timeouts (hooks.rs:233-281). The comment at L320-326 claims the slow work is moved after the commit, but only worktree deletion is.

**Impact.** Removing a project with many live sessions holds the store for dozens of git invocations; a slow git holds it for up to 10 s per call. All of that time is felt by every other request.

**Fix.** Collect the teardown work and run it in after_commit like the worktree removal, or make project.remove itself staged and run the closes' external phases before opening the transaction.

**Verifier note.** The comment at workspace.rs:320-326 does not actually claim the hook teardown is deferred. It defers only the PTY kills and the worktree deletion, and lists "hooks uninstalled" as one of the rules close keeps. The real cost is about 2 git invocations per open session, roughly 10-20 ms each normally and up to 10 s each if git hangs. That is noticeable but bounded, so medium is right for a rare, user-initiated op. Fix: make project.remove/workspace.remove staged and run each close's teardown in the external phase, or collect the (repo, worktree, Teardown) tuples and run them in after_commit next to the worktree removal. Out of scope for this finding but nearby in the same file: WsDiscover (workspace.rs:114) does a depth-4 directory walk, and ProjectClone (workspace.rs:233) runs `git clone` through Command::output with no timeout. Both are registered with plain `e.register` and so hold the store mutex, a larger instance of the same invariant breach.

**Also at:** `crates/relay-core/src/engine.rs:325`, `crates/relay-core/src/handlers/session.rs:352`, `crates/relay-core/src/handlers/workspace.rs:173`

<a id="ra-195"></a>

#### RA-195 · project.remove / workspace.remove permanently delete the project's board, notes and modules with no warning, undo or backup, and moving a repo leaves no other option

`crates/relay-core/src/handlers/workspace.rs:364` · **medium** · Data loss · confirmed · effort M

**Problem.** workspace.rs:354-380 runs `DELETE FROM messages ... tasks ... modules ... notes ... notifications ... file_trash ... integrations ... WHERE project_id=?1`, then deletes the project row. These are hard deletes, with no set_undo and no store.backup_with. The native confirmation (shell/registry.rs:539-581) reads 'Remove “X” from Relay?', 'N agents will be stopped and closed.' and 'Repository files are never touched.'. It never mentions tasks or notes. ProjectUpdateIn (relay-bus ops/workspace.rs:44-48) has no `path` field, so a project whose folder was moved or renamed can only be repointed by remove + add. workspace.remove with force runs the same cascade for every project (workspace.rs:172-175). D56 calls this 'forgets Relay metadata', but tasks and notes are user-authored content that exists nowhere else.

**Impact.** A user who removes and re-adds a project after moving its repository, or who tidies the sidebar, permanently loses that project's data: every task (with sub-tasks, labels and commit links), every note (including the standing note injected into agents), modules, mailbox history and file-trash records. Ctrl+Z cannot undo it. Only restoring a whole-store backup (manual, or the last pre-upgrade copy) recovers it, and that also loses everything done since.

**Fix.** Make removal a soft delete (an archived_at column; rows kept; restorable from the sidebar). At minimum, take `store.backup_with(ctx.tx(), "project-remove")` in the handler and report its path. Show the counts that will be deleted (tasks, notes, modules) in the dialog. Add a relocate op (project.update {path}, validated as the same repository, e.g. same root commit) so moving a repo never requires removal.

**Verifier note.** Severity is medium rather than high. It is a deliberate, confirmed, user-only action, and D56 makes the deletion a documented design choice. The concrete defects are that the dialog does not disclose the loss, that there is no undo or snapshot, and that there is no relocate path. The cheapest fix is `store.backup_with(ctx.tx(), "project-remove")` before the cascade, plus task/note counts in the confirmation. A project.update path, validated as the same repository, removes the need for remove-and-re-add after a move.

**Also at:** `crates/relay-core/src/handlers/workspace.rs:172`, `apps/relay-native/src/shell/registry.rs:567`, `crates/relay-bus/src/ops/workspace.rs:44`, `docs/engine/DECISIONS.md:219`

#### RA-196 · Every session.changed event, from any project, re-fetches the whole board and rebuilds all its cards

`apps/relay-native/src/agent_menu.rs:134` · **medium** · Performance · confirmed · effort S

**Problem.** apply_session_event ends with `if matches!(self.page.borrow().as_str(), "board" | "dashboard") { self.refresh_page(); }` (133-135). The event loop lets session.* events through regardless of project (app.rs:1213-1229). For "board", refresh_page runs pages::refresh: task.list + module.list (pages.rs:41-78). Then Board::render clears and rebuilds every card (board_view.rs:1181-1221). The board shows no session-row data, only the task["sessions"] names that come from task.list. Session transitions that affect a task already emit task.changed (session.rs:1396-1398, 104-108), which refreshes the page through the generic branch.

**Impact.** With several agents working, session.changed fires on every idle/running/blocked flip (session.rs:1423-1426, engine.rs:1328-1338). While the board is open, each one triggers (coalesced) a full-project task.list under the store mutex, about 10 queries per task, plus a rebuild of every card on the GTK thread. The board stutters, hover and drag state resets, and every other bus request waits on the mutex.

**Fix.** Remove "board" from that condition and let task.changed drive board refreshes. Refresh the dashboard only if it shows session state, and only for current-project sessions, or debounce it.

**Verifier note.** Frequency is lower than "every flip" might suggest. session.report emits only when state_changed or provider_ref_changed (session.rs:1423), so it fires about once per transition per agent, not once per hook. Scroll positions are restored after render, but the cards are rebuilt, so hover, focus and any in-progress drag are reset. task.list runs under the store mutex with prepare_cached statements: a modest cost, not a bus freeze. Fix: drop "board" from the condition, or skip it when payload project_id is not the current project. Check whether a task.changed is missing for a new task_sessions link before relying on that event alone.

#### RA-197 · Agent settings "Save changes" always sends model and effort for a session that hasn't started, so saving fails with the default (empty) values

`apps/relay-native/src/agent_menu.rs:546` · **medium** · Bug · confirmed · effort S

**Problem.** `if !spawned { payload["model"] = model.text().as_str().into(); payload["effort"] = effort.text().as_str().into(); }` (545-548) sends both fields even when unchanged and when empty. The entries' placeholders are "Provider default" and "Default", and `text(session,"model")` is "" when the provider default is used. session.update passes them to `providers::validate_options` (session.rs:1439). It rejects an empty model (`if model.is_some_and(|model| model.trim().is_empty()) { return Err(... "model cannot be empty") }`, providers.rs:253-255) and any effort not in the provider's list, "" included (providers.rs:260-266). `spawned` is computed once, when the popover opens (476). After the first spawn the engine refuses any model/effort field (session.rs:1433-1436).

**Impact.** Take a session that was created but not started, using the provider's default model. Toggling "Agent bus writes" or "UI control" and pressing Save fails with "Invalid session.model: model cannot be empty". Setting only a model fails on the blank effort. If the agent starts while the popover is open, even a switch-only Save fails with session.already_spawned. The Launch options section can't be used with its defaults.

**Fix.** Build the payload from what changed compared with `original` (522). Include model or effort only when changed and non-empty, and the switches only when changed. Make effort a dropdown of the provider's allowed values instead of free text.

**Verifier note.** This applies only to sessions that exist but have not spawned yet (spawned_at null and epoch 0), which is less common than a live agent, so medium is right. Also note: model.text() is not trimmed, and effort is free text checked against a fixed list. Fix: send only the fields that differ from `original`, never send an empty model or effort, and make effort a dropdown of the provider's allowed values.

#### RA-198 · Reconnecting throws away the wall's pane order and focused pane, and the next save persists the reset

`apps/relay-native/src/app.rs:1143` · **medium** · Bug · confirmed · effort S

**Problem.** connect() runs `self.ordered.borrow_mut().clear(); self.layout();` (app.rs:1143-1144). With no names, layout() sets `*self.focused.borrow_mut() = names.first().cloned()`, which is None (shell.rs:148-155). The saved arrangement is only re-applied by restore_layout, which returns early when `self.restored_project.get() == project` (shell.rs:323-325). Only open_project resets restored_project (shell.rs:33); connect() does not. reconcile() then rebuilds `ordered` in session.list order (app.rs:1459-1465). The next save_layout (any navigation, mode change or sidebar toggle; it only requires restored_project == project, shell.rs:290) writes that order to native.layout.current.{project}.

**Impact.** After an engine restart, or a click on the Reconnect key that appears beside any notice, agent tiles come back in creation order, and in focus mode the first agent replaces the one the user had focused. The drag-arranged order is then overwritten permanently on the next navigation.

**Fix.** Don't clear `ordered` in connect(); reconcile() already prunes names that no longer have sessions. Or reset `restored_project` to 0 in connect() so the next refresh re-applies the saved layout.

**Verifier note.** The simplest fix is `self.restored_project.set(0)` in connect(), which matches what open_project already does. That re-applies the saved order and focus on the first refresh after reconnecting.

#### RA-199 · Board undo retries the same stale row forever, so older changes, including a deleted task, become unrecoverable

`apps/relay-native/src/board_view.rs:885` · **medium** · Bug · confirmed · effort M

**Problem.** undo_last lists the 50 newest user task.* audit rows (882). It always picks the newest row that has an inverse and is not yet undone: `rows(&history, "rows").iter().find(|r| !r["undo_op"].is_null() && r["undone_by"].is_null())` (885-888). It then calls `ui.call("audit.undo", json!({"audit_id":row["id"]})).await?` (890). audit.undo refuses with `audit.stale` when the entity's updated_at has moved since the op (crates/relay-core/src/handlers/audit.rs:58-63), and it leaves undone_by NULL. The next Ctrl+Z therefore selects the same row and fails again. Nothing skips the row, and `force` is never offered. The context menu's Delete runs without confirmation and says `"Ctrl+Z on the board restores it"` (2218-2226). The native client has no other task.restore or include_deleted path. A successful undo does not say what it undid.

**Impact.** Example: delete task A, then drag task B to Ready. An agent dispatched to B, or any agent task.update or link_commit on B, bumps B's updated_at. From then on every Ctrl+Z fails with 'the entity changed after the audited operation', and A cannot be restored from the app. Rows older than the 50 most recent task ops are also out of reach. A successful Ctrl+Z can silently revert an editor change made hours earlier.

**Fix.** When audit.undo fails with audit.stale or not_undoable, tell the user which task and op are blocked, and offer 'undo anyway' (force) or 'skip' (remember the skipped audit ids and move to the next candidate). On success, show 'Undid <op> on #id <title>'. Put Delete behind crate::app::confirm_inline, which already exists for destructive keys, or add a restore path for deleted tasks (task.list include_deleted plus task.restore).

**Verifier note.** This is not permanent data loss: task.delete is a soft delete (deleted_at), and task.restore can still be reached through the CLI or MCP, just not from the app. A deleted task's own delete row rarely goes stale, because the session updates guard on `deleted_at IS NULL`. The failure is that the deleted task gets shadowed by a newer stale row. Fix as proposed: on audit.stale, offer 'undo anyway' (force) or 'skip' (remember skipped ids and try the next candidate), and say what was undone on success. Also add a confirmation or a restore path for Delete.

**Also at:** `apps/relay-native/src/board_view.rs:2218`, `apps/relay-native/src/board_view.rs:882`, `crates/relay-core/src/handlers/audit.rs:58`, `apps/relay-native/src/app.rs:96`

#### RA-200 · Repeated P, Shift+J/K or [ ] presses are computed from the stale task list and collapse into one step

`apps/relay-native/src/board_view.rs:1137` · **medium** · Bug · confirmed · effort M

**Problem.** Keyboard commands read `self.tasks`, which changes only when a refresh round-trip lands in show() (502). `p` sends `order[(at + 1) % 4]`, with `at` taken from `text(&task, "priority")` (1136-1141). `[` and `]` take the target from the task's current column (1121-1131). nudge takes `next` from column_order (1163-1172). act() is fire-and-forget with no local update: it spawns the request and calls `ui.refresh_page()` (823-831). Nothing records the pending change.

**Impact.** Press P three times, or Shift+J three times, or hold Shift+J with key repeat, before task.list, module.list and a full render have come back. Every press sends the same payload ('high', or position at+1), so the card moves one step instead of three and the other presses are lost. On a large board, where the render alone is slow, normal typing speed is enough to hit this.

**Fix.** Apply the change to self.tasks optimistically (priority, column, position) and re-render before sending the request; the server's refresh then confirms or corrects it. Alternatively keep a per-task pending value that later presses build on.

**Verifier note.** Severity is medium at most, because the result is visible and self-correcting. The suggested fix is fine: apply the priority, column or position change to self.tasks and re-render before sending, then let the refresh reconcile.

#### RA-201 · Shift+J/K reorders against the unfiltered, ungrouped column, so it often does nothing visible

`apps/relay-native/src/board_view.rs:1163` · **medium** · Bug · confirmed · effort S

**Problem.** nudge finds the neighbour with `let order = self.column_order(&column);` (1163). column_order sorts every task in the column by (position, id) and ignores search, filters and grouping (811-821). nudge then sends `self.move_to(task, &column, Some(next as usize))` with `next = at ± 1` (1167-1172). The lane on screen, by contrast, comes from sorted() (1515-1529), which applies filters and orders by group_of first.

**Impact.** Filter type=bug on a column ordered bug1, chore1, bug2. Shift+J on bug1 moves it to index 1, after the hidden chore1, so the visible order stays bug1, bug2 and a second press is needed. With 'group by priority' the visible order is by group first. Shift+J then swaps a card with a card in another group, again with no visible change. Shift+K on the first card of a lower group does nothing. Whenever a filter, search or grouping is active, the doc comment's promise ('swaps places with its neighbour') does not hold.

**Fix.** Take the neighbour from the rendered lane (self.layout, which already reflects filters and grouping), then send `drop_index(&self.column_order(&column), id, neighbour, delta > 0)`. While grouping is active, refuse a move across groups, or tell the user why nothing moved.

**Verifier note.** Take the neighbour from the rendered lane (self.layout for this column), then compute the index with drop_index(&self.column_order(&column), id, neighbour, delta > 0), as drop_on already does. Under grouping, refuse moves across group boundaries.

#### RA-202 · Picking the current Status in the peek moves the card to the bottom of its column; the other pickers write no-op updates

`apps/relay-native/src/board_view.rs:2273` · **medium** · Bug · confirmed · effort S

**Problem.** picker() wires every value, the current one included: `key.connect_clicked(move |_| { ... pick(&board, value); })` (2273-2280). The current value is only styled (`key.add_css_class("selected")`, 2267-2269). Picking a Status calls `board.move_to(&moving, c, None)` (2356). For a non-done column, move_to sends `task.move` with no position (845-849), and the engine then appends the card at the end: `None => next_position(...)` (crates/relay-core/src/handlers/task.rs:901). The context menu disables only its current column (2158-2161); its Priority and Type keys stay clickable (2173-2199), and so do the peek's. task.update always rewrites updated_at (task.rs:887).

**Impact.** Open the peek on the second card in Ready and pick Status → Ready, which is a natural way to dismiss the picker. The card silently drops to the bottom of Ready, and an undo row is recorded. Re-picking the current priority, type or size writes a no-op task.update that bumps updated_at, which makes earlier undo rows for that task stale (see the undo finding).

**Fix.** In picker(), skip pick() when `value == current`, or make that key insensitive the way the context menu does for its current column. Apply the same rule to the context menu's priority and type keys.

**Verifier note.** Main harm: the card moves to the end of its column and the user can undo it with Ctrl+Z. The no-op updates are harmless apart from adding undo rows and bumping updated_at. Medium (a real bug on a less common path) is the right rating; it is not high. Fix: in picker(), make the current value's key insensitive or return early when `value == current`; do the same for the context menu's Priority and Type keys. Alternatively, have the engine's Move handler keep the task's position when `p.column == before.column && p.position.is_none()`.

#### RA-203 · is_conflict misses both-added (AA) and both-deleted (DD) merge conflicts

`apps/relay-native/src/code_git.rs:119` · **medium** · Bug · confirmed · effort S

**Problem.** `text(file, "index") == "U" || text(file, "worktree") == "U"` (118-120). Git's porcelain v1 marks unmerged entries as DD, AU, UD, UA, DU, AA or UU, and the engine passes both columns through unchanged (crates/relay-core/src/worktree.rs:106-108). Verified in a scratch repo: two branches adding the same file produce `AA new.txt` with conflict markers in it. change_summary (1779, `contains('U')`), note_changes (project_files.rs:559) and the engine's switch check (handlers/git.rs:415) all use the same U-only rule.

**Impact.** An AA conflict, for example two agents creating the same new file and their branches being merged, is not shown under MERGE CHANGES. It appears in both STAGED and CHANGES as an ordinary added file with Stage/Unstage keys. "Commit 1 staged" then fails with git's unmerged-files error, and pressing Stage silently resolves the conflict with the markers still in the file.

**Fix.** Add one shared helper that treats DD, AU, UD, UA, DU, AA and UU as unmerged, and use it in is_conflict, change_summary and note_changes (and in the engine's switch check).

**Verifier note.** The engine switch check matters less than the finding implies. A missed AA/DD falls into the `tracked` dirty list, and with carry_changes git itself refuses the checkout because the index is unmerged, so the user only gets a vaguer error. The fix is one shared helper: unmerged when either column is U, or the pair is AA or DD. Use it in is_conflict, change_summary, note_changes and the engine (better still, have the engine send an `unmerged` bool in FileStatus).

#### RA-204 · "Commit all" and "Mark as resolved" commit unresolved conflict markers

`apps/relay-native/src/code_git.rs:330` · **medium** · Bug · confirmed · effort S

**Problem.** Conflicted files are excluded from `staged` (257-258). With only conflicted files, `let smart_all = staged.is_empty();` is true (330), so the primary key reads "Commit all N" and is enabled whenever `files` is non-empty (344). "Commit all changes" is enabled the same way (364), and Ctrl+Enter computes `all = !has-staged` (277). With all=true the engine runs `git add -A` before committing (crates/relay-core/src/handlers/git.rs:544-547). "Mark all as resolved" and "Mark as resolved" (472, 906) call git.stage without checking for markers. Reproduced in a scratch repo: a UU merge conflict followed by `git add -A` and `git commit --no-verify` records the <<<<<<< and >>>>>>> lines in the commit.

**Impact.** After a merge or stash pop with conflicts, typing a message and pressing the default Commit key (or Ctrl+Enter) finishes the merge with conflict markers committed into the files.

**Fix.** Disable both commit modes and Ctrl+Enter while the conflicts group is non-empty, and say why. Before staging a conflicted file, scan it for conflict markers (or have the engine do it) and ask for confirmation. Have the engine refuse `all` when the index has unmerged entries.

**Verifier note.** Both trigger paths need a typed message. The Commit key refuses an empty one, and select_checkout clears it. The impact is recoverable: the commit can be amended or reverted, but it does land on the branch, possibly in an agent's worktree. Engine-side fix: refuse `all` (or any commit) while `git diff --name-only --diff-filter=U` is non-empty, and have the UI disable the commit keys while MERGE CHANGES is non-empty. Also covers AA files (see #8).

#### RA-205 · Change lists are rendered with no cap and rebuilt on every refresh

`apps/relay-native/src/code_git.rs:488` · **medium** · Performance · confirmed · effort M

**Problem.** `for file in group { group_section.body.append(&e.change_row(&ui, file, staged_group)); }` (487-489) runs for every git.status entry. The engine builds that list with `git status --porcelain=v1 -z --untracked-files=all` (worktree.rs:86-97), so every file inside an un-ignored directory appears. change_row creates about 8 widgets per file, plus motion and click controllers for images (855-929). Each refresh also walks the whole explorer through note_changes (172), which scans every change once per folder (project_files.rs:522-586). show_commit renders one row per file of a commit the same way (1480-1520).

**Impact.** A worktree with thousands of changes (an un-ignored venv, vendor or build directory, or a large codemod by an agent) makes each refresh build tens of thousands of widgets on the GTK main thread. Refreshes repeat on every file event, so the window stays frozen while agents work. At around 20K entries (about 100 bytes each) the git.status response exceeds the 2 MiB control-line limit and disconnects the client. Clicking a large import commit in History freezes the window once in the same way.

**Fix.** Render at most N rows per group (for example 500) followed by a "N more files" row, or use a GtkListView backed by a model. Cap the commit-file list the same way. Have the engine bound git.status output, or collapse untracked directories (--untracked-files=normal).

**Verifier note.** The trigger needs thousands of changes. In practice that means an un-ignored dependency or build directory, which --untracked-files=all expands file by file, or a very large codemod. Most repos ignore those directories, so this is an edge path rather than a normal flow. Medium, not high. The refresh only runs while the page is "code" or "agents" (editor.rs:509), not on every page. The fix is right: cap each group, or use a ListView, and pass --untracked-files=normal or cap the list in the engine so the 2 MiB frame cannot overflow.

#### RA-206 · The diff for a staged row or a renamed file compares HEAD with the working tree, not the change the row lists

`apps/relay-native/src/code_git.rs:898` · **medium** · Bug · confirmed · effort M

**Problem.** Rows under both STAGED and CHANGES call `ed.open_diff(&ui, diff_path.clone())` (896-899), and open_diff sends only `{"path":path}` (1333). git.diff.file always compares `revision_text(HEAD, path)` with `working_text(path)` and accepts no staged or old_path input (crates/relay-core/src/handlers/git.rs:235-255; DiffFileIn in crates/relay-bus/src/ops/git.rs:26), even though the engine already has index_text for the staged case. A renamed row's `renamed_from` (889) is not passed on.

**Impact.** When a staged file is changed again (routine when an agent edits a file the person staged), the STAGED row shows the newer, unstaged edits as if they were what will be committed. A renamed file shows as entirely new (+N −0) instead of showing what was edited.

**Fix.** Add `staged` and `old_path` to git.diff.file: HEAD↔index for staged rows, index↔working tree for unstaged rows, and the old path for renames. Pass them from change_row.

**Verifier note.** Renames show up in porcelain only once they are staged, so the rename case is a STAGED row. The fix as described holds: add staged and old_path to DiffFileIn, diff HEAD against the index for staged rows and the index against the working tree for unstaged rows, and use old_path in HEAD for renames.

#### RA-207 · invalidate() refreshes on file events from any project or checkout and re-raises a false 'Files changed on disk' banner

`apps/relay-native/src/editor.rs:508` · **medium** · Bug · confirmed · effort M

**Problem.** `pub fn invalidate(self: &Rc<Self>, ui: &Rc<Ui>)` gets no event; its only filter is `matches!(ui.page.borrow().as_str(), "code" | "agents")` (509, 517). app.rs:1232-1240 calls it for every "file.changed" | "git.changed" | "worktree.changed" | "integration.changed" | "integration.result". The project filter at app.rs:1213 skips only events whose envelope `project_id` is Some(other), but watcher events go out via `engine.emit_system("file.changed", payload)` (watch.rs:128) and `Event::new` sets `project_id: None` (envelope.rs:242), so they pass for every project. Watchers are never unregistered (watch.rs:134-139 only inserts). Lines 530-532, outside the page check: `if !self.path.borrow().is_empty() && !self.busy.get() && self.buffer.is_modified() { ui.show_error("Files changed on disk. Save checks for conflicting edits; discard reloads the file.") }`. Nothing compares the payload's worktree/path with the open document.

**Impact.** Any root that has ever been watched in this engine lifetime keeps triggering refreshes. That includes any checkout of any project the editor viewed, and any agent worktree touched by file_*/git_status MCP calls. Each agent edit makes the editor reload the tree, expanded folders, Git rail and scopes (or re-run the search) about once a second for a checkout that did not change. A user with unsaved edits gets the 'Files changed on disk' banner re-shown on every such event, even on other pages, while their file is untouched. The one real warning is then lost in the noise.

**Fix.** Pass `&e.payload` into invalidate. Ignore events whose payload project_id differs from ui.project, or whose canonical `worktree` is not the editor's root (map "" to the project path); still refresh scopes on worktree.changed. Raise the banner only when the payload `path` equals the open document (bus writes carry it) or after a hash check against `original`. Engine: emit watcher events with `Event::in_project(project_id)` so app.rs:1213 filters them.

**Verifier note.** The project mismatch is only part of it. Even with `Event::in_project`, other worktrees of the same project would still pass, so invalidate must also compare `payload.worktree` (canonical) against the editor's root, mapping "" to the project path. Watcher-originated file.changed has no `path`, so the banner needs either the changed path from the watcher or a sha check against `original`.

**Skeptic note.** Corrections to the first verifier:
- The data-loss claim ("points at Discard") is speculative. Save is protected by the sha check, and the banner text steers the user toward Save.

Corrections to the finding's impact:
- "Each agent edit" overstates it. An agent's file edits reach the editor only if its worktree is watched.
- The banner is frequent anyway: same-project worktree.changed (every spawn), git.changed, integration.* and agent commits (refs under the main .git) arrive regardless of watching.
- Add two paths:
  - the user's own save, echoed by the watcher about 125ms later;
  - other-project bus events, which app.rs:1213-1219 lets through on the dashboard and notifications pages.

Corrections to the fix:
1. `Event::in_project` alone does not stop the banner on the dashboard and notifications pages. The payload check inside `invalidate` is required.
2. Canonicalize the editor's root on the client before comparing. Map "" to `project.path`. Paths from `worktree.list` may not be canonical.
3. Events with no `worktree` (worktree.changed, integration.*) should refresh only and never raise the banner.
4. Watcher payloads carry no paths, although BUS.md:124 says they carry "the list of paths". git.* operations (checkout, reset, stash) can rewrite the open file while emitting only git.changed. So the banner should come from a sha check of the open file against `original`, run once in the debounced callback rather than on every event. Any path match must also match the worktree.
5. The sha check also silences the own-save echo.

**Blind re-check note.** 1. Watcher events carry no `path` (watch.rs:126 sends only project_id and worktree). Gating the banner on payload `path` would therefore miss real external edits to the open file, which agents usually make with their own tools. The hash/mtime check against `original` (or a re-read) is the necessary branch, not an optional alternative.
2. The payload `worktree` is canonicalized (watch.rs:52/76), so the editor's root must be canonicalized before comparing. For the main checkout, "" maps to the project path.
3. The app.rs:1213 filter is bypassed on the dashboard and notifications pages. invalidate's banner check runs there too, so the payload check in invalidate is still needed even after the engine tags these events with a project.
4. The claim that the refresh "reloads expanded folders" was not fully established. load_tree clears the tree and refetches the current directory.

#### RA-208 · An open document is never reloaded when its file changes on disk; a later save can only be resolved by discarding the edit

`apps/relay-native/src/editor.rs:517` · **medium** · Bug · confirmed · effort M

**Problem.** invalidate reloads only the tree or search, the Git rail and the scopes (517-526). read_file is called only from the Discard handler (`editor.read_file(&ui, path, true)`, 559-560) and from open (597). git_action clears the document only for `"git.branch.create" | "git.branch.switch"` (code_git.rs:1276-1279), not for pull/merge or other on-disk changes. On save the engine rejects a changed file with `file.edit_conflict` "File changed or was removed. Your draft has not been written." (file.rs:77-90). The editor shows it and re-enables Save (`ui.show_error(..); e.save.set_sensitive(true)`, 718-721), and Save then fails the same way.

**Impact.** Example: README.md is open and clean, then the user pulls through the Git panel, or an agent edits that file in the viewed checkout. The editor keeps showing the old text indefinitely, with no indication. If the user edits it, the save is rejected and the only action offered is Discard, which reloads and throws the draft away; otherwise they must copy it out by hand.

**Fix.** On a matching invalidate, if a document is open and clean, re-read it and replace the buffer, keeping cursor and scroll. If it is dirty and the on-disk hash differs from `original`, show a conflict bar with Reload (lose edits), Compare (reuse the diff view: disk vs draft) and Overwrite (save without expected_sha256 after confirmation).

**Verifier note.** The example 'the user pulls through the Git panel' is wrong: the native Git panel has no pull op (it has fetch, stage/unstage, commit, push, pr.open and branch create/switch/delete). Real triggers are agent writes in the viewed checkout, a terminal or external editor on the same files, and integration merges into the main checkout. A clean stale document can be refreshed by clicking the file in the tree again (open_path -> read_file), but nothing prompts the user to do so. Severity is medium, not high: the view is stale, but the conflict check blocks data loss.

#### RA-209 · Explorer refresh tears down and rebuilds the whole tree, snapping the scroll position to the top on every refresh

`apps/relay-native/src/editor.rs:589` · **medium** · Bug · confirmed · effort L

**Problem.** On success load_tree does `clear(&e.tree); e.render_tree(&ui, &e.tree, rows(&v, "entries"), revision);` (589-590). render_tree recreates each expanded folder with an empty `children` box and re-fetches its contents asynchronously: `if self.expanded.borrow().contains(&path) { toggle(true); }` → `glib::spawn_future_local(... ui.call("file.tree", payload) ...)` (841-854, 866-868). At the next layout only top-level rows exist. clear_document also runs `clear(&self.tree)` (505) whenever a document is closed.

**Impact.** Suppose folders are expanded and the user has scrolled into them. Each refresh (about once a second while agents work, see invalidate) collapses the content height before the children return. GtkViewport clamps the vertical adjustment, so the view jumps toward the top, and always to the top when the root listing is shorter than the sidebar. Expanded contents blink out and back, one nesting level per round trip. The focused row and any open right-click menu are destroyed.

**Fix.** Reconcile instead of rebuilding: keep rows keyed by path, update badges and classes in place, and insert or remove only changed entries. Alternatively move to gtk::ListView with a TreeListModel, which also virtualizes. At minimum, save the vadjustment value before clear() and restore it after the expanded loads finish, and stop clearing the tree in clear_document.

**Verifier note.** Drop the clear_document part. Every caller follows clear_document with load_tree (editor.rs:905-908, project_files.rs:96-97 and 387-388, code_git.rs:1277-1278), so it is a reload rather than a separate wipe. The jump happens only when the user has scrolled past the height of the root listing. That is common with expanded folders, but the effect is visual and nothing is lost, so medium rather than high. This was not run, because relay-native cannot be built here. The minimum fix: save the vadjustment value and restore it after the expanded children render, or skip the rebuild when the entries are unchanged. A ListView with TreeListModel is the full fix.

#### RA-210 · The explorer renders every entry of a directory eagerly (about 15 widgets and controllers per row) with no cap or virtualization

`apps/relay-native/src/editor.rs:746` · **medium** · Performance · confirmed · effort L

**Problem.** `for entry in entries { ... let row = button("", "tree-row"); ...}` (746-885). Each row gets a content box, chevron box, glyph box, label, badge, DrawingArea guides and an icons::image with two signal handlers. bind_tree_row adds two GestureClicks and a DragSource, plus a DropTarget for folders (project_files.rs:263-337). file.tree returns the whole directory (file.rs:508-525) over the control connection, which is capped at 2 MiB per line (client.rs:48).

**Impact.** Opening, or keeping expanded, a folder with thousands of entries (assets, fixtures, generated docs) blocks the GTK main thread on each render. Because the tree is rebuilt on every refresh, the stall repeats about once a second during agent activity. A directory of roughly 10k entries produces a file.tree response over 2 MiB, which disconnects the UI (client.rs:200-205).

**Fix.** Use gtk::ListView with a TreeListModel, which creates and recycles rows on demand. At minimum, page large directories (first N entries plus 'Show more') and ask the engine for a bounded listing.

**Verifier note.** The trigger is narrower than the finding implies. list_dir already drops .git, .relay and every is_generated_path directory (node_modules, target, build, dist, Intermediate, Saved, DerivedDataCache, Binaries, ...), so it takes a large hand-kept folder (icon sets, fixtures, asset dumps) to hit the stall. The repeat comes from invalidate's 1 s debounce re-fetching every expanded folder, not from a generic refresh. Cheapest useful fix: cap entries per file.tree response with a `truncated` flag plus a 'Show more' row, and refresh only changed folders rather than rebuilding every expanded one. ListView with TreeListModel is the full fix.

#### RA-211 · Dropping a tree item onto a file row moves it to the project root

`apps/relay-native/src/editor.rs:949` · **medium** · Bug · confirmed · effort S

File rows and the `children` box that holds a folder's contents (editor.rs:793-798) have none, so a drop over them bubbles up to the root target with `into == ""`. **Fix.** Give file rows (or each folder's children box) a drop target whose `into` is the row's parent folder, as VS Code does. Treat `parent(path) == into` as a no-op that returns false.

**Verifier note.** Also covers releasing a short drag over the dragged file itself. Fix as proposed: give file rows (or each children box) a drop target whose `into` is the parent folder, and treat `parent(path) == into` as a no-op that returns false.

#### RA-212 · Explorer search renders unbounded hit lines; one long line (minified JS, source map) disconnects the UI from the engine

`apps/relay-native/src/editor.rs:1110` · **medium** · Bug · confirmed · effort S

**Problem.** run_search asks for up to 100 hits (`json!({"query":query,"limit":100,"regex":false})`, 1110). It renders each hit's full text as a label (`label(text(&hit, "text").trim(), "search-snippet")`, 1156) and as a tooltip (`b.set_tooltip_text(Some(text(&hit, "text")))`, 1160). The engine's hit text is the whole matching line (`text: text[start..end].trim_end_matches('\r').to_string()`, file.rs:364), and search does not skip dist/build output (file.rs:629-635). The UI control connection rejects any line over `MAX_LINE = 2 * 1024 * 1024` (client.rs:48) by returning `Err(Error::Protocol(format!("frame exceeds {} MiB", ..)))` from the reader (client.rs:200-205), which tears the connection down. app.rs:1267-1275 then marks the engine disconnected until the user clicks Reconnect.

**Impact.** Searching for an identifier that also appears in a single-line source map or minified bundle fails with 'Invalid engine response: frame exceeds 2 MiB' when that line is 2 MiB or more, or when up to 100 long lines add up past 2 MiB. Every UI request then fails until the manual reconnect, which also restarts the terminal panes. Shorter long lines still make Pango shape hundreds of KB per label on the GTK main thread.

**Fix.** Engine: return a bounded snippet around the match (e.g. 240 chars or fewer, cut on char boundaries) plus line/col, and skip generated directories as the tree does. Client: truncate snippet and tooltip text before creating labels.

**Verifier note.** Unverified: the claim that reconnecting 'restarts the terminal panes' was not checked and should be dropped. Also note the root cause of the divergence: search uses its own skip_dir list, which has drifted from watch::is_generated_path, the list the tree uses. Fix: have the engine return a bounded snippet around the match (cut on char boundaries) plus line/col, reuse is_generated_path in search, and optionally add a total-bytes budget for the response.

**Skeptic note.** 1. Keep the terminal-pane claim, reworded. It is accurate: Ui::connect stops and drops every pane (app.rs:1139-1142) and rebuilds them. Suggested wording: "Reconnect tears down and re-creates every terminal pane; agent processes keep running." Add that terminals keep working while the control channel is down.

2. Add to the impact: the retained search text re-runs the search on the next file.changed or git.changed event (app.rs:1240, editor.rs:508-523). The UI therefore disconnects again until the user clears the search box.

3. Note the reproduction: in the author's own checkout, "fn" and "Some" produce 6.7 MB responses. The source is font-index.json under .agents/.claude/skills, which is git-excluded but still searched.

4. Corrections to the fix:
- Skipping is_generated_path directories would not fix the author's own case, because that file is not under a generated directory. Bounding the hit text in the engine is the essential part. Respecting .gitignore and .git/info/exclude is optional.
- col is a byte offset into the whole line (file.rs:363). If text becomes a window around the match, either cap only lines that are too long and add an optional field such as text_offset or truncated, or redefine col. Update BUS.md:853 to match.
- Add a total-bytes budget per response.
- Truncating on the client only fixes GTK rendering. It cannot prevent the frame error, because the line is rejected before it is parsed.
- Hardening for the whole class of oversize responses: make the control reader fail only the oversized response instead of tearing down the connection. It can discard bytes up to the newline and take the request id from the {"v":1,"id": prefix, which shape() already relies on.

**Blind re-check note.** The line numbers in the claim are roughly right: skip_dir is at about file.rs:629 and the disconnect handler at about app.rs:1267. Reconnecting restarts the terminal panes in the client only; the engine sessions keep running. Caveats on the fix:
- file.search is also an agent/MCP op. Changing `text` to a snippet changes the bus contract for those callers. Prefer adding a capped `snippet` field (or capping only when the line is very long), or document the change in BUS.md.
- Adding dist/ and build/ to skip_dir by name could hide hand-written source directories called "build". Gitignore-aware skipping would be safer than a fixed name list.

**Also at:** `crates/relay-core/src/handlers/file.rs:364`, `apps/relay-native/src/client.rs:48`, `apps/relay-native/src/client.rs:200`, `apps/relay-native/src/app.rs:1267`

#### RA-213 · Clicking a search hit opens the file but ignores the hit's line and column

`apps/relay-native/src/editor.rs:1165` · **medium** · Bug · confirmed · effort S

**Problem.** The row shows `format!("{directory} · line {}", hit["line"])` (1147-1151), but the click handler is just `ed.open(&ui, path.clone())` (1163-1166). read_file takes no position and never moves the cursor after `e.buffer.set_text(content)` (660-671). The engine returns 1-based `line` and a byte `col` per hit (file.rs:356-363).

**Impact.** Every search result opens at the wrong place, with the caret at end of buffer (see the set_text finding) rather than on the match. The user has to search again with Ctrl+F.

**Fix.** Carry an Option<(line, col)> into read_file. After set_text, place the cursor with `buffer.iter_at_line_index(line-1, col-1)` (col is a byte offset), select the match, and scroll with `view.scroll_to_mark(&buffer.get_insert(), ..)`.

**Verifier note.** col is a 1-based byte offset within the line, so use iter_at_line_index(line-1, col-1). Then select the query length and call scroll_to_mark on the insert mark, ideally after the view has its size allocated (e.g. idle_add), or the scroll may not take effect.

#### RA-214 · Trashed files and soft-deleted notes cannot be restored from the app: no op lists them and the Undo button is transient, yet the delete dialog promises 'restored from Relay trash'

`apps/relay-native/src/editor.rs:1225` · **medium** · Data loss · confirmed · effort M

**Problem.** editor.rs:1225 tells the user 'The file can be restored from Relay trash.' The only restore path is the 'Undo trash' button appended to file_undo (1300-1334). reset() clears it on any project switch (476), and it does not survive a restart. The bus has file.restore {trash_id} but no op that lists trash (relay-bus ops/file.rs). notes.list always filters `deleted_at IS NULL` and has no include_deleted (handlers/notes.rs:341-345, ops/notes.rs:6). The board's Ctrl+Z only searches `op_prefix: task.` (board_view.rs:882). Trash payloads are stored inside the worktree (file.rs:230), so they vanish when a pooled worktree is removed while the file_trash row stays open. BUS.md §5.4 promises these items are 'restorable by *.restore for the grace window'.

Note also that nothing ever hard-deletes file_trash rows or payloads: the only DELETE is on project removal (workspace.rs:369), so the 'grace window' in §5.4 is not enforced for files. The fix should add the listing ops, a trash and recently-deleted UI, and trash storage that outlives the worktree.

#### RA-215 · file_action closes the open document and leaves the agents view after any create/rename/trash, even for unrelated paths

`apps/relay-native/src/editor.rs:1294` · **medium** · Bug · confirmed · effort S

**Problem.** `e.set_busy(true)` (1265). set_busy switches the content stack whenever busy: `if busy || !self.agents_visible() { ... set_visible_child_name(... "source" ...) }` (456-464). On success the handler always runs `e.clear_document()` (1294) and then, for a file, opens the result with `e.open(&ui, text(&v, "path").to_string())` (1335-1337). The expanded set is remapped for a renamed folder (1273-1287), but a document open inside that folder is not. bind_tree_drop already does both correctly: it saves `let agents = ed.agents_visible()`, remaps the open path by suffix and restores agents (project_files.rs:374-394), and select_checkout also preserves agents (95-109).

**Impact.** Trashing or renaming some other file from the explorer while watching agents switches the main area to the editor and closes the document being read. Renaming a folder that contains the open file closes it instead of following it. The post-move logic now exists twice and the copies have diverged.

**Fix.** Factor the drop handler's follow-up into one helper: remap the open path by prefix, close it only if it was deleted, and keep the agents view. Call it from file_action and bind_tree_drop. For non-document operations, mark busy without switching views.

**Verifier note.** Not every case named is wrong. After file.create, and after renaming the open file itself, opening the result (1335-1337) is reasonable. The defects are: (1) set_busy(true) leaves the agents view for every op; (2) file.delete, and file.rename of a folder or of some other file, close the current document. Renaming an unrelated file even opens that file in place of the current one. Fix: one shared post-move helper used by file_action and bind_tree_drop. It remaps the open path by prefix, closes the document only when it was itself deleted, and restores the agents view. set_busy should not switch views for explorer-only operations.

#### RA-216 · Bundled Medium/SemiBold fonts are unreachable from CSS weights: Fira Mono 500/600 render Regular on this machine, and without system Fira every weight collapses

`apps/relay-native/src/fonts.rs:21` · **medium** · Bug · confirmed · effort S

**Problem.** fonts.rs:21-30 registers the fontsource subsets unchanged, and resources/fonts/README.md confirms the naming tables were not edited. fontconfig (fc-scan) therefore sees one family per weight. fira-sans-latin-500 is family 'Fira Sans Medium' and 600 is 'Fira Sans SemiBold'. fira-mono-latin-500 is 'Fira Mono Medium'. Condensed 500/600 are 'Fira Sans Condensed Medium'/'… SemiBold'. Only the Condensed *700* file has family 'Fira Sans Condensed'. The CSS requests weights inside the base families: `'Fira Sans'` at 500/600 (theme.css:25 buttons, :48 session names), `'Fira Sans Condensed'` at 600 (theme.css:20 section labels, board.css:47 lane titles) and `'Fira Mono'` at 500/600 (git_files.css:66 `.tree-badge`, :102 `.git-branch-name`, :199 `.scm-letter`, theme.css:323 `.notification-count`, tools.css:137/143, usage.css:59). Fontconfig matches the family name first. I reproduced this with Pango 1.58 and explicit family+weight descriptions, as GTK builds them. With this machine's real font set plus the app's registered files, 'Fira Mono' 500 and 600 resolve to the Regular face; this machine has no system Fira Mono. With a private FONTCONFIG_FILE that sees only the bundled files, 'Fira Sans' 500/600 resolve to Regular, and 'Fira Sans Condensed' 400/500/600 all resolve to the Bold face. The system ttf-fira-sans package installed here hides the Sans/Condensed part. No italic face is bundled, so the italic rules (guardrails.css:13, git_files.css:68) get synthesized obliques.

**Impact.** On the author's machine, every medium/semibold Fira Mono label renders Regular: git status letters and badges, notification counts, branch names, usage percentages. On any machine without system Fira fonts, which is the case bundling exists for, every 500/600 Fira Sans weight renders Regular and every condensed caption renders Bold. The type hierarchy in DESIGN.md is lost. The smoke assertion (smoke.rs:62-69) only loads 'Fira Mono 10' at weight 400, so it cannot catch this.

**Fix.** Give the bundled files typographic names: with fontTools, set name IDs 1/2 (or 16/17) to 'Fira Sans' + 'Medium'/'SemiBold' etc., or ship the upstream Fira TTFs, which carry these names. Alternatively, install an app fontconfig scan-time rule that maps the per-weight families back to the base family. Extend the smoke font check to assert a 600 Sans, a 600 Condensed and a 500 Mono face.

**Verifier note.** The impact is visual only (lost weight hierarchy) but appears in normal use, so medium is fair. A further detail: the Condensed 700 face is reached only because its family name happens to be the base family. The fix stands: rename the families (name IDs 1/2 or 16/17) with fontTools, or ship the upstream TTFs. Extend smoke.rs to assert a 500 Mono face, a 600 Sans face and a 600 Condensed face.

`apps/relay-native/src/guardrail_pages.rs:431` · **medium** · Security · confirmed · effort M

**Problem.** The prompt pops up by itself on `guardrail.held` and renders the agent's text in full, in wrapping selectable labels: `let why = paragraph(&format!("“{reason}”"), "body");` (431) and `card.append(&mono(value));` (427). Nothing bounds that text: `grants::validate` (crates/relay-core/src/guardrail/grants.rs:195-216) only checks emptiness and `..`, and `guardrail.request` is AgentOnly, "every agent may call it" (relay-bus ops/guardrail.rs:103). "Review exact action" pretty-prints the whole frozen payload: `shown.push_str(&serde_json::to_string_pretty(&request["payload"])...)` (333). The Claude hook sends the entire resulting file as `new_text` for every Write and Edit (crates/relay-cli/src/main.rs:415, 432), and an agent's destructive_write hold keeps that envelope. The control socket caps a line at 2 MiB, and an over-long line tears the whole connection down (client.rs:48, 200-205 `Err(Error::Protocol("frame exceeds ..."))`). Several calls return these texts on that socket: restore_prompts calls `guardrail.requests.list {state: open}` (706) on every connect (app.rs:1160), the Guardrails page calls `guardrail.holds.list` (pages.rs:45), and the dashboard's `holds_open` has no LIMIT (handlers/notify.rs:168).

**Impact.** An agent that pastes a build log into `reason` (or a prompt-injected one, on purpose) pops a label of that size onto the main thread: a long freeze, repeated on every relayout. Past about 2 MiB, `guardrail.request.get`, the open-request list sent on connect, the Guardrails page and the dashboard all exceed the frame cap. The desktop client then disconnects right after every reconnect, until the request is answered from another client or its session closes. Reviewing an agent's held rewrite of a large file (for example a regenerated lockfile) has the same effect: above 2 MiB it disconnects. Because "Allow once" is only enabled after a successful review, such a hold can never be allowed from the desktop.

**Fix.** Put no unbounded text in labels. Cap value and reason at a few KB, with a "Show all (N KB)" expander that opens a TextView. For the exact action, show op, path, sizes and a capped preview or diff stat instead of the raw new_text. Cap value and reason length in `grants::validate`. Have `guardrail.hold.get` elide large string fields unless explicitly asked. Bound the list ops (and dashboard `holds_open`).

**Verifier note.** Rated medium rather than high because every trigger is abnormal. It needs an agent that is confused or prompt-injected into writing a multi-MB reason or value, or a held rewrite of a file over 2 MiB. A held destructive_write does not cause the reconnect loop: holds.list details carry only numbers and the path, and new_text appears only in hold.get, so that case gives one failed review and one reconnect, not a loop. The loop comes only from exception requests. Fix: cap reason and value length in grants::validate, cap engine request line size, show new_text as a capped preview or summary in the exact-action view, and truncate long labels behind an expander.

**Also at:** `apps/relay-native/src/guardrail_pages.rs:427`, `apps/relay-native/src/guardrail_pages.rs:333`, `apps/relay-native/src/guardrail_pages.rs:706`, `apps/relay-native/src/guardrail_pages.rs:805`, `apps/relay-native/src/pages.rs:45`, `apps/relay-native/src/client.rs:200`, `apps/relay-native/src/tools.rs:365`, `crates/relay-core/src/guardrail/grants.rs:195`, `crates/relay-cli/src/main.rs:432`, `crates/relay-core/src/handlers/notify.rs:168`

`apps/relay-native/src/guardrail_pages.rs:551` · **medium** · Bug · confirmed · effort S

#### RA-219 · The image decoder's 100-megapixel guard never fires on gdk-pixbuf 2.44 (glycin), and the decoder is chosen by content sniffing

`apps/relay-native/src/image_preview.rs:123` · **medium** · Bug · confirmed · effort S

**Problem.** decode_to records dimensions in `connect_size_prepared` and checks `i64::from(width) * i64::from(height) > 100_000_000` only after each `loader.write(chunk)` (112-127). With gdk-pixbuf 2.44's glycin backend, which this machine uses (gdk-pixbuf2 2.44.7, glycin 2.1.5), writes are only buffered and size-prepared fires inside `close()`. Scratchpad experiment: a 341 KB PNG declaring 11000x10000 (110 MP) went through 42 writes with no size-prepared, was fully decoded at close and scaled to 4095x3723, and the process peaked at 393 MB RSS. `PixbufLoader::new()` (109) picks the format from the file's content, not its name. So a file named .png can be decoded by any installed decoder, including third-party ones that run inside the process (here libopenraw_pixbuf.so, which registers TIFF signatures).

**Impact.** Holding the pointer over a worktree image for 350 ms (bind_image_hover), or opening it, decodes it at full resolution regardless of the limit. A small, highly compressed PNG written by an agent or pulled from a repo, for example 30000x30000 RGBA (3.6 GB decoded), can exhaust memory and get the GTK client OOM-killed. Several hovers decode at the same time.

**Fix.** Read the dimensions from the header before decoding (for example with a header parser such as the imagesize crate) and reject images over the limit, keeping a check after close as well. Create the loader with `PixbufLoader::with_type` from the file extension so the content cannot select a different decoder.

**Verifier note.** Change the category from security to bug or resource exhaustion. The worst outcome is the GTK client being OOM-killed, not an escape or an engine compromise, and I did not establish whether glycin's own sandbox memory limits stop the 3.6 GB case. The content-sniffing half of the finding is weak. Repo images are untrusted whichever decoder runs, and with_type from the extension would still route PNG, TIFF and similar files to the same decoders. Drop that half. Fix: read the dimensions from the image header before decoding, reject anything over the limit, and repeat the check after close().

**Also at:** `apps/relay-native/src/image_preview.rs:109-130`, `apps/relay-native/src/image_preview.rs:337-351`, `apps/relay-native/src/image_preview.rs:409-412`

#### RA-220 · Opening New session builds 11 full agent forms with 11 copies of every open task card synchronously on the GTK thread, and keeps them after the sheet closes

`apps/relay-native/src/launch.rs:628` · **medium** · Performance · confirmed · effort M

**Problem.** `let profiles: Rc<Vec<_>> = Rc::new((0..11).map(|i| Profile::new(i, compact)).collect());` (454). The count control only offers 1 to 6 (`gtk::DropDown::from_strings(&["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"])`, 437) and a review group uses profiles 0 to 2, so profiles 6 to 10 can never be shown. After task.list returns, the loader runs `for (profile_index, profile) in p.iter().enumerate() { ... for (index, row) in tasks.iter().filter(|t| text(t, "column") != "done").enumerate() { ... } }` (628-717) with no await. Each card is a ToggleButton, an Overlay, 2 Boxes, 4 Labels (one holding the full task body) and an Image, plus a lowercased search string. Nothing clears `launch_box` when the sheet hides: close, scrim and Escape only call `set_reveal_child(false)` (384, app.rs:985, 1004).

**Impact.** Example: a project with 300 open tasks gets 3,300 task cards, about 30k widgets, each body label holding the whole task text. They are created in one main-loop turn every time the user presses New session (or Ctrl+N), which freezes the whole window, terminals included. Tens of MB stay retained in the hidden revealer afterwards. The cost grows linearly with the backlog.

**Fix.** Create profiles only up to the selected count (at most 6). Use one task model shared by all profiles (a GridView over a ListStore with per-profile selection sets), or build a profile's cards only when its key is first shown. Clear `launch_box` when the sheet hides.

**Verifier note.** There are 3 Boxes per card (card, line, overlay child), not 2. Nothing is retained across opens: clear(&self.launch_box) at the start of show_launch frees the previous form, so retention is bounded to one form, and the 'tens of MB' figure is not established. Medium is right: it is a backlog-scaled UI stall, small at typical backlog sizes. The cheapest fix is to build only 6 profiles, or to build lazily the profiles the count shows, and to fill a profile's task grid when its member key is first selected.

#### RA-221 · Launch stages task queues only after every agent is allocated, so a later allocation failure drops earlier agents' queues while the error says they are preserved

`apps/relay-native/src/launch.rs:810` · **medium** · Error handling · confirmed · effort S

**Problem.** Allocation loop: `if let Some(task)=tasks.first(){payload["task_id"]=json!(task);} let session=ui.call("session.create",payload).await?;` (804-805). Only after all agents exist: `for(session,tasks,_)in &allocated{for task in tasks{ ... ui.call("task.dispatch",json!({"task_id":task,"session":session["name"],"start":false})).await?;}}` (810). Any `?` exits the block, and the user then sees `"Launch incomplete: {e}. Created sessions and queues are preserved. Start the remaining sessions individually from the wall."` (824). session.create records only the first task in task_sessions (session.rs:821-825). The move to the active column and the rest of the queue come only from task.dispatch (task.rs:667, 671).

**Impact.** Example: a solo launch of 3 agents, where agent 1 has tasks #4, #7 and #9, and agent 3's worktree create fails (fetch error, name reservation, review_group_full). Agents 1 and 2 exist, but #7 and #9 were never staged and #4 was never moved to active. The banner says the queues are preserved, so the user starts agent 1 from the wall and it only ever works on #4. A dispatch failure partway through (for example a task moved to done meanwhile) likewise leaves the later queues unstaged and starts no agent.

**Fix.** Dispatch each agent's tasks (start:false) right after its own session.create, inside the allocation loop. Build the failure message from what was actually staged, naming the agents and tasks that were not.

**Verifier note.** The first task is linked through task_sessions but stays in its original column. The rest of the queue is lost. Fix: dispatch each agent's tasks with start:false right after its own session.create, and word the error from what was actually created and staged.

#### RA-222 · Closing the main window leaves mirror windows, and a docked mirror's stream, running; the process does not exit

`apps/relay-native/src/mirror.rs:630` · **medium** · Resource leak · confirmed · effort S

**Problem.** Mirror windows are application windows: `gtk::Window::builder().application(&ui.window.application().unwrap()).transient_for(&ui.window)`, with no destroy_with_parent (587-593). The main window's close handler (app.rs:1032-1072) closes panels, destroys the Notes window explicitly (1062-1064) and stops panes, but never closes mirror views. VIEWS holds every view and its session task strongly (52-57), including a docked view whose Dock lives in the main window's overlay (643).

**Impact.** With a mirror window open, closing Relay's main window leaves the process running with an orphan mirror window. Its engine connection, the scrcpy server on the phone and FFmpeg keep streaming. A docked mirror inside the destroyed main window keeps streaming invisibly until the last mirror window is closed. Once the `Ui` has been dropped, Retry (`start`, 707), Dock (628/584) and the device picker (956, stuck on "Loading devices…") in the orphan window do nothing.

**Fix.** Add `mirror::close_all()`, which calls `close()` on every view in VIEWS, and call it from the main window's close handler next to the Notes cleanup. Alternatively, set `destroy_with_parent(true)` on mirror windows and close docked views explicitly.

**Verifier note.** Narrower than claimed. With only a docked mirror and no mirror window, no application window remains, so the process exits and nothing leaks. The orphan stays visible and the user can close it, after which the app exits. Fix: add mirror::close_all() and call it in the close handler next to the Notes cleanup.

#### RA-223 · Mirror control keys keep keyboard focus after a click, so Space and Enter re-press Back, Power and the others instead of reaching the phone

`apps/relay-native/src/mirror/glyphs.rs:53` · **medium** · Bug · confirmed · effort S

**Problem.** Every strip, rail and nav control is a plain `gtk::Button::new()` from `glyphs::key` (52-61): focusable, focus-on-click. GtkButton grabs focus on press and binds Space/KP_Space/Return/ISO_Enter/KP_Enter to "activate" in its own bubble-phase shortcut controller. The mirror's key handler is an EventControllerKey on `self.root` (mirror.rs:480-532), which sees an event only after the focused button has. A control click only sends the event (mirror.rs:374-391); focus returns to the picture only on a drag (406).

**Impact.** Click Back (or Recents, Volume, Power, Screen off), then type "hello world". The letters reach the device, but the space activates the focused button again and presses Back mid-sentence. If Power was clicked, the space turns the screen off; Enter after Home re-presses Home. Keyboard input after any mouse use of the controls is unreliable.

**Fix.** In `glyphs::key`, call `button.set_focus_on_click(false)` (or `set_focusable(false)` for rail and nav keys), or have the control click handler call `view.picture.grab_focus()` after sending.

**Verifier note.** The strip keys are affected as well: after clicking Full screen, Space toggles full screen again. The simplest fix is button.set_focus_on_click(false) inside glyphs::key, which keeps the keys reachable by Tab for accessibility. Calling view.picture.grab_focus() at the end of the controls' click handler also works.
