#### RA-224 · Unsaved notes of other projects are hidden with no indicator, and the quit guard blocks on them without saying where they are

`apps/relay-native/src/note_pages.rs:1126` · **medium** · Bug · confirmed · effort M

**Problem.** workspace() hides every other project's tab, dirty or not: `let mine = doc.project == project; doc.draft.layout.set_visible(mine);` (1125-1126). Unsaved dots exist only on library rows of the project being shown (738, 839-846). The project picker shows names only (pages.rs:187-251). Reopening Notes from the main window switches it to the main window's project: show_notes -> `show_project(ui, ui.project.get())` -> `window.project.set(project)` (notes_window.rs:153-164). The quit guard counts drafts of every project, `.note_drafts.borrow().values().any(|d| d.busy.get() || d.dirty())`, and says only 'Save or discard note changes before closing.' (app.rs:1037-1044). It also never calls note_pages::flush (298-307), even with autosave on.

**Impact.** Trigger: edit a note in project A (autosave is off by default), switch the main window to B, and open Notes from the sidebar or pick B in the Notes picker. The A tab disappears, nothing in Notes shows that an unsaved draft exists, and Relay refuses to quit with a generic message. The user has to step the picker through every project to find the draft. If A is then removed, the hidden draft can never be shown again: the picker lists only existing projects, and nothing else calls edit() for it. Relay then can't be closed normally at all. With autosave on, quitting within 1.5 s of the last keystroke is refused instead of saved.

**Fix.** Track drafts that are dirty in a project other than the shown one, and surface them with a picker badge or a banner whose 'Show' links call show_project(doc.project) and focus the tab. Make the quit guard name the notes and their projects, and open Notes on the first one. On quit with autosave on, call note_pages::flush and close once the saves land. Close or migrate docs whose project was removed (see the removed-project finding).

**Verifier note.** There is one partial way out: open_note (pages.rs:26-28) switches Notes to the note's own project. So opening a note of project A from elsewhere in the app shows the hidden tab, but nothing tells the user to do that. The 'with autosave on, quit within 1.5 s is refused' part is minor, because retrying after the timer fires succeeds. Medium severity stands, driven by the hidden draft plus the generic quit refusal, and by the unrecoverable case after a project is removed.

#### RA-225 · Engine strings containing U+0000 trip glib's NUL check: a panic in the debug build the app runs, an empty editor in release

`apps/relay-native/src/note_pages/doc.rs:145` · **medium** · Bug · confirmed · effort S

**Problem.** `buffer.set_text(text(note, "body"));`. The same happens at line 102 (the title Entry builder) and at lines 523/525 in load. In glib 0.22.9, both `to_glib_none` for str and `GString::from(&str)` run `if cfg!(debug_assertions) { GStr::check_interior_nuls(self).unwrap(); }` (translate.rs:563-565, gstring.rs:1953-1955). The workspace keeps debug assertions in the dev profile, which is what run.sh launches (Cargo.toml:46-57). Nothing in the engine strips NUL from notes.append/create/update text or from session.done summaries, and serde_json decodes "\u0000" into the String. The same labels and tooltips exist in notification_center.rs:220/228/234, session_context.rs:145-159 and note_pages.rs:742.

**Impact.** Trigger: an agent appends text containing a NUL to a note, for example output read from a binary file.
- Activating that note from the library (a row_activated signal) panics inside an extern "C" trampoline and aborts the client; unsaved notes are lost.
- Inside refresh futures, glib's executor swallows the panic and the render stops part-way: the Notes library list empties, the bell list or slate card is left incomplete.
- In a release build GTK refuses the insert because g_utf8_validate fails on NUL. The buffer stays empty while base keeps the body, the note shows Modified, and any save writes "" over the stored body.

**Fix.** Sanitise at the boundary. Replace '\0' (e.g. with U+FFFD) in `text()`, or before any string reaches GTK. Also reject NUL in the engine's note, session and report text inputs with a typed error.

**Verifier note.** I could not establish how often agents really produce \u0000, so the frequency is uncertain. The mechanism is not. The best fix is to reject NUL in the engine's text inputs (notes.*, session.done/report summaries, notify bodies) with a typed error, because one rule there covers every client. The client can also map '\0' to U+FFFD in its shared `text()` helper as a second guard.

**Also at:** `apps/relay-native/src/note_pages/doc.rs:102`, `apps/relay-native/src/note_pages/doc.rs:525`, `apps/relay-native/src/notification_center.rs:220`, `apps/relay-native/src/notification_center.rs:228`, `apps/relay-native/src/session_context.rs:148`, `apps/relay-native/src/note_pages.rs:742`

<a id="ra-226"></a>

#### RA-226 · Every buffer 'changed' signal copies the whole note 2–3 times, so Replace all or undo on a large note freezes the UI for O(matches × size)

`apps/relay-native/src/note_pages/doc.rs:369` · **medium** · Performance · confirmed · effort S

**Problem.** `doc.buffer.connect_changed(move |_| changed());` calls `fn changed(..) { self.refresh_state(ui); self.schedule_counts(); self.schedule_autosave(ui); }`. That one handler does all of this:
- refresh_state calls `self.dirty()` (563). That is Draft::dirty, which calls `(self.snapshot)()` and so `buffer_text()`: a full copy plus a JSON compare (task_pages.rs:174-179, doc.rs:297).
- refresh_state calls `self.name()` (584).
- refresh_state calls `super::update_chrome(ui)` (594), which clones all docs via current_doc and calls `doc.name()` and `doc.dirty()` again (note_pages.rs:820-824).
- schedule_autosave calls `self.dirty()` once more when autosave is on (601).
GtkSourceView's replace_all does a delete plus an insert per match, which is two 'changed' emissions per match, and undo replays them. The cursor-position notify also runs update_count per shifted offset.

**Impact.** Example: Replace all on a 500 KB note with 5,000 matches. That is 10,000 handler runs, each making 2–3 full-text copies and comparisons, about 15 GB copied. The GTK main thread freezes for seconds, and for minutes on MB-sized notes; undoing it does the same. Typing in a multi-MB note costs several full copies per keystroke.

**Fix.** Coalesce the work. The changed handler should only mark the state stale and schedule one idle callback, as schedule_counts already does, that runs refresh_state and schedule_autosave once. Compute dirty once per idle, or keep a cheap edit counter and compare text only then. Pass the already-computed dirty flag and name to update_chrome.

**Verifier note.** The freeze needs both a large note (hundreds of KB or more, which notes.append can grow) and many matches, so it is an uncommon path and the severity stays medium, not high. The auditor's '15 GB' figure is a worst-case extrapolation and was not measured. The fix stands: mark the state stale in the handler and do one idle refresh that computes dirty once and passes it to update_chrome and schedule_autosave.

**Also at:** `apps/relay-native/src/note_pages/doc.rs:371`, `apps/relay-native/src/note_pages/doc.rs:563`, `apps/relay-native/src/note_pages/doc.rs:594`, `apps/relay-native/src/note_pages/doc.rs:601`, `apps/relay-native/src/note_pages.rs:818`, `apps/relay-native/src/task_pages.rs:174`, `apps/relay-native/src/note_pages.rs:823`, `apps/relay-native/src/task_pages.rs:174-179`, `apps/relay-native/src/note_pages/menu.rs:426`

**Merged duplicates:** native-notes-a#6

<a id="ra-227"></a>

#### RA-227 · Note bodies have no size limit but the UI socket caps lines at 2 MiB: one large note, or a project's notes over 2 MiB in total, disconnects the UI on every refresh

`apps/relay-native/src/note_pages/doc.rs:1130` · **medium** · Bug · confirmed · effort M

**Problem.** save() sends the whole buffer (`"body": next["body"]`) with no size check. notes.create, notes.update and notes.append accept any size (notes.rs:356-487). Three messages carry full note bodies:
- the update response;
- the `notes.changed` event, built as `ctx.emit("notes.changed", serde_json::to_value(note))` (notes.rs:63-66);
- notes.list, which returns every live note's full body (`SELECT * FROM notes WHERE project_id = ?1 AND deleted_at IS NULL`, notes.rs:341-349).
The UI's control connection rejects any line over `MAX_LINE = 2 * 1024 * 1024` (client.rs:48, 200-205) by ending its reader with `Error::Protocol("frame exceeds 2 MiB")`. That fails every pending request and emits Notice::Disconnected, and app.rs:1267-1275 then drops the client. The same connection subscribes to notes.changed (app.rs:1154). refresh_notes runs on notes events (app.rs:1210) and on every refresh or reconnect (app.rs:1440), and it calls notes.list for the whole project (notes_window.rs:208).

**Impact.** Trigger: paste a ~2 MB log into a note and save, or let agents keep appending to the standing note until the project's live notes exceed about 2 MiB. The save is committed but reported as "Not saved: Invalid engine response: frame exceeds 2 MiB", and the whole UI goes to "Engine disconnected". Every Reconnect immediately re-fetches notes.list, or receives the next notes.changed, and drops again. The desktop client stays unusable until the note is shrunk from the CLI.

**Fix.** Enforce a body cap in the engine: notes.create, update and append should reject anything over a limit (e.g. 512 KiB) with a typed error, and Doc::save should check the same limit before sending. Make notes.list return previews and fetch bodies with notes.get. Emit notes.changed without the body. At minimum, skip an oversized event line instead of tearing down the whole connection.

**Verifier note.** I rate this medium, not high. Reaching 2 MiB takes a very large paste or long-term accumulation, so it is not a normal-flow failure. Once reached, though, it persists. One mechanism detail: the reconnect loop only re-fetches notes.list when the notes window is open (refresh_notes returns early otherwise, notes_window.rs:168-171). With the window closed, the UI drops on the next notes.changed for the oversized note, for example an agent appending to the standing note. The fix direction is right: an engine-side body cap (create, update and append), list previews, and an event without the body.

#### RA-228 · Save as new note drops anything typed while notes.create is in flight and puts the cursor back at the top

`apps/relay-native/src/note_pages/doc.rs:1215` · **medium** · Data loss · confirmed · effort S

**Problem.** Found while tracing callers of note_pages::open_doc; this file is outside the assigned chunk. save_as snapshots the text when the request starts (`let snapshot = (doc.draft.snapshot)();`, 1202) and does not lock the editor. On success it calls `discard_close(&ui, &doc);` (1215). That copies the *current* text into base so the Draft will let the tab close (1260-1273). It then runs `super::open_doc(&ui, note, position).view.grab_focus()` (1216), which builds the replacement tab from the server's copy of the old snapshot. doc::build places the cursor at the start (147).

**Impact.** Trigger: press Ctrl+Shift+S, or click 'Save as new note' in the conflict or deleted notice, and keep typing. Every keystroke typed during the round trip is discarded without a prompt. The round trip is longer when the engine is busy. Typing that continues afterwards lands at the very top of the new note.

**Fix.** On success, compare the current snapshot with the one that was sent. If they differ, load the current text into the new doc and keep its base as the server copy, so it shows as modified. Carry the cursor offset over. Alternatively, make the view read-only while save_as is in flight.

**Verifier note.** The window is normally a local Unix-socket round trip of milliseconds. It widens when the engine's store mutex is held by other work, so a typical loss is a few keystrokes. That fits medium (a real bug in a less common path), not higher. Fix: on Ok, compare the current snapshot with the one sent. If they differ, load the current text into the new doc over the server base so it shows as Modified, and carry the cursor offset across.

**Also at:** `apps/relay-native/src/note_pages/doc.rs:1202`, `apps/relay-native/src/note_pages/doc.rs:1260-1273`, `apps/relay-native/src/note_pages/doc.rs:147`, `apps/relay-native/src/note_pages.rs:901-937`

#### RA-229 · Notes window keeps listing a removed project: after removal every main-window refresh shows a not-found error, and that project's open notes can't be saved

`apps/relay-native/src/notes_window.rs:172` · **medium** · Bug · confirmed · effort M

**Problem.** refresh_notes only fills in a zero project, with `if window.project.get() == 0 { window.project.set(ui.project.get()); }` (172-174), then lists it with `ui.call("notes.list", json!({"project_id":project}))` (208). Nothing checks that window.project still exists. project.remove deletes the notes and the project row (crates/relay-core/src/handlers/workspace.rs:366,380). From then on notes.list fails in assert_actor_project -> get_project with project.not_found (crates/relay-core/src/handlers/notes.rs:340, workspace.rs:41). Once any render has happened, the Err arm runs `ui.show_error(&error.to_string())` (218). The main window handles removal of its own project (app.rs:1391-1410). registry_removed only moves ui.project (shell/registry.rs:678-695). Nothing touches NotesWindow.project. refresh_notes runs at the end of every Ui::refresh (app.rs:1440) and on every notes.* event (app.rs:1209-1211), whether or not Notes is visible. The window is created at startup (app.rs:366).

**Impact.** Trigger: remove the project the Notes window last showed. This is often the project you were working in, because show_notes points Notes at ui.project. After that, every Ui::refresh pops 'NotFound project.not_found: no project N' in the main window. Ui::refresh runs on project/workspace events, on session events not applied in place (app.rs:1225,1230) and after every successful ui.mutate button (app.rs:1124). This continues until the user opens Notes and picks another project, or restarts. Inside Notes, Ctrl+N fails because new_note posts notes.create to the dead project. The stale library and picker still list the removed project. An open draft of that project can't be rescued in-app: Save gives notes.not_found, then 'Save as new note' sends notes.create into the removed project and fails again. If that draft is dirty and hidden, it also blocks quitting (see the hidden-drafts finding).

**Fix.** In refresh_notes, before listing, check whether window.project is in ui.projects. If it is not, or if notes.list returns project.not_found, set window.project to ui.project and loop again; when that is 0, show an empty state. When a project disappears, resolve its docs: offer to save each dirty one as a new note in the project now shown, or to discard it. Then remove them from DOCS and note_drafts so they stop blocking quit.

**Verifier note.** Minor: when the removed project was the last one, ui.project becomes 0 and Ui::refresh `continue`s before refresh_notes (app.rs:1416-1419). In that case the spam comes only from notes.* events. The picker in Notes goes stale because it is rebuilt only on a successful render (note_pages.rs:1121-1122). Fix as proposed: in refresh_notes, if window.project is not in ui.projects (or notes.list returns project.not_found), fall back to ui.project, or to an empty state when that is 0. Then decide what happens to that project's open docs.

**Skeptic note.** Severity should be medium.

Recovery is easier than the finding says. Clicking Notes in the main window (or Notes in the page list) resets window.project through show_notes. The finding says the state lasts until the user picks a project inside Notes or restarts.

"Every Ui::refresh" is too broad in two ways:
- Refreshes with ui.project == 0 skip refresh_notes (app.rs:1416-1419), as do those that break early on a dirty editor (app.rs:1397-1399).
- Session events rarely cause a refresh, because full session.changed rows are applied in place (agent_menu.rs:99-137).

The quit-blocking point belongs to the hidden-drafts finding. While Notes is stuck on the dead project, that project's tabs stay visible, and the deleted notice offers Close (doc.rs:1185-1194).

Fix requirements:
1. Trigger the fallback on the project.not_found code from notes.list, or on the ids from registry_removed / project.deleted. Do not rely only on ui.projects membership, which can be stale when refresh_notes runs from note actions or events.
2. Fall back only to a project that is in ui.projects and differs from the dead id; otherwise show an empty state. Otherwise the retry loops forever whenever ui.project is still the dead id: with a dirty editor, open_project refuses to switch (shell.rs:15-17) and Ui::refresh breaks early (app.rs:1397-1399).
3. For the empty state, also clear shell.project, rendered_project and the library rows, so new_note stops targeting the dead id.
4. Resolving the dead project's docs is required. A successful fallback render hides every doc with doc.project != project (note_pages.rs:1125-1126). A hidden dirty draft then blocks quit (app.rs:1037-1044) with no way back to it, so a naive fix makes things worse. Saving into the shown project needs save_as to take a target project, because Doc.project is a plain i64 (doc.rs:18) and save_as posts doc.project (doc.rs:1207).
5. Optionally, prune the dead project's entry from the persisted SESSION tabs map.

A separate issue, not this root cause: the removal dialog never says that notes, tasks and modules are deleted. It says only "Repository files are never touched." (registry.rs:566-572).

**Also at:** `apps/relay-native/src/notes_window.rs:208`, `apps/relay-native/src/notes_window.rs:213-219`, `apps/relay-native/src/app.rs:1391-1410`, `apps/relay-native/src/app.rs:1440`, `apps/relay-native/src/app.rs:1209-1211`, `apps/relay-native/src/shell/registry.rs:678-695`, `apps/relay-native/src/note_pages.rs:955-970`, `apps/relay-native/src/note_pages/doc.rs:1171-1174`, `crates/relay-core/src/handlers/notes.rs:340`, `crates/relay-core/src/handlers/workspace.rs:41`

#### RA-230 · A failed first settings.get still marks Notes as loaded, so the first render overwrites saved Notes prefs, library rail and per-project tabs with defaults

`apps/relay-native/src/notes_window.rs:201` · **medium** · Error handling · confirmed · effort S

**Problem.** The code is `if !window.restored.replace(true) { if let Ok(value) = ui.call("settings.get", ...).await { ... restore_state(...) } window.loaded.set(true); if window.persist_wanted.replace(false) { window.persist(&ui); } }` (188-205). An Err is ignored, but `loaded` is still set. `restored` is already true, so the read is never retried. This breaks the contract stated in the field's own comment: `/// Settings were read; until then a persist would overwrite them with defaults.` (15). The first workspace() then calls `shell.split.set_position(owner.rail_width.get())` (note_pages.rs:1114). GtkPaned always notifies `position` there, and the handler calls `owner.persist(&ui)` (note_pages.rs:565-573). 300 ms later settings.set writes rail_width 270, rail_collapsed false, the default prefs, and a session map holding only this run's tabs. settings::set first deletes the whole native.notes.window subtree (crates/relay-core/src/handlers/settings.rs:205).

**Impact.** Trigger: the engine restarts or disconnects, or a request hits the 30 s timeout, during the client's first Notes refresh. The next successful library render then silently replaces everything the user saved: autosave, wrap, zoom, sort, toolbar and font prefs, the library width and collapsed state, and every project's remembered open and active tabs. No user action is needed.

**Fix.** Set `restored` and `loaded` only after a successful read. On failure leave `restored` false so the next refresh_notes retries, and keep deferring persist through persist_wanted until a read has succeeded.

**Verifier note.** The trigger is narrow. At startup ui.project is 0, so the first real read happens from Ui::refresh after connect. It fails only if the engine drops, or a request times out, during that first notes refresh. A later reconnect does not re-read, but in-memory state is intact by then, so that case is harmless. The fix is as proposed: set restored and loaded only after a successful read.

**Also at:** `apps/relay-native/src/notes_window.rs:15`, `apps/relay-native/src/notes_window.rs:188-205`, `apps/relay-native/src/note_pages.rs:565-573`, `apps/relay-native/src/note_pages.rs:1113-1114`, `crates/relay-core/src/handlers/settings.rs:203-212`

#### RA-231 · Every main-window refresh and every notes event re-lists all notes and rebuilds the whole library, even while Notes is hidden

`apps/relay-native/src/notes_window.rs:208` · **medium** · Performance · confirmed · effort M

**Problem.** refresh_notes has no visibility check. Whenever the window exists, which is always since startup, it fetches `notes.list` with every note body (208) and calls workspace(). It runs from Ui::refresh (app.rs:1440, which itself runs after every successful ui.mutate at app.rs:1124 and on project, workspace and session events). It also runs on every notes.changed / notes.deleted event (app.rs:1209-1211), although that event already carries the full note. workspace() clones the list again with `notes.to_vec()` (1123). It rebuilds the project picker with `clear(&shell.picker); shell.picker.append(&super::workspace_picker(...))` (1121-1122) and reconciles every doc. render_rows then removes and recreates every row (771-785), rebuilding `haystack: format!("{title}\n{body}").to_lowercase()` (763), the preview and the date, and calling doc.dirty() for each open doc (738). The header func scans all rows for every row: `rows.iter().any(|r| r.note["pinned"] == true)` (594). When nothing is pinned this is O(n^2) per render and per search keystroke.

**Impact.** Each refresh does work proportional to all note text, holding about five copies of it, on the GTK thread. This happens for every agent notes.append, every main-window action and every project or session event, even for a window the user may not have open. While Notes is open, the user also sees it: an open project-picker popover closes under the pointer, keyboard focus on a library row is destroyed, and the selection jumps back to the active doc.

**Fix.** While the window is hidden, skip refresh_notes and only mark the library stale, then refresh when the window is presented. Apply notes.changed and notes.deleted payloads in place by updating or removing the one row with that id, instead of re-listing. Rebuild the picker only when ui.projects changes. Compute the any-pinned flag once per render and store it on Shell.

**Verifier note.** The cost scales with the note count per project, which is usually tens to low hundreds. The cost is real but moderate, not a freeze. The O(n^2) header scan is a secondary point. The main cost is rebuilding every row and the picker on each refresh. The best fix is to skip refresh while the window is hidden (mark stale and refresh on present) and to rebuild the picker only when projects change.

#### RA-232 · After a failed first submit, onboarding keeps the workspace it just created and silently ignores later edits to the workspace directory and name

`apps/relay-native/src/onboarding.rs:517` · **medium** · Bug · confirmed · effort S

**Problem.** `if setup.workspace.borrow()["id"].is_null() { let path = setup.workspace_path.text().trim().to_owned(); ... setup.ui.call("workspace.create", ...).await? ... *setup.workspace.borrow_mut() = workspace; }` (517-523) runs before `project.add`/`project.clone` (527). When the project step fails, `setup.workspace` keeps the new id, so every retry skips this block. `discover` also switches to `self.workspace.borrow()["path"]` (327-330). The fields stay editable (`setup.body.set_sensitive(true)`, 536) and the button is relabelled "Add project" (update_action, 369).

An empty, stray workspace stays in the sidebar (the workspace.changed event refreshes the registry) even after the dialog is closed.

Alternatively, on retry compare the entry with the created workspace's path and create or look up a new one if it changed. That is a plausible multi-agent flow, so medium stands. A dirty buffer should keep its text, with a notice.

#### RA-234 · LAST REPORT is chosen by created_at, but the engine's dedup rewrites a notification's body without updating created_at, so the card can show the wrong report and a stale time

`apps/relay-native/src/session_context.rs:65` · **medium** · Bug · confirmed · effort S

**Problem.** `notifications.iter().find(|n| matches!(text(n, "category"), "agent_done" | "agent_blocked") && text(n, "title").starts_with(&prefix) && ...)` runs over notify.list, which is ordered `created_at DESC` (notify.rs:71). The card then shows `relative_time(text(report, "created_at"))` (177). The engine's dedup (session.rs:261-271) looks for an unread notification with the same project, category, title and link. If it finds one, it runs `UPDATE notifications SET body=?1 WHERE id=?2` and leaves created_at untouched.

**Impact.** Example: a session finishes at T1 (A, "X finished"), blocks at T3 (B, "X is blocked"), then finishes again at T5 while A is still unread. A's body becomes the T5 summary but keeps T1. The slate shows "LAST REPORT Blocked: … · <T3>" although the last report was the T5 completion. Whenever a body is rewritten, the time shown is the first report's ("3 h ago" for a summary written a minute ago). The bell popover shows the same stale time and leaves the row buried (notification_center.rs:224).

**Fix.** When record_agent_notification updates an existing row, also bump created_at, or add an updated_at column and order notify.list by it. In last_report, pick the row with the newest such timestamp instead of the first match.

**Verifier note.** Small correction: the blocked title is '<name> needs attention' (session.rs:1406), not 'is blocked'. Line 1209's 'is blocked' is the headline for session.report. The mechanism is the same. The fix stands: bump created_at, or add an updated_at column to order by, when the dedup rewrites the body. Adding a column requires a migration and a SCHEMA_VERSION bump.

#### RA-235 · Describing a stopped pane runs `git status --untracked-files=all` on every restorable worktree in every project, serialised on the UI's only connection

`apps/relay-native/src/session_context.rs:99` · **medium** · Performance · confirmed · effort M

**Problem.** `if sessions.iter().any(|s| text(s, "state") == "restorable") { if let Ok(data) = self.call("session.restorable", json!({})).await {`. The op takes no filter (`Empty => RestorableOut`, relay-bus ops/session.rs:166). Its handler (session.rs:1484-1503) opens every restorable session's worktree and runs `worktree::is_dirty`. That is `git status --porcelain=v1 -z --untracked-files=all` with a 10 s timeout, once per worktree, one after another (worktree.rs:78-97). The engine answers each connection's requests strictly in order: socket.rs:335-743 awaits every dispatch before reading the next line. ui.call uses the single control connection (app.rs:1111-1117). describe runs for every stopped pane that reconcile creates: at startup, on reconnect (connect() clears all panes), and on every project switch (shell.rs:10-37 → reconcile → app.rs:1494-1499 → shell.rs:743).

**Impact.** After an app restart most sessions are restorable. On every project switch or reconnect this call goes out first, and the project's own session.list, notes and board requests queue behind N git status walks. That takes seconds on large repos (e.g. UE projects). If it passes the 30 s client timeout (client.rs:65-71), this call and the requests queued behind it fail with "Request timed out". The card then falls back to "Relay was closed" with no uncommitted-changes flag, even after a crash.

**Fix.** Add a session or project_id filter to session.restorable so it covers only the panes being described. Alternatively, return `reason` without the dirty walk and fetch worktree_dirty lazily per pane, or cache it per worktree. Another option is to issue the call on a separate connection, as lifecycle requests already do. Do not show "Relay was closed" when the lookup failed.

**Verifier note.** Impact depends on worktree count and size. With a few small repos the scan takes milliseconds, so how often it really hurts is not established. On large UE checkouts with untracked-files=all it can take seconds per worktree. The visible wall itself switches synchronously from sidebar_sessions (shell.rs:27-31); only refreshed data lags behind. The fix stands: filter session.restorable by project or session, or split the dirty check out and run it lazily per pane, or cache it per worktree.

#### RA-236 · A refresh in flight across a project switch saves the old layout over the new project's saved layout, which is then never restored

`apps/relay-native/src/shell.rs:327` · **medium** · Bug · confirmed · effort S

**Problem.** refresh captures layout_revision at the top of each iteration (app.rs:1371). It calls restore_layout(revision) only after awaiting project.list/workspace.list and session.list (app.rs:1373-1439). restore_layout reads self.project only when it starts (322). Suppose the user switches to P2 during those awaits. open_project has set restored_project=0 (33), and its navigate has bumped the revision. The stale iteration then calls restored_project.set(P2) (326), sees `layout_revision != revision`, and calls save_layout() (327-329). save_layout now passes its restored_project == P2 check and persists the current state as native.layout.current.P2. The next iteration returns early at 323 because restored_project == P2. The same happens when settings.get fails (341): restored_project is already set, so the next save overwrites a layout that was never applied.

**Impact.** Clicking project A then project B quickly permanently replaces B's remembered mode, columns, focused agent, split and page with A's (or the startup defaults). Clicking a project during the startup refresh does the same, and it is more likely when the store mutex is busy with many agents. B's real saved layout is never read.

**Fix.** Pass the iteration's project into restore_layout, and return without touching restored_project when it differs from self.project. On a failed read, reset restored_project so the next refresh retries. If the user edited the layout during the read, merge that edit into the stored layout instead of overwriting all of it.

**Verifier note.** Primary site: the stale-iteration path is shell.rs:322-329 together with app.rs:1439, which calls restore_layout without checking that the iteration's project is still current. Fix: capture the project with the revision at the top of the iteration and pass both in. If self.project differs, return without touching restored_project. Reset restored_project to 0 when settings.get fails. A layout edit made before the restore should apply on top of the stored layout rather than replace it.

**Also at:** `apps/relay-native/src/app.rs:1371`, `apps/relay-native/src/app.rs:1439`, `apps/relay-native/src/shell.rs:33`, `apps/relay-native/src/shell.rs:341`

#### RA-237 · Window-level capture-phase shortcuts steal Ctrl+K, Ctrl+N and Ctrl+1/2/3 from agent terminals, and Ctrl+N wipes an open launch form

`apps/relay-native/src/shell.rs:1067` · **medium** · Bug · confirmed · effort S

**Problem.** `keys.set_propagation_phase(gtk::PropagationPhase::Capture);` is installed on the window (1066-1067, 1101). Whenever no panel is open it matches the bindings and returns `glib::Propagation::Stop` (1076-1093): `"palette" => ui.command_palette()` for Ctrl+K, `"new_session" => ui.show_launch(None)` for Ctrl+N, and navigate for Ctrl+1/2/3 and Ctrl+, (defaults in shortcuts.rs:3-11). The capture phase runs before the focused VteTerminal handles keys, so the terminal never receives these chords. `show_launch` always runs `clear(&self.launch_box)` and rebuilds (launch.rs:368), even when the sheet is already open.

**Impact.** In an agent pane, Ctrl+K (kill to end of line in readline-style prompt editors) opens the command palette, and Ctrl+N (next history) opens the launch sheet; neither key reaches the CLI. Pressing Ctrl+N while configuring agents, including while typing in the Additional instructions box, discards every prompt, model, provider and task selection in the form.

**Fix.** Skip global shortcuts when the focus widget is a VteTerminal or an editable, or run them in the bubble phase so the terminal and text fields consume their keys first. Make `show_launch` only focus the sheet when `self.launch.reveals_child()` is already true.

**Verifier note.** Fix: skip the global match when the focus widget is a vte4::Terminal, or an editable or text view without a modifier other than Ctrl. Alternatively use the bubble phase so focused widgets consume the key first. In show_launch, return early and only focus the sheet when launch.reveals_child() is already true. Ctrl+1/2/3 and Ctrl+, are much less likely to matter in a terminal than Ctrl+K and Ctrl+N.

<a id="ra-238"></a>

#### RA-238 · Sidebar stores its rebuild key as the projects_box widget name; GTK interns each key as a permanent GQuark, and any agent state change rebuilds the whole tree

`apps/relay-native/src/shell/registry.rs:136` · **medium** · Resource leak · confirmed · effort M

**Problem.** 127-137: `let signature = format!("{active}:{}:{}:{:?}:{collapsed:?}:{expanded:?}:{query}", serde_json::to_string(&projects).., serde_json::to_string(&workspaces).., sessions.iter().map(|s| (s["project_id"].as_i64(), text(s, "state")..)).collect::<Vec<_>>()); if self.projects_box.widget_name() == signature { return; } self.projects_box.set_widget_name(&signature); clear(&self.projects_box);`. gtk_widget_set_name interns the name as a GQuark (the CSS node id), and quarks are never freed. I verified this with a scratch PyGObject experiment against the installed GTK 4.22.5: after set_name, GLib.quark_try_string(name) is non-zero, and it stays non-zero after renaming and dropping the widget. The key embeds every project row (including updated_at, protected_paths and critical_files) and the state of every session in every project. render_projects runs on every session.changed (agent_menu.rs:131), which the engine emits on each running/idle/blocked transition (session.rs:1424-1426).

**Impact.** Each distinct sidebar state leaks a full copy of the serialized registry (several KB) into the process-wide quark table for the life of the app. Growth slows down only while projects and session lists stay unchanged. Each state change also rebuilds every row: an open ⋯ menu disappears under the cursor, keyboard focus in the sidebar is dropped, hover tools flicker, and every row's popover is rebuilt (and leaked, per the registry_menu finding). The full registry is also re-serialized on the GTK thread for every session event.

**Fix.** Keep the cache key in the `Sidebar` thread-local (or as a u64 hash) instead of the widget name. Derive it from what is actually rendered: ids, names, pinned, order, and per-project open/held/running. Then a running/idle change that does not change a lamp does nothing. Update lamps on existing rows instead of rebuilding them.

**Verifier note.** The memory growth is slower than implied. A new quark is created only for a never-before-seen signature, and repeated running/idle flips of the same session set reuse existing quarks. New strings come from session create/close, active-project changes, fold changes and each keystroke in the sidebar filter (the query is in the key). Project updated_at changes only on project.update (workspace.rs:276). The leak itself is low severity. The more user-visible cost is the full rebuild on every state flip, which dismisses open menus and drops focus; that is what justifies medium. Fix: keep a u64 hash in the Sidebar thread-local instead of the widget name, and update the per-project lamps in place instead of rebuilding the tree.

Usage.get reads the files live (usage.rs), so the cheapest fix is a throttled refresh_usage(false) when a session.changed moves a session to idle. Otherwise default to a non-zero interval and correct both strings.

#### RA-240 · Task/module Save treats a change to any editable field as a conflict, so edits fail while an agent works on the task

`apps/relay-native/src/task_pages.rs:214` · **medium** · Bug · confirmed · effort S

**Problem.** The save handler takes every snapshot key, not just the edited ones: `let keys: Vec<String> = next.as_object().unwrap().keys().cloned().collect();` (214), then `if draft_conflicts(&base, &latest, &keys)` (215), which shows "This item changed elsewhere…" (216). `expected` is built from base for all keys (218) and the payload is the whole snapshot (219). For tasks that is 8 fields: title, body, changelog, priority, state, type, size, module_id (596). The engine changes some of them on its own. The session hook flips a builder's active task between running and blocked (crates/relay-core/src/handlers/session.rs:1390-1399). Completion sets awaiting_review (session.rs:104). Agents may rewrite body/changelog (task.rs:868 allowlist; task.changelog.write task.rs:965). The engine's own atomic check rejects any supplied `expected` field that differs (task.rs:871-880). The comment at 986 says "Auxiliary changes never invalidate an unsaved editor", and the unit test (1201-1212) only passes the edited fields, but the real caller passes all of them. The pre-flight `task.get` + `draft_conflicts` repeats the engine's atomic check, adding one extra round trip. Its `deleted_at` arm can never fire, because task.get and module.get never return deleted rows (get_task(..., false)).

**Impact.** A user opens a task an agent is working on, fixes only the description, and clicks Save. Meanwhile the agent's hook flipped state running→blocked, or the agent wrote its changelog. Save is refused with "This item changed elsewhere… Copy it before discarding and reopening the latest version." The user changed none of those fields. For a running task this happens almost every time. The only way out is to copy the text, discard, reopen, paste and save before the next state flip. A Save with no changes still sends get + update, which writes an audit row, bumps updated_at and refreshes the board. The module editor (note_pages.rs:1363-1364) has the same problem.

**Fix.** Take an `initial = snapshot()` when the form is built. On Save, compute the changed keys (`next[k] != initial[k]`). If none changed, say so and stop. Send only the changed fields, and put only those fields' base values in `expected`. Then remove the pre-flight `get` and `draft_conflicts`, and map the engine's `task.edit_conflict` / `module.edit_conflict` codes to the friendly message. The engine check is atomic; the client one is not.

**Verifier note.** "Almost every time" is overstated. A conflict needs the state at Save to differ from the state at open, so a running->blocked->running round trip does not trip it. It still fires in the normal flow of editing a task an agent is working on. The module editor's snapshot is only name/priority/icon, which the engine does not change on its own, so it is affected only by a concurrent human edit of another field and is minor. The fix is as proposed: send only the changed keys and their base values as `expected`, drop the redundant pre-flight get and draft_conflicts, and map task.edit_conflict/module.edit_conflict to the friendly message.

**Skeptic note.** 1. "Almost every time" is overstated. The Save fails only when a field's value at Save differs from its value at open. Add the other engine writers of `tasks.state`: session.rs:662 (failed on PTY exit), session.rs:1177 (blocked on a short `session.done`) and task.rs:667 (dispatched). The running/blocked oscillation comes mainly from Claude builders, through idle_prompt and permission_prompt.
2. The module editor is low impact. Its snapshot is name/priority/icon, which only a concurrent edit from another client can change.
3. Fix refinements:
   - Diff against an `initial = snapshot()` taken when the form is built, not against `base`, and set `initial = next` after each successful save. Otherwise later saves send fields saved earlier again.
   - Diffing against the initial snapshot also matters for a second reason. `module.list` without `include_archived` excludes completed modules (module.rs:145). A task in a completed module therefore opens with no active row in the module combo, so the snapshot has `module_id: null` while base holds the id. The current code then sends `module_id: null` with a matching `expected` on every Save, which silently unlinks the task from its module. This is a separate bug worth its own finding (inferred from GTK `set_active_id` semantics, not run). A fix that diffed against `base` would keep that bug.
   - Remove or rewrite the `draft_conflicts` test.
   - The change is in apps/relay-native, which cannot be compiled in an agent session, so the summary and PR must say so.

**Blind re-check note.** "For a running task this happens almost every time" is overstated. A conflict needs a running/blocked flip (a permission prompt or resume), a completion, or an agent body/changelog write between opening the editor and pressing Save. Tasks outside the active column are never affected. The current pre-check also prevents the full-snapshot payload from silently putting back stale engine-set fields, so the defect is the all-fields payload/expected, not the conflict check itself. The module editor shares the design, but in practice nothing changes module fields on its own, so its impact is negligible.

#### RA-241 · Every task detail, module editor and New-task panel leaks its Panel and widgets through closures that hold their owner strongly

`apps/relay-native/src/task_pages.rs:230` · **medium** · Resource leak · confirmed · effort S

**Problem.** Draft::controls connects `save.connect_clicked(move |_| { … d … })` with `let d = self.clone()` (a strong Rc<Draft>, 205-207). It then moves `save` itself, strongly, into `key.connect_key_pressed(move |...| { … save.emit_clicked(); … })` (228-235). That controller is added to `self.layout` (236). This forms a cycle: Draft.layout → EventControllerKey → closure → save → clicked closure → Rc<Draft>. cleanup() (145-151) clears form and footer, and Panel::close clears the body (panel.rs:278). Nothing removes the controller, so the Draft is never dropped. compose() has the same mistake. `create.connect_clicked` captures `form` and `p` (an Rc<Panel>) (488-507), while `create` sits in `footer` inside `form` (457-459). `cancel` also captures `p` (479-487). After Panel::close clears the body, form ↔ create-closure keeps the form and the Panel alive. GTK4 frees an unparented widget only when its last reference goes, and these cycles never release it.

**Impact.** Each opened task detail leaks. So does each action, because action() closes the detail and reopens a fresh one. Each module editor and each New task panel leaks too. What leaks: the Draft and its Panel (layer, frame, scroll), the base JSON, and the snapshot closure with its widgets, including combos with their models and two TextViews holding the full description text. Panel.focus also keeps the previously focused board card alive. Growth has no bound over a long-running session; roughly tens of KB per open.

**Fix.** In the key controller capture `save.downgrade()` and upgrade it before `emit_clicked`. In compose capture `form.downgrade()` and `Rc::downgrade(&panel)`, or use `glib::clone!(@weak …)`.

**Verifier note.** Note drafts (new_note, doc.rs:301) do not call controls() and do not leak this way. The fix as proposed is right: capture save.downgrade() in the key closure (or have the controller hold a Weak<Draft>), and in compose capture form.downgrade() and Rc::downgrade(&panel). I cannot compile apps/relay-native here; this was established by reading the code.

#### RA-242 · Catch-up replays only the last 256 KiB with no terminal state, so recreated panes lose bracketed paste, alternate screen and mouse modes

`apps/relay-native/src/terminal.rs:31` · **medium** · Bug · confirmed · effort L

**Problem.** A fresh Pane starts with `Sequence::default()` (211) and attaches with null epoch and from_seq (483-484). The engine answers with `ring.bounded_bytes_from(0)`: the last ATTACH_CATCHUP_BYTES (256 KiB), aligned to a 64 KiB read boundary (pty.rs:19, 96-101, 314). The client feeds it as-is: `Some((_, s)) if catch_up || seq == s + 1 => Step::Feed` (31), then `self.terminal.feed(&data)` (515). Only a new epoch resets the terminal (512). Panes are recreated on every project switch (`open_project` clears `ordered` and reconciles, shell.rs:24-31; reconcile stops panes that left the wall, app.rs:1473-1480), on reconnect, and on GUI restart. A same-pane re-attach splices the same way after more than 256 KiB was produced while it was hidden. D97 caps catch-up for speed (DECISIONS.md:430), and docs/perf/BASELINE-2026-09-19.md:494 notes the gap. A TUI emits its mode switches once at start-up, so they fall outside that tail for any agent that has run a while. The spike recorded Claude Code using the alternate screen and bracketed paste (docs/upstream-v3/spike/P3-terminal.md:152, 190).

**Impact.** The user switches to another project and back, or restarts the GUI, after an agent has produced more than 256 KiB (minutes of TUI redraws, per D97). The new VTE never saw the mode-set sequences. A multi-line paste is then sent without bracketed-paste markers, and VTE turns each newline into Enter, so a CLI that relies on bracketed paste can submit a partial prompt after the first line. The mouse wheel scrolls VTE's own buffer instead of the app, and redraws land on the normal screen. A splice can also start mid escape sequence and print garbage.

**Fix.** Have the engine track the PTY's terminal modes by scanning output for DECSET/DECRST 1, 25, 47/1047/1049, 1000-1006 and 2004. Prefix every catch-up with a prelude that restores them, plus a clear-screen when the catch-up was truncated. Longer term, keep a headless emulator per PTY (for example the vt100 crate) and send a screen snapshot instead of a byte tail.

**Verifier note.** A same-pane re-attach (D97 hidden pane) keeps its VTE and so keeps its modes. There the only problem is the splice: the gap is skipped and the tail may start mid-sequence. Mode loss applies only to recreated panes, after a project switch, a GUI restart, or a reconnect that rebuilds panes. The 256 KiB alignment is to a frame boundary (a PTY read chunk), not to a 64 KiB read boundary. The suggested fix is right: track DECSET/DECRST state per PTY in the engine and prepend a restore prelude, plus a clear, to a truncated catch-up, or keep a headless emulator and send a screen snapshot. Full ring replay would not be enough, because the ring itself is capped at 8 MiB.

**Also at:** `crates/relay-core/src/pty.rs:96`, `crates/relay-core/src/pty.rs:314`, `apps/relay-native/src/terminal.rs:512`, `apps/relay-native/src/shell.rs:30`, `docs/engine/DECISIONS.md:430`

#### RA-243 · Keystrokes are sent one round trip at a time over the pane's output socket, and are dropped when the client is absent or 64 are queued

`apps/relay-native/src/terminal.rs:223` · **medium** · Bug · confirmed · effort M

**Problem.** The commit handler drops input instead of queuing it: `if p.client.borrow().is_none() { p.status.set_text("Input unavailable: reconnect"); } else if tx.try_send(text.into()).is_err() { p.status.set_text("Input queue full: keystroke not sent"); }` (221-225); the channel is bounded to 64 (217). The sender awaits each `client.request(&p.rt, "session.input", ...)` before taking the next item (229-247). It uses the same connection that carries the PTY frames. The reply waits behind frames in the engine's shared `out_tx` (socket.rs:295, 744) and in the client's 64-slot notice channel (client.rs:179, 242), and the engine reads the next request only after it has queued the previous reply. Items already queued are dropped silently if `p.client` became None in the meantime (234-246, no else branch). The client is None from activation until attach answers (476-487) and during every gap re-attach.

**Impact.** Under heavy output (a build log, a large catch-up), or after a large paste that the agent drains slowly, each keystroke's round trip waits behind the frame backlog. Continued typing fills the 64 slots and further keys are discarded with only a status note. Typing right after restoring the window or returning to the Agents page loses the first keystrokes while the pane re-attaches, which can take up to 30 s when the store lock is busy.

**Fix.** Send input on a connection that carries no frames, either the control client or a per-pane input client. Pipeline requests without awaiting each reply: order is kept by the single writer and the engine's sequential loop. Buffer keystrokes typed while (re)attaching instead of dropping them.

**Verifier note.** The "64 queued keystrokes fill up" scenario is speculative. The first keystroke (e.g. Ctrl+C) is written at once; only the replies, and therefore later keystrokes, queue behind the frame backlog. VTE feeding is fast, so filling 64 slots needs a long backlog. The real loss path is the client==None window (both the commit-time drop and the silent drop at 234). Fix: buffer input while (re)attaching and flush after attach. Pipeline requests instead of awaiting each reply, or send input on a frame-free connection.

#### RA-244 · A terminal pane whose stream hits any error stays dead: the loop breaks but `active` stays true, so update_attachments never re-attaches it

`apps/relay-native/src/terminal.rs:466` · **medium** · Error handling · confirmed · effort S

**Problem.** `set_active` returns early when nothing changed: `if self.active.replace(active) == active { return; }` (443). The stream loop: `Ok(()) => { p.status.set_text("Recovering output"); } Err(e) => { p.status.set_text(&e.to_string()); break; }` (462-469). After the break nothing resets `active` or the finished `stream` handle. `update_attachments` (app.rs:1567-1583) is the only caller of set_active, so later calls with `true` are no-ops. `session.attach` is a locked handler (`e.register::<Attach>`, session.rs:1640), queued behind the store mutex, with the default 30 s client timeout (client.rs request_timeout).

**Impact.** Any transient attach or stream error leaves the pane frozen on stale output. Triggers include a 30 s attach timeout while the store lock is held by a long op (project.clone, a large workspace.discover), a handler panic that closes the pane's socket, and `session.not_spawned` during a state race. The pane shows text such as "Request timed out. Its outcome is unknown; refresh before retrying.", with no retry and nothing to refresh. It recovers only if the user leaves the Agents page, minimizes and restores, or switches project and back.

**Fix.** On Err, retry with backoff while `active` is still true, and stop only on final errors (for example not_spawned when the row is no longer live). Alternatively, set `active` to false and clear `stream` when the loop exits so the next reconcile re-attaches. Give the status strip a Retry action.

**Verifier note.** The not_spawned race is narrow: the spawn path writes state='running' and set_pty in the same handler (session.rs:678-686). The likelier triggers are the attach timeout under a long locked operation and an engine/socket disconnect. Simplest fix: at loop exit, set `active` to false and drop `stream` so the next reconcile re-attaches. Better: retry with backoff while active, and stop only on terminal errors.

`apps/relay-native/src/tools.rs:81` · **medium** · Performance · confirmed · effort M

Impact is bounded by the coalescing: at most one dashboard.get in flight, so the cost is one rebuild per round trip during a burst, not one per event. That is still medium for a UI that resets hover, focus and scroll and can drop clicks. Fix as proposed: a trailing throttle of about 1 s on dashboard refreshes. A further option is to stop routing events from other projects that the dashboard does not display.

#### RA-248 · The Skills and Plugins pages reload the whole catalog and rebuild every row on every unrelated engine event, even when nothing changed

`apps/relay-native/src/tools_market.rs:108` · **medium** · Performance · confirmed · effort S

**Problem.** app.rs:1263-1265 sends every event not handled earlier to `ui.refresh_page()`. That covers task.changed, mailbox.*, notify.*, guardrail.*, overlap.*, module.*, device.*, run.*. For these pages refresh_page runs market::refresh, which always does `*market.data.borrow_mut() = rows(&value, spec.list_key);` and then `market.render(ui);` (:102-108), with no check for unchanged data. render clones the whole catalog (`let data = self.data.borrow().clone();` :535) and clones the filtered set again (:553-561). It then calls `self.list.remove_all()` (:566) and recreates every row, card, Switch and FlowBox (:569-599). On the engine side, skill.list is a locked handler (provider.rs:86 `e.register::<SkillList>`) that runs 1+N queries and copies every body under the store mutex. plugin.list (provider.rs:269) does a read_dir of every project root for each plugin.

**Impact.** While agents work, an open Skills or Plugins page loops refresh→render almost continuously. refresh_page coalesces requests but re-runs while dirty, and this also happens while the window is minimised. Each pass re-sends and re-parses the full catalog including bodies, takes the store mutex that every agent request needs, and destroys and recreates all rows. What the user sees:
- keyboard focus on a list row is lost because the focused row is destroyed;
- the idle that restores the scroll position fights a user who is scrolling;
- a press on a card switch can be dropped;
- hover state flickers.
With a large library, each event also risks the 2 MiB disconnect above.

**Fix.** In refresh(), compare the new rows with `*market.data.borrow()`. If they are equal, skip render() (still hide errors and set loaded). In app.rs, send only skill.*, plugin.* and project.* events to these two pages. Later, patch rows in place instead of calling remove_all().

**Verifier note.** plugin.list is registered with register_unlocked (provider.rs:269). Its project-root detection runs without the store mutex; only the enable edges are read under ctx.read. skill.list is locked, but its 1+N prepared queries are cheap at realistic sizes, so the engine-side mutex cost is minor. The real cost is client-side churn and UI disruption, plus re-sending bodies (see #1). The proposed fixes are sound: route only skill.*, plugin.* and project.* events to these pages, and skip render() when the rows are unchanged.

#### RA-249 · The detail pane is cached on (item, scope) only, so it misses project renames and additions and palette changes, and project events never repaint the page

`apps/relay-native/src/tools_market.rs:634` · **medium** · Bug · confirmed · effort S

**Problem.** `let next = item.map(|v| (v.clone(), scope)); if *self.shown.borrow() == next { return; }` (:633-636). The detail that spec.detail builds also reads other state:
- ui.projects and ui.workspaces: enable_block uses project_name and reach (:766, :777), project_switches reads `ui.projects.borrow().clone()` (:803-804), and switch tooltips embed project names (:705-706);
- ui.palette: markdown() resolves `relay-{palette}` once (:1030).
project.changed and project.deleted events (add, rename via project.update, reorder, remove) only run `ui.registry_dirty.set(true); ui.refresh();` (app.rs:1223-1225). refresh() repaints only board and dashboard (app.rs:1441-1443). This contradicts the module doc, which says 'every engine event repaints it through tools::refresh' (:5-9).

**Impact.** Rename project Foo to Bar while a skill or plugin is selected. On the next repaint the picker and hint say Bar, but the detail still says 'On in Foo' and lists Foo in the Projects tab. Add a project that a plugin does not detect: the plugin's item JSON doesn't change, so its Projects tab never gets a switch for the new project and 'On in X of N projects' stays wrong. Because `shown` lives in the mounted Market, this survives navigating away and back, until a different item is selected. A palette change leaves the SKILL.md and doc views in the old style scheme. A switch for a removed project stays visible, and turning it fails.

**Fix.** Invalidate `shown` whenever the inputs change: set it to None in sync_picker when picker_ids changes, on workspace changes, and on appearance changes. Alternatively, put a projects/workspaces revision and the palette into the cache key. Have app.rs repaint the skills and plugins pages on project.* and workspace.* events, and correct the module comment.

**Verifier note.** Switches still act on the right project id. A switch for a removed project fails cleanly: get_project returns NotFound and the guarded restore runs. Most of the impact is stale or wrong labels and counts, plus a missing switch for a newly added project. The palette point is minor: the documents also sit in market.cache. Simplest fix: put a projects/workspaces fingerprint (or a revision counter bumped when the registry reloads) and the palette into the cache key, or clear `shown` in sync_picker when picker_ids changes. Also repaint the plugins and skills pages on project.* and workspace.* events, and correct the module comment.

#### RA-250 · The per-project enable switch is written three times; the copy in shell.rs lost the re-entrancy guard and loops forever when an enable fails

`apps/relay-native/src/tools_market.rs:718` · **medium** · Bug · confirmed · effort M

**Problem.** market::toggle (:690-742) guards with `if !switch.is_sensitive() { return glib::Propagation::Proceed; }`. The guard is needed because the error path calls `switch.set_active(!on)`, and GtkSwitch::set_active emits state-set again. tools_plugins.rs:105-161 (`plugins::switch`, used only by shell.rs project_plugins) re-implements the same switch with the same guard (:123). shell.rs:873-888 (project_skills) re-implements it inline without the guard: `Err(error) => { key.set_active(!on); ... }` (:882). The enabled_in and suggested_for checks are also copied (tools_plugins.rs:92-102, shell.rs:860-862, shell.rs:971-973).

**Impact.** In the 'Agent skills' popover, if skill.enable fails, set_active(!on) re-enters the handler and sends the opposite request. That fails too and flips the switch back, without end. Failure cases:
- engine restarted or disconnected: `ui.call` fails at once, so the main loop spins flipping the switch until reconnect, and then whichever value was last in flight is written, at random;
- skill deleted or project removed by another client: a request storm that never stops; each request takes the store mutex and writes an audit row (skill.enable is Audit::Always and NotFound failures are audited, engine.rs:1075), until the app exits.
The futures hold the switch, so closing the popover doesn't stop the loop.

**Fix.** Keep one implementation: market::toggle, or a small shared `enable_switch(ui, op, id_key, id, project, on_result)`. Call it from shell.rs project_skills and project_plugins, delete plugins::switch and the inline copy, and share the enabled/suggested predicates.

**Verifier note.** The root cause is a bug (a missing guard that causes an infinite re-entrant request loop), so the category is bug rather than duplication. The trigger needs a failure in a less common path, so medium rather than high. The immediate fix is to add the `if !key.is_sensitive() { return glib::Propagation::Proceed; }` guard in shell.rs:873. The longer-term fix is to consolidate onto one shared switch helper, as proposed.

`apps/relay-native/src/tools_settings.rs:34` · **medium** · Bug · confirmed · effort M

**Problem.** `if ui.page_projects.borrow().get("settings") == Some(&project) { return; }`. The button is `action(ui, &agents, "Refresh providers", "provider.refresh", json!({}))` (396-402). That goes through Ui::mutate (app.rs:1118-1130), which throws away the returned ListOut and calls refresh_page, which returns at line 34. The provider.version event that provider.refresh emits is not in the subscription list (app.rs:1154). 'Update now' ends in provider_updates::event, which only calls ui.refresh(). The button greys out and comes back, but the card still says 'Not installed' or shows the old version until they switch projects or restart the app. The same staleness means the form never shows values changed elsewhere, which is what lets Save revert them (see the Save finding).

More generally, invalidate page_projects["settings"] on reconnect and on settings.changed when there are no local edits.

#### RA-252 · Unsaved Settings edits, including the embedded guardrail editor, are silently thrown away when the project changes, although nothing on the page is per-project

`apps/relay-native/src/tools_settings.rs:81` · **medium** · Bug · confirmed · effort S

**Problem.** The page is rebuilt whenever page_projects["settings"] differs from the current project (34): `clear(page)` (81), then a rebuild from engine values. The content is global settings plus `crate::pages::guardrail_settings(ui)` (458), which is the guardrail editor built with `build(ui, Scope::Global).0` and no guard (guardrail_settings.rs:427-429). The panel version of that editor does install `set_guard(... editor.dirty() == 0)` (guardrail_settings.rs:661). Navigation only checks panels: app.rs:1316 calls dismiss_panels, which looks at ui.panels only.

**Impact.** The user edits shortcuts, Android paths, sliders or guardrail limits without saving, clicks another project in the sidebar (which goes to its agents page), then returns to Settings: every edit is gone with no prompt. The same happens immediately when the phone sends ui.page.switch with another project (shell.rs:443), or when the active project is removed while Settings is open (shell/registry.rs:685). Leaving Settings without switching project keeps the edits, so the behaviour is inconsistent.

**Fix.** Key the page on the connection generation rather than the project; the guardrail editor already reads ui.project when its scope toggles change. Otherwise, check a dirty flag, including the guardrail editor's dirty(), before clearing the page, and block or confirm the switch.

**Verifier note.** Category: this is lost unsaved form input, not lost persisted data, so it is a bug rather than data-loss. The edits lost to a guardrail-editor rebuild are only the ones not yet saved there, because that editor saves on its own. Keying the page on the connection generation, not the project, also fixes native-tools#4's reconnect staleness.

#### RA-254 · Save changes rewrites every setting on the page, not only the edited ones, silently reverting or clamping other values and flooding the audit log and events

`apps/relay-native/src/tools_settings.rs:652` · **medium** · Data loss · confirmed · effort M

**Problem.** collect_settings (606-692) walks the whole page and, for every widget named `setting:*`, does `settings.push(("settings.set", json!({"path":...,"value":value})))` (652-655) whether or not it changed. That is 23 requests: mode, three sliders, two rotation fields, font size, two auto-update flags, two provider paths, parking, four Android paths and seven shortcuts, plus notify.settings.set (141). Only the wallpaper fields are compared against a saved value (132-139). The values come from a snapshot taken when the page was first built for this project (34, 84-86). Scale::set_value clamps to the widget range, which commit 54e6bbc narrowed from 0.5-1 to 0.72-1 for panel_alpha and from 0-0.85 to 0-0.75 for wallpaper_dim (292-293). load_appearance still accepts 0.5-1 and 0-0.85 (shell.rs:1179, 1217).

**Impact.** (a) A panel opacity of 0.6 set with an older build stays in effect until the user saves anything else, such as a shortcut; that Save silently writes 0.72, and the same happens to wallpaper dim above 0.75. (b) Any setting changed from the CLI or phone after the page was built is reverted by the next Save. (c) Every click writes about 24 audited rows with undo entries, even with nothing changed. Each settings.set also emits settings.changed, which runs load_appearance about seven times and load_keybindings seven times. Each load_appearance makes 8 settings.get calls, including the full wallpaper library via wallpaper_rotation::refresh, reloads the window CSS and decodes the wallpaper on the UI thread.

**Fix.** Record each control's loaded value when it is built, and on Save send only the fields whose current value differs, as the wallpaper fields already do. Do the same diff for the notification patch.

**Verifier note.** Main mechanism to stress: the page snapshot never refreshes while the project stays the same, so the window during which another writer's change can be reverted lasts the whole app session, not just a short race. The exact request count depends on how many controls exist and is not decisive. Fix: record each control's initial value at build time and send only the fields that differ, as the wallpaper fields already do. Do the same for the notification patch. Optionally, also make the settings.set handler skip writing, auditing and emitting when `before == value`.

#### RA-255 · Each wallpaper's 'preview' is a second copy of the full image: it halves the 1.5 MB library and every gallery redraw decodes every full-size image on the UI thread, even while Settings is hidden

`apps/relay-native/src/tools_settings.rs:1011` · **medium** · Performance · confirmed · effort S

**Problem.** `library.push(json!({"id":...,"name":name,"image":image,"preview":image}))`, then the cap `if serde_json::to_vec(&library)...len()>1500000` (1012). render_wallpapers base64-decodes `item["preview"].as_str().or(item["image"].as_str())` and calls `gtk::gdk::Texture::from_bytes` for every card (838-853), plus `wallpaper_texture(current_image)` (903). sync_wallpaper (15-31) redraws the gallery whenever the current wallpaper changes and the user has no pending pick, i.e. on every rotation tick. That happens even while another page is visible, because the gallery is kept after leaving Settings.

**Impact.** Each image counts twice against the 1.5 MB cap. Measured data URLs for 1280-px re-encodes were 25-166 KB, and photographs are larger, so 'Wallpaper library is full' arrives after half as many images; with photographs that can be as few as 2-5, which also limits rotation. Every pick, remove, clear or add, and every rotation tick, decodes all full-size images on the main thread to draw 132×66 thumbnails. Every appearance.wallpapers transfer (each load_appearance and each rotation tick) and every library undo row in the audit table is twice as large.

**Fix.** In the spawn_blocking step, also make a small thumbnail (for example Pixbuf::from_file_at_scale(path, 264, 132)) and store that as preview, or omit preview, since the renderer already falls back to image. Cache textures by id, and skip the redraw while the gallery is not mapped.

**Verifier note.** The real user-visible cost is that the library holds half as many images as the cap allows. The per-tick decode cost is modest: a few JPEG decodes every 15 minutes by default, minimum 1 minute. Simplest fix: drop `preview` (the renderer falls back to `image`), or generate a small thumbnail in the spawn_blocking step. Raising or recomputing the cap is then optional. Existing stored libraries keep the duplicated data until they are rewritten.

#### RA-256 · 'Update from GitHub' always reinstalls from the repository's default branch, not the branch the skill was installed from

`apps/relay-native/src/tools_skills.rs:177` · **medium** · Bug · confirmed · effort M

**Problem.** The button sends `json!({"url": skill["source_url"], "subdir": skill["source_path"]})` (177). The engine stores source_url without the branch: github.rs:137 `format!("https://github.com/{}/{}.git", parts[0], repo)`. The branch parsed from a tree/<branch>/... URL (138-139) is used only for the clone and is not stored (DownloadedSkill at 190; the UPDATE at provider.rs:491-494 writes no ref). Parsing the stored URL again gives `branch` None, so the update runs `git clone --depth 1` on the default branch. The existing row is matched by source_url + source_path (provider.rs:425-444), so it is overwritten in place.

**Impact.** A skill installed from https://github.com/o/r/tree/dev/skills/x is, on 'Update from GitHub', silently replaced by the default branch's SKILL.md with a new revision. If that path does not exist on the default branch, the update fails with 'skills/x/SKILL.md does not exist in the repository'.

**Fix.** Store the ref, either by keeping the tree/<ref> form in source_url or adding a source_ref column with a migration, and pass it when updating. Until then, show the branch the skill came from and warn that an update uses the default branch.

**Verifier note.** A related effect: the unique index skills_source(source_url, source_path) (store.rs:277) means the same path installed from two branches collapses into one row, and each install overwrites the other. Store the ref, either in source_url as the tree/<ref> form or in a migrated source_ref column, and include it in the identity.

#### RA-257 · Explorer and Source Control file names never show their git status colour: `.tree-name`/`.scm-name` override every `.git-*` rule

`apps/relay-native/src/css/git_files.css:63` · **medium** · Bug · confirmed · effort S

**Problem.** git_files.css:31-36 set the status colours with single-class rules (`.git-modified { color: #e2c08d; }`, `.git-added, .git-untracked {…}`, `.git-deleted`, `.git-renamed`, `.git-conflict`, `.git-ignored`), specificity 0,1,0. Later in the same file, line 63 `.tree-name { font-size: 12.5px; color: @ink; }` and line 193 `.scm-name { font-size: 12.5px; color: @ink; }` have the same specificity, so source order makes them win. The Rust puts both classes on the same label: editor.rs:775-780 (`label(name, "tree-name")` then `name.add_css_class(class)`), code_git.rs:873-876 and 1493-1496 (`label(name, "scm-name")` then `title.add_css_class(class)`). Only ignored files were special-cased (`.tree-name.git-ignored`, line 38, 0,2,0). I checked this in a throwaway GTK 4.22 process loading the real concatenated stylesheet: tree-name/scm-name plus git-modified/added/deleted/conflict all compute to #ececea (ink), and scm-name plus git-ignored is also ink. Only the `scm-letter`/`tree-badge` letters get #e2c08d.

**Impact.** Every changed file in the Code explorer and Source Control list shows its name in plain ink. That contradicts the file's own comment (line 30: "names and letters, explorer and Source Control alike") and DESIGN.md. The folder re-tint pass in project_files.rs:566-579 removes and re-adds STATUS_CLASSES on every folder name at each status refresh, with no visible result. Only the strikethrough on deleted names and the one-letter badges show status.

**Fix.** Remove `color: @ink` from `.tree-name` (line 63) and `.scm-name` (line 193). Both labels already inherit ink from `button.tree-row` (line 52), `button.scm-open` (line 189) or the dialog. Alternatively, move the `.git-*` block below those rules. Then delete the now-redundant `.tree-name.git-ignored` (line 38).

**Verifier note.** A further correction: `.scm-name.git-ignored` is not covered by line 38, though ignored files are filtered out of SCM lists anyway. Status still reaches the user through the badge and letter labels, which is why this is medium rather than high. The fix is as proposed: drop `color: @ink` from `.tree-name` and `.scm-name` (button.tree-row and button.scm-open already set ink), or raise the specificity of the status selectors.

<a id="ra-258"></a>

#### RA-258 · Smoke harness compiled into relay-native acts on whatever engine it reaches; only env vars gate it, and run.sh's partial scrub points it at the live engine

`apps/relay-native/src/smoke.rs:452` · **medium** · Data loss · confirmed · effort S

**Problem.** main.rs:10-14 declares `mod roadmap_smoke; mod smoke; mod smoke_project_files; mod smoke_registry;` with no cfg or feature. app.rs:368 calls `crate::smoke::install(&ui)` on every activation, and the only gate is `let Ok(path) = std::env::var("RELAY_NATIVE_SCREENSHOT") else { return; };` (smoke.rs:452). Nothing checks which engine `ui.path` points at before acting.

With RELAY_NATIVE_FIXTURE=1 the page path does the following:
- At 1 s, `verify_terminal_input` (smoke.rs:507-510, app.rs:1616-1621) calls `pane.terminal.paste_text(&format!("native-paste-check-{name}\n"))` on every pane, which terminal.rs:219-241 forwards as `session.input`.
- `edit_fixture` renames `tasks[0]` (smoke.rs:333, 400-411).
- It also overwrites `notes[0]`'s body with 'Native note save verified.' and saves via notes.save (smoke.rs:339, 381-386, 413-416).
- Or, on the launch page, it creates a task and launches a review group (smoke.rs:341-366).
- On page=code it inserts '\nNative editor save verified.\n' into README.md and saves (smoke.rs:709-714, editor.rs:606-611).
- On page=settings it writes terminal.font_size 9.75, appearance.panel_alpha 0.96 and the global guardrail destructive_write.min_removed_pct 62.5, and never restores them (smoke.rs:144-157).

Without FIXTURE:
- page=project-launch clicks Start (smoke.rs:571-585).
- The setup '*-submit' pages click setup-add (smoke.rs:536-568, 660-671).

Roadmap branch:
- It only asserts `fixture && RELAY_INSTANCE == "test"` (smoke.rs:476), yet README.md:22 documents `./run.sh test` as an ordinary persistent instance, with data in ~/.local/share/relay-v4/test.
- smoke_registry.rs:45 and roadmap_smoke.rs:59-62 also require `ui.path.starts_with(std::env::temp_dir())`.
- smoke_notes.rs:39-43 and smoke_project_files.rs:84-88/269-273 check env vars only. The 'files' part edits and saves the project's README.md and writes preview.PNG and broken.png into the project root; the 'lifecycle' part creates and spawns five `claude` sessions.

run.sh:12 runs only `unset RELAY_NATIVE_SOCKET` ('Never inherit a stale screenshot/test socket'), so SCREENSHOT, FIXTURE, PAGE and ROADMAP pass through to the real app.

**Impact.** Normal use cannot trigger this: nothing in the product sets RELAY_NATIVE_SCREENSHOT.

Trigger: the binary starts with harness variables set but no RELAY_NATIVE_SOCKET. Two realistic ways:
- A developer exported RELAY_NATIVE_SCREENSHOT, FIXTURE and PAGE in fish to rerun one smoke page, then later runs `./run.sh` from the same shell. run.sh drops only the socket override.
- An agent session on this machine runs `RELAY_NATIVE_SCREENSHOT=/tmp/x.png RELAY_NATIVE_FIXTURE=1 RELAY_NATIVE_PAGE=notes target/debug/relay-native` to grab a screenshot.

Consequence: the client connects to $XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/relay-v4/dev.sock, the live engine. Depending on the page it then:
- types `native-paste-check-<name>⏎` into every running agent's terminal;
- overwrites the user's first note or renames the first task (recoverable only through audit.undo, and only if noticed);
- edits and saves README.md in the selected project;
- silently changes the global destructive-write guardrail threshold and terminal/appearance settings;
- launches paid provider sessions.

After 4 s it closes itself.

The roadmap 'files' and 'lifecycle' parts do the same against a persistent `test` instance.

**Fix.** Make isolation one precondition in `install`: before arming any page, fixture or roadmap action, require `ui.path.starts_with(std::env::temp_dir())`, which all four driver scripts already satisfy, and exit with an error otherwise. Then drop the per-part env-only checks.

Have run.sh also `unset RELAY_NATIVE_FIXTURE RELAY_NATIVE_PAGE RELAY_NATIVE_ROADMAP RELAY_NATIVE_BURST`. test-launcher-real.py already pops FIXTURE and PAGE and only needs SCREENSHOT and VERIFY_CONNECTION.

Longer term, put the harness modules and the verify_* helpers behind a `smoke` cargo feature that only the scripts enable.

`crates/relay-cli/src/remote.rs:114` · **medium** · Error handling · confirmed · effort S

The systemd unit (Restart=on-failure) restart-loops until it hits its start limit.

The engine may answer a ping for a moment before exiting, because its socket is bound at line 97, but the process still exits immediately. The fix is as proposed: on load or save failure, log the error and continue without the door, tunnel or direct_port update. Do not reset the file, which the load comment rightly forbids.
