#### RA-318 · A scalar stored at guardrails.projects.<id> (or .workspaces.<id>) makes every guardrail config read for that project panic

`crates/relay-core/src/guardrail.rs:174` · **low** · Bug · confirmed · effort S

**Problem.** settings.set accepts any value at any valid path (settings.rs:217-224). In layers(), put_raw(own, "", 5) calls merge_value, which replaces the {} with the scalar (207-209; settings.rs:115); `merge_value(&mut next, &own)` (161) makes `next` a number; `next["protected_paths"] = json!(protected_paths);` (174) is serde_json IndexMut on a non-object, which panics.

**Impact.** After e.g. `settings.set {path:'guardrails.projects.3', value:false}`, authorize() for every agent mutation in project 3, every guardrail.gate (hooks see a dropped connection and block all tools), session.spawn/resume (plan_launch reads the config) and guardrail.config.get/set/layers panic; config.set cannot repair it because it calls layers() first, and doing it from the UI zombifies its connection (previous finding). Recovery needs settings.reset from the CLI.

**Fix.** Only merge layer values that are objects (flag others as invalid config), and replace the IndexMut with `if let Some(map) = next.as_object_mut()`; optionally validate guardrails.* subtrees in settings.set.

**Verifier note.** settings.set is Actors::UserOnly (relay-bus ops/notify.rs:23-24), so only the user, typing a bad CLI or API call, can trigger this. Agents cannot. Hooks see 'connection closed' and exit 2, so tools are blocked (fail closed), not bypassed. A workspace-only scope does not panic: typed() returns an error. settings.reset repairs it. Fix as proposed: merge only object-valued layers, and use `as_object_mut()` instead of IndexMut.

#### RA-320 · gate write-path resolves no symlinks: a symlink made in the worktree escapes write_roots / protected_paths

`crates/relay-core/src/guardrail.rs:628` · **low** · Security · confirmed · effort S

**Problem.** write_target (guardrail.rs:623-664) rejects `..` and, for an absolute path, string-prefix-strips the worktree, but never canonicalizes symlinks; a relative path with no `..` is accepted as InWorktree (guardrail.rs:628-630) and protected_paths/destructive are then matched against the literal relative string (guardrail.rs:512,548). The file.* bus ops are protected because file.rs::safe_join canonicalizes and rejects escapes (file.rs:489-506), but the PreToolUse gate that binds the providers' own Write/Edit tools has no equivalent.

**Impact.** An agent runs `ln -s ~/.ssh link` (a Bash exec, not denied), then uses the Write tool on `link/authorized_keys`: the gate sees relative `link/authorized_keys`, treats it as in-worktree, allows it, and the provider writes through the symlink to a path outside the worktree and outside every allowed_write_root. The same trick defeats protected_paths (symlink named differently from the protected pattern). write_roots is a stated policy (D102); this silently voids it.

**Fix.** Canonicalize the write target (or its nearest existing ancestor) in write_target before the worktree/root/protected checks, exactly as file.rs::safe_join already does, and refuse paths whose real location leaves every write root.

**Verifier note.** Treat this as a small extra on top of #1, not a separate medium-severity hole. The fix is cheap and still worth doing: canonicalize the nearest existing ancestor of the target, as file.rs::safe_join does, before the worktree, root and protected checks. Compare the real path against canonicalized roots, so a worktree path that itself goes through a symlink does not get misclassified as outside.

#### RA-323 · install_git rewrites the shared .git/config on every launch/create/commit, and refresh_git does it without hooks::writes(), so lock contention fails the operation

`crates/relay-core/src/hooks.rs:75` · **low** · Concurrency · confirmed · effort S

**Problem.** `git(repo, &["config", "extensions.worktreeConfig", "true"])` runs unconditionally. Verified: git rewrites .git/config (new inode) even when the value is unchanged, and fails with "could not lock config file .git/config: File exists" (exit 255) while another writer holds config.lock. `refresh_git` is called on every git.commit (git.rs:548-553) without taking `hooks::writes()`. Other writers of .git/config include agents' `git push -u`, `branch_cleanup`'s `config --remove-section` (branch_cleanup.rs:319) and `git branch -m`.

**Impact.** An agent pushing with -u at the same moment as a launch, create or bus commit makes it fail (`session.spawn` errors, or git.commit returns `git.hook_refresh_failed`). Every bus commit also spawns 4-5 git processes and rewrites the shared config for nothing.

**Fix.** Read `git config --get extensions.worktreeConfig` and set it only when missing; take `hooks::writes()` in refresh_git; skip the rewrite when the hook script and hooksPath are already current.

**Verifier note.** The impact is an occasional spurious failure, not a frequent one. The fix is as proposed: read before setting extensions.worktreeConfig, take hooks::writes() in refresh_git, and skip the rewrite when the script and hooksPath are already current (this also removes about 4 git subprocesses per bus commit). Lock contention with agents' own git commands cannot be fully removed; a short retry on "could not lock config file" would cover it.

#### RA-325 · Relay rewrites a repository-tracked .codex/hooks.json with machine-specific commands, and git-ignores the path for new files

`crates/relay-core/src/hooks.rs:494` · **low** · Bug · confirmed · effort M

**Problem.** `install_codex` merges Relay's handlers, which hold the absolute path to the user's relay binary and `--instance`, into `<worktree>/.codex/hooks.json` and rewrites the file pretty-printed (494-548). `ensure_excluded` adds `.codex/hooks.json` to `.git/info/exclude` (worktree.rs:39-41), which does nothing for a tracked file. `git.commit {all:true}` runs `git add -A` (git.rs:545).

**Impact.** In a repository that commits its Codex project hooks, the file shows as modified throughout every Codex session. An `add -A` commit by an agent or by Relay pushes `'/home/<user>/…/relay' --instance 'dev' hook codex-pre-tool` to teammates, whose Codex then calls a binary that does not exist on every tool use. Teardown leaves formatting churn. Conversely, a `.codex/hooks.json` the user creates for their project is silently ignored by git.

**Fix.** Check whether the file is tracked (`git ls-files --error-unmatch`). If it is, deliver Relay's hooks through a layer that is not shared (a per-launch config override or a user-level, cwd-scoped hooks file), or refuse clearly. Exclude the path only when Relay created it.

A .codex/hooks.json the user creates anywhere in the repository is silently ignored by git. Repositories that commit .codex/hooks.json are uncommon, so severity stays low. Fix as proposed: detect a tracked file with `git ls-files --error-unmatch` and either use a non-shared hook layer or refuse clearly. Exclude the path only when Relay created the file.

#### RA-327 · Update result message comes from the head of the output, with stderr appended after stdout

`crates/relay-core/src/provider_updates.rs:85` · **low** · Bug · confirmed · effort S

**Problem.** `let keep = count.min(65536usize.saturating_sub(saved.len()));` keeps the first 64 KiB of each stream. Then `output.extend(stderr.join()...)` and `output.lines().rev().find(|line| !line.trim().is_empty())` take the last line of stdout followed by stderr.

**Impact.** When an updater prints more than 64 KiB, its final status or error line is discarded and the notification shows a line from the middle. When an updater writes progress to stderr, the reported 'result' is the last stderr line rather than the outcome on stdout.

Fix: keep each stream separate, report stdout's last line on success and stderr's (falling back to stdout's) on failure, and keep a tail rather than the head if the cap stays.

#### RA-328 · A timed-out provider probe is recorded as 'not installed', clearing cached version and sign-in and raising a spurious version-changed notification

`crates/relay-core/src/providers.rs:336` · **low** · Error handling · confirmed · effort S

**Problem.** On timeout, command_output returns `Some(Output { success: false, stdout: String::new() })` (lines 367-369), so version and signed_in_as become None. `let version_changed = previous_version.is_some() && previous_version != version;` is then true, the provider_cache row's version and signed_in_as are overwritten with NULL, and the handler inserts '<name> version changed' with body '<old> → not installed' (handlers/provider.rs:23-28).

**Impact.** A cold start slower than 3 s, for example with many agents building, produces a false notification and wipes the cached version and account, so the UI shows the provider as signed out until the next refresh. The recovery itself is silent because previous_version is then None.

**Fix.** Treat a failed or timed-out probe as 'unknown' and keep the cached version/signed_in_as. Report a change only when both values are known, or when the executable path disappeared.

**Verifier note.** An extra trigger: the post-update refresh at provider_updates.rs:62 can clear version/signed_in_as when the new binary's first run is slow. Fix: distinguish a timed-out or failed probe from a missing executable, keep the cached version/signed_in_as on an unknown result, and set version_changed only when both versions are known or the path disappeared.

**Also at:** `crates/relay-core/src/providers.rs:362`, `crates/relay-core/src/handlers/provider.rs:20`

<a id="ra-329"></a>

#### RA-329 · Ring trims after extending, so the VecDeque grows to as much as 16 MiB per PTY and copies the ring on growth

`crates/relay-core/src/pty.rs:65` · **low** · Performance · confirmed · effort S

**Problem.** `self.buf.extend(data); if self.buf.len() > SCROLLBACK_BYTES { let excess = ...; self.buf.drain(..excess); ... }`. Once len reaches a capacity near 8 MiB, the next extend triggers RawVec's amortized growth (max(2×cap, needed)), copying the whole ring under the ring lock, and the capacity never shrinks. A resumed PTY's first push is the saved history, which can exceed 8 MiB after lossy UTF-8 expansion.

**Impact.** Depending on the first frame's size, each full ring ends up with between 8 and 16+ MiB of capacity, and as the window rotates through the buffer all of it becomes resident. With 10-20 sessions that is tens to about 160 MiB of avoidable RSS, plus a one-off 8 MiB memcpy on each PTY's reader thread.

**Fix.** Create the ring with `VecDeque::with_capacity(SCROLLBACK_BYTES + 64 * 1024)` (virtual until touched), or trim before extending and push only the last SCROLLBACK_BYTES of an oversized slice.

**Verifier note.** The doubling does not depend on the size of the first frame. Any ring that fills settles at about 2x SCROLLBACK_BYTES, because the extend-then-trim order always asks for more than the cap once the ring is full. The cost is about 8 MiB of extra RSS per long-lived session, plus a one-time 8 MiB memcpy under the ring lock on the reader thread (attach/scrollback wait for it). Fix: trim before extending (drain max(0, len+n-cap) first, and keep only the last SCROLLBACK_BYTES of an oversized slice), or allocate with_capacity(SCROLLBACK_BYTES + 64 KiB) up front.

**Also at:** `crates/relay-core/src/pty.rs:190`, `crates/relay-core/src/pty.rs:192`

**Merged duplicates:** lens-perf#20

<a id="ra-330"></a>

#### RA-330 · Pty::spawn does not check cwd; portable-pty silently falls back to $HOME, where the relative --settings/--mcp-config paths resolve

`crates/relay-core/src/pty.rs:182` · **low** · Bug · confirmed · effort S · rechecked after PR #30/#31: still present

**Problem.** `cmd.cwd(&spec.cwd);` with no check. portable-pty 0.9's CommandBuilder::as_command picks `.filter(|dir| Path::new(dir).is_dir()).unwrap_or(home.as_ref())`. prepare_launch checks `cwd.is_dir()` (session.rs:472), but it runs unlocked and the spawn happens later, in finish_launch.

**Impact.** If the worktree disappears between prepare and the locked spawn (deleted outside Relay while the launch waits for the store lock), the agent starts in the user's home. Claude's relative `--mcp-config .relay/relay.mcp.json` and `--settings .relay/relay.settings.json`, and the worktree's .claude/.codex hook files, then resolve against $HOME. The session runs without its Relay guardrail hooks, while RELAY_WORKTREE still names the missing path.

**Fix.** In Pty::spawn, refuse when `!spec.cwd.is_dir()` with a typed error (session.worktree_missing) rather than inheriting the dependency's fallback.

**Verifier note.** The trigger is a narrow race. The worktree has to be deleted from outside Relay after prepare_launch has just written hook, brief and role files into it, and before finish_launch acquires the lock (normally milliseconds). Relay's own close/discard paths change the session state, and finish_launch's recheck catches that. The most likely result is that Claude fails to start because its relative settings file is missing in $HOME, not a working unguarded session. Bus ops are still token-gated. The cheap defence is still right: check `spec.cwd.is_dir()` in Pty::spawn (or re-check it in finish_launch) and return session.worktree_missing.

**Also at:** `crates/relay-core/src/handlers/session.rs:472`, `crates/relay-core/src/providers.rs:173`

#### RA-331 · Signal deaths are recorded as exit code 1, though the doc promises None

`crates/relay-core/src/pty.rs:235` · **low** · Bug · confirmed · effort S

**Problem.** `let code = child.wait().ok().map(|s| s.exit_code() as i32);`. For a signalled child, portable-pty 0.9's `From<std::process::ExitStatus>` sets `code: status.code().map(|c| c as u32).unwrap_or(1)` and keeps the signal name separately. The doc at pty.rs:165-166 says '(with its exit code, `None` if killed by signal)'.

**Impact.** An agent that is OOM-killed, segfaults or receives SIGKILL is stored as exit_code=1. The slate then says 'The process exited with code 1' (session_context.rs:196-199), indistinguishable from an ordinary error exit, so the crash cause is lost. The documented None appears only when wait() itself fails.

**Fix.** Check `s.signal()` and record None, or a distinct value such as 128+signo, for signal deaths, then update the doc. The UI can then say 'killed by signal'.

**Verifier note.** Use `s.signal()` to record None, or 128+signo, and update the doc and the slate text. The impact is diagnostic only: the session still ends as exited and the builder task still becomes failed in either case.

**Also at:** `apps/relay-native/src/session_context.rs:196`, `crates/relay-core/src/handlers/session.rs:653`

<a id="ra-332"></a>

#### RA-332 · Pty::kill signals the process group only while the leader is alive and never escalates for surviving members; the reader outlives the master

`crates/relay-core/src/pty.rs:364` · **low** · Resource leak · confirmed · effort S

**Problem.** `if !self.exited() { libc::kill(-(pid), SIGTERM) ...; if !self.exited() { libc::kill(-(pid), SIGKILL) ... } }`. Escalation depends only on the leader, and nothing is sent once the leader has exited. The module doc (line 3) says 'kill child → drop master → the reader ends on EIO', but the reader owns its own dup of the master (try_clone_reader, line 186). It therefore ends only when every holder of the slave has exited; dropping `master` closes just one fd.

**Impact.** On park or close, group members that survive SIGTERM after the leader exits (slow cleanup handlers, or handlers that ignore it) are never SIGKILLed. If the provider crashed or the user typed /exit, close signals nothing at all, so members that ignored the kernel's SIGHUP keep running until the next engine start reaps them by RELAY_SESSION. That can include a worktree that close has just deleted. Any such survivor still holding the slave keeps the reader thread and its 8 MiB ring alive.

**Fix.** Always signal -pid, whatever exited() says. After the grace period, SIGKILL the group if any member remains (`kill(-pid, 0) == 0`). Optionally also reap this session's env-tagged descendants with relay_children filtered to the session name, the rule recovery already applies at startup. Correct the module comment.

**Verifier note.** Impact is lower than the finding implies. When the session leader (the provider, which portable-pty setsid()s and gives a TIOCSCTTY) exits, the kernel already sends SIGHUP+SIGCONT to the foreground process group. Only members that ignore SIGHUP and also survive SIGTERM linger, and grandchildren that setsid() or setpgid() away escape -pid either way. The next engine start reaps env-tagged survivors (recovery.rs:67). The fix as proposed stands: always signal -pid, check kill(-pid,0) after the grace and SIGKILL the group, and correct the line-3 comment.

**Also at:** `crates/relay-core/src/pty.rs:3`, `crates/relay-core/src/pty.rs:186`, `crates/relay-core/src/handlers/session.rs:1566`, `crates/relay-core/src/recovery.rs:64`

<a id="ra-333"></a>

#### RA-333 · The socket door stays open, and keeps dispatching, while serve() kills sessions; SocketServer cannot stop live connections

`crates/relay-core/src/socket.rs:134` · **low** · Concurrency · confirmed · effort S

**Problem.** Drop only aborts the accept task and unlinks the socket. Per-connection tasks are detached `tokio::spawn`s (113-117) with no shutdown signal. serve.rs:50-51 runs `served.engine.shutdown()` before `drop(served)`; shutdown() takes up to 2 s plus 2 s per live PTY, in sequence. Dispatch never checks `is_quitting()`.

**Impact.** During app.quit or SIGTERM, connected clients (native app, MCP calls, phone) keep dispatching, and new connections are still accepted. A `session.wake` or `session.spawn` in that window inserts a PTY after shutdown() has drained the map. That PTY is neither killed nor marked restorable, and its row stays 'running' for the next recovery, which is the pid-reuse path above.

**Fix.** Give SocketServer a CancellationToken or JoinSet for its connections, and close the door (stop accepting, end connections) before `engine.shutdown()`. Once `request_quit` is set, have dispatch refuse mutations with `app.quitting`.

**Verifier note.** The window is bounded by shutdown() itself, because once serve() returns the runtime and its detached tasks are dropped. remote.rs::serve_with_door has the same sequence. The simplest fix is to make dispatch refuse lifecycle mutations once `is_quitting()` is true (SIGINT/SIGTERM must call request_quit first), and/or drop the SocketServer before calling engine.shutdown().

**Also at:** `crates/relay-core/src/serve.rs:44-51`, `crates/relay-core/src/engine.rs:571-584`, `crates/relay-core/src/engine.rs:633-659`

#### RA-334 · MirrorAttachment::drop always announces `stopped`, relabelling a lost or failed mirror and duplicating stop events

`crates/relay-core/src/socket.rs:237` · **low** · Bug · confirmed · effort S

**Problem.** `self.runtime.finish(crate::device::MirrorState::Stopped, None, None);` ignores the return value, then `self.engine.emit_system("mirror.changed", json!({"mirror_id":self.runtime.id,"state":"stopped"}))` runs unconditionally. `finish` is first-terminal-wins (device.rs:245-258), and handlers/device.rs:736-744 emits only when finish returns true. This event also omits the `device` field that the other emitters include.

**Impact.** Trigger: the device is unplugged (`lost` is emitted) and the window then closes, or `device.mirror.stop` has already emitted `stopped`. Listeners then receive another `mirror.changed {state:"stopped"}`, and anything keyed on the last event shows "stopped" instead of "lost" or "failed". device.rs:245-246 says this relabel must not happen.

**Fix.** `if self.runtime.finish(MirrorState::Stopped, None, None) { emit_system("mirror.changed", json!({.., "device": self.runtime.device, "state": "stopped"})) }`.

**Verifier note.** Gate the emit on `finish(..)` returning true and include `"device": self.runtime.device`, as the other emitters do. Removing the entry from `attached_mirrors` once the stream reaches a terminal state would also stop the stale attachment outliving its mirror.

**Also at:** `crates/relay-core/src/device.rs:245-258`, `crates/relay-core/src/handlers/device.rs:109-129`, `crates/relay-core/src/handlers/device.rs:736-745`

#### RA-335 · Request lines have no size limit: one long line is buffered whole and copied several times, which can OOM the engine

`crates/relay-core/src/socket.rs:373` · **low** · Resource leak · confirmed · effort S · rechecked after PR #30/#31: still present

**Problem.** `let mut lines = BufReader::new(r).lines();` and `lines.next_line().await?` read until '\n' with no cap. The line is then parsed into a `Request` Value and cloned: `req.clone()` for attach, detach, mirror and runs; `req.payload.clone()` in subscribe and wait; and `serde_json::from_value(payload.clone())` in pty_fast_path. The handler then deserializes it again into the typed payload. The native client bounds incoming lines at 2 MiB before allocating (apps/relay-native/src/client.rs:48, 186-205), but the engine bounds nothing. The phone bridge forwards lines of up to tungstenite's default 64 MiB.

**Impact.** Trigger: a local client that writes without newlines (e.g. a file piped into the socket by mistake), or a huge payload such as `relay cmd file.write -` of a multi-GB file or a giant paste sent as `session.input`. Consequence: the engine holds 3-4x the line in memory. At GB scale it is OOM-killed, and every agent session dies with it.

**Fix.** Read with a bounded fill_buf/read_until loop, as the native client does (e.g. a 16-32 MiB cap). Answer an over-limit line with a typed `bus.too_large` error and discard the rest of that line. Pull the needed fields out before moving `req`, to avoid the extra clones.

**Verifier note.** Downgrade to low: no other local user or network peer can reach it, and the remote path is bounded at 64 MiB by tungstenite. The fix is still reasonable: a bounded read_until loop like the native client's (client.rs:186-205), answering over-limit lines with a typed error.

**Also at:** `apps/relay-native/src/client.rs:186-212`, `crates/relay-core/src/engine.rs:1276`

<a id="ra-336"></a>

#### RA-336 · bus.subscribe, bus.wait and bus.unsubscribe skip the pipeline's envelope and actor checks

`crates/relay-core/src/socket.rs:414` · **low** · Invariant · confirmed · effort S

**Problem.** These branches deserialize the payload directly (`serde_json::from_value::<SubscribeIn>(req.payload.clone())`, and likewise `WaitIn`) and never call dispatch. There is no `req.v != ENVELOPE_V` check and no resolve_actor. The registered handlers only return `door_only` (handlers/bus.rs:108-110).

**Impact.** A request that claims `"actor":"system"` is accepted, although BUS.md §1.1 says "Every door rejects a request that claims it". So is `test` on a stable instance, and `agent:x` with a wrong or missing token. Each receives the global event stream, which is not scoped by project. The practical risk today is small because `user` needs no credential, but the documented contract isn't enforced, and any later per-actor event scoping would be bypassed here.

**Fix.** Add an `Engine::preflight(&req, Door::Socket)` that runs the envelope, door, actor, schema and allowlist checks without a handler, and call it before the socket-native branches.

**Verifier note.** Line numbers are approximately right (subscribe branch at 362, wait at ~400, unsubscribe at ~446). There is a simpler fix than a new preflight API: in each of these branches, call engine.resolve_actor (or a small envelope+actor check) on a blocking thread and return the error first. Note that for agents this also skips layer-2 role authorization. That only matters if some role is meant to be denied bus.wait or bus.subscribe.

**Also at:** `crates/relay-core/src/socket.rs:400-454`, `crates/relay-core/src/handlers/bus.rs:108-110`

#### RA-337 · Event stream and audit log bypass agent read scoping: any agent sees every project's mail, session metadata and written file contents

`crates/relay-core/src/socket.rs:414` · **low** · Security · confirmed · effort M

**Problem.** bus.subscribe and bus.wait are answered inside handle_conn before any dispatch: no resolve_actor, no token check, and no filter beyond the event name (`let mut rx = engine.subscribe(); .. if f.matches(&ev.ev)`, 362-399 and 400-449). mailbox.new events carry the whole message (`ctx.emit("mailbox.new", serde_json::to_value(&message))`, notes.rs:625), yet mailbox.list refuses another session's mailbox (`not_own("mailbox")`, notes.rs:662-663). audit.list and audit.get (handlers/audit.rs:29-46) return rows from any project with stored payloads up to 64 KB, including mailbox.send text and file.write or guardrail.gate file contents, without checking the caller's project. D106 says 'an agent sees the metadata of any session in its own project and nothing outside it.' bus.wait is exposed as an MCP tool (mcp.rs:159-163 excludes only subscribe and unsubscribe).

**Impact.** An agent in project A can read private mail between other sessions, including those in other projects, by calling `bus_wait {events:["mailbox.new"]}` repeatedly or `audit.list {op_prefix:"mailbox.send"}`. The same channels give it file contents other sessions wrote and session.changed metadata (worktree, pid) for every project, all of which the per-handler checks and D106 deliberately withhold. A smaller inconsistency: subscribe and wait accept the system actor, and the test actor even on a stable instance, which every other door rejects.

**Fix.** Resolve and authenticate the actor for subscribe and wait like any other request. On agent connections, pass only events whose project_id is the session's own, and drop mailbox.new events not addressed to that session. Scope audit.list and audit.get (and guardrail.holds.list and guardrail.requests.list) to the agent's own project, and redact payloads of rows that carry other sessions' mail.

**Verifier note.** Still worth fixing for consistency: resolve the actor for subscribe and wait, filter agent connections by project_id and drop mailbox.new events not addressed to that session, and scope audit.list/get (and guardrail.holds.list/requests.list) for agent actors. The fix should not claim this creates confidentiality, because agents keep filesystem read of the store.

**Also at:** `crates/relay-core/src/socket.rs:400`, `crates/relay-core/src/handlers/audit.rs:29`, `crates/relay-core/src/handlers/notes.rs:625`, `crates/relay-core/src/handlers/notes.rs:662`, `crates/relay-core/src/handlers/guardrail.rs:306`, `crates/relay-cli/src/mcp.rs:159`

#### RA-338 · A lagging subscriber silently loses events and the client is never told to resync

`crates/relay-core/src/socket.rs:437` · **low** · Error handling · confirmed · effort S

**Problem.** The forwarder handles `Err(RecvError::Lagged(n))` with only `tracing::warn!(lagged = n, "subscriber lagged; events dropped")` and keeps looping; nothing is written to the client. The channel is `broadcast::channel(4096)` (engine.rs:437). The per-connection mpsc (capacity 1024) is shared with PTY frames, so a slow reader backs up into the forwarder.

**Impact.** If the UI stops reading long enough for 4096 events to pass (heavy load, a stalled client), it misses events such as guardrail.held or session.changed. Because the client applies events in place, it keeps the stale state with no signal to refetch.

**Fix.** On Lagged, send a synthetic `{"ev":"bus.lagged","payload":{"dropped":n}}` line so the client can refresh. For waiters, return early with a lagged flag.

**Verifier note.** Low severity is right. The waiter case matters more than the finding says, because a dropped guardrail answer makes an agent wait for the full timeout (up to 1 h). On Lagged, a waiter should re-check the stored answer (resolved_event) or return early.

#### RA-339 · `bus.wait` blocks the connection's read loop for up to an hour and never notices the client leaving

`crates/relay-core/src/socket.rs:476` · **low** · Resource leak · confirmed · effort M

**Problem.** `let waited = tokio::time::timeout(timeout, async { loop { match rx.recv().await { ... } } }).await;` is awaited inside the request loop, with a timeout of up to 3_600_000 ms (line 409). Nothing polls the read half meanwhile, so neither EOF nor further pipelined requests are seen until the wait ends.

**Impact.** Trigger: an agent is parked or closed, or its MCP call is interrupted, in the middle of the documented exception flow ("call guardrail.request ... then bus.wait", guardrail/grants.rs:24-28). Consequence: the engine keeps the connection, its task, its fd and a broadcast receiver alive until the timeout. Any other request pipelined on that connection waits the whole time.

**Fix.** Run each wait in its own task owned by the connection, so the loop keeps reading and EOF aborts the wait. Alternatively, `select!` the wait against EOF on the reader.

**Verifier note.** Drop the claim that requests pipelined on the same connection are delayed, since no in-tree client pipelines behind bus.wait. A cheap fix is to tokio::select! the wait against lines.next_line() returning None or an error (treating any other line as a protocol error or queueing it), or to cap the default lower. Effort S rather than M.

**Also at:** `crates/relay-core/src/socket.rs:400-449`, `crates/relay-core/src/guardrail/grants.rs:24-28`

`crates/relay-core/src/socket.rs:513` · **low** · Bug · confirmed · effort S

The socket then parses `req.payload.clone()`, the unfilled original, into AttachIn with `.unwrap_or(AttachIn { session: String::new(), from_seq: None, epoch: None })`. Detach reads `req.payload.get("session")` (line 513). Both ops admit agents (relay-bus ops/session.rs:153-154).

**Fix.** Have the attach and detach handlers return the resolved session name (and epoch/seq) and use the response, or have dispatch expose the filled request. Never default to an empty name.

<a id="ra-341"></a>

#### RA-341 · The socket door blocks tokio worker threads on the store mutex and on fd writes

`crates/relay-core/src/socket.rs:521` · **low** · Concurrency · confirmed · effort S

**Problem.** Several blocking calls run directly on runtime worker threads:
- After a successful session.attach, the async task calls `crate::handlers::session::pty_by_name(&engine, &p.session)` (socket.rs:469), which does `let conn = engine.store.lock();` (session.rs:1733) on the runtime thread.
- The app.resources.watch tick task does `let conn = engine.store.lock();` inside `handle.spawn(async …)` every 2 s (handlers/app.rs:121-124).
- Keystrokes that pass answers_from_memory are dispatched inline (socket.rs:735-739) and call pty.write (engine.rs:1284). That takes the PTY writer mutex, which a paste over 1 KiB holds on the blocking pool across a blocking write_all (pty.rs:290-295).
- If the PTY vanishes between the check and the dispatch, the request falls through to the locked session.input handler, still inline.
- Drop impls call stop() methods that can block (socket.rs:238, 276).

**Impact.** Whenever a locked handler runs long (a clone, a dispatch, a worktree removal), each attach and each resource tick parks a whole tokio worker on the mutex. With several panes re-attaching, all of the runtime's workers can be parked. That stalls every connection, including the D148 keystroke fast path, which exists so typing never waits on the store.

**Fix.** Resolve the PTY from memory (engine.pty_named) or inside the spawn_blocking closure. Read resource rows through spawn_blocking. Run Drop-time stop() calls through spawn_blocking. Only inline a keystroke after a try_lock of the PTY writer succeeds.

**Verifier note.** The realistic cost is that one tokio worker is lost for the duration of a long locked handler (resource tick), plus a narrow attach window. Drop the Drop-impl part of the claim. Fix by resolving the PTY with engine.pty_named (memory) in the attach path, reading resource rows inside spawn_blocking, and inlining keystrokes only when try_lock on the writer succeeds.

**Also at:** `crates/relay-core/src/handlers/session.rs:1733`, `crates/relay-core/src/handlers/app.rs:122`, `crates/relay-core/src/engine.rs:1284`, `crates/relay-core/src/socket.rs:739`, `crates/relay-core/src/pty.rs:291`, `crates/relay-core/src/handlers/session.rs:1732-1740`, `crates/relay-core/src/engine.rs:600-608`, `crates/relay-core/src/engine.rs:1222-1273`, `crates/relay-core/src/device.rs:279-290`, `crates/relay-core/src/handlers/session.rs:1732`, `crates/relay-core/src/engine.rs:600`, `apps/relay-native/src/terminal.rs:476`

<a id="ra-342"></a>

#### RA-342 · store.db, its WAL and the backups are created with default permissions (typically 0644 in a 0755 directory)

`crates/relay-core/src/store.rs:388` · **low** · Security · confirmed · effort S

**Problem.** `create_dir_all(dir)` creates the data dir and `Connection::open_with_flags(path, READ_WRITE|CREATE|NO_MUTEX)` creates the store, using SQLite's default 0644 masked by the umask. backup_to's `Connection::open(&dest)` does the same, and nothing sets 0700 or 0600.

**Impact.** On systems whose home directories other users can traverse (0755 homes), other local accounts can read the audit log (up to 64 KB of each request payload, including file contents and commands), notes, mailbox, and sessions.token values. CachyOS's 0700 homes are not affected.

**Fix.** Create ~/.local/share/relay-v4/<instance> and backups/ with DirBuilder::mode(0o700), and chmod the store and backup files to 0600 after opening them.

**Verifier note.** The impact depends on the environment. Exposure needs a traversable home directory with a world-readable ~/.local/share, which is uncommon on current Fedora, Arch/CachyOS, Debian 12+ and Ubuntu 21.04+, where homes are 0700 or 0750. A leaked session token cannot be replayed by another user, because the socket itself is 0600 inside a 0700 directory, so the exposure is confidentiality of stored content only. The fix is to create the relay-v4/<instance>, backups/ and logs/ directories with mode 0700. That covers the -wal and -shm files as well, so chmodding each file is optional.

#### RA-343 · read_codex aborts the whole scan when one file's 1 MiB tail starts inside a UTF-8 character

`crates/relay-core/src/usage.rs:61` · **low** · Error handling · confirmed · effort S

**Problem.** `let raw = read_tail(&path, CODEX_TAIL).ok()?;` returns None from read_codex on the first unreadable file, without moving on to the next. read_tail seeks to len-1 MiB and calls `file.read_to_string(&mut raw)?` (line 96), which fails with InvalidData if the seek lands inside a multi-byte character. The partial first line is only dropped afterwards (line 98).

**Impact.** For any rollout over 1 MiB whose byte at len-1 MiB is a UTF-8 continuation byte (common in CJK, accented or emoji-heavy sessions; 0 of 181 such files on this machine today), or any file that cannot be opened, Codex usage disappears entirely for that read, even when the next file holds valid data.

**Fix.** Read the tail into a Vec<u8>, skip past the first b'\n', then use String::from_utf8_lossy. On a per-file error, `continue` instead of using `?`.

**Verifier note.** Also covers a truncated trailing character in a file still being written, not just the seek point. The fix is right: read the bytes, skip to the first b'\n', use from_utf8_lossy, and `continue` on per-file errors.

**Also at:** `crates/relay-core/src/usage.rs:90`, `crates/relay-core/src/usage.rs:96`, `crates/relay-core/src/handlers/provider.rs:66`

**Merged duplicates:** lens-errors-panics#8

#### RA-344 · Watcher's git-metadata handling assumes .git is a directory; in pooled worktrees index/HEAD live outside the watched root, so staging never refreshes

`crates/relay-core/src/watch.rs:89` · **low** · Bug · confirmed · effort M

**Problem.** `let index_path = root.join(".git/index")` and the `.git/` rules in is_generated_path (162-168) only work for the primary checkout. In a linked worktree `.git` is a file, and the index and HEAD are in `<repo>/.git/worktrees/<name>/`, outside the watched root. The primary's watcher classifies `.git/worktrees/...` paths as generated.

**Impact.** `git add`/`git reset` run by an agent in its own worktree never produce `file.changed`, so staged badges in the Code view stay stale until some unrelated event invalidates it.

**Fix.** Resolve the worktree's git dir (gix `repo.git_dir()`), watch it non-recursively for index and HEAD, and compare against that index path.

**Verifier note.** The impact is narrower than stated. A commit in a linked worktree updates `<repo>/.git/refs/heads/relay/<name>`. If the primary checkout's watcher is registered, it passes that change through as a refs change and emits file.changed, which the native client applies to the whole view. So only staging-only (and HEAD-only, e.g. a checkout of the same tree) operations made from a shell go unseen, and only until the next unrelated event. Fix: resolve `repo.git_dir()` with gix, compare against `git_dir/index`, and add a non-recursive watch on the git dir, or let `.git/worktrees/*/index|HEAD` through in the primary watcher and map them to the owning worktree.

**Also at:** `crates/relay-core/src/watch.rs:162`

#### RA-345 · is_generated_path treats any build/dist/target/coverage/Saved/Binaries component at any depth as generated, hiding tracked source directories

`crates/relay-core/src/watch.rs:169` · **low** · Bug · confirmed · effort M

**Problem.** `relative.components().any(|component| matches!(value, ".relay" | "node_modules" | "target" | "build" | ... | "dist" | "coverage" ...))`. file.rs list_dir uses the same predicate to drop entries from the tree (file.rs:519).

**Impact.** Tracked directories with those names (the committed `dist/` of a JavaScript GitHub Action, `scripts/build/`, a `src/target/` module) are invisible in the Code view's tree, and edits under them never trigger a refresh.

**Fix.** Decide by git ignore rules (gix exclude stack, `git check-ignore`) or by root-level build directories, not by name at any depth.

**Verifier note.** There is also a divergence: file.search uses a separate, narrower list, `skip_dir` (file.rs:629-636), with only .git/.relay/node_modules/target. So search finds and opens files under `build/`, `dist/`, `Saved/` and similar directories that the tree hides, which makes the behaviour inconsistent. Fix: decide with the gix exclude stack (ignored and untracked) for the tree listing, or at least exempt directories that contain tracked entries. Keep the cheap name list only as a watcher event filter.

#### RA-346 · worktree::contains accepts any directory whose .git file names an existing slot, without checking that the slot points back

`crates/relay-core/src/worktree.rs:170` · **low** · Bug · confirmed · effort S

**Problem.** contains reads <candidate>/.git and returns `canon(&gitdir).starts_with(&slots) && gitdir.join("gitdir").is_file()`. It never compares the slot's gitdir back-pointer with the candidate. The doc comment says this is 'exactly what git worktree list reads', but git actually lists a worktree from the slot's gitdir file. root_verify (file.rs:427-441) relies on contains to admit any `worktree` path a caller passes to file.* and git.* ops, agents included.

**Impact.** A `cp -r` copy of a worktree, or any directory given a forged .git pointer, is accepted as a checkout of the project. Git ops there run against the original worktree's index and HEAD: a commit from the copy moves the original's branch and leaves its index describing the copy's files.

**Fix.** Also require that the slot's gitdir file names this checkout: `canon(Path::new(read_to_string(gitdir/"gitdir").trim()).parent()) == want`.

**Verifier note.** Re-categorise it as a bug, not security. One nuance for the fix: a worktree moved by hand with `mv` (without `git worktree move`) also fails the proposed back-pointer check, although git still works there. Report it as 'run git worktree repair' rather than as 'not a worktree'.

**Also at:** `crates/relay-core/src/handlers/file.rs:433`

#### RA-347 · purge_build follows symlinked parent directories, and deletes tracked build/ and dist/ before removal is known to succeed

`crates/relay-core/src/worktree.rs:345` · **low** · Bug · confirmed · effort S

**Problem.** For each BUILD_DIRS entry: `let p = wt.join(d); if p.is_dir() { freed += dir_size(&p); let _ = std::fs::remove_dir_all(&p); }`. is_dir() follows symlinks, and for nested entries (node_modules/.cache, app/build) remove_dir_all resolves a symlinked parent component, so the deletion lands outside the worktree. build/ and dist/ are often tracked source. remove() purges them before `git worktree remove` runs (360-362).

**Impact.** If node_modules in a worktree is a symlink to a shared install (a common disk-saving setup with many worktrees), removing the worktree wipes the shared install's .cache, and freed reports the shared directory's size. A removal that then fails leaves the worktree missing its tracked build/ or dist/ content and any uncommitted changes in them.

**Fix.** Check every path component with symlink_metadata, or canonicalize and require the result to stay under the canonical worktree. Skip tracked directories. Purge only after git confirms the worktree can be removed.

**Verifier note.** Drop the tracked-build/dist part. There is a related and more serious problem in the same function. worktree.remove (git.rs:129-144) never checks that `p.path` is a worktree of the project: it only checks for an owning session, and remove() only refuses the primary. A non-worktree path makes `git worktree remove` fail, and the fallback then rm -rf's that path, after purge_build has already deleted its target/build/dist. The op is UserOnly and the desktop passes listed paths, so this needs a mistaken or crafted request. Even so, the fallback should only run for a path that `contains()` or the worktree list confirms. Separately, WorktreeRemove is registered with plain `Engine::register`, so its dir_size walk, git subprocess and rm -rf run with the store mutex held, which breaks the CLAUDE.md invariant.

**Also at:** `crates/relay-core/src/worktree.rs:360`

#### RA-348 · CPU% baseline is shared by every sampler, so a refresh right after a request reports 0% or ~1000% spikes

`crates/relay-core/src/handlers/app.rs:279` · **low** · Bug · confirmed · effort S

**Problem.** cpu_pct reads and overwrites one per-pid baseline in engine.resource_cpu on every call: `(ticks.saturating_sub(*prior) as f64 / hz / now.duration_since(*at).as_secs_f64() * 100.0)` then `samples.insert(pid, (ticks, now))`. app.resources.get samples every pane, then spawns refresh_disk_cache whose resource_snapshot(rows, engine, true) samples the same pids milliseconds later and emits the result as resource.sample; dashboard.get (notify.rs:188) and the 2 s watch loop share the same baseline. The native panel calls watch then get back-to-back (status.rs:115-118).

**Impact.** With CLK_TCK=100 and a ~1 ms gap, a busy pane reads 0 ticks (0%) or 1 tick (1000%), so the first resource.sample after opening the panel, and samples after dashboard refreshes, plot garbage CPU. The map is never pruned: every pid ever sampled stays, and a reused pid starts from a foreign baseline.

**Fix.** Let only the periodic sampler own/advance the baseline; one-shot readers compute against it without overwriting (or require a minimum interval and reuse the last value); drop entries for pids not in the current rows.

**Verifier note.** The garbage value self-corrects on the next 2 s watch tick, so the impact is a cosmetic glitch in the plotted CPU history (the first sample after opening the panel, and samples after a dashboard refresh). Growth of the map is one small entry per pid ever sampled. Fix: enforce a minimum interval, reusing the last computed value when the gap is under ~500 ms, and retain only pids present in the current rows.

**Also at:** `crates/relay-core/src/handlers/app.rs:76`, `crates/relay-core/src/handlers/app.rs:200`, `crates/relay-core/src/handlers/notify.rs:188`, `apps/relay-native/src/status.rs:115`

<a id="ra-349"></a>

#### RA-349 · avd.boot reports 'started' for any successful spawn, discards the emulator's output and never reaps it

`crates/relay-core/src/handlers/device.rs:360` · **low** · Error handling · confirmed · effort S · rechecked after PR #30/#31: changed

**Problem.** In the after-commit closure, stdin, stdout and stderr are all `Stdio::null()` (line 357), and `let state = if command.spawn().is_ok() { "started" } else { "failed" };` (line 358) drops the `Child` immediately without waiting on it. AvdBoot also does not check `running_serial` before booting.

**Impact.** An emulator that exits immediately (AVD already running, missing system image, KVM unavailable, AVD locked) is shown as 'started', with no error anywhere. Every emulator that later exits stays a zombie until Relay quits.

**Fix.** Hand the Child to a small reaper thread that keeps the tail of stderr and emits `avd.changed {state:"failed", message}` if the emulator exits within roughly the first 10 s (and a stopped state later). Refuse when the AVD already has a running serial.

**Verifier note.** The UI never shows a 'started' label. tools_devices.rs:103-119 only shows the Boot and Cold boot buttons, or the running serial. So the visible symptom is a boot that silently does nothing: the Boot button stays and there is no error. The UI also hides Boot when running_serial is set, so the 'already running' case is mostly guarded on the client side, although the engine does not check it. A zombie costs only one PID-table entry per boot. Fix as proposed: a reaper thread that waits on the child, keeps the tail of stderr, and emits a failed avd.changed with a message on early exit.

**Recheck after PR #30/#31 note.** The mechanism is unchanged, but the impact is worse. Emulators now boot headless (`-no-window`), so the user no longer sees an emulator window or error dialog when a boot fails. A missing system image, a locked AVD or missing KVM now leaves only the `started` event and no other sign of the failure. Most of the fix still applies, with three adjustments. (1) The new avd.stop already emits a `stopped` event for explicit stops, so the reaper thread only needs to report unexpected exits (failed within about 10 s, stopped later) and must not emit a second event for an avd.stop kill. (2) Emulators stopped through avd.stop still become zombies, because `emu kill` ends the process and no code anywhere in the crates calls wait on it or ignores SIGCHLD. Keeping and waiting on the Child, as the fix already says, removes these zombies too. (3) The new avd.stop refuses with `avd.not_running` when the AVD has no running serial. avd.boot should refuse in the same way (for example `avd.already_running`) when the AVD already has one.

**Also at:** `crates/relay-core/src/handlers/device.rs:344`

#### RA-350 · find_avdmanager picks the last cmdline-tools directory in string order, so 9.0 wins over 19.0

`crates/relay-core/src/handlers/device.rs:465` · **low** · Bug · confirmed · effort S

**Problem.** When there is no `cmdline-tools/latest`, the candidates `cmdline-tools/*/bin/avdmanager` are sorted as paths and the last one is taken with `pop()` (lines 441-444). `latest_build_tool` uses the same `.max()` over paths (lines 1957-1964). cmdline-tools versions include 9.0 and 10.0 through 19.0, and '9.0' sorts after '19.0'.

**Impact.** With several versioned cmdline-tools installed and no `latest`, avd.create and avd.catalog run the oldest avdmanager, which may not recognize newer system-image packages ('Package path is not valid').

**Fix.** Compare parsed numeric version components, falling back to path order for names that are not numeric.

**Verifier note.** The related latest_build_tool (device.rs:1957-1964) is effectively unaffected. build-tools versions all have two-digit majors (17.x-36.x), so lexical order matches numeric order within the same digit count; at most an '-rcN' suffix could misorder. Fix by comparing parsed numeric version components in find_avdmanager.

**Also at:** `crates/relay-core/src/handlers/device.rs:1957`

#### RA-351 · `adb devices -l` parsing turns the 'no permissions ...' state into 'no'

#### RA-352 · The `forge-android/gradlew` fallback runs a nested wrapper from the repo root, where Gradle finds no settings file

`crates/relay-core/src/handlers/device.rs:1081` · **low** · Bug · confirmed · effort S

**Problem.** `gradle_wrapper` returns `./forge-android/gradlew` when the root has no wrapper (lines 1059-1064). But `stream_command` runs every command with `.current_dir(root)` (line 1824) and nothing passes `-p forge-android`. Gradle locates the build from the working directory, not from where the wrapper lives. The user's own Avex repo has a root `gradlew` shim that does `cd "$APP_HOME/forge-android" && exec ./gradlew "$@"` because tools 'look for ./gradlew at the tree root', so this fallback is never reached there.

**Impact.** Any project that relies on the fallback gets device.run/device.build failures ('does not contain a Gradle build' or task not found). The branch is a project-specific special case inside a general handler, and it is effectively dead for the project it was written for.

**Fix.** Drop the hard-coded subproject, since the configured run_cmd already covers it. Otherwise run the wrapper with `current_dir` set to its own directory (or pass `-p <subdir>`) and search generically for the nearest `settings.gradle(.kts)`.

**Verifier note.** The fix 'drop it, the configured run_cmd already covers it' holds only for device.run. `build_command` (1082-1094) ignores run_cmd/build_cmd and also uses `gradle_wrapper`, so device.build has no override. Better fix: return the wrapper's directory and run `<wrapper> -p <subdir>`, or `cd <subdir> &&` before it. Otherwise look generically for the nearest settings.gradle(.kts) instead of the literal `forge-android`. Also see the related site at 1089.

**Also at:** `crates/relay-core/src/handlers/device.rs:1824`, `apps/relay-native/src/agent_menu.rs:87`

#### RA-353 · keytool failures are reported from stderr, which holds only its progress line; the real error is on stdout

`crates/relay-core/src/handlers/device.rs:1417` · **low** · Error handling · confirmed · effort S

I checked the local JDK keytool: a runtime failure prints `keytool error: java.io.FileNotFoundException: ...` on stdout and exits 1, while stderr contains only 'Generating 2048-bit RSA key pair and self-signed certificate (SHA384withRSA) ... for: CN=x'.

**Impact.** When signing.create fails, the user sees 'Generating 4096-bit RSA key pair and self-signed certificate (SHA384withRSA) with a validity of 10000 days ...' as the error. It reads like progress and hides the actual cause.

**Fix.** Report stdout (the `keytool error:` line) and fall back to stderr, or join both trimmed outputs.

#### RA-354 · Native crashes never raise run.crash because only Java's 'FATAL EXCEPTION' is matched

`crates/relay-core/src/handlers/device.rs:1801` · **low** · Bug · confirmed · effort S

**Problem.** `if !crash_reported && line.contains("FATAL EXCEPTION") { ... report_crash(...) }` (lines 1780-1783). A native crash (SIGSEGV or SIGABRT in C/C++, the NDK or a game engine) logs `F libc: Fatal signal 11 (SIGSEGV) ... pid N (pkg)` from the app's own pid, so that line is in the `--pid` stream. The tombstone comes from crash_dump, which has a different pid and is filtered out.

**Impact.** Native crashes produce no run.crash event and no 'App crashed on device' notification. Combined with the pid-bound stream, the run just stays in 'running'.

**Fix.** Also match libc's `Fatal signal` and `Abort message` lines, and on any match mark the run as crashed.

**Verifier note.** Match 'Fatal signal' (and optionally 'Abort message') in addition to FATAL EXCEPTION. Ending the run on a crash belongs to #9's fix, not this one.

**Also at:** `crates/relay-core/src/handlers/device.rs:2200`

#### RA-355 · Run commands get ` 2>&1` appended as text while the child's stderr goes to /dev/null, so a chained run_cmd loses Gradle's errors

`crates/relay-core/src/handlers/device.rs:1846` · **low** · Bug · confirmed · effort S

**Problem.** The spawn uses `.args(["-lc", &format!("{command} 2>&1")])` together with `.stderr(Stdio::null())` (lines 1825-1828). The redirection applies only to the last simple command. For `./gradlew installDebug && adb shell am start ...`, only `adb` gets `2>&1`; with a trailing `# comment` the redirection is swallowed entirely.

**Impact.** For a configured run_cmd that chains commands, Gradle's stderr is thrown away, and that is where 'FAILURE: Build failed...' and compiler errors go. The run log just ends with 'device.build_failed: build or install command failed'.

**Fix.** Give the child's stderr the same OS pipe as stdout (duplicate the pipe's file descriptor) and drop the text suffix, or wrap the command for fish as `begin\n{command}\nend 2>&1`.

**Verifier note.** Only configured run_cmd values are affected, not the default Gradle command. The simplest fix: pass the same pipe as stderr (e.g. os_pipe or dup of the stdout fd) and drop the text suffix, or wrap the command as `begin\n{command}\nend 2>&1`.

**Also at:** `crates/relay-core/src/handlers/device.rs:1828`

#### RA-356 · adb shell command lines are built from an unvalidated applicationId read from the worktree's output-metadata.json

`crates/relay-core/src/handlers/device.rs:2067` · **low** · Security · confirmed · effort S

**Problem.** `variant_application_ids` takes `applicationId` verbatim from any `build/outputs/apk/**/output-metadata.json` found under the worktree (lines 2110-2153). It is passed as an argument to `adb -s .. shell cmd package resolve-activity ... &package` (2033-2047) and `shell pidof -s package` (2092-2093), and the derived component goes to `shell am start -W -n &component` (2062). `adb shell` joins its arguments into one string that the device's `sh -c` parses, so `;`, `$()` and similar are interpreted on the device.

**Impact.** A worktree file, for example one an agent wrote in its own checkout, containing `"applicationId": "x; pm uninstall com.other"` runs that command as the device `shell` user when the user runs that worktree. This happens even with a custom run_cmd that never runs the agent's Gradle (the pidof path at 1709-1724). The impact is limited because a default run already executes the worktree's build scripts on the host, but this is exactly the `adb shell` injection pattern.

**Fix.** Before use, validate the applicationId and component against the Java package grammar (`^[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9_]*(\.[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9_]*)+$`, plus `/[A-Za-z0-9_.$]+` for the component), or shell-quote each argument.

**Verifier note.** The `am start -n <component>` sink is less direct. The component must be a line of the device's own resolve-activity output that starts with `<package>/`, so the injection happens at resolve-activity and pidof, not at am start. The fix is right: validate against the Java package grammar before any adb call.

**Also at:** `crates/relay-core/src/handlers/device.rs:2062`, `crates/relay-core/src/handlers/device.rs:2093`, `crates/relay-core/src/handlers/device.rs:2118`

#### RA-357 · device.release reports other holders' lapsed leases as released by the caller

`crates/relay-core/src/handlers/device_lease.rs:55` · **low** · Bug · confirmed · effort S

**Problem.** `let released = leases.release_where(|lease| ...)`, and `release_where` starts with `let mut gone = expire(&mut map);` (device_lease.rs:234), which returns every lapsed lease of any holder. All of `released` then goes into `ReleaseOut { released: views }`.

**Impact.** Trigger: agent A calls device.release for its phone. The response also lists session B's lapsed claim on another device as released, which an agent reading the result can misattribute to itself.

**Fix.** Have release_where return (expired, selected) separately. Emit events for both, but return only the selected leases.

#### RA-358 · Release events for leases pruned during a refused request are discarded with the rolled-back transaction

`crates/relay-core/src/handlers/device_lease.rs:113` · **low** · Error handling · confirmed · effort S

**Problem.** `acquire` and `check` remove pruned or expired leases from the in-memory map and queue their events on ctx (`for gone in released { ctx.emit(RELEASED, gone.event()); }`) before returning `device.busy`. On an ordinary handler error the engine rolls back and never sends ctx's queued events (engine.rs:1073-1095). guardrail `gate` returns the error without `commit_error` (guardrail.rs:531-533), and so does RunOp (handlers/device.rs:150). Conversely, a lease taken before a later failure in the same request (use_grants in gate, or the commit in RunOp) stays in memory and its ACQUIRED event is dropped.

**Impact.** Leases dropped while refusing someone else are released silently, so agents waiting on device.lease.released for those devices are not woken.

**Fix.** Emit lease releases with `engine.emit_system` at the moment of removal, as release_run and release_session already do, independent of the request's outcome.

**Verifier note.** Emit releases through engine.emit_system at the moment of removal, as release_run and release_session do. A related, more serious case is out of this finding's scope: in RunOp, if the transaction commit fails after acquire, the Kind::Run lease and its device_runs entry stay and never prune, because live_runs still contains the id.

**Also at:** `crates/relay-core/src/engine.rs:1073`, `crates/relay-core/src/handlers/guardrail.rs:532`, `crates/relay-core/src/handlers/device_lease.rs:122`

#### RA-359 · file.read truncation can split a UTF-8 character, which turns a text file into base64

`crates/relay-core/src/handlers/file.rs:57` · **low** · Bug · confirmed · effort S

**Problem.** The bytes are cut to exactly `limit` (L54-55), and then `String::from_utf8(bytes.clone())` (L57) fails if the cut falls inside a multi-byte character, so the whole result is returned as `bytes_b64`. The clone also copies up to 32 MiB.

**Impact.** Agents reading large non-ASCII text files with max_bytes get base64 they cannot use, and every read does a needless allocation.

**Fix.** When truncated, back off to `Utf8Error::valid_up_to()` if `error_len()` is None. Use from_utf8(bytes) and recover the buffer with into_bytes() on error.

**Verifier note.** When truncated and the error's error_len() is None (an incomplete trailing sequence), truncate to utf8_error().valid_up_to() and keep the text. Use String::from_utf8(bytes) and recover the buffer with FromUtf8Error::into_bytes() to avoid the clone.

#### RA-360 · file.write replaces a symlinked file with a regular file and leaks temp files on failure

`crates/relay-core/src/handlers/file.rs:115` · **low** · Bug · confirmed · effort S

**Problem.** The temp file is written to `root/.relay/tmp/<uuid>.tmp` (L107-110) and then `fs::rename(&temp, &path)` (L115). rename replaces the directory entry, so when `path` is a symlink inside the worktree (which safe_join accepts) the link becomes a regular file and its target is not updated. Any error after L110 (set_permissions, rename, including EXDEV when the target directory is another mount) returns with `?` and leaves the temp file behind.

**Impact.** Saving a symlinked file in the editor (for example a doc that is a symlink to a shared file) silently breaks the link, leaves the real file stale and shows a typechange in git. Failed saves accumulate stray temp files.

**Fix.** Resolve the final symlink first (canonicalize when symlink_metadata says link). Create the temp next to the real target (tempfile::NamedTempFile::new_in(parent) then persist), and remove it on every error path.

**Verifier note.** Rare edge case (symlinked files edited through Relay) with no content lost, so low rather than medium. Fix: when symlink_metadata(path) reports a link, resolve it with canonicalize (already proven inside the root), write the temp file next to the resolved target and rename onto that. Remove the temp file on every error path.

**Also at:** `crates/relay-core/src/handlers/file.rs:107`, `crates/relay-core/src/handlers/file.rs:111`

<a id="ra-361"></a>

#### RA-361 · file.delete moves the file before the transaction commits; a failed commit rolls back the AUTOINCREMENT id, and the next delete reuses the trash slot

`crates/relay-core/src/handlers/file.rs:232` · **low** · Data loss · confirmed · effort S

**Problem.** The handler inserts the file_trash row and takes `last_insert_rowid()` as N (225-229), then calls `fs::rename(&path, &trash)` into `.relay/trash/N/payload` (230-232), all before the pipeline appends the audit row and commits. If the append or commit fails (SQLITE_FULL or an I/O error), the transaction rolls back, sqlite_sequence included, so the next file.delete in that worktree is assigned the same N and renames onto the orphaned payload.

**Impact.** Rare (it needs a failed commit, for example a full disk, which is exactly when users delete files). The orphaned file, whose only copy is the trash payload, is silently replaced by the next deleted file. If the payload is a directory, every later file.delete in that worktree fails until someone cleans the directory by hand.

**Fix.** Move the file into a uuid-named trash directory and record that path, or perform the rename in after_commit, staging the move first and renaming it back on failure.

**Verifier note.** The rename is at file.rs:232 and the failure windows are file.rs:233 and engine.rs:1015-1024. There is a more likely trigger than a failed commit. Any time the store's sequence falls behind the on-disk .relay/trash directories (a fresh store or a copied-back backup, while the worktrees are kept), ids are reused against existing trash/N/payload directories, with the same silent overwrite or permanent EISDIR jam. Fix: create the slot with fs::create_dir rather than create_dir_all, so an existing directory is refused, or name it with a uuid. Either way, never rename onto an existing payload.

**Also at:** `crates/relay-core/src/handlers/file.rs:225`

<a id="ra-362"></a>

#### RA-362 · file.restore writes without any guardrail check and trusts the stored root

`crates/relay-core/src/handlers/file.rs:248` · **low** · Security · confirmed · effort S

**Problem.** Restore (L238-252) takes root from the file_trash row (L245), never calls root_verify or guardrail::enforce, and renames the payload into place (L248). Every other file mutation calls guardrail::enforce, either directly or through guard_path_mutation.

**Impact.** A bus_writes session can put back any trashed file, including one at a protected path and in a checkout that is not its own (for example something the user deleted from the primary checkout).

**Fix.** Re-verify the root, and run guardrail::enforce (protected path plus ownership) for the restored path.

**Verifier note.** The claim that it can restore into 'a checkout that is not its own' is not a separate hole. Under D111 every file.* op already accepts any worktree of the project, including `worktree: "@project"`. root_verify only checks that the path is a worktree of this project, and no op checks which session owns a worktree. The real gap is the missing protected-path and shape-gate check on the restored path. Fix: run guardrail::enforce(GateKind::Write, original_path, content of the payload) before the rename. Optionally re-run root_verify on the stored root.

<a id="ra-363"></a>

#### RA-363 · file.restore_head runs `git checkout` under the store lock without a timeout

`crates/relay-core/src/handlers/file.rs:256` · **low** · Invariant · confirmed · effort S

**Problem.** `crate::worktree::git_mutate(&root, &["checkout", "--", &p.path])` goes to worktree.rs:26-33 `Command::new("git")...output()`, with no proc::output_with_timeout, inside `e.register::<RestoreHead>`. A checkout runs smudge filters (LFS) and post-checkout hooks.

**Impact.** Breaks the CLAUDE.md rule that every handler subprocess goes through output_with_timeout. A slow or hung filter or hook freezes the whole bus while the user restores one file.

**Fix.** Register it staged: run git in prepare through proc::output_with_timeout, and keep finish to the event emission.

**Verifier note.** Severity drops to low because no client flow calls this op today, so it is a latent invariant breach rather than a freeze in normal use. Fix: register it unlocked or staged, run git through proc::output_with_timeout with nothing held, and only emit file.changed under the lock. git_mutate itself has no timeout, so audit its other locked callers as well.

**Also at:** `crates/relay-core/src/worktree.rs:26`, `crates/relay-core/src/worktree.rs:36`

<a id="ra-364"></a>

#### RA-364 · restore_head restores from the index rather than HEAD, treats the name as a pathspec, and validates after git runs

`crates/relay-core/src/handlers/file.rs:256` · **low** · Bug · confirmed · effort S

**Problem.** `git checkout -- <path>` copies the index version, so a staged change survives "restore head". The argument is a pathspec: glob characters in real file names (e.g. `[id].tsx` routes), `.` (allowed by rel()) and pathspec magic widen the revert. safe_join is called at L258, after git has already run.

**Impact.** The one-click answer to a guardrail.violation leaves a staged destructive change in place. A file name containing glob characters can also revert uncommitted work in sibling files.

**Fix.** Run `git restore --source=HEAD --staged --worktree -- :(literal)<normalized path>` after safe_join, and refuse `.` or empty paths.

**Verifier note.** The symlink and ordering point is cosmetic, since git rejects paths beyond a symlink. The real issues are the source (index instead of HEAD) and the pathspec interpretation, including `.`. Fix: validate with safe_join first, reject empty and `.`, and run `git restore --source=HEAD --staged --worktree -- :(literal)<path>` through proc::output_with_timeout off the lock.

**Also at:** `crates/relay-core/src/handlers/file.rs:258`

<a id="ra-365"></a>

#### RA-365 · file.import does all of its copying and whole-file reads under the store lock, is not atomic, and cannot be replayed after a hold

`crates/relay-core/src/handlers/file.rs:293` · **low** · Invariant · confirmed · effort M

**Problem.** `e.register::<Import>` is locked. For each source, guard_path_mutation reads the source fully (L286, L578), then the recursive `copy(source, &dest)` (L293, L612-627) copies whole trees. Sources are processed one at a time, so an error, refusal or user-bypass hold on source N leaves sources 1..N-1 on disk while the transaction rolls back (or commits only the hold). Replaying a confirmed hold reruns the whole op, which then fails at `dest.exists()` (L287) for the files already copied. Nothing refuses a source directory that contains the destination, so that copy recurses into its own output until path limits.

**Impact.** Dragging a large folder in freezes every bus request for the length of the copy. Failed or held imports leave partial copies behind and cannot complete through confirmation.

**Fix.** Stage the op: check every destination and gate first, copy without the lock into a temp dir inside the worktree, then rename the results in. Refuse sources that are ancestors of the destination, and drop the content read for directory sources.

**Verifier note.** Severity drops to low because the op has no caller in any client; only a manual `relay q file.import` reaches it. The 'drop the content read for directory sources' part is moot, since read_to_string on a directory errors immediately and yields an empty string. Fix as proposed (validate every destination and gate first, copy off the lock, refuse a source that is an ancestor of the destination), or remove the op until a client needs it.

**Also at:** `crates/relay-core/src/handlers/file.rs:286`, `crates/relay-core/src/handlers/file.rs:612`

<a id="ra-366"></a>

#### RA-366 · file.search fails entirely on the first unreadable or vanished directory

`crates/relay-core/src/handlers/file.rs:318` · **low** · Error handling · confirmed · effort S

**Problem.** Inside the walk: `fs::read_dir(&dir).map_err(|e| io_err("file.search_failed", &dir, e))?` (317-318), whereas unreadable files are skipped (`if read.is_err() { continue; }`, 334-339); skip_dir excludes only .git/.relay/node_modules/target.

**Impact.** A root-owned docker volume directory, a permission-restricted folder, or a build/ or dist/ directory deleted mid-walk by a concurrent build makes every project search from the editor return `file.search_failed` instead of results.

**Fix.** Skip directories whose read_dir fails (optionally report how many were skipped).

**Verifier note.** The error kind is unavailable, so the editor shows a failure rather than an empty result. Fix: on a read_dir error, `continue` and optionally count the skipped directories in the result.

<a id="ra-367"></a>

#### RA-367 · file.search glob uses the guardrail matcher, so `*.rs` matches only root-level files

`crates/relay-core/src/handlers/file.rs:330` · **low** · Bug · confirmed · effort S

**Problem.** `crate::guardrail::path_matches(glob, relp)`: in that matcher `*` stays within one path segment (guardrail.rs:1158-1160).

**Impact.** Agents passing ripgrep-style globs get silently incomplete results with no error.

**Fix.** Match the basename when the glob contains no `/`, or use globset with ripgrep semantics.

**Verifier note.** Workaround: `**/*.rs` matches files at depth. A pattern with no `/` also matches a whole directory subtree through the prefix rule (`src` matches everything under src/), which ripgrep's glob does not do. Fix: when the glob has no `/`, match it against the basename, and document the semantics in the op schema.

<a id="ra-368"></a>

#### RA-368 · file.tree fails entirely when one entry vanishes between read_dir and stat

`crates/relay-core/src/handlers/file.rs:522` · **low** · Error handling · confirmed · effort S

**Problem.** `.map(|e| entry(root, &e.path(), ...)).collect::<Result<Vec<_>, _>>()?` together with entry's `fs::symlink_metadata(path).map_err(...)?` (L533).

**Impact.** While agents create and delete temp files, the Code page's tree refresh (rerun on every invalidation) fails intermittently with file.stat_failed.

**Fix.** Skip entries whose stat returns NotFound.

**Verifier note.** There is also a deterministic trigger besides the race: a subdirectory that cannot be read (for example a root-owned directory created by a Docker bind mount) fails read_dir with EACCES. Any file.tree with depth > 1 then errors permanently, not intermittently. Fix: skip entries whose stat fails with NotFound, and for unreadable subdirectories return the directory entry with children: None instead of failing the whole tree.

#### RA-369 · Inconsistent error kinds: io_err maps every filesystem error to `unavailable`, gix_err maps bad revisions to `unavailable`

`crates/relay-core/src/handlers/file.rs:659` · **low** · Error handling · confirmed · effort S

**Problem.** io_err always returns `BusError::unavailable(code, ...)` regardless of io::ErrorKind (658-660), so file.read/move/rename/delete of a missing path return kind=unavailable code=file.not_found (via safe_join 498), while file.tree returns kind=not_found for the same code (25-28). gix_err (git.rs:1441-1443) maps every gix error to unavailable, so git.log {branch:'nope'} / git.show {sha:'bad'} give unavailable `git.revision` (258-261, 278-280), while git.branch.create's unknown start point is invalid (362-364) and branch.switch's is not_found (1342).

**Impact.** error.rs:1 tells agents to react to kind and code; a typo'd path or revision reads as an infrastructure outage (CLI exit 4, retry later) instead of a caller mistake (exit 1), so MCP agents retry instead of fixing the argument.

**Fix.** Map io::ErrorKind::NotFound to not_found, AlreadyExists to conflict, PermissionDenied to refused; map gix rev-parse failures to not_found/invalid.

**Verifier note.** No in-repo client (native, CLI, remote) branches on these kinds, so the impact is limited to inconsistent contract signals and exit codes for agents, not a concrete malfunction. The claim that MCP agents retry is speculative. Fix as proposed: match on io::ErrorKind in io_err, and map rev_parse failures to not_found or invalid.

`crates/relay-core/src/handlers/git.rs:156` · **low** · Performance · confirmed · effort S

**Problem.** `disk_mb: worktree::dir_size(path)` walks the whole checkout, including target/, build/, node_modules/.cache and the rest. `build_mb: Some(worktree::build_size(path))` then walks BUILD_DIRS again (155-156).

**Impact.** For worktrees with a multi-GB target/ (the SPEC §8 '73GB problem'), the dominant part of each worktree.disk call is done twice.

**Fix.** Do one walk that also attributes the bytes under BUILD_DIRS to build_mb.

**Verifier note.** Better framing: duplication plus perf. handlers/app.rs:233-258 (`dir_usage`) already does a single walk that attributes build bytes, so a one-pass implementation exists. Its definition of 'build' has drifted from BUILD_DIRS: it counts any nested `target`/`build`/`.gradle` anywhere and leaves out `node_modules/.cache` and `dist`. As a result, `app.resources` and `worktree.disk` report different build_mb for the same worktree. Fix: one shared single-pass, multi-threaded walker in worktree.rs that uses BUILD_DIRS, used by both.

<a id="ra-372"></a>

#### RA-372 · Unlocked and prepare-phase subprocesses still bypass proc::output_with_timeout

`crates/relay-core/src/handlers/git.rs:617` · **low** · Invariant · confirmed · effort S

**Problem.** - git.push's prepare runs `worktree::git_mutate(&root, &args)` (git.rs:617), which is a plain `.output()` (worktree.rs:27). It also lacks GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0, which fetch_remote does set (git.rs:943).
- github.status runs `Command::new(gh).args(["api","user",…]).output()` (github.rs:45).
- github.repo.list runs `gh api --paginate …` with `.output()` (github.rs:68-70).
- skill.install's prepare runs `git clone --depth 1` with `.output()` (github.rs:106-109).
- avd.catalog runs `avdmanager list device -c` with `.output()` (device.rs:315).
- avd.list runs `emulator -list-avds` (device.rs:478).
- The normal (unlocked) git.commit prepare runs the user's pre-commit hook via run_user_pre_commit, `.output()` with no deadline (hooks.rs:210-213).
None of these hold the store lock on their normal path. CLAUDE.md still requires every handler subprocess to go through output_with_timeout.

**Impact.** Some of these calls can block forever: a push waiting for credentials (git prompts on the engine's controlling terminal when relay serve was started from a shell), or a gh/git call on a stalled network. When that happens, the blocking-pool thread is leaked and the client waits until its own timeout, while the push may still complete later without anyone seeing it. If any of these ops is ever invoked nested via invoke_registered, the hang moves under the lock.

**Fix.** Run all of them through proc::output_with_timeout with suitable deadlines, and set GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0 / GH_PROMPT_DISABLED=1.

**Verifier note.** A push prompt can hang only when the engine has a controlling tty. `.output()` already gives the child a null stdin, but git opens /dev/tty for credentials unless GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0 is set. Note also that github::connect (`gh auth login --web`, `.status()`) blocks without a deadline, apparently on purpose; at least give it a generous one.

#### RA-373 · git.branch.clean_merged stops at the first failed delete and does not report, audit or announce the branches it already deleted

`crates/relay-core/src/handlers/git.rs:712` · **low** · Error handling · confirmed · effort S

**Problem.** The loop `for branch in &candidates { git_mutate(.."branch","-d",branch).map_err(..)?; }` returns on the first failure. The transaction rolls back, changed() is never emitted, and the response carries only the error.

**Impact.** Branches 1..k-1 are already gone, but the caller is told the op failed. The audit trail has no record of those deletions, and the UI is not told to refresh.

**Fix.** Attempt every candidate and collect per-branch outcomes. Return them, as branch_cleanup does with its rows, and emit git.changed if anything was deleted.

**Verifier note.** Same fix as proposed: try every candidate, return deleted and failed lists, and emit changed() if anything was deleted. Alternatively use `git branch -D` only after the engine's own base-merged check, since that is the check the op is meant to apply.

#### RA-376 · Concurrent worktree/session creations run parallel `git fetch --all --prune` in one repository; one fails on ref locks and its launch is aborted

`crates/relay-core/src/handlers/git.rs:942` · **low** · Concurrency · confirmed · effort S

**Problem.** refresh_new_worktree (969-974) calls fetch_remote (`git fetch --all --prune`, 938-960) for every new branch. It is reached from WorktreeCreate (113-114) and session.create's prepare (session.rs:866); git.fetch calls fetch_remote too (583). These prepare phases now run concurrently (they are off the store mutex), and nothing serializes fetches per repository. Verified: two concurrent `git fetch --all --prune` into one clone while the remote had new commits; in 5 of 5 rounds one exited 1 with "cannot lock ref 'refs/remotes/origin/main': is at X but expected Y". Any fetch error is a refusal by design ('A failed fetch must never silently launch from stale refs').

**Impact.** Starting two agents at nearly the same time while origin has new commits makes one launch fail with git.fetch_failed. Ways this happens: two clicks, desktop plus phone, or pressing Fetch during a launch.

**Fix.** Serialize fetches per repository with a mutex keyed by the common dir. A caller that arrives while a fetch is in flight waits and reuses its result, or treats a fetch completed within the last few seconds as fresh.

**Verifier note.** Downgraded to low: rare trigger, and the failure is retryable with no data harm. The suggested fix (a per-common-dir mutex, plus reusing a fetch that completed seconds ago) is fine. Related problem outside this finding: because task.dispatch runs session.create's prepare under the held transaction (engine.rs:325-341), a dispatch that creates a session runs the network fetch (up to 20 s) and the worktree checkout while holding the store mutex. That freezes the bus, which is a CLAUDE.md invariant issue worth its own finding.

**Also at:** `crates/relay-core/src/handlers/git.rs:969`, `crates/relay-core/src/handlers/session.rs:866`, `crates/relay-core/src/handlers/git.rs:583`
