#### RA-377 · git.branch.switch classifies failures by git's English stderr, so it breaks under a non-English locale

`crates/relay-core/src/handlers/git.rs:1349` · **low** · Bug · confirmed · effort S

**Problem.** run_switch sets only GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT (git.rs:1347-1349). It classifies failures by matching English text: "is already checked out at ", "is already used by worktree at ", "local changes to the following files would be overwritten" and "untracked working tree files would be overwritten" (1361-1384). git translates these messages through gettext; for example, /usr/share/locale/fr/LC_MESSAGES/git.mo is installed on this machine. device.rs:1937 and 1944 already force LC_ALL=C for the same reason.

**Impact.** Under a non-English locale, switching to a branch held by another worktree, or a switch that would overwrite changes, returns the generic git.branch_switch_failed with translated stderr. The user loses the git.branch_checked_out and git.checkout_conflict codes and their guidance. git_branch_switch.rs:92 and :146 fail on such a machine.

**Fix.** Add `.env("LC_ALL", "C").env("LANGUAGE", "C")` to the run_switch command, and to any other git call whose stderr is parsed.

**Verifier note.** No correctness or safety impact: git refuses and changes nothing on every one of these paths. Only the error code and the guidance text are lost. Set LC_ALL=C (or LANGUAGE=C plus LC_MESSAGES=C) on this command. Today it is the only git stderr-text classifier in relay-core.

#### RA-381 · Import numbers task positions and module ord from 0 regardless of existing rows, and drops v3 note tags without a warning

`crates/relay-core/src/handlers/import_v3.rs:197` · **low** · Bug · confirmed · effort S

**Problem.** `let pos = positions.entry(col_s).or_insert(0);` (193-199) and module ord `i as i64` (173-174) start at 0, while task.rs:452-454 next_position appends after MAX(position). v3 notes carry `tags` (fixture tests/store.rs:113-114) that the notes loop (283-296) never reads or warns about. D14 says priorities 'carry over as-is' but map_priority (49-56) maps unknown values to medium.

**Impact.** Importing into a project that already has tasks/modules interleaves imported items with existing ones in board and module order (ties broken by id); v3 note tags are lost silently.

**Fix.** Seed each column counter from next_position and modules from MAX(ord)+1; append tags to the note body or emit a warning; correct D14.

**Verifier note.** The trigger is rare. The only UI caller (onboarding.rs:532) imports into the project that was just created by project.add or project.clone, so it is empty. Only a CLI or MCP import into a populated project hits the ordering issue (the op is UserOnly). Tag loss is not established: the only fixture has `"tags": []`, and I could not confirm that v3 ever stored non-empty tags. The D14 claim is weak: v3's priority domain is low/medium/high/urgent, which map_priority carries over as-is, and only out-of-domain values fall back to medium.

**Also at:** `crates/relay-core/src/handlers/task.rs:452`, `crates/relay-core/tests/store.rs:113`, `docs/engine/DECISIONS.md:39`

<a id="ra-382"></a>

#### RA-382 · v3 import copies attachment files under the store mutex and before commit; a later failure leaves orphan files

`crates/relay-core/src/handlers/import_v3.rs:263` · **low** · Invariant · confirmed · effort M

**Problem.** ImportV3 is registered with plain e.register (app.rs:59); import() does `std::fs::create_dir_all(&dest_dir)` / `std::fs::copy(&src, &dest)` for each attachment inside the task loop (259-263), plus notes.json/sessions.json reads and canonicalize calls, all inside the request transaction.

**Impact.** Importing a v3 store with many or large attachments (screenshots, recordings) freezes every other bus request for the copy duration (CLAUDE.md: slow work belongs in register_staged). If anything fails afterwards (a bad name, I/O error, non-UTF-8 notes.json at 280) the DB rolls back but copied files stay under attachments/<id>/, and because the rollback also rewinds AUTOINCREMENT, the next real task with that id inherits a directory of foreign files.

**Fix.** register_staged: prepare reads the v3 DB and copies into a staging dir with nothing locked; finish inserts the rows; on finish error delete the staged files.

**Verifier note.** The 'next task inherits foreign files' impact is overstated. Attachments are listed from the DB (task.rs:253-255), and task.attach writes `{id}-{name}` (task.rs:522), so the leftover files are invisible orphaned disk usage, not attachments that show up. While reading this I found a worse problem on the same lines: import_v3.rs:262 does `dest_dir.join(&name)` with the raw v3 original_name and no safe_name() check (compare task.rs:489-502). An absolute name or one containing `../` writes outside attachments/<id>/, and two attachments with the same name on one task overwrite each other. Fix: sanitise the name the way task.rs does (safe_name plus an id prefix). Copy in a staged prepare phase (register_staged), or at least delete the copied files if the handler returns an error.

**Also at:** `crates/relay-core/src/handlers/app.rs:59`, `crates/relay-core/src/handlers/import_v3.rs:280`

<a id="ra-383"></a>

#### RA-383 · integration.request passes caller-supplied branch names to `git merge` with no `--`, so a ref named like an option changes how the merge runs

`crates/relay-core/src/handlers/integration.rs:124` · **low** · Security · confirmed · effort S

**Problem.** Caller-supplied branches are only checked to resolve: `repo.rev_parse_single(branch.as_str())` (integration.rs:29). They are then sorted and passed as-is: `std::iter::once("merge").chain(["--no-ff", "--no-edit"]).chain(integration.branches.iter().map(String::as_str))` (integration.rs:124-127). A ref with a leading dash can be created. In a scratch repo, `git update-ref refs/heads/-Xtheirs HEAD` succeeded, and `git merge --no-ff --no-edit -Xtheirs main` parsed `-Xtheirs` as a strategy option rather than a commit. `git merge ... -- main` works as a separator. integration.request is in the builder role's default allowlist (handlers/settings.rs:36). Because '-' sorts before letters, such a ref always lands first in the argument list. Not verified: that gix rev_parse_single resolves the short name `-Xtheirs`.

**Impact.** A builder agent creates `refs/heads/-Xours` in the shared repo and requests an integration with it plus two real branches. The merge then silently resolves every conflict in favour of the integration base, and the run reports success. With `-s<name>` git instead looks for a `git-merge-<name>` program. Other branch names can inject further merge options. Agents already control the branch contents, so the added power is small, but the integration result no longer means what it says.

**Fix.** Reject branch names that start with '-' in integration.request (or validate them with `git check-ref-format --branch`), and add `"--"` before the branch list in merge_args.

**Verifier note.** `-sours` is a stronger variant than `-Xours`. The merge then keeps the base tree entirely and still reports success, so the integration/build tests none of the branches' changes. With an unknown `-s<name>`, git looks for a `git-merge-<name>` program. That gives no extra power, because the agent already runs code as the same user. The impact is limited to a misleading integration result, so low severity is right. Fix: reject names starting with '-' (or run check-ref-format --branch) and insert "--" before the branch list. Note that git merge's `--` handling is recent: older git versions treated `--` as the end of options only in some forms, so the name validation is the more robust half.

**Also at:** `crates/relay-core/src/handlers/integration.rs:29`, `crates/relay-core/src/handlers/settings.rs:36`

<a id="ra-384"></a>

#### RA-384 · set_state checks 'discarded' under one lock and writes unconditionally under another, so a discard can be overwritten

`crates/relay-core/src/handlers/integration.rs:268` · **low** · Concurrency · confirmed · effort S

**Problem.** set_state takes the store lock three times: `if get(&conn, id)?.state == IntegrationState::Discarded { return Ok(()); }` (266-271), a separate SELECT project_id (274-282), then system_write with `UPDATE integrations SET state=?1, ... WHERE id=?7` (283-284) and no state guard. integration.discard (58-66) can commit between the first lock and the write.

**Impact.** A discard that lands while a run transitions (most likely as it finishes; discard holds the lock for the whole worktree removal, so a set_state already past its check waits and then writes) flips the row back to passed/failed with a worktree path that no longer exists, inserts a spurious 'Integration passed' notification, and device.run will accept it as a passed integration.

**Fix.** Do the check and the write in the one system_write transaction (`... WHERE id=?7 AND state!='discarded'`, skip events/notification when 0 rows changed), read project_id there too (two fewer lock round trips per transition), and return a discarded signal so run() stops.

**Verifier note.** Consequence correction: device.run with that integration_id will not succeed — resolve_run_root canonicalizes the removed worktree path (device.rs:1016-1017) and fails with device.worktree; the visible effects are a resurrected passed/failed row, a spurious notification, and (if overwritten to a live state like building) integrations_live blocking project.remove. Fix as proposed: `... WHERE id=?7 AND state!='discarded'` in the single system_write, skipping events when 0 rows change.

**Also at:** `crates/relay-core/src/handlers/integration.rs:58`, `crates/relay-core/src/handlers/device.rs:1004`, `crates/relay-core/src/handlers/integration.rs:284`, `crates/relay-core/src/handlers/integration.rs:62`, `crates/relay-core/src/handlers/integration.rs:234`, `crates/relay-core/src/handlers/workspace.rs:387`

**Merged duplicates:** lens-concurrency#17, lens-sqlite#21

<a id="ra-385"></a>

#### RA-385 · notes.append has no size cap; the standing note grows without bound and is injected into every brief, including Codex argv

`crates/relay-core/src/handlers/notes.rs:477` · **low** · Bug · confirmed · effort S

**Problem.** For an explicit note_id or the standing note, Append only checks `text.is_empty()` (466) and then writes `format!("{}{separator}{text}", before.body)` (477). The 500-character cap and the timestamp/session/task stamp apply only to the `target: suggestions` arm (438-455). `(Some(id), None, "standing") if p.target.is_none() => (id, p.text)` (415) accepts the suggestions note's id too. notes.append is in all three role allowlists (settings.rs:36-38). awareness.rs:285-297 puts the full standing body into the compact brief, and providers.rs:81-93 passes the whole brief to Codex as a single argv string `developer_instructions=<json>`.

**Impact.** Repeated agent appends grow the standing note forever, and every later dispatch carries all of it. Once the brief passes Linux's 128 KiB per-argument limit (MAX_ARG_STRLEN), every Codex spawn or resume in the project fails with E2BIG. A builder can also append unstamped, unlimited text to the suggestions note by id, forging entries that appear to come from other sessions and tasks.

**Fix.** Cap each append and the total standing-note size (or truncate it when building the brief, with a pointer to notes.get). Route any append that targets the suggestions note through the suggestions path, whichever way it was addressed.

**Verifier note.** The root cause is wider than notes.append: the compact brief has no size bound and goes into Codex argv. state_public also embeds every assigned task's full body and changelog (awareness.rs:224-241), and the plugins section is unbounded too. A long standing note written through notes.update, or a long task body, triggers the same E2BIG without any append. The fix belongs in the brief and Codex path: cap or truncate each section of the compact brief and point to notes.get / session.bootstrap for the full text, or pass Codex the instructions by file if it supports that. Separately, route appends to the suggestions note through the suggestions arm (or refuse note_id when the note is the suggestions note). Note also that this argv is world-readable through `ps`, which awareness.rs:246-248 acknowledges for the launch assignment but not for standing notes or task bodies.

**Also at:** `crates/relay-core/src/handlers/notes.rs:415`, `crates/relay-core/src/handlers/notes.rs:438-455`, `crates/relay-core/src/awareness.rs:285-297`, `crates/relay-core/src/providers.rs:81-93`, `crates/relay-core/src/handlers/settings.rs:36-38`

<a id="ra-386"></a>

#### RA-386 · D106's 'an agent sees nothing outside its project' is not enforced: dashboard.get, audit.list/get, task.list and holds.list return every project's data to any agent

`crates/relay-core/src/handlers/notify.rs:157` · **low** · Security · confirmed · effort M

**Problem.** D106 (DECISIONS.md:491-497) and BUS.md §9.1 layer 2 (453-456) state one boundary: an agent sees the metadata of any session in its own project and nothing outside it. authorize() (guardrail.rs:328-353) only checks payload `session`/`task_id` fields, then returns Ok for every query. dashboard.get (notify.rs:157-189) iterates `SELECT id FROM projects` and returns all projects' live peers (name, branch, claimed files, task title, intent), every in_review task with its body and every open hold with details; audit.list/audit.get (handlers/audit.rs:30-47) are unscoped and return stored payloads (up to 64 KiB) of any request; task.list without project_id (task.rs:831-839), guardrail.holds.list (handlers/guardrail.rs:306-331) and notify.list are likewise global. All roles get 'all queries'.

**Impact.** An agent in project A can read project B's session metadata, task bodies, guardrail holds and, via audit.get, the full payloads other actors sent (mailbox texts, file.write contents, task bodies) - the cross-project probing D106 was written to stop. The live store is opened EXCLUSIVE, so the bus is the normal read path to this data.

**Fix.** Scope agent queries centrally: force project_id to the agent's project for project-filterable queries (task.list, audit.list, holds.list, notify.list), restrict audit.get to the agent's project, and filter dashboard.get to the agent's project or make it user_only.

**Verifier note.** The impact is overstated for this threat model. Every project belongs to the same single user. Agents already read any project's files with their provider-native Read/Bash tools, which no guardrail gates for reads. D106's stated purpose is consistent boundaries so agents do not learn to probe, not secrecy. The only data reachable solely through the bus is store-only content: task bodies, mailbox texts and request payloads in audit.get, and hold details. Hold rows do not carry the frozen envelope or token (hold_row, guardrail.rs:1305-1318). Rated low. The fix stands: scope agent queries to the caller's project centrally in authorize, or make dashboard.get and audit.get user_only.

**Also at:** `crates/relay-core/src/handlers/audit.rs:30`, `crates/relay-core/src/handlers/task.rs:831`, `crates/relay-core/src/handlers/guardrail.rs:306`, `crates/relay-core/src/guardrail.rs:350`, `docs/engine/DECISIONS.md:491`, `docs/engine/BUS.md:455`

#### RA-387 · Claim path normalization differs between overlap.flag and session.claim (and five validators exist), so equivalent claims never collide

`crates/relay-core/src/handlers/overlap.rs:82` · **low** · Bug · confirmed · effort S

**Problem.** overlap.rs relative_path rejects any non-Normal component and does not trim (L82-96). session.rs claim_path trims, rejects only absolute paths and `..`, and stores `path.display()`, keeping `./` or `//` (session.rs:223-237). gix status reports `src/a.rs`, and apply_scan compares strings (`files.contains(path)`, `a.1 != b.1`). session.claim's own collision query uses `path=?2`. Separate validators also live in file.rs:470, git.rs:780 and guardrail.rs:1135.

**Impact.** A claim recorded as `./src/a.rs` never matches a peer's change or a claim on `src/a.rs`, so collisions go unreported. Each validator applies different rules (see the protected-path finding).

**Fix.** Write one normalize_relative(path) -> String (Normal components only, `/` separators, trimmed) and use it in all five places and when storing claims.

**Verifier note.** The real bug is that claim paths are stored without normalization in session.claim/session.release (session.rs:223, used at 1263 and 1327) and that the two claim entry points apply different rules. The 'five validators' framing is overstated. file.rs:470 `rel`, git.rs:780 `validate_path` and guardrail.rs:1135 `relative_path` are near-identical guards that reject `..`/root/prefix before a filesystem join. They never key a string comparison, so normalizing them adds little. Fix: have claim_path keep only Normal components and join them with '/' (or reuse overlap::relative_path after a trim), so stored claims and overlap.flag agree. Folding the three FS guards into one helper is optional cleanup.

**Also at:** `crates/relay-core/src/handlers/session.rs:223`, `crates/relay-core/src/handlers/file.rs:470`, `crates/relay-core/src/handlers/git.rs:780`, `crates/relay-core/src/guardrail.rs:1135`, `crates/relay-core/src/handlers/session.rs:236`, `crates/relay-core/src/handlers/overlap.rs:82-96`, `crates/relay-core/src/handlers/overlap.rs:377`, `crates/relay-core/src/handlers/overlap.rs:400`, `crates/relay-core/src/handlers/session.rs:1271-1273`

#### RA-388 · One unreadable peer worktree aborts the whole overlap scan, so overlap.flag fails

`crates/relay-core/src/handlers/overlap.rs:308` · **low** · Error handling · confirmed · effort S

**Problem.** `let files = changed_files(path)?;` in collect_changes. changed_files maps any gix open or status error to an internal error (L99-110). Only a missing directory is skipped (L305).

**Impact.** A half-removed, pruned or permission-broken checkout of any session makes every overlap.flag and overlap.scan in the project fail, so no agent can flag.

**Fix.** Log and skip a checkout that fails to open or scan, and continue with the rest.

**Verifier note.** Reaching it needs a broken checkout behind a still-open session, or a transient status error, so low is right. Fix: on a changed_files error, log a warning and skip that session (or record it as unscanned), then continue.

#### RA-389 · overlap.scan/flag finish re-activates overlaps for a session that closed while the scan ran

`crates/relay-core/src/handlers/overlap.rs:317` · **low** · Concurrency · confirmed · effort S

**Problem.** collect_changes runs in prepare, from scan_targets read earlier (overlap.rs:455-464, 531-535). apply_scan, in finish, builds File/Symbol findings purely from that snapshot (overlap.rs:320-347). It runs `UPDATE overlaps SET active=0 WHERE project_id=?1` and re-inserts the findings with `ON CONFLICT(fingerprint) DO UPDATE … active=1` (overlap.rs:424-437). Only claims are re-read joined against live sessions (overlap.rs:350-356). The doc comment claims "A session that closed while the scan ran simply has no row to collide with" (overlap.rs:315-316). session.close's release_claims deactivates that session's overlaps (session.rs:250-254), and a scan prepared before the close turns them back on.

**Impact.** If a session closes while a scan or flag is running, the overlap list shows active file/symbol collisions naming the closed session until the next scan.

**Fix.** In apply_scan, drop `changes` entries whose session is no longer live, by re-reading the live session names inside the transaction. Correct the comment.

**Verifier note.** In apply_scan, filter `changes` to session names that are still non-closed in the transaction before building any findings, and fix the comment. The impact is a stale overlap entry that the next scan clears.

**Also at:** `crates/relay-core/src/handlers/overlap.rs:315`, `crates/relay-core/src/handlers/overlap.rs:424`, `crates/relay-core/src/handlers/session.rs:250`

#### RA-390 · Overlap rows are never pruned, and each scan rewrites every historical row under the lock

`crates/relay-core/src/handlers/overlap.rs:425` · **low** · Resource leak · confirmed · effort S

**Problem.** `UPDATE overlaps SET active=0 WHERE project_id=?1` has no `AND active=1` (L424-428). New fingerprints, which include session names, are upserted (L429-437). Nothing deletes rows except project.remove (workspace.rs:368); session close and recovery only deactivate them (session.rs:251-252, recovery.rs:166-172).

**Impact.** The table grows with every new session pairing. Each flag or scan touches all rows and their `(project_id, active, last_seen)` index entries inside the transaction, so it gets slower over time.

**Fix.** Add `AND active=1` to the deactivate statement, and prune inactive rows older than N days in reconcile.

**Verifier note.** Growth is real but slow. Rows appear only when an overlap or claim exists, and scans happen only on overlap.flag or overlap.scan, never on a timer. A long-lived project reaches perhaps thousands of rows, so the extra per-scan UPDATE costs milliseconds under the lock rather than anything user-visible. Low. Fix: add `AND active=1` to the deactivate statement, and in recovery/reconcile delete inactive rows that reference no live session, or are older than N days.

**Also at:** `crates/relay-core/src/handlers/session.rs:251`, `crates/relay-core/src/recovery.rs:169`, `crates/relay-core/src/handlers/workspace.rs:368`

#### RA-391 · overlap.flag returns and emits the first claim row for the path, ignoring the symbol

`crates/relay-core/src/handlers/overlap.rs:476` · **low** · Bug · confirmed · effort S

**Problem.** `.find(|overlap| overlap.kind == OverlapKind::Claim && overlap.path == path && overlap.sessions.contains(&own.session.name))` does not compare symbols, and list() orders by path then symbol, NULL first (L52-53).

**Impact.** Flagging `a.rs#foo` while already holding `a.rs` (or `a.rs#bar`) returns and broadcasts the other claim, so the agent misreads what it holds.

Among the matches, prefer the row whose sessions == [own name], so the agent gets its own claim rather than a pair row. Impact is cosmetic or misleading only: the claims table itself is written correctly.

#### RA-392 · usage.get's reported fallback selects and dates rows by sessions.updated_at and reads every session ever

`crates/relay-core/src/handlers/provider.rs:47` · **low** · Bug · confirmed · effort M

**Problem.** `SELECT provider,usage,updated_at FROM sessions WHERE usage IS NOT NULL ORDER BY updated_at DESC,id DESC` loads all rows, including closed sessions, and uses `taken_at` = updated_at (line 57). updated_at changes on every state change, not only on usage.report (line 80). Discovered usage then replaces the result regardless of age (`latest.insert(...)`, line 67).

**Impact.** A session that reported usage hours ago but changed state a minute ago wins over a fresher report from another session, and its stale windows are labelled as taken a minute ago. Every call also reads and parses the usage JSON of every session ever created, under the store lock.

**Fix.** Record the report time with the payload (a usage_at column via a migration, or embedded in the stored JSON), select the newest per provider with LIMIT 1, and compare taken_at before letting file-discovered usage override.

**Verifier note.** The impact is lower than stated. The reported fallback is only seen when file discovery finds nothing, and usage rows exist only when agents choose to call usage.report, so 'every session ever' is a small set in practice. A cheap fix that needs no migration: embed the report time in the stored usage JSON (or select by a dedicated usage_at column if one is added later), and filter to the newest row per provider.

**Also at:** `crates/relay-core/src/handlers/provider.rs:75`

#### RA-393 · Tombstoned skills keep their UNIQUE name forever; skill.update and some installs hit conflicts the user cannot see or clear

`crates/relay-core/src/handlers/provider.rs:161` · **low** · Bug · confirmed · effort M

**Problem.** skill.update's duplicate check, `SELECT id FROM skills WHERE name=?1 COLLATE NOCASE AND id!=?2`, includes soft-deleted rows and answers 'that name is used by skill {id}', a skill that skill.list hides. In install_downloaded_skill, when name_match is a tombstone different from source_match, every reclaim arm requires `source_match.is_none()`, so it falls into the conflict arm with can_replace false (455-487). The hint says 'remove one explicitly before refreshing', but both rows may already be removed. store.rs:260 declares name UNIQUE COLLATE NOCASE.

**Impact.** Renaming a skill to the name of any skill ever deleted is refused, citing an invisible id. A refresh whose upstream name now equals a deleted local skill's name becomes a permanent conflict that cannot be cleared from the UI.

**Fix.** When the conflicting row is a tombstone, free its name (rename it to a unique placeholder or hard-delete it) and proceed.

**Verifier note.** A non-obvious workaround exists: skill.create with the tombstone's name revives it, and a skill.update rename then frees the name. The user-visible part is mostly the skill.update refusal. The minimal fix is to exclude tombstones from the duplicate check and free a tombstone's name (rename to a placeholder or hard-delete) before the UPDATE, and to do the same in the install conflict arm when name_match is a tombstone.

#### RA-394 · skill.enable bumps skills.updated_at, which is the materialization stamp, so one toggle recopies the folder in every checkout

`crates/relay-core/src/handlers/provider.rs:201` · **low** · Performance · confirmed · effort S

**Problem.** `ctx.tx().execute("UPDATE skills SET updated_at=?1 WHERE id=?2", ..)` runs on every enable or disable. skills.rs:157 builds the stamp as `format!("{id} {updated_at} {revision}\n")`, and write_skill removes and recopies any folder whose stamp differs, up to 64 MiB / 4000 files (skills.rs:308-347).

**Impact.** Toggling a skill in one project deletes and recopies its unchanged folder in every other project root, every session worktree and both user-scope folders. While a copy is in progress, an agent loading that skill can find it missing or half-written.

**Fix.** Derive the stamp from content (body hash plus revision), or do not bump updated_at for an edge-only change.

**Verifier note.** Do not just remove the bump. updated_at is also the undo precondition (set_undo passes `{"updated_at":skill.updated_at}`) and the version carried by the skill.changed event. A better fix is to separate the materialization stamp from updated_at: derive it from the content (a hash of the body, plus revision and id), or keep a separate content-version column that only body, name and asset changes bump.

#### RA-396 · A reviewer can attach arbitrary commit SHAs to a task through session.done, although its role is not allowed task.link_commit

`crates/relay-core/src/handlers/session.rs:98` · **low** · Bug · confirmed · effort S

**Problem.** `INSERT OR IGNORE INTO task_commits(task_id,sha,branch,linked_at)` inserts whatever `sha` the caller passed (97-99), and this runs for reviewers too (1165). The reviewer allowlist leaves out task.link_commit (settings.rs:37), and BUS.md says reviewers do "nothing that writes files, commits, or moves the task". The sha is also stored without trimming or checking that it exists, whereas task.link_commit trims it (task.rs:547).

**Impact.** A reviewer can link nonexistent or unrelated commits to the task it reviews, bypassing its role allowlist, and ' abc' and 'abc' are recorded as different commits.

**Fix.** Accept `sha` only from builders, trim it and verify it resolves in the worktree, or route it through task.rs link_commit.

**Verifier note.** This is not a security hole. The bypass lets a reviewer, a cooperating local agent, add a display-only metadata row to the task it reviews. It is a role-policy inconsistency plus a missing trim, so the category is bug rather than security. Simplest fix: ignore sha for reviewers and route the builder path through task::link_commit so trimming is shared.

#### RA-397 · The launch prompt is never cleared, so a fresh restart and session.bootstrap keep re-issuing an assignment that was already finished

`crates/relay-core/src/handlers/session.rs:135` · **low** · Bug · confirmed · effort S

**Problem.** launch_nudge uses `row.launch_prompt` in preference to the current task (135-143). launch_prompt is never cleared when the work is reported done; prepare_launch keeps writing it into the brief file (500-506), and bootstrap keeps returning it as `assignment` (awareness.rs:474).

**Impact.** session.clear_restorable (a fresh launch) types "begin this assignment: <original prompt>" into a session that finished that assignment long ago and has moved through its queue. A freshly started agent's bootstrap then gives it two conflicting directives.

**Fix.** Clear launch_prompt on the first completed session.done, or use it as the nudge only on the first spawn.

**Verifier note.** The only re-trigger of the nudge is session.clear_restorable, a rare user action; session.spawn can only run from Created. The launch text may also carry standing instructions (the native sheet's 'Additional instructions' field), so clearing it on the first done could lose those. A safer fix: on a non-first Fresh spawn, nudge with the current task and present launch_prompt as the original launch instructions, or record whether it has been delivered.

**Also at:** `crates/relay-core/src/handlers/session.rs:500-506`, `crates/relay-core/src/awareness.rs:474`

<a id="ra-398"></a>

#### RA-398 · PAIR checks look in different directions, so a group's second builder cannot read its own reviewer's brief or scrollback

`crates/relay-core/src/handlers/session.rs:165` · **low** · Bug · confirmed · effort S

**Problem.** assert_own allows a pair read only when the target row's pair_with names the actor (164-169), while guardrail::authorize checks the actor's own pair_with (guardrail.rs:335). In a group, R.pair_with=B1 and B2.pair_with=R. Close clears pair_with only on rows that point at the session being closed (1609), so after B1 closes, R.pair_with is NULL while B2 still points at R. validate_pair (762) then skips every group check for the next session that pairs with R.

**Impact.** The second builder in a group is refused session.brief and session.scrollback on its own reviewer (session.not_own), although D106 promises own-session-or-PAIR access. Once the first builder leaves, a new session can join R in any role (for example a second reviewer), or push the group past the two-builder limit.

**Fix.** Treat PAIR membership symmetrically (either side's pair_with, or a group id) in assert_own, authorize and validate_pair.

**Verifier note.** The claim that the group can grow past two builders does not hold as written. After B1 closes and B3 joins R, the builder count is 2, R.pair_with becomes B3, and the next join is checked again. Pairing with B2 is refused because B2 is not a reviewer (766-768). What does happen is that a second reviewer, or any other role, can join R while R.pair_with is NULL. The main effect is that B2 cannot read its reviewer's brief or scrollback. Mailbox and session.get still work.

**Also at:** `crates/relay-core/src/guardrail.rs:335`, `crates/relay-core/src/handlers/session.rs:1609`, `crates/relay-core/src/handlers/session.rs:762`

<a id="ra-399"></a>

#### RA-399 · When a builder's process exits, its current task is marked failed even if this builder had already completed it and its partner is still working

`crates/relay-core/src/handlers/session.rs:662` · **low** · Bug · confirmed · effort S

**Problem.** `if row.session.role == Role::Builder { if let Some(task_id) = row.session.task_id { UPDATE tasks SET state='failed' ... WHERE id=?2 AND col='active' ...` (659-668) never checks this session's task_sessions.completed_at, or whether other builders are still working on the task.

**Impact.** A builder that has already called done and is waiting for its PAIR partner exits (the user quits its CLI). The task, still active because the partner is working on it, shows as failed on the board until the partner's next tool use resets it. The same happens to a queued task the builder had just advanced to and never started.

**Fix.** Add `AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM task_sessions WHERE task_id=?2 AND session_id=?3 AND completed_at IS NOT NULL)`, and skip the update while other builders of the task are live.

**Verifier note.** The flag is display state that heals itself, so this stays low. Fix: guard with `AND NOT EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM task_sessions WHERE task_id=?2 AND session_id=?3 AND completed_at IS NOT NULL)`, and also skip the update when another non-closed builder in the same worktree still has an open task_sessions row for the task.

#### RA-400 · session.done with status blocked or partial releases all of the session's claims and deactivates its overlaps, although its task stays current

`crates/relay-core/src/handlers/session.rs:1187` · **low** · Bug · confirmed · effort S

**Problem.** Done computes `let session_state = if status == "completed" { "idle" } else { "blocked" };` and then calls `release_claims(ctx, s)?;` for every status. release_claims (248-257) runs `DELETE FROM claims WHERE session_id=?1` and `UPDATE overlaps SET active=0 ...`. BUS.md:734 says blocked/partial "leave only the current task in place, set it blocked, notify agent_blocked" and says nothing about claims. The role instructions (providers.rs:42) say "Declare the files you are taking on with session.claim", and after a blocked report the task stays current, with no queue advance. The hook path for the same situation, session.report {kind:"blocked"} (1349-1414), keeps claims. done_can_say_blocked_and_the_task_does_not_move (agent_features.rs:207-260) never claims anything, and finishing_or_closing_releases_claims_for_the_next_agent (123-138) covers only a completed done. I could not establish author intent; no decision entry covers it.

**Impact.** Agent A claims src/parser.rs, hits a blocker and reports session.done {status:"blocked"}. Peers now see no claim. Agent B's `session.claim {exclusive:true}` on the same file succeeds with no collision, and B starts editing the file A resumes once unblocked. Active overlaps involving A disappear until the next scan.

**Fix.** Release claims only when status == "completed". Extend done_can_say_blocked_and_the_task_does_not_move to claim a path before the blocked report and assert the claim survives.

**Verifier note.** Severity is low, not medium. Claims are advisory and not enforced (D116), so the consequence is only that a peer's session.claim/peers no longer reports A's files during the blocked interval. The blocked/partial done path is itself uncommon. Fix as proposed: release only on completed, and extend done_can_say_blocked_and_the_task_does_not_move to assert that a claim survives.

**Also at:** `crates/relay-core/src/handlers/session.rs:248`, `crates/relay-core/src/handlers/session.rs:1402`, `docs/engine/BUS.md:734`, `crates/relay-core/tests/agent_features.rs:207`

<a id="ra-401"></a>

#### RA-401 · session.report, the busiest agent op, recompiles its SQL on every call and hashes the whole hook payload while holding the lock

`crates/relay-core/src/handlers/session.rs:1354` · **low** · Performance · confirmed · effort S

**Problem.** Report runs on every PostToolUse of every agent. It re-reads done_pending_stop with an uncached `query_row` (1354-1356) even though `sessions::by_name` already loaded the row. The state update (1371), the done_pending_stop clear (1376) and the task update (1393) use `Connection::execute`, which compiles the SQL each time. The CLI forwards the entire hook JSON, including tool_response (relay-cli main.rs:490-496), and the audit append serializes and SHA-256-hashes all of it under the lock, although it stores only 2 KB.

**Impact.** Each tool call costs several SQL compilations plus a hash of what can be hundreds of KB, all under the global store lock, multiplied by the number of agents and tool calls. CLAUDE.md asks for prepare_cached on hot paths.

**Fix.** Add done_pending_stop to Row_, switch to prepare_cached, merge the two session UPDATEs, and drop tool_response in the CLI hook adapter.

**Verifier note.** The cost is small in absolute terms: a few tens of microseconds of SQL compilation per call, plus about 1 ms to hash a payload of a few hundred KB, all under the store lock. That is real but modest, so low is right. CLAUDE.md asks for prepare_cached over Connection::query_row; it does not single out hot paths, but this is one. The simplest high-payoff part of the fix is stripping tool_response (and tool_input content) in the CLI adapter, because Report only reads /tool_input/command, session_id, message and notification_type.

#### RA-402 · session.update runs git subprocesses with no timeout while holding the store lock, and can rename the primary checkout's branch

`crates/relay-core/src/handlers/session.rs:1460` · **low** · Invariant · confirmed · effort M

**Problem.** session.update is registered with `e.register::<Update>` (a locked transaction) and calls `worktree::rename_branch(Path::new(&s.worktree), &branch)` (1460). That runs `git check-ref-format` and `git branch -m` through worktree.rs `git()`, which is `Command::new("git")...output()` with no proc::output_with_timeout (worktree.rs:26-33, 373-379). Only PAIR sessions are refused (1459). Separately, Create's finish (900-910) runs hooks::uninstall_git (git subprocesses) with the store held, after first waiting on hooks::writes(). A concurrent launch holds that lock across install_git, skill-folder copying and brief writes (480-560).

**Impact.** A hung or slow git (lock contention, a reference-transaction hook) freezes every bus request for as long as it runs, with no deadline. For a not-yet-spawned session on the primary checkout, `git branch -m` renames the user's checked-out base branch (e.g. main), which breaks the project's base_branch and the other sessions' rows. A refused create holds the store mutex while it waits for another launch's preparation to finish.

**Fix.** Make Update a staged op: rename in its prepare phase via proc::output_with_timeout, and refuse when the worktree is shared or primary. Move the refused-create uninstall to after_commit or a worker thread.

**Verifier note.** Restrict the finding to Update -> worktree::rename_branch (session.rs:1460, worktree.rs:26-33 and 373-380). Drop the Create-finish and launch-lock part: uninstall_git is already bounded by a 10 s timeout. Severity is low because the rename is reachable only by a user calling the CLI by hand on a session that has not spawned yet. Fix: run the rename through proc::output_with_timeout, ideally in a staged prepare phase, and refuse a rename when the worktree is the primary checkout or is shared with another non-closed session.

**Also at:** `crates/relay-core/src/worktree.rs:26-33`, `crates/relay-core/src/worktree.rs:373-379`, `crates/relay-core/src/handlers/session.rs:900-910`, `crates/relay-core/src/handlers/session.rs:480-560`

#### RA-403 · audit.undo of a session.update always fails once the session has been spawned

`crates/relay-core/src/handlers/session.rs:1474` · **low** · Bug · confirmed · effort S

**Problem.** The undo payload always contains `"branch": s.branch` (a non-null string) plus model and effort (1474-1477). Replaying it hits `if spawned && (p.branch.is_some() || ...)`, which returns conflict session.already_spawned (1434-1437). The undo's updated_at guard is also invalidated by every tool-use report, because Report sets updated_at (1372).

**Impact.** Undoing any session.update (e.g. a bus_writes or allow_ui toggle) on a running session can never succeed. The undo would also leave behind the task_sessions row that the update inserted.

**Fix.** Put only the fields the update actually changed into the inverse payload, and never include branch/model/effort once the session has spawned.

**Verifier note.** Severity stays low: the op is user-only, rarely undone, and the failure is a clean refusal, not corruption. Fix: include in the inverse only the fields the update actually changed, and omit branch, model and effort once the session has spawned (or whenever they are unchanged).

`crates/relay-core/src/handlers/session.rs:1482` · **low** · Security · confirmed · effort S

#### RA-405 · Worktree removal on session.close / project.remove / discard_restorable force-deletes uncommitted work with no dirty check, and session.close removes by default

`crates/relay-core/src/handlers/session.rs:1578` · **low** · Data loss · confirmed · effort S

**Problem.** session.rs:1548 sets `let remove = p.remove_worktree.unwrap_or(true);`, and 1577-1579 call `worktree::remove(&repo, wt, p.purge_build.unwrap_or(true))` (git worktree remove --force) with no status check. DiscardRestorable does the same (1519-1523). project.remove with remove_worktrees queues the same removal after commit (workspace.rs:330-345). In the UI, the 'Also remove the worktree' checkbox (agent_menu.rs:594) sits under 'Stop this agent and close its pane? The branch is kept.' and gives no hint of uncommitted changes. By contrast, git.branch.switch (git.rs:411-432), the device primary sync (device.rs:1566-1571) and branch_cleanup (branch_cleanup.rs:295-301) all refuse a dirty checkout. BUS.md:733 documents the remove-by-default.

**Impact.** An agent that has not committed yet (crashed, interrupted or mid-task) loses all its edits and new files in three cases: the user ticks 'Also remove the worktree'; the user removes a project with 'Also delete agent worktrees'; or any bus client calls `session.close {session}` relying on the documented default.

**Fix.** In the prepare phases, run worktree::status_files on the checkout. Refuse with conflict `worktree.dirty` (details: count and sample paths) unless the caller passes an explicit `discard_changes: true`. Show the count in the confirm strip and dialog. Change remove_worktree's API default to false to match the UI.

**Verifier note.** The trigger is narrower than claimed. session.close and discard_restorable are Actors::UserOnly (ops/session.rs:38-39), so agents cannot call them. The native client closes with remove_worktree false by default: the checkbox starts unticked (agent_menu.rs:594/612) and shell.rs:734 sends false. Native never calls session.discard_restorable. project.remove removes worktrees only when its dialog checkbox is ticked (registry.rs:627). Every removal therefore needs an explicit user opt-in. What is missing is a warning that the checkout holds N uncommitted changes, plus an API default (remove_worktree=true, BUS.md:733) that is riskier than the UI's. Low severity: add a dirty check that refuses with worktree.dirty unless discard_changes is set, and flip the API default.

#### RA-406 · session.scrollback copies and serializes up to the full 8 MiB scrollback while holding the store lock

`crates/relay-core/src/handlers/session.rs:1701` · **low** · Performance · confirmed · effort S · rechecked after PR #30/#31: still present

When `lines` is omitted it calls `pty.scrollback(None)`, which copies the whole ring (up to 8 MiB) and decodes it lossily, and the register wrapper serializes that string to JSON before the transaction commits. The live-PTY branch needs the store only for by_name.

#### RA-407 · settings.set flattens object keys verbatim into dotted paths; dotted keys and root-level scalars do not read back

`crates/relay-core/src/handlers/settings.rs:72` · **low** · Bug · confirmed · effort S

**Problem.** flatten builds `format!("{prefix}.{k}")` for every object key with no validation (68-78) while valid_path checks only the request path, and set_at splits stored paths on '.' (86). A root write of a non-object or {} stores a row at path "" (flatten pushes ("", v)), which tree() applies (*root = v) but subtree() never selects (ancestors come from '.' positions and exclude "", 155-158). Python model: settings.set keybindings {"ctrl+.":{"op":"ui.toast"}} reads back as {"ctrl+":{"":{"op":"ui.toast"}}}.

**Impact.** BUS.md:909 documents keybindings as 'shortcut -> op envelope', so any shortcut containing '.' is corrupted on save; values like {"a.b":1,"a":{"b":2}} collide and fail with an internal PK error; after settings.set {path:"", value:{}} the whole-tree read returns {} while leaf reads still return defaults, breaking the D150 agreement tests/bus.rs:760 asserts.

**Fix.** In flatten, reject (BusError::invalid) object keys that are not valid path segments; require a non-empty object for settings.set at "" (or write root keys individually); if root rows must exist, include "" among subtree's ancestors.

**Verifier note.** The trigger needs user-supplied input that no shipped client produces. Impact is a corrupted or inconsistent settings row, not data loss elsewhere. Fix: validate each object key in flatten against the same segment rule as valid_path and return BusError::invalid, and reject settings.set at "" unless the value is a non-empty object. Including "" among subtree's ancestors is not needed once that write is refused.

#### RA-408 · get_task recompiles its SQL on every call, and assert_parent fully hydrates the parent and each ancestor just to read three columns

`crates/relay-core/src/handlers/task.rs:350` · **low** · Performance · confirmed · effort S

**Problem.** get_task uses `tx.query_row(sql, [id], |row| row_task(tx, row))` (350), the uncached form CLAUDE.md says to avoid. It runs per row in module.rs:115 (tasks_for), Children (1185-1187) and fanout (1069). assert_parent calls get_task on the parent (378) and on every ancestor (400) only to read project_id, depth and parent_id, yet each call runs row_task's ~10 statements and walks that node's entire subtree for its rollup.

**Impact.** Re-parenting inside a large tree hydrates the root (up to 1+100+10,000 descendants at 2 queries each) under the global lock just to read one parent_id. module.get and module.changelog.draft also recompile the SELECT for every task.

**Fix.** Use prepare_cached in get_task. In assert_parent, read `project_id, parent_id` with one cached statement and take depth from depth_of.

**Verifier note.** Recompiling the trivial SELECT * is the minor part. Most of the cost is row_task's full hydration and rollup walk when only three scalar columns are needed. A lightweight cached `SELECT project_id,parent_id FROM tasks WHERE id=?1 AND deleted_at IS NULL`, plus depth_of, fixes assert_parent. Switching get_task to prepare_cached is a separate, trivial win.

#### RA-409 · Attachment files are never reclaimed: detach, rollback and delete all leave files on disk

`crates/relay-core/src/handlers/task.rs:524` · **low** · Resource leak · confirmed · effort M

**Problem.** attach_bytes writes the file (`std::fs::write(&path, bytes)`, 524) before the transaction commits. If a later step in the same request fails, for example task.create's second attachment with invalid base64 (747-748), the row rolls back but the file stays. Detach only runs `DELETE FROM attachments WHERE id=?1` (1038-1040). task.delete and restore never touch files, and no code removes anything under attachments/<task>/.

**Impact.** The store's attachments directory only grows. Every detach, every detach and undo cycle (which copies the file again) and every failed create leaves files that no row references.

**Fix.** Remove files written during a failed request (a guard that deletes on Err) or write them after commit. Garbage-collect unreferenced files in recovery, keeping detached files only while their undo row is still undoable.

**Verifier note.** Keeping files after detach is required for undo, so a GC must keep any file an undoable audit row still references. A further leak site is workspace.rs:362, where project delete removes attachment rows and leaves their files.

<a id="ra-411"></a>

#### RA-411 · Agents can read every project's tasks and modules; task.list, module.* and task.label.list ignore the actor's project

`crates/relay-core/src/handlers/task.rs:832` · **low** · Security · confirmed · effort S

**Problem.** Layer-2 authorization only scopes payload `session` and `task_id` fields (guardrail.rs:328-349), and Scope::Project metadata is enforced nowhere. task.list does `if let Some(project_id) = p.project_id { get_project(...) }` and applies no project filter when project_id is absent, even with include_deleted (832-838). module.get (module.rs:125-144), module.list (145), module.stats (207), module.changelog.draft (208-215) and task.label.list (task.rs:1235-1249) never compare against the agent's project. notes.rs:47-61 assert_actor_project returns `not_own("project")` for exactly this case, session.list/get stop at the project (D106), and task.get is limited to the agent's own task.

**Impact.** Every role may call every query. An agent working an untrusted repository (and so exposed to prompt injection) can call `task.list {}` or `task.list {project_id: <other>, include_deleted: true}` and `module.get` on other projects' modules. That returns full task bodies, changelogs, attachment paths, linked commits and session names for all of the user's projects, which the agent can then exfiltrate. The boundary is also inconsistent: task.get refuses a same-project task that task.list returns, the kind of inconsistency D106 removed for sessions.

**Fix.** For agent actors, default task.list's project_id to the session's project and refuse any other. Call assert_actor_project (or session.rs's actor_project) in module.get/list/stats/changelog.draft and task.label.list.

**Verifier note.** Downgrade to low. The real cost is an inconsistent agent visibility boundary: task.get refuses a same-project task that task.list returns. Bus reads are not a confidentiality boundary, because file.read across projects and direct filesystem access both bypass it. The fix is still reasonable for consistency: scope task.list, module.* and task.label.list to the agent's project the way notes::assert_actor_project does. If cross-project reads are ever meant to be confidential, file.read's project_id needs the same check.

<a id="ra-412"></a>

#### RA-412 · task.list hydrates every task, including all done tasks, with about 10 queries each on every board refresh

`crates/relay-core/src/handlers/task.rs:862` · **low** · Performance · confirmed · effort M

**Problem.** `while let Some(row)=rows.next()? { tasks.push(row_task(ctx.tx(), row)?) }` (859-862). row_task runs about 9 statements per task (sessions, commits, attachments, labels, three relation edges, children, depth walk) plus two per descendant for the roll-up (task.rs:229-342). The native board asks for `task.list {project_id}` with no column filter (pages.rs:43), so done tasks are included, and they are never archived or hard-deleted. refresh_page re-runs it on every task.changed event (app.rs:1264). A Python reproduction of the same statement set took 25 ms for 2000 tasks.

**Impact.** Each board refresh costs time linear in all tasks the project ever had, under the store lock. Agent state changes that emit task.changed trigger it repeatedly.

**Fix.** Batch the per-task lookups (WHERE task_id IN (...) or JOINs grouped in Rust), and let the board page done tasks or fetch them lazily.

**Verifier note.** The impact is small at realistic sizes, a few ms per refresh, but it grows with every task the project has ever had and runs under the store lock. A cheaper first step than batching all the lookups: have the board skip or page done tasks, or fetch the done column lazily. Batching the per-task lookups into IN(...) or GROUP BY queries is the fuller fix.

**Also at:** `crates/relay-core/src/handlers/task.rs:229`, `apps/relay-native/src/pages.rs:43`

<a id="ra-413"></a>

#### RA-413 · Agent task and note writes have no optimistic check, so an agent silently overwrites a newer user edit

`crates/relay-core/src/handlers/task.rs:871` · **low** · Concurrency · confirmed · effort S

**Problem.** task.update applies `expected` only when the caller supplies it (task.rs:871-881), and agents may write body/changelog (868-870). task.changelog.write has no expected at all (965-981). notes.update is the same (notes.rs:379-389), and the default 'docs' role may call it (settings.rs:38). The UI always sends `expected` (task_pages.rs:219, note_pages/doc.rs:1133), so it never clobbers an agent's edit. The reverse is unchecked, and the board's undo lists only the user's own rows (board_view.rs:882).

**Impact.** Suppose an agent reads a task body or note, the user then saves an edit, and the agent writes afterwards. The user's text is replaced with no conflict. The user's version survives only in the audit row's undo_op, reachable through audit.undo from the CLI.

**Fix.** Require `expected` (or an expected updated_at) for agent writes of task body/changelog and notes, and return task.edit_conflict otherwise. Add `expected` to task.changelog.write.

**Verifier note.** The impact is limited: the previous text is recoverable through audit.undo, and only a race between a user edit and an agent write triggers it. A cheaper fix than requiring `expected` on every agent write: have agent task.update and changelog.write refuse when the row's updated_at is newer than the agent's last read, or accept an `expected` on changelog.write and have the MCP tool descriptions ask agents to send it.

**Also at:** `crates/relay-core/src/handlers/task.rs:965`, `crates/relay-core/src/handlers/notes.rs:379`, `crates/relay-core/src/handlers/settings.rs:38`

<a id="ra-414"></a>

#### RA-414 · Undoing task.detach re-attaches a renamed, retyped copy instead of restoring the attachment

`crates/relay-core/src/handlers/task.rs:1043` · **low** · Bug · confirmed · effort S

**Problem.** Detach deletes the row and records the inverse `task.attach {"task_id":task.id,"path":attachment.path}` (1041-1045). The path variant of Attach takes the name from `src.file_name()`, which is the stored `"{id}-{name}"`, forces mime `"application/octet-stream"` (994-998), and attach_bytes inserts a new row and writes a new file `{newid}-{oldid}-{name}`.

**Impact.** Detach followed by Ctrl+Z brings the attachment back under a new id, renamed (for example '17-screenshot.png'), typed application/octet-stream, with a second copy of the file. Each detach and undo cycle prefixes another id and duplicates the file again.

**Fix.** Soft-delete attachments (a deleted_at column) and make the inverse a restore of that row, or carry name and mime in the undo payload and restore the original row.

**Verifier note.** Detach also never deletes the attachment file, so files of detached attachments accumulate on disk. That is a minor leak of the same design. A soft-delete column with a restore inverse fixes both.

**Also at:** `crates/relay-core/src/handlers/task.rs:985-998`, `crates/relay-core/src/handlers/task.rs:505-538`

<a id="ra-415"></a>

#### RA-415 · Dispatch fanout copies the parent's whole session template (branch, worktree, pair_with, prompt) into every child

`crates/relay-core/src/handlers/task.rs:1073` · **low** · Bug · confirmed · effort S

**Problem.** `let template = p.create.clone();` (1064), then each child gets `dispatch_task(ctx, id, None, template.clone(), start)` (1073). dispatch_task overrides only task_id and module_id (681-682). CreateIn also carries branch, worktree, pair_with and prompt (ops/session.rs:7-16). worktree::create runs `git worktree add <path> <branch>` for an existing branch (worktree.rs:204-206). launch_nudge prefers launch_prompt over the task (session.rs:134-143).

**Impact.** With `branch` set, the parent's session creates the branch, then the first child's `git worktree add` fails ('already checked out'). The whole dispatch rolls back after the parent's worktree, hooks and agent were already created (see the dispatch-under-lock finding). With `prompt` set, every child agent is told 'begin this assignment: <parent's prompt>' instead of its own task. With `worktree:"primary"`, a path, or the D160 default, all children share one checkout and become a single group, contradicting 'one fresh session each'.

**Fix.** For fanned children, clear branch, prompt and pair_with, and force worktree to "new". Alternatively, refuse fanout when the template sets any of these.

**Verifier note.** Drop the D160 'primary' part of the impact. When a plugin sets default_checkout to primary, sessions are meant to share the primary checkout, so that case is intended. The real defects are branch, prompt and pair_with being copied. Severity is low because no shipped in-scope client uses fanout. Fix: for fanned children, clear branch, prompt and pair_with (or refuse fanout when the template sets them) and leave worktree as given.

**Also at:** `crates/relay-core/src/handlers/task.rs:1064`, `crates/relay-core/src/handlers/task.rs:674-682`, `crates/relay-core/src/handlers/session.rs:134-143`, `crates/relay-core/src/worktree.rs:204-217`

#### RA-416 · Undoing task.approve is a plain task.move: the commit link stays and the task's prior state is lost

`crates/relay-core/src/handlers/task.rs:1141` · **low** · Bug · confirmed · effort S

**Problem.** Approve inserts a task_commits row (`link_commit`, task.rs:1128) and forces `state='none'` (1132). Its undo is only `task.move {task_id, column, position}` (1141-1145). Move keeps `before.state` except for Done→InReview (`moved_state`, 902), and it never touches task_commits. `link_commit` accepts any non-empty string as a sha (540-559), and the board tests pass `"cafe"`/`"deadbeef"`. board.rs:732-736 checks only column order after the undo.

**Impact.** Trigger: approving an active or ready task by mistake, then pressing Undo. Consequence: the card returns to its column with state `none` instead of `dispatched`/`running`. task.get still lists the approval's commit link, so the board shows a commit on an unapproved task, and a later approval adds a second one.

**Fix.** Give approval its own inverse: an undo payload that restores column, position and state, and deletes the task_commits row only if this approval inserted it. Assert state and commits in the undo test.

**Verifier note.** State loss happens only when the approval came from a column other than in_review. Approving from in_review, the normal path, is restored correctly to awaiting_review by `moved_state`. Approving from ready also loses nothing in practice, since ready tasks presumably already carry state 'none'. The stray task_commits row is the part that always happens. A re-approval with the same sha is absorbed by INSERT OR IGNORE, so a second link appears only if the branch head moved.

<a id="ra-417"></a>

#### RA-417 · task.parent.set writes its caller-supplied position into the board's column-order field without bounds or renumbering

`crates/relay-core/src/handlers/task.rs:1154` · **low** · Bug · confirmed · effort S

**Problem.** `let position = p.position.unwrap_or(before.position).max(0);` (1154) is written to tasks.position (1157). That is the field column_index, open_slot and next_position use for column order (452-479), and child_ids orders siblings by it. next_position computes `COALESCE(MAX(position),-1)+1` (453).

**Impact.** A client that passes a sibling index (for example 0 to put a child first) silently moves the card within its board column, with ties at 0 broken by id. A value at i64::MAX makes MAX(position)+1 overflow to REAL in SQLite, `r.get::<i64>` fails, and every task.create, end-of-column move, dispatch and approve into that column errors until the row is fixed.

**Fix.** Drop `position` from parent.set, or apply it through open_slot-style index semantics clamped to 0..=column length.

**Verifier note.** Only bus/MCP callers (agents included) can trigger this; native never sends position. Fix: remove position from parent.set, or route it through open_slot for the task's column so it is clamped to the column length.

**Also at:** `crates/relay-core/src/handlers/task.rs:452-479`, `crates/relay-core/src/handlers/task.rs:1155-1158`

#### RA-418 · task.relate records an undo even when nothing changed, and its duplicate_of replace misses edges to deleted tasks

`crates/relay-core/src/handlers/task.rs:1257` · **low** · Bug · confirmed · effort S

**Problem.** `let replaced = if p.relation == TaskRelation::DuplicateOf { task.duplicate_of } else { None };` (1257) reads row_task's duplicate_of, which filters `t.deleted_at IS NULL` (275). The `INSERT OR IGNORE INTO task_relations` result is discarded (1261-1266), and `set_undo("task.unrelate", ...)` is recorded whenever replaced is None (1269-1276). LabelAdd, by contrast, checks `added > 0`.

**Impact.** First, re-linking an existing blocked_by (the task page's Link combobox lists every task) changes nothing, yet Ctrl+Z on that row deletes the relation that existed before. Second, if the current duplicate_of target is soft-deleted, a new duplicate_of leaves the old edge in place, giving two duplicate_of rows. Restoring the old target can then make the stale edge win (`ORDER BY r.to_task`), and unrelating the visible one reveals the other.

**Fix.** Use the INSERT's changed count and skip set_undo when it is 0. For duplicate_of, query existing edges without the deleted filter and delete them all before inserting.

**Verifier note.** Fix as proposed: use the INSERT's changed count to decide whether to set_undo. For duplicate_of, read the existing edges without the deleted filter, then delete them all (and record the prior target for undo) before inserting.

#### RA-419 · ui.layout.save without state reads layout.current.<id>, a key nothing writes, so it saves a hard-coded grid

`crates/relay-core/src/handlers/ui.rs:34` · **low** · Bug · confirmed · effort S

**Problem.** fallback_state reads `settings::get(ctx.tx(), Some(&format!("layout.current.{project_id}")))` and otherwise returns `json!({"page":"agents","agent_layout":"grid"})`. The native client persists its arrangement under `native.layout.current.{project}` (shell.rs:308, 334). project.remove deletes only the exact path layout.current.<id> (workspace.rs:378-379), but settings::set stores an object as leaves (layout.current.7.page ...), so neither key's leaves are ever removed.

Since projects.id is a plain INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, a new project that reuses a removed project's id restores the dead project's layout.

**Fix.** Read the key the client writes (or have the client write the engine's key), and on project removal delete `path = ?1 OR path LIKE ?1||'.%'` for both keys.

#### RA-420 · In-memory UI model drifts: close leaves no pane flagged focused, popout leaves empty windows, move ignores edge and emits a different ui.changed shape

`crates/relay-core/src/handlers/ui.rs:115` · **low** · Bug · confirmed · effort S

**Problem.** PaneClose sets `ui.focused = ui.panes.last().map(...)` without setting that pane's `focused` flag (114-116). WindowPopout strips the pane from its old window (277-279) but never removes the now-empty popout. PaneMove does `ui.panes.remove(from); ... ui.panes.insert(to.min(len), pane)`, which lands after the target when moving forward and before it when moving backward, ignores `edge` and window membership, and emits ui.changed as `{"move":{...}}` (178-181) while every other ui op emits the full StateOut. PaneOpen ignores `at` (BUS.md:917).

**Impact.** ui.state reports `focused: pane-N` while no PaneInfo has focused=true; the native apply_ui_event keys on the per-pane flag and on page/panes (shell.rs:438-458), so it ignores the move payload and ui.pane.move is a no-op that returns success; repeated popouts accumulate empty windows in ui.window.list, and panes grow without bound if never closed.

**Fix.** Set the flag on the new focused pane; drop popout windows that become empty; compute the insert index after removal relative to the target and honour edge, or reject what is unsupported; always emit the full state.

**Verifier note.** The impact is smaller than stated. The native client does not model engine panes, ordering or popout windows at all, so pane.move and popout have no visible effect whatever their payload shape. The concrete harm is that agents reading ui.state/ui.window.list see an inconsistent model (no focused flag, empty popouts). Fix: set the flag in PaneClose, drop emptied popout windows, emit the full state from PaneMove, and either document these ops as model-only or reject `edge` values that are not implemented.

**Also at:** `crates/relay-core/src/handlers/ui.rs:174`, `crates/relay-core/src/handlers/ui.rs:277`, `apps/relay-native/src/shell.rs:438`

#### RA-421 · os.reveal/os.open_url spawn xdg-open and never reap it; reveal opens path.parent() even when it is a file

`crates/relay-core/src/handlers/ui.rs:345` · **low** · Resource leak · confirmed · effort S

**Problem.** `ctx.after_commit(move |_| { let target = path.parent().unwrap_or(&path); let _ = std::process::Command::new("xdg-open").arg(target).spawn(); });` (343-346) and the same fire-and-forget `.spawn()` for URLs (356-360). The Child is dropped without wait and nothing in the engine reaps children (no SIGCHLD handling found). The only path check is is_absolute().

**Impact.** Every link click (tools_skills.rs:170) or reveal leaves a defunct xdg-open in the process table for the engine's lifetime. A path like `/tmp/x.jar/anything` makes reveal run `xdg-open /tmp/x.jar`, opening (for some types, executing) the file with its desktop handler instead of showing a folder; reachable by agents granted allow_ui.

**Fix.** Reap in a detached thread (`std::thread::spawn(move || { let _ = child.wait(); })`); for reveal, open `path` if it is a directory, else its parent only if that is a directory (or use the FileManager1 ShowItems D-Bus call).

**Verifier note.** The reveal-opens-a-file case is not a guardrail escape. Only an agent already granted allow_ui can reach it, that grant is a deliberate escape hatch, and the same session can normally run xdg-open itself under its command guardrails. Treat it as a minor correctness bug, not a security finding. Fix: after spawning, reap the child in a detached thread (`std::thread::spawn(move || { let _ = child.wait(); })`). For reveal, open `path` itself when it is a directory, otherwise open its parent only if that is a directory, and otherwise return an error. The FileManager1 ShowItems D-Bus call is a better option if selecting the file is wanted.

#### RA-422 · Legacy project.update protected_paths/critical_files are a second, unvalidated way to set guardrail patterns; one bad entry blocks every agent in the project

`crates/relay-core/src/handlers/workspace.rs:271` · **low** · Error handling · confirmed · effort S

**Problem.** ProjectUpdateIn still accepts protected_paths and critical_files (ops/workspace.rs:46) and the handler stores them verbatim (workspace.rs:271-277) — no validate_pattern. guardrail::layers merges those columns into the project's effective config (guardrail.rs:154-178) and typed() runs validate_config (292-302), which rejects empty, absolute or `..` patterns. The UI path, guardrail.config.set, validates before writing.

**Impact.** `relay q project.update '{"project_id":1,"protected_paths":["/home/me/secrets"]}'` succeeds; afterwards guardrail::config for project 1 errors, so authorize() fails every agent mutation and guardrail.gate fails every PreToolUse hook — all Bash/Edit/Write calls of every agent in the project are blocked with "bad relative path pattern" until the user finds the legacy column, which the guardrail settings page does not edit.

**Fix.** Migrate the two columns into the project guardrail layer once and drop them from ProjectUpdateIn, or at minimum run validate_pattern on them in project.update.

**Verifier note.** The trigger is narrow. project.update is Actors::UserOnly, and the native UI never sends these fields (guardrail_settings.rs edits the settings layer). Only a user typing a hand-written CLI/bus call with an absolute or `..` pattern can store a bad entry. The op is undoable (Undo::Inverse), and a second project.update fixes it. A real but rare self-inflicted failure, so low severity. The fix stands: run validate_pattern on both lists in project.update, or migrate the columns into the guardrail settings layer and drop them from ProjectUpdateIn.

<a id="ra-423"></a>

#### RA-423 · project.remove with remove_worktrees starts deleting checkouts as soon as the agents are signalled, not after they are dead

`crates/relay-core/src/handlers/workspace.rs:338` · **low** · Concurrency · confirmed · effort S

**Problem.** The comment at workspace.rs:321-325 says the removal is queued "for after the commit too, behind those kills". It is queued behind the start of those kills, not their end. Each forced `session.close` (invoked with remove_worktree:false) defers its kill as `ctx.after_commit(move |_| kill_detached(pty, Duration::from_millis(150)))` (session.rs:1606). `kill_detached` (session.rs:366-376) only spawns a `pty-kill-<pid>` thread and returns. Inside that thread, `Pty::kill` (pty.rs:363-384) sends SIGTERM, waits up to 150 ms, then sends SIGKILL and waits up to 2 s more. Engine::dispatch runs the after_commit closures one after another on the request thread (engine.rs:1030-1035). So project.remove's closure `for wt in &doomed { crate::worktree::remove(&repo, wt, true) ... }` (workspace.rs:338-344) runs right after those threads are spawned, possibly before SIGTERM has even been delivered. `worktree::remove` (worktree.rs:352-369) runs purge_build, dir_size and then `git worktree remove --force` with a remove_dir_all fallback. session.close's own remove path does the opposite, killing synchronously first: "Stop writers before undoing their hooks and deleting their checkout" with `pty.kill(Duration::from_millis(150))` (session.rs:1567-1571).

**Impact.** Trigger: project.remove {force:true, remove_worktrees:true} on a project whose agents are busy, for example in a build or a file-writing tool call. The agent and its process group keep running for up to 150 ms (2+ s if they ignore SIGTERM) while purge_build and `git worktree remove --force` delete the tree under them. A writer that creates files mid-delete makes remove_dir_all fail with ENOTEMPTY. worktree::remove then returns an error that is only logged as a warning, so a half-deleted pool directory and stale worktree metadata stay on disk after the project has been forgotten. Nothing is left in Relay to clean them up. Agents also see their checkout disappear while they are still running, which leads to spurious tool errors and partial writes. The path is uncommon and the window is short, so the severity is low.

**Fix.** Make the removal wait for the kills. Before invoking session.close for each open session, have project.remove take the PTYs itself with `ctx.engine().take_pty(id)`, so session.close finds none to defer. Move them into the existing after_commit closure, and there call `pty.silence_exit(); pty.kill(Duration::from_millis(150))` synchronously for every PTY before the `worktree::remove` loop. That matches session.close's own remove path. Fix the comment at workspace.rs:321-325 to match.

**Verifier note.** Severity stays low. SIGTERM goes to the whole process group within microseconds of the thread being spawned, and most agents exit quickly, so the race window is short. It matters only when force and remove_worktrees are both set and an agent or its build is actively writing. A leftover directory is an unlikely outcome, not a typical one. The proposed fix is sound: take each PTY before session.close runs, then kill them synchronously with exit silenced inside the after_commit closure, before the remove loop.

**Also at:** `crates/relay-core/src/handlers/session.rs:1606`, `crates/relay-core/src/handlers/session.rs:366`, `crates/relay-core/src/handlers/session.rs:1567`, `crates/relay-core/src/pty.rs:363`, `crates/relay-core/src/worktree.rs:352`, `crates/relay-core/src/engine.rs:1030`

#### RA-425 · Each agent-settings popover leaks, because its own buttons' handlers hold the popover strongly

`apps/relay-native/src/agent_menu.rs:451` · **low** · Resource leak · confirmed · effort S

**Problem.** `let p = popover.clone();` is moved into the click handlers of `brief` (451-455), `save` (541-556) and both confirm strips (578-580, 608-610). Every one of those buttons lives inside `body`, which is the popover's child. connect_closed only unparents the popover on idle (371-374). confirm_strip also captures `let r = revealer.clone();` in its Cancel handler (835-836), and that Cancel key sits inside the same revealer. An unparented GTK4 widget is disposed only when its last reference is dropped, and these cycles never drop it.

**Impact.** Each click on an agent's settings key leaks a full popover: about 40 widgets (entries, switches, DropDown, revealers) plus their closures. Memory grows with every popover opened, with no bound. phone_status keeps writing to the leaked labels.

**Fix.** Capture `popover.downgrade()` and `revealer.downgrade()` and upgrade them inside the handlers, or use `glib::clone!(@weak popover => …)`.

**Verifier note.** The Cancel handler's `revealer.clone()` (confirm_strip 835-836) is not a separate root cause. That cycle would be broken by the popover's dispose if the popover were ever disposed. The popover captures are the only real cause. Impact is small: the popover is unrealized on unparent, so its GdkSurface is freed, and the leak is tens of KB of widgets and closures per manual click. Growth is bounded by how often the user opens the popover, which is why low fits better than medium. Fix: capture popover.downgrade() in those closures, or keep the popover per key and reuse it.

#### RA-426 · Phone install state goes stale: Stop hits the previous run while a new install starts, and a reopened popover's install button stays disabled

`apps/relay-native/src/agent_menu.rs:802` · **low** · Bug · confirmed · effort S

**Problem.** phone_status only sets `phone.run` when given Some (802-804) and never clears it. Stop is shown when `busy && run.is_some()` (652, 812). A new install sets busy=true with run=None ("Looking for a phone…" 685, "Building …" 730), so the old run id stays. Stop (656-667) then sends device.run.stop for the finished run, which the engine accepts and ignores (device.rs:263-288). **Impact.** Pressing Stop while a new build is starting seems to work, but the build keeps going. After a run ends, the Build & install button in a popover opened during the run stays disabled until the popover is reopened. The phone map grows slowly without bound.

**Fix.** Reset `run` to None when an install starts. Keep a weak ref to the install button in Phone and set its sensitivity in phone_status. Remove `phone` entries when a session closes.

**Verifier note.** The map growth is negligible: one small struct per session name whose popover was opened, for the life of the process. It does not justify the 'unbounded' framing. The main fixes are to clear `run` in phone_status when busy starts with None, and to have phone_status update a weak ref to the current install button.

#### RA-427 · NON_UNIQUE application: the present-existing-window branch is dead, and a second launch starts a second full client

`apps/relay-native/src/app.rs:322` · **low** · Bug · confirmed · effort S

**Problem.** `.flags(gtk::gio::ApplicationFlags::NON_UNIQUE)` (app.rs:322). activate begins with `if let Some(window) = app.active_window() { window.present(); return; }` (app.rs:325-328), but a NON_UNIQUE app never forwards a second launch to the running process, and nothing in the crate re-emits activate. The installed desktop entry runs run.sh, which ends with `exec "$PWD/target/debug/relay-native"` (run.sh:46).

**Impact.** Launching Relay again (for example from the app menu while its window is on another workspace) opens a second independent client. Both play every notification sound, both write native.layout.current.{project} (shell.rs:305-309), and each follows the other's page switches through ui.changed (app.rs:1247-1248).

**Fix.** Drop NON_UNIQUE and use an instance-specific application id (for example com.quietsoftware.Relay4.dev) so dev and stable can still run side by side; the existing activate branch will then present the running window.

**Verifier note.** NON_UNIQUE probably exists so that clients for different instances can run side by side: scripts/native-smoke.py:114 starts a client with RELAY_INSTANCE=test next to a real one, and dev/stable are separate instances. The fix therefore needs an instance-specific application id (for example com.quietsoftware.Relay4.<instance>, with StartupWMClass and the .desktop file updated to match), as proposed. The trigger is less common than it sounds: GNOME's dash usually focuses an already-running app instead of launching a new one. That is why this is low.

<a id="ra-428"></a>

#### RA-428 · The "Reconnect to engine" key follows the notice's visibility, so it appears beside every message while connected

`apps/relay-native/src/app.rs:969` · **low** · Bug · confirmed · effort S

**Problem.** `ui.notice.connect_label_notify(move |notice| { recovery_label_key.set_visible(!notice.text().is_empty()); })` and `ui.notice.connect_visible_notify(move |notice| recovery_key.set_visible(notice.is_visible()))` (app.rs:963-969). show_error is the single banner for errors, info and toasts (for example "Wait for agent launch to finish before closing.", provider update messages and ui.toast text). Clicking the key runs connect(), which drops the healthy client and stops and recreates every terminal pane (app.rs:1137-1144), with no launch_busy or dirty check.

**Impact.** Users are offered an engine reconnect next to unrelated messages. Using it needlessly re-attaches every terminal, drops keystrokes still queued in each pane's input channel (Pane::stop aborts the input task), loses the wall order (see the reconnect finding) and, mid-launch, removes the launch's placeholder panes.

**Fix.** Show the key only while `!ui.connected.get()`, toggling it wherever `connected` changes, and refuse connect() while launch_busy.

**Verifier note.** Harm only comes from a deliberate click on a key labelled "Reconnect", so the impact is a confusing affordance plus a disruptive re-attach, not silent damage. Low is right. Fix: make the key's visibility depend on `!ui.connected.get()` (toggle it where `connected` is set in connect() and in the close handler), and refuse connect() while launch_busy.

**Also at:** `apps/relay-native/src/app.rs:1131`, `apps/relay-native/src/terminal.rs:576`
