#### RA-429 · The event subscription is a hand-maintained allow-list that omits workspace.deleted, although the router handles every workspace.* event

`apps/relay-native/src/app.rs:1154` · **low** · Bug · confirmed · effort S

**Problem.** The bus.subscribe list (app.rs:1154) includes "workspace.changed" but not "workspace.deleted", which the engine emits on workspace.remove (workspace.rs:179). The router treats `e.ev.starts_with("project.") || e.ev.starts_with("workspace.")` as a registry change (app.rs:1223-1225). The engine's filter supports `prefix.*` subscriptions (socket.rs:212-221).

**Impact.** Removing an empty workspace from the CLI, the phone or another window leaves it in the native sidebar, because no project.deleted accompanies it, until some other registry event arrives. "Add a project…" under it then fails.

**Fix.** Subscribe by prefix for the families the router handles by prefix ("project.*", "workspace.*", "session.*", "notify.*", "guardrail.*", …), and keep the list as one const next to the router.

**Verifier note.** Narrow trigger: only an empty workspace removed by another client. Removing a non-empty one also emits project.deleted, which is subscribed. Adding "workspace.deleted" (or "workspace.*") to the list fixes it.

**Also at:** `crates/relay-core/src/handlers/workspace.rs:179`, `apps/relay-native/src/app.rs:1223`

#### RA-430 · connect() does not re-check the generation after awaiting bus.subscribe, so a superseded attempt marks the UI connected

`apps/relay-native/src/app.rs:1155` · **low** · Concurrency · confirmed · effort S

**Problem.** The generation is checked only before `*ui.client.borrow_mut() = Some(client)` (app.rs:1150-1153). After `ui.call("bus.subscribe",…).await` the code unconditionally runs `ui.connected.set(true)`, `ui.status.set_text("")`, `ui.notice.set_visible(false)`, `ui.refresh()`, `load_appearance()` and so on (app.rs:1154-1164). The Reconnect key is visible while "Connecting to the Relay engine…" is shown (app.rs:963-969), so a second click during a slow subscribe starts generation N+1 while N is still waiting.

**Impact.** The stale continuation hides the new attempt's "Connecting…" banner, clears the status bar and fires refreshes with no client (spurious "Connection closed" errors). If the newer attempt then fails, `connected` stays true: its error auto-dismisses (show_error only times out notices while connected, app.rs:1086-1091) and the status bar stays blank although nothing is connected.

**Fix.** After every await in the connect future, run `if generation != ui.generation.get() { return; }` before touching shared state, including before the device.watch call and on the error paths.

**Verifier note.** Rare in practice. Both connects go to a local Unix socket and bus.subscribe is answered inline (socket.rs:362), so the window is milliseconds. The bad end state, connected stuck at true while nothing is connected, also needs the newer attempt to fail right after the older one succeeded, which is unlikely against the same engine. The usual result is a few spurious "Connection closed" notices from refreshes fired while ui.client is None. Fix: re-check `generation == ui.generation.get()` after each await.

<a id="ra-431"></a>

#### RA-431 · ui.toast text is shown unattributed in the system error banner

`apps/relay-native/src/app.rs:1246` · **low** · Bug · confirmed · effort S

**Problem.** `} else if e.ev == "ui.toast" { ui.show_error(text(&e.payload, "text")); }` (app.rs:1245-1246) ignores `e.actor` and the payload's `level` and `ttl_ms` (handlers/ui.rs:331-333). Agents that were granted allow_ui can call ui.toast (ops/ui.rs:1, 38; guardrail.rs:369-381).

**Impact.** An agent with UI control can place arbitrary text, such as instructions to run a command, in the same banner that carries Relay's own engine errors (with the Reconnect key beside it), and the user cannot tell them apart. Info-level toasts also read as errors.

**Fix.** Prefix the actor ("agent:foo: …"), style by level, honour ttl_ms, and keep the reconnect key off toasts.

**Verifier note.** I rated this a functional bug, not a security issue. allow_ui is a deliberate per-session grant, and it already gives os.open_url, ui.page.switch and pane control (ops/ui.rs). So a spoofed banner adds very little to what such an agent can already do, and the call is audited (Audit::AgentOnly). What is really wrong: level is ignored, so info toasts look like errors; ttl_ms is ignored; nothing shows who sent the toast; and the reconnect key appears next to it. The fix stands: show the toast in its own style, or at least prefix the actor, style it by level, honour ttl_ms, and keep the recovery key off toasts.

**Also at:** `crates/relay-core/src/handlers/ui.rs:331`, `crates/relay-bus/src/ops/ui.rs:38`

<a id="ra-432"></a>

#### RA-432 · Coarse event routing re-fetches whole pages, the full appearance and the Notes rail for unrelated changes

`apps/relay-native/src/app.rs:1264` · **low** · Performance · confirmed · effort M

**Problem.** Every event without a dedicated branch, including usage.changed, notify.*, guardrail.*, run.changed and device.* after their own handling, reaches `} else { ui.refresh_page(); }` (app.rs:1263-1265). On the Board that means task.list, module.list and board_view::show (pages.rs:41-88). Each settings.changed under appearance.* or terminal.font_size calls load_appearance() (app.rs:1257-1262). That issues six settings.get calls, decodes the base64 wallpaper JPEG on the GTK thread, reloads a display-wide CssProvider and restyles every terminal (shell.rs:1116-1245). The Settings page saves one settings.set per changed field (tools_settings.rs:147-151), so one Save triggers the full reload once per appearance field, with no coalescing. Every Ui::refresh() also calls refresh_notes (app.rs:1440): a notes.list plus a full rebuild of the Notes rail and picker (notes_window.rs:206-210, note_pages.rs:1121-1131), although notes changes arrive as their own events (app.rs:1209-1212).

**Impact.** Background agent activity keeps re-querying and re-rendering whichever page is open, adding requests to the single serialized control connection. Saving appearance settings stutters the UI through several main-thread JPEG decodes and CSS recomputes.

**Fix.** Map events to the pages they affect (task.*/module.* → board/modules, mailbox.* → mailbox, guardrail.* → guardrails) and ignore the rest. Coalesce load_appearance with pending/dirty flags as refresh() does, and re-decode the wallpaper only when appearance.wallpaper changed. Drop refresh_notes from refresh() except while the Notes window has no project yet.

**Verifier note.** Part of the claim is overstated. refresh_page is coalesced (page_dirty/page_pending, app.rs:1662-1686) and does nothing on the agents/code pages (app.rs:1672), which is where the user usually is while agents work. So the extra page re-queries only happen when Board, Mailbox or similar is open. refresh_notes returns at once unless the Notes window exists (notes_window.rs:168-177), so it does not rebuild the rail on every refresh(). The cost that remains: several wallpaper decodes and CSS reloads per Save, and Board re-fetches (task.list plus module.list) on unrelated events. Fix: decode the wallpaper only when appearance.wallpaper changed, coalesce load_appearance with a dirty/pending flag, and route events to the pages they affect.

**Also at:** `apps/relay-native/src/app.rs:1257`, `apps/relay-native/src/app.rs:1440`, `apps/relay-native/src/shell.rs:1222`, `apps/relay-native/src/tools_settings.rs:147`

#### RA-433 · refresh() clears registry_dirty before fetching and never restores it on failure, leaving a stale or empty project list (and possibly opening onboarding)

`apps/relay-native/src/app.rs:1372` · **low** · Error handling · confirmed · effort S

**Problem.** `if ui.registry_dirty.replace(false) { let (projects, workspaces) = tokio::join!(ui.call("project.list",…), ui.call("workspace.list",…)); … (Err(e), _) | (_, Err(e)) => { ui.show_error(&e.to_string()); break; } }` (app.rs:1372-1388). Nothing sets the flag back. Later passes skip the registry fetch and use `ui.projects` as it is. With an empty list the next pass sets the project to 0 and runs `if !ui.setup_checked.replace(true) && ui.projects.borrow().is_empty() { ui.open_repository(); }` (app.rs:1412-1414). Realistic failures: a 30 s timeout while the control socket is stalled behind a slow op, or a refresh() triggered by open_project/mutate while connecting (client None → Disconnected). restore_layout has the same consume-before-fetch pattern: it sets restored_project before its settings.get (shell.rs:326-341), so a failed read means that project's saved layout is never applied and the next save_layout overwrites it.

**Impact.** If project.list fails on the first connection, the next refresh shows "No project" and an empty sidebar and opens the add-repository onboarding even though projects exist. On later connections the sidebar stays stale (removed projects listed, new ones missing) until some project.* or workspace.* event arrives.

**Fix.** Set registry_dirty back to true on the error path, or clear it only after a successful fetch. Likewise, set restored_project only after settings.get succeeds.

**Verifier note.** The onboarding scenario needs project.list to fail on the first connection, right after bus.subscribe succeeded on the same client (a 30 s timeout, client.rs:65-70). That is rare. The more likely case is a reconnect where the user clicks during "Connecting…", which leaves a stale list rather than opening onboarding, because setup_checked is already true. The generation-mismatch `continue` at 1377 is safe, since connect() sets the flag again. Fix as proposed: restore the flag on error, or clear it only after success. Do the same for restored_project.

**Also at:** `apps/relay-native/src/app.rs:1412`, `apps/relay-native/src/shell.rs:326`

#### RA-434 · refresh() replaces the wall's session rows wholesale, dropping launch placeholders mid-launch

`apps/relay-native/src/app.rs:1427` · **low** · Bug · confirmed · effort S

**Problem.** `*ui.sessions.borrow_mut() = all.iter().filter(|s| s["project_id"].as_i64() == Some(project)).cloned().collect();` (app.rs:1427-1431) discards the synthetic `"placeholder": true` rows that launch_placeholders pushed (agent_menu.rs:219-223). It also admits the launch's own `created` rows, which apply_session_event deliberately withholds while launch_busy (agent_menu.rs:123-127). launch_adopt then cannot find the placeholder's slot in `ordered` (agent_menu.rs:255-259).

**Impact.** A refresh during a launch (session.create can run for 180 s), triggered by any project.* or workspace.* event such as an edit from the phone or CLI, makes the "new agent N" panes vanish. launch_progress updates then go nowhere, and adopted agents land at the end of the wall instead of in their slot.

**Fix.** While launch_busy, keep placeholder rows and apply the same created-row filter as apply_session_event when replacing ui.sessions.

**Verifier note.** The launch does not trigger this itself. launch_busy is set (launch.rs:779) before open_project (launch.rs:791), so open_project never refreshes there. session.create and session.spawn emit row-bearing session.changed events, which are applied in place. Only an outside refresh() during the launch window causes it: a project.* or workspace.* event from another client, a non-row session event, or another UI action that ends in mutate()/refresh(). The result is cosmetic and temporary: launch_abort and the final refresh() (launch.rs:823-825) restore a consistent wall. Fix as proposed: while launch_busy, keep placeholder rows and filter out `created` rows when refresh() replaces ui.sessions.

**Also at:** `apps/relay-native/src/agent_menu.rs:125`, `apps/relay-native/src/agent_menu.rs:257`

#### RA-435 · verify_burst hard-codes 11 panes, so the perf baseline's burst run (6 sessions) always panics

`apps/relay-native/src/app.rs:1634` · **low** · Bug · confirmed · effort S

**Problem.** app.rs:1634 asserts `assert_eq!(self.panes.borrow().len(), 11);` and app.rs:1659 prints `println!("BURST_RENDERED=11");`. Both are reached from smoke.rs:706 and 749 whenever RELAY_NATIVE_FIXTURE=1 and RELAY_NATIVE_BURST=1.

native-smoke.py happens to build exactly 9+2 sessions. scripts/perf/native-baseline.py:190-193 creates six, then runs `open_page("agents-burst", "agents", {"RELAY_NATIVE_FIXTURE": "1", "RELAY_NATIVE_BURST": "1"}, ...)` (line 259).

**Impact.** The measurement documented in docs/perf/BASELINE-2026-09-19.md:563-567 ('once with the smoke harness's 2 048-line burst into every pane') can never be produced. About 2.5 s in, `assert_eq!(6, 11)` panics and the hook exits 1. The perf row then records exit 1 with counters sampled from a dead process.

**Fix.** Assert against `self.sessions.borrow().len()`, or an expected count passed in an env var, and print the actual count. Let native-smoke.py assert `BURST_RENDERED=11` itself.

**Verifier note.** Only the perf script's burst row is affected; the smoke harness itself passes. Fix: assert against the session count, or an expected count passed in an env var, and print the real count. native-smoke.py keeps its own `BURST_RENDERED=11` check.

#### RA-436 · Grouping by size orders the groups L, M, None, S, and the fallback groups sort among the real ones

`apps/relay-native/src/board_view.rs:131` · **low** · Bug · confirmed · effort S

**Problem.** For size and type, group_of falls back to `key => task[key].as_str().unwrap_or("None").to_string()` (131), and sorted() orders by that raw string (1522-1524). Only priority gets an ordinal prefix (127-130). The fallbacks 'Top level', 'No module' and 'Unassigned' (118-125) also sort by spelling; 'Unassigned' sorts ahead of every lowercase session name because 'U' < 'a'.

**Impact.** With 'group by size', the groups appear as L, M, None, S, which is not size order. The fallback groups land in arbitrary positions among the real ones.

**Fix.** Prefix size with an ordinal as priority already does ("0 S", "1 M", "2 L", "9 None") and strip it in group_title. Force the fallback groups to sort last.

**Verifier note.** Purely cosmetic. Type is in the same position but has no natural order, so only size is clearly wrong. The fix as proposed is right: give size an ordinal prefix through SIZES and strip it in group_title (134), and push the fallback groups to the end.

#### RA-438 · The board header's workspace picker is built once per mount and goes stale when projects are added, renamed or deleted

`apps/relay-native/src/board_view.rs:513` · **low** · Bug · confirmed · effort S

**Problem.** Board::mount appends `workspace_picker(ui, project, "board")` (513). workspace_picker reads ui.projects and ui.workspaces when it is built (pages.rs:187-249). The header is not rebuilt until the project changes (show, 479-490). The Notes workspace, by contrast, rebuilds its picker on every refresh: `clear(&shell.picker); shell.picker.append(&super::workspace_picker(ui, project, "notes"));` (note_pages.rs:1121-1122).

**Impact.** While the board stays open: a renamed project keeps its old name in the header; a newly added project is missing from the menu; a deleted project is still listed, and choosing it switches to an id that the next refresh() rejects.

**Fix.** Keep a slot Box in the header and rebuild the picker in render() or show(), the way note_pages::workspace does.

**Verifier note.** If the open project itself is deleted, refresh() switches ui.project, and the next show() remounts with a fresh picker. The stale state therefore only affects other projects: renamed, added or deleted ones. Picking a stale deleted id leads to an open_project on a missing row, which the next refresh resolves by falling back to the first project.

#### RA-439 · The header 'New task' button always opens quick-create on Backlog; its focused-card lookup can never succeed

`apps/relay-native/src/board_view.rs:747` · **low** · Bug · confirmed · effort S

**Problem.** `add.connect_clicked(move |_| { ... let column = board.current().map(|(column, _)| column); board.open_quick(column.as_deref().unwrap_or("backlog")); })` (745-750). current() reads the window's live focus (968). By the time `clicked` fires, a mouse press has already moved focus to the button: GtkButton focus-on-click is on by default and button() does not change it. Activating the button from the keyboard also needs focus on it. current() therefore always returns None.

**Impact.** With a card focused in Ready, clicking 'New task' preselects Backlog, not Ready as the code intends. Only the C key preselects the column correctly.

**Fix.** Use the remembered card instead: `board.focused.get().and_then(|id| board.task(id)).map(|t| text(&t, "column").to_string())`.

**Verifier note.** This depends on GTK's focus-on-click behaviour, which was not checked against 4.22 in a running build. Note that the remembered `focused` id may belong to a Done card. "done" is not in QUICK_COLUMNS, so open_quick still falls back to index 0, which is harmless.

**Also at:** `apps/relay-native/src/board_view.rs:967`

<a id="ra-442"></a>

#### RA-442 · Capture-phase board keys steal Enter, Space and arrows from card buttons and from popovers inside the page

`apps/relay-native/src/board_view.rs:998` · **low** · Bug · confirmed · effort S

**Problem.** The page's key controller runs in the capture phase (646). It steps aside only for `widget.is::<gtk::Editable>() || widget.is::<gtk::TextView>()` (995-1002). current() treats any focus inside a card as the card itself: `.position(|(_, card)| focus == *card || focus.is_ancestor(card))` (972). With focus on a card's Copy, Peek or Open button (1714-1738), Enter is claimed by `Key::Return ... => task_pages::open` (1088-1092) and Space by `toggle_peek` (1093-1097). Both return Stop before the button sees the key. The card's context menu is parented to the card (2095), so the same applies to its items. Arrow keys are handled whatever has focus (1053-1075, falling back to focus_board()). Escape closes the quick bar and clears its title (1038-1041), or closes the peek.

**Impact.** Certain: Tab to a card's Copy button and press Enter or Space. The editor opens or the peek toggles, and nothing is copied. Not established, because it needs GTK4 to propagate popover key events through the popover's parent chain to the page, which I could not run: (1) in the menu opened with '.', Enter on 'Delete task' or on a MOVE TO key opens the full editor instead; (2) Down in that menu, in a quick-bar DropDown list or in the workspace/filter popovers moves focus to a card; (3) Escape to dismiss a quick-bar DropDown list closes the bar and throws away the typed title. This breaks keyboard use of a board designed to be keyboard-first.

**Fix.** In key(), return Proceed when any focus ancestor is a gtk::Popover, or is a Button, DropDown or MenuButton other than the card itself. Make current() match only `focus == *card`, or count a descendant as the card only when it is not interactive. Alternatively, attach the controller to `content` in the bubble phase so focused widgets handle their keys first.

**Verifier note.** The popover cases are not established. The '.' menu (2094-2095) and DropDown lists are popovers parented to the card or the bar, and whether their key events pass through the page's capture controller depends on whether GTK puts a grab on autohide popovers, which would stop propagation at the popover. I could not verify that without the GTK C sources or a build. The author tests the keyboard-first menu, which also argues against that part. The confirmed part only affects Tab-focused card tool buttons, mostly Copy, since Open and Peek have key equivalents, so it rates low. Fix: in key(), return Proceed when focus is a Button, DropDown or MenuButton, or sits inside a Popover, rather than on the card itself. Or make current() match only `focus == *card`.

**Also at:** `apps/relay-native/src/board_view.rs:646`, `apps/relay-native/src/board_view.rs:972`, `apps/relay-native/src/board_view.rs:1088`, `apps/relay-native/src/board_view.rs:1053`, `apps/relay-native/src/board_view.rs:2095`

#### RA-443 · Ctrl+Z bypasses the undo button's in-flight guard, so key repeat fires overlapping undos

`apps/relay-native/src/board_view.rs:1004` · **low** · Concurrency · confirmed · effort S

**Problem.** undo_last disables the button while it runs (`key.set_sensitive(false)`, 875). Ctrl+Z, however, calls `self.undo.emit_clicked()` (1003-1005), and emitting the signal runs the handler whether or not the button is sensitive. Each call spawns its own audit.list followed by audit.undo (877-902).

**Impact.** Holding Ctrl+Z, or pressing it twice quickly, starts several undo_last tasks at once. Every list answered before the first undo commits picks the same row; the extra undos fail with 'audit row N was already undone' in the banner, and later ones undo further rows. How many steps get undone is unpredictable.

**Fix.** Return early from the Ctrl+Z branch when `!self.undo.is_sensitive()`, or keep an `undoing: Cell<bool>` on Board that undo_last checks and sets.

**Verifier note.** The practical effect is a spurious error banner on a quick double press, or a varying number of steps undone under key repeat. Nothing is corrupted, because the already-undone check runs inside the transaction. Fix: check `self.undo.is_sensitive()` in the Ctrl+Z branch, or call activate() / use an `undoing: Cell<bool>` guard.

**Also at:** `apps/relay-native/src/board_view.rs:875`

#### RA-444 · Board shortcuts compare raw keyvals, so they stop working while Caps Lock is on

`apps/relay-native/src/board_view.rs:1053` · **low** · Bug · confirmed · effort S

**Problem.** key() matches lowercase keyvals directly (`Key::j | Key::k`, `Key::c`, `Key::n`, `Key::f`, `Key::v`, `Key::g`, `Key::p`; 1053-1134). It treats an uppercase J/K as Shift+J/K only when `shift` is set (1014, 1049), and Ctrl+Z requires `key == Key::z` (1003). With Caps Lock on, GDK delivers the uppercase keyval without SHIFT_MASK, so `Key::J` fails the `if shift` guard and no other arm matches.

**Impact.** With Caps Lock on, j/k/h/l navigation, C, N, F, V, G, P and Ctrl+Z all silently do nothing on the board.

**Fix.** Match on `key.to_lower()` for letters, and take the reorder intent from SHIFT_MASK alone.

**Verifier note.** Normalise once at the top with `let key = key.to_lower();` and take the reorder intent from SHIFT_MASK alone (Shift+j/k and Shift+Up/Down). Ctrl+Z is covered by the same normalisation.

#### RA-445 · Scroll positions are restored by index, so V or hiding a column applies offsets to the wrong scroller

`apps/relay-native/src/board_view.rs:1223` · **low** · Bug · confirmed · effort S

**Problem.** `let saved: Vec<f64> = self.scrolls.borrow().iter().map(|a| a.value()).collect();` (1187) is zipped onto the new scrollers by position (1223-1234). The scroller list differs by view: the board pushes its horizontal adjustment first, then one vertical adjustment per visible lane (1610, 1634); the list pushes a single vertical adjustment (1855). The restore handler stays connected until the saved offset becomes reachable.

**Impact.** Switching from board to list applies the board's horizontal offset to the list's vertical scroll, and switching back does the reverse. Hiding Backlog gives Ready the old Backlog offset, Active the old Ready offset, and so on. When a saved offset cannot be reached immediately, the armed handler can jump the lane later (for example on a window resize), after the user has scrolled.

**Fix.** Key the saved values by role ("board-h", "lane:<column>", "list") in a map and restore only matching keys. Disconnect the handler once it has fired, or after the first allocation.

**Verifier note.** The 'jumps later after the user has scrolled' part is minor: the handler fires once, and the next render (on any event) discards the adjustment. The main bug is the index-based mapping. Key the saved offsets by role (board-h, lane:<column>, list).

<a id="ra-450"></a>

#### RA-450 · The reader drains pending replies before closing the notice channel, so a request issued in between waits its full timeout; the comment says the opposite

`apps/relay-native/src/client.rs:264` · **low** · Concurrency · confirmed · effort S

**Problem.** On exit the reader runs `for (_, reply) in waiting.lock().unwrap().drain() {…}`, then `// Close before notifying so request callers and drains cannot wait forever.` followed by `let _ = reader_notices.send(Notice::Disconnected(error)).await; reader_notices.close();` (client.rs:259-265). The code notifies first, with an await that blocks while the 64-slot queue is full, and closes afterwards. request_with_id's only guard is `if self.0.notices.is_closed()` before inserting into `pending` (client.rs:309-315). A request made in that window is inserted after the drain. If the reader died of a protocol error (such as the 2 MiB cap), the writer and socket are still alive: the request is written, its reply is never read, and because the caller's Client clone keeps the Connection alive, Connection::drop never clears it.

**Impact.** Such a request hangs for its whole timeout (30 s; 180 s for session.create/task.dispatch; 30 min for project.clone) instead of failing immediately.

**Fix.** Track the closed state inside the pending mutex (for example Option<HashMap>) and set it in the same critical section as the drain, so request_with_id refuses atomically. Correct the comment.

**Verifier note.** Simply reordering to close-then-send would lose the Disconnected notice (async_channel rejects send after close), and is_closed-then-insert would still be a TOCTOU. Use the proposed fix: keep closed state inside the pending mutex (Option<HashMap>) and set it in the same critical section as the drain. Also fix the comment. Impact is limited to a rare stray 30 s wait.

**Also at:** `apps/relay-native/src/client.rs:309`

But git.status returns "HEAD" for a detached head (`.unwrap_or_else(|| "HEAD".into())`, crates/relay-core/src/handlers/git.rs:166-171). upstream is then None, so `can_push = upstream.is_none() || ...` is true (495), the key reads "Publish" (510-516), and the "Not published to a remote" cloud icon is shown (198-203).

#### RA-452 · A stale Git panel stays usable after a checkout switch or a failed status, and its keys act on the newly selected checkout

`apps/relay-native/src/code_git.rs:483` · **low** · Bug · confirmed · effort S

**Problem.** refresh_git returns without touching the panel when the scope changed or git.status failed (160-169). select_checkout and open_path change self.worktree and call refresh_git, but they neither clear e.git nor bump git_revision (project_files.rs:87-106, editor.rs:903-911). If a refresh is already in flight, the new one waits for it to finish, including its git.pr.list call. The panel's closures read the scope when clicked, not when rendered: `ed.git_action(&ui, op, json!({"paths":paths}), None)` (483) and `json!({"paths":[path]})` (917), and git_action builds its payload with `self.payload(ui, extra)` from the current self.worktree (1224). open_diff from a row does the same (896-899).

**Impact.** For several seconds after picking another checkout, the old checkout's change list stays clickable. When status keeps failing (for example, the selected agent worktree was removed), it stays clickable indefinitely. "Stage all changes" then runs `git add -- <the old checkout's paths>` in the newly selected checkout, which may be an agent's worktree, and a row opens the same path in the other checkout.

**Fix.** On a scope change, clear e.git and bump git_revision, as reset() does. Capture project and worktree when each row or key is rendered, pass them explicitly in the payload, and refuse when `!e.matches(...)`. When git.status fails, replace the panel with the error instead of keeping stale rows.

**Verifier note.** The impact is smaller than claimed. select_checkout clears the commit message, so the stale Commit keys refuse with "Enter a commit message first". Stage and unstage are reversible index changes, and they fail with a pathspec error unless the same paths are also changed in the new checkout. The "indefinitely" case on a failed git.status mostly involves a checkout where git_action would fail as well, for example a removed worktree. The window is normally well under a second, or a few seconds with a slow PR list. Fix: on a scope change, clear e.git (or make it insensitive) and bump git_revision. Capture project and worktree in the row closures and refuse when they no longer match.

**Also at:** `apps/relay-native/src/code_git.rs:160-169`, `apps/relay-native/src/code_git.rs:917`, `apps/relay-native/src/code_git.rs:1224`, `apps/relay-native/src/project_files.rs:87-106`, `apps/relay-native/src/editor.rs:903-911`

#### RA-453 · git_action silently drops its result if the open document changed while it ran

`apps/relay-native/src/code_git.rs:1248` · **low** · Error handling · confirmed · effort S

**Problem.** After the op returns: `if !e.matches(&ui, project, &worktree) || revision != e.revision.get() { return; }` (1248-1250). `revision` is the document revision, which any read_file bumps. read_file checks only `self.busy`, not git_busy (editor.rs:617-621), and clicking a search hit calls it directly (editor.rs:1163-1166). The early return does protect edits made in a file opened during the action from clear_document, but it also skips everything else.

**Impact.** Opening a file from search results while a push, fetch or commit is running throws the outcome away. A rejected push's error is never shown, the commit message is not cleared, refresh_git and refresh_scopes do not run after the action, and a branch switch refused as git.checkout_dirty never offers "Bring changes".

**Fix.** While the scope still matches, always handle messages, errors, the refresh and the dialogs. Skip only the document-affecting steps (set_busy(false), clear_document, load_tree) when the document revision has moved.

**Verifier note.** The panel refresh the finding says is lost mostly comes back anyway. The engine emits git.changed after a mutation, and invalidate then runs refresh_git and refresh_scopes. What is really lost is the user-facing outcome: error and success toasts, the commit-message clear and the checkout_dirty dialog. The trigger is a narrow interaction, so low is right. Fix: check only the scope match before handling the result, and gate only the document-affecting steps on the revision.

#### RA-454 · Diff line mapping assumes lines end only at LF, but the engine's diff also ends a line at a lone CR

`apps/relay-native/src/code_git.rs:1640` · **low** · Bug · confirmed · effort M

**Problem.** diff_marks and inline_diff walk `unified.lines()` and `new.lines()` (1640, 1676, 1679), which split only on \n. The engine builds hunks with similar's TextDiff::from_lines, whose tokenizer also ends a line at a lone '\r' (similar-2.7.0 src/text/abstraction.rs:101-120). GtkTextBuffer also breaks lines at '\r'.

**Impact.** For files containing a lone CR (old Mac line endings, captured progress output), a removed line can be merged into a context line (" a\r-b" is read as one context line) and every later line number shifts. Red and green marks land on the wrong lines, and inline mode shows text in the wrong place.

**Fix.** Have the engine return structured hunks (tag plus old and new line numbers) instead of re-parsing text, or split lines with the same rules as similar.

**Verifier note.** This only affects files that contain a lone CR, so low is right. A minimal fix is to split the unified text, and `new`, with the same CR/LF/CRLF rule similar uses. Returning structured hunks from the engine is the more robust option.

#### RA-455 · is_dirty() treats an in-flight read as unsaved changes, so closing the window and switching projects are refused with a misleading message

`apps/relay-native/src/editor.rs:452` · **low** · Bug · confirmed · effort S

**Problem.** `self.buffer.is_modified() || self.busy.get() || self.git_busy.get()` (452). `busy` is also set while merely reading a file (read_file, 627), an image (open_image) or a diff (open_diff). The close handler refuses with 'Save or discard your editor changes before closing.' (app.rs:1046-1049). open_project refuses with 'Save or discard editor changes before switching projects.' (shell.rs:15-18). refresh() stops at app.rs:1397-1400.

**Impact.** Closing the window or switching project while a file is still loading is refused with a message about unsaved changes that do not exist. The load can take up to the 30 s request timeout when the UI connection is backlogged.

**Fix.** Split is_dirty into has_unsaved_edits() (modified, or a write in flight) and is_loading(). Let navigation and close cancel loads by bumping the revision instead of refusing.

**Verifier note.** Also affects app.rs:1691 (adding a project). A write or git op in flight should still block close. Only the read, image and diff loads should be cancellable by bumping `revision`. A simple fix is to have is_dirty() check modified || git_busy || a separate `writing` flag.

#### RA-457 · Editing a CRLF file inserts LF-only lines, so the saved file has mixed line endings

`apps/relay-native/src/editor.rs:660` · **low** · Bug · confirmed · effort S

**Problem.** read_file loads the raw text with `e.buffer.set_text(content)` (660), and save_file writes `self.buffer.text(&start, &end, false)` back verbatim (689-692). There is no newline-type detection (GtkSourceFile/FileLoader is not used), and GtkTextView/GtkSourceView insert "\n" for Enter.

**Impact.** Saving a Windows-origin file (.bat, .sln, an Unreal .ini) after adding lines leaves CRLF and LF lines mixed. This shows up as diff noise and can break tools that expect one convention.

(code_git.rs:1722-1762). For the user, protected paths and large rewrites are holds (guardrail.rs:1028-1034 user_bypass).

**Verifier note.** The realistic triggers are protected_paths and shape_gates. A large rewrite of a tracked file is usually not held (allow_if_recoverable). The user can recover by discarding and reloading, so this is a UX gap rather than a stuck state. Fix: reuse guarded() for the editor's file.write and the other file.* mutations. On success it returns the outcome result, so the baseline can then be updated.

After an answer, the keys go insensitive and the card is removed, leaving no widget focused.

**Impact.** A user typing in an agent terminal who answers a prompt must click back into the terminal before their keystrokes land again.

**Fix.** Call `set_focus_on_click(false)` on each prompt key (once, always, deny, X, more), or remember the previously focused widget and restore it in close_prompt; correct the comment.

**Verifier note.** The Deny form grabs focus on purpose (entry.grab_focus at ~399). That is fine and should stay. The fix is to set focus_on_click(false) on once, always, deny, X and the overflow key, and to correct the comments at 516 and 566.

**Also at:** `apps/relay-native/src/guardrail_pages.rs:445`, `apps/relay-native/src/guardrail_pages.rs:455`

<a id="ra-464"></a>

#### RA-464 · A prompt can outlive its request: shown after a stale read, stale waiting entries promoted, and error paths leave it up

`apps/relay-native/src/guardrail_pages.rs:683` · **low** · Bug · confirmed · effort S

**Problem.** guardrail_event awaits `guardrail.request.get`, then shows the prompt if `request["state"] == "open"` (682-684). It does not re-check whether a `guardrail.resolved` for that id was processed during the await. restore_prompts closes stale tray prompts (709-713) before it filters WAITING against `open` (714), so close_prompt can promote a waiting entry that is itself stale. When confirm or reject fails because the hold is already resolved (`guardrail.hold_resolved`), the approve path only re-enables the keys (483-488).

**Impact.** A request answered from the phone or CLI, or expired, while its prompt is being fetched stays on screen. Pressing Approve then shows "hold N is Confirmed", and the prompt remains until the user finds the X.

**Fix.** Track resolved ids (or reuse DISMISSED) and skip show_prompt for them after the await. In restore_prompts, filter WAITING first. On a `guardrail.hold_resolved` or `not_found` error, call `close_prompt(id)` instead of re-enabling the keys.

**Verifier note.** Part 2 (a stale waiting entry promoted) is the reliable trigger. It needs more than TRAY_LIMIT=3 open requests and a session that has requests both in the tray and in WAITING when it closes. Part 1 (the stale-read race) is a narrow window of one local round trip. Part 3 is what makes either case linger. The fix is right: filter WAITING before the close loop, record ids resolved while a fetch is in flight, and close the prompt on a hold-resolved or not-found error instead of turning the keys back on.

**Also at:** `apps/relay-native/src/guardrail_pages.rs:709`, `apps/relay-native/src/guardrail_pages.rs:714`, `apps/relay-native/src/guardrail_pages.rs:483`

`apps/relay-native/src/icons.rs:231` · **low** · Bug · confirmed · effort M

The effect is purely cosmetic and transient, so low. Two fixes are reasonable: repaint when the button's css-classes change and after an appearance reload, or install the glyphs as *-symbolic icons in a theme search path so GTK recolours them.

<a id="ra-467"></a>

#### RA-467 · Hover thumbnails download and fully decode the whole file on every hover, cannot be cancelled, and have no size or concurrency limit

`apps/relay-native/src/image_preview.rs:338` · **low** · Performance · confirmed · effort M

**Problem.** After HOVER_DELAY the timeout calls `Client::image_read(..., "max_bytes":MAX_BYTES)` (338-339), which opens a new socket every time (client.rs:124-130), then `spawn_blocking(move || decode_to(value, THUMB_EDGE))` (344-349). decode_to only shrinks the image after a full decode, so a 256 px thumbnail costs a full-resolution decode. Leaving the row or closing the card does not cancel the read or the decode, and nothing limits how many run at once. The explorer already knows each file's size (the hover stamp, editor.rs:871) but does not use it to skip large files. For files over 16 MiB the engine still reads and base64-encodes 16 MiB (about 21 MiB on the wire) before the client throws it away as truncated.

**Impact.** Moving the pointer down a folder of 8K textures, common in the Unreal/Blender projects Relay targets, starts a 268 MB decode for each row the pointer rests on. Each decode follows a ~21 MiB socket transfer and keeps running after the pointer has moved on, several in parallel. That is seconds of CPU and gigabytes of transient memory for thumbnails no one is looking at any more.

**Fix.** Skip thumbnails for files above a size threshold, using the size the tree already reports. Allow one thumbnail in flight (latest wins) and drop results for closed cards. Ask the engine for a downscaled thumbnail instead of the raw file.

**Verifier note.** Lines: the request is at image_preview.rs:337-339, the decode at 341-349 and the cache store at 359. Impact: a one-time cost per file per stamp (results are cached), started only after a 350 ms dwell, with no main-thread freeze. Full-size decode applies to PNG and similar formats; the JPEG loader DCT-scales. Cheapest fix: in bind_image_hover, skip the fetch when the known size exceeds MAX_BYTES and cache a 'too large' caption without a round trip. This needs the size passed alongside the stamp, because editor.rs:871 has it and code_git.rs:901 does not. Optionally drop the result when the popover has closed. A server-side downscale is a larger change than the payoff justifies.

**Also at:** `apps/relay-native/src/image_preview.rs:275-361`, `apps/relay-native/src/client.rs:124-130`, `apps/relay-native/src/editor.rs:871`

<a id="ra-468"></a>

#### RA-468 · The thumbnail cache keeps transient failures

`apps/relay-native/src/image_preview.rs:359` · **low** · Bug · confirmed · effort S

**Problem.** Failures are cached like successes: `Err(error) => Thumb { texture: None, caption: format!("No preview · {error}") }` and then `remember(key, thumb.clone())` (357-359). An explorer row's key uses size:mtime as its stamp (editor.rs:871), and a timeout or a lost connection does not change either.

**Impact.** A hover during a 30 s timeout, an engine restart or a reconnect shows "No preview · Request timed out…" for that image on every later hover, until the file changes or 64 newer thumbnails push the entry out.

**Fix.** Cache only successful decodes and errors that will not change on retry (bad format, over the limit). Do not cache transport errors.

**Verifier note.** This applies fully to explorer rows (editor.rs:871). Code-git rows (code_git.rs:901) recover on the next git_revision bump. Fix: call remember() only for Ok results and for deterministic decode errors (truncated, format or dimension errors). Do not cache Err values that come from Client::image_read or from a spawn_blocking join failure.

**Also at:** `apps/relay-native/src/editor.rs:871`

`apps/relay-native/src/launch.rs:621` · **low** · Error handling · confirmed · effort S

Each card then does `let installed = info.is_some_and(|p| p["installed"] == true); key.set_sensitive(installed);` and its caption falls back to "CLI not installed" (632-646), while the footer still says "Ready to launch" (769). A Codex-only user must switch every agent's provider by hand before Launch works.

In practice provider.list fails only when task.list fails too, as on a disconnect, and that path already shows task_result's error. The more relevant half is that Codex-only users always start on Claude. Fix: when provider.list fails, show the error, and default each profile to the first installed provider.

#### RA-472 · Mirror key-up events are recomputed from release-time modifiers, leaving keys stuck down or sending lone key-ups

`apps/relay-native/src/mirror.rs:571` · **low** · Bug · confirmed · effort S

**Problem.** Press sends DOWN for `input::keycode(key).or_else(|| (ctrl || alt).then(|| input::chord_keycode(key)).flatten())` (508). Release recomputes that expression from the release event's modifiers (526-529) instead of remembering what was sent. Press also intercepts Escape-in-full-screen (484-487) and Ctrl+V (493-505) without sending a DOWN, while release excludes only F11 (523).

**Impact.** Press Ctrl+A and release Ctrl before A: the device gets DOWN(KEYCODE_A, CTRL) and never an UP, so its input state keeps A pressed. Esc to leave full screen sends a lone UP for KEYCODE_BACK, and Ctrl+V sends a lone UP for KEYCODE_V with CTRL. Android usually drops such events, but the key stream is malformed and effects vary by app.

**Fix.** Record, per hardware keycode (the `keycode` callback argument), the Android keycode sent on press, e.g. in a `RefCell<HashMap<u32, u32>>`. On release, send UP only for a recorded entry and remove it; clear the map when a session ends.

**Verifier note.** Rare and mostly absorbed by Android's input consistency checks, so it stays low. Fix as proposed: keep a map from hardware keycode to the Android keycode sent on press, send UP only for a recorded entry, and clear the map in start()/close().

**Also at:** `apps/relay-native/src/mirror.rs:484`, `apps/relay-native/src/mirror.rs:493`, `apps/relay-native/src/mirror.rs:508`

#### RA-475 · Rotation resize swaps the window's axes without clamping to the monitor

`apps/relay-native/src/mirror.rs:1010` · **low** · Bug · confirmed · effort S

**Problem.** On an orientation change, `window.set_default_size(phone_h + CHROME_W, phone_w + CHROME_H)` (899-901) just swaps the current phone area. The initial size from `window_size` is clamped to 560..=960 px tall (688).

**Impact.** If the window first opened while the device was in landscape (about 1816×918 on a 1080p monitor, per 693), rotating to portrait requests about 878×1856, pushing the nav bar and hint line off-screen.

**Fix.** Clamp the new height to the same monitor-derived bound `window_size` uses, and derive the width from the picture's aspect ratio.

**Verifier note.** The trigger is narrower than 'first opened in landscape'. On a fresh open, dims is (0,0), so window_size uses the 9:19.5 portrait default, and the first landscape frame does not count as a rotation (ow==0). A portrait window rotating twice round-trips correctly (455x918 → 878x495 → 455x918). An oversized request needs a landscape-shaped window first: undocking or moving a dock out (detach → window_size with known landscape dims) while the device is in landscape, or a user-enlarged window. Fix: clamp the new height to the window_size bound and derive the width from the aspect ratio.

**Also at:** `apps/relay-native/src/mirror.rs:688`

<a id="ra-476"></a>

#### RA-476 · Screenshot is PNG-encoded and written synchronously on the GTK thread, and a destination with no local path is silently ignored

`apps/relay-native/src/mirror.rs:1051` · **low** · Error handling · confirmed · effort S

**Problem.** After the file dialog, `let Some(path) = file.path() else { return };` (941) drops any GIO location without a local path, with no message. `texture.save_to_png(&path)` (943) encodes and writes on the main loop.

**Impact.** Choosing a network/GVFS location that has no FUSE path saves nothing and reports nothing. Saving to a slow or FUSE-mounted path freezes the whole UI (main window and every mirror) until the write finishes.

**Fix.** Use `texture.save_to_png_bytes()` with `file.replace_contents_future(bytes, None, false, gio::FileCreateFlags::REPLACE_DESTINATION)`, which is async and works for any GFile, and flash the error on failure.

**Verifier note.** The impact is a short, user-initiated UI stall and a rare silent no-op, not a general freeze. The proposed fix (save_to_png_bytes plus File::replace_contents_future, and flashing the error in the None branch) is sound. Note that save_to_png_bytes still encodes on the main thread, so only the write becomes async; moving the encode off-thread needs the texture downloaded first. This is native-client code that cannot be compiled in this environment.

`apps/relay-native/src/note_pages.rs:1361` · **low** · Bug · confirmed · effort S

**Problem.** The snapshot normalizes the icon: `"icon":if icon.text().trim().is_empty(){Value::Null}else{json!(icon.text().trim())}` (note_pages.rs:1361). `Draft::new(ui, "Module", module.clone(), ...)` keeps the engine's raw value as base. The engine stores whatever it is given: module.create binds `p.icon` unchanged (handlers/module.rs:122), and module.update does `let icon=p.icon.unwrap_or(before.icon.clone())` with no trim or empty-to-NULL step (module.rs:158). `UpdateIn.icon` is `Option<Option<String>>` (relay-bus ops/module.rs:21), so `"icon":""` and `"icon":" bug "` are both accepted. `Draft::dirty` compares each key: `m.iter().any(|(k, v)| self.base.borrow()[k] != *v)` (task_pages.rs:174-179), and `can_close` refuses while dirty (task_pages.rs:137-140). The two first-party clients normalize before sending (native create sends no icon, note_pages.rs:1317; mobile sends `icon.trim() || null`, Module.tsx:142). So the raw value comes from an agent, the CLI or MCP calling module.create/module.update.

**Impact.** An agent sets a module's icon to "" or " x ". The user opens that module: the editor shows the unsaved-changes state immediately, close and navigation are refused with "Save your changes or choose Discard and close", and "Add task" is gated the same way. Saving the untouched form clears it, but it also rewrites the icon the agent set. This is the same mechanism as native-tasks#2 and native-notes-b#9, in an editor neither of them covers.

**Fix.** Normalize in the engine: in module.create and module.update, trim the icon and store NULL when it is empty, as the name is already trimmed. That fixes every client at once. Alternatively, build the Draft base by running the stored module through the same normalization the snapshot uses.

**Verifier note.** The trigger is narrower than "an agent". None of the default role allowlists (handlers/settings.rs:36-38: builder, reviewer, docs) includes module.create or module.update. The raw value has to come from a user-run `relay` CLI call with an arbitrary payload, or from a custom role that has been granted module ops. Saving the form also has a side effect: it sends the normalized icon with `expected` set to the raw base, and that passes. The main fix (trim, and store NULL when empty, in module.create/update) is right.

**Also at:** `crates/relay-core/src/handlers/module.rs:122`, `crates/relay-core/src/handlers/module.rs:158`, `apps/relay-native/src/task_pages.rs:174`, `apps/relay-native/src/task_pages.rs:137`, `apps/relay-mobile/app/screens/RelayScreen/Module.tsx:142`

#### RA-482 · Ctrl+scroll zooms a whole step per scroll event, so touchpads and high-resolution wheels jump straight to 50% or 300%

`apps/relay-native/src/note_pages/doc.rs:478` · **low** · Bug · confirmed · effort S

Every event calls `super::zoom(&ui, if dy < 0. { 1 } else { -1 })`, whatever the size of dy. Each step runs set_prefs, which reloads the CSS provider in apply_font and calls persist (note_pages.rs:259-278).

**Impact.** A two-finger Ctrl+scroll sends dozens of small-delta events, so the zoom hits its limit at once, with a CSS reload per event. One notch on a hi-res wheel (several 1/8-notch events) zooms several steps.

**Fix.** Add EventControllerScrollFlags::DISCRETE so GTK accumulates whole steps, or accumulate dy yourself and step when |acc| ≥ 1.

#### RA-483 · F3 in a note whose find field is empty skips the first match

`apps/relay-native/src/note_pages/doc.rs:821` · **low** · Bug · confirmed · effort S

**Problem.** `if self.find.query.text().is_empty() { self.find.query.set_text(&super::last_query()); }`. set_text fires the entry's changed handler (399), so find_incremental runs and selects the first match at or after the cursor (808-813). find_step then calls `self.search.forward(&end)` from the end of that selection (828-833) and selects the second match.

**Impact.** Search "foo" in note A, switch to note B (its find field is empty), press F3: the selection jumps to the second "foo" after the cursor. The first one is skipped.

**Fix.** Pre-fill the query with its changed handler blocked, or set the search text directly without the incremental select, then search forward from the cursor.

**Verifier note.** Only the forward direction (F3, Enter in the entry, the down arrow) skips. The simplest fix is to compute (start, end) from the selection or cursor before pre-filling. You can also block the changed handler while pre-filling, or call settings.set_search_text directly.

The second branch, `selected.starts_with(before) && selected.ends_with(after)`, matches when all of "**bold**" is selected. Both branches delete one '*' from each side.

#### RA-485 · Notice buttons discard unsaved note text in one click: the conflict notice's 'Reload theirs' skips the confirmation and clears undo, and the deleted notice's 'Close' skips the save prompt

`apps/relay-native/src/note_pages/doc.rs:1167` · **low** · Data loss · confirmed · effort S

**Problem.** Conflict notice: `("Reload theirs", |ui, doc| reload(ui, doc, false))`. reload(…, false) never asks, and doc.load() then replaces the text inside `begin_irreversible_action()` (524-526), which clears the undo stack. The reconcile notice's identical button calls `reload(ui, doc, true)` (1355), which does ask "Your unsaved changes to this note will be lost." Deleted notice: `("Close", |ui, doc| discard_close(ui, doc))` (1191). discard_close copies the snapshot into base and closes. request_close (1277-1311) would have asked "Save changes … before closing?". The notice also has its own × Dismiss button (658-668), so "Close" reads as closing the notice.

**Impact.** These notices appear exactly when the user has unsaved work: after a save conflict or a remote delete. One click on "Reload theirs" or "Close" discards all of it, with no prompt and no undo. Separately, reconcile's automatic load (1343-1346) also clears the undo history every time an agent changes a note the user has open.

**Fix.** Use reload(ui, doc, true) in the conflict notice. Route the deleted notice's "Close" through request_close, or rename it "Discard and close" and confirm when dirty. Load remote text as a user action instead of an irreversible one so Ctrl+Z can bring the user's text back.

**Verifier note.** I rate this low. Each loss needs a deliberate click on a labelled button. Reconcile's automatic load (1343-1346) runs only when !doc.dirty(), so it never discards unsaved text; it only drops the undo history of already-saved edits, which is minor. The fix is to use reload(ui, doc, true) in the conflict notice and to send "Close" through request_close or rename it "Discard and close".

#### RA-486 · Notes shortcuts compare raw keyvals, so Ctrl+S/N/W/F/H/G/O do nothing on non-Latin keyboard layouts

`apps/relay-native/src/note_pages/menu.rs:429` · **low** · Bug · confirmed · effort M

**Problem.** The capture-phase EventControllerKey (379-386) runs `let lower = key.to_lower(); let name = if mods == ctrl { match lower { Key::n => "new", Key::o => "open", Key::s => "save", ... } }` (429-448). The keyval it receives is already translated for the active layout. GTK's own accelerator matching (GtkShortcutController / gdk_key_event_matches) also matches the same physical key in the first layout, so Ctrl+S works under a Cyrillic layout. This hand-written matcher has no such fallback. The accelerator table also exists a second time as the menus' 'accel' attributes in model() (145-226), and the two have to be kept in agreement by hand.

**Impact.** With a Russian, Greek or Hebrew layout active, Ctrl+S produces Cyrillic_yeru (or the equivalent), no arm matches, and the key falls through. Save, new note, close tab, find, replace, go to line and zoom silently stop working in Notes, while GTK's built-in Ctrl+C/V/Z keep working.

**Fix.** Replace the hand-written dispatcher with a capture-phase gtk::ShortcutController built from a single (trigger, action) table, using ShortcutTrigger::parse_string with NamedAction or CallbackAction. A CallbackAction can keep the body-only rule for Ctrl+B/I/K and the Escape condition. Generate the menu accel attributes from the same table.

**Verifier note.** This only affects users who type with a non-Latin layout active. Function-key and Tab/PageUp bindings are unaffected. A smaller fix than rewriting into a ShortcutController: when the keyval does not match, translate the event's hardware keycode in group 0 (gdk::Display::map_keycode / translate_key) and match on that. The duplicated accel table in model() is a separate low-value maintenance note.

**Also at:** `apps/relay-native/src/note_pages/menu.rs:379-386`, `apps/relay-native/src/note_pages/menu.rs:145-226`

#### RA-487 · The Markdown line helpers misread thematic breaks and indented headings

`apps/relay-native/src/note_pages/text.rs:34` · **low** · Bug · confirmed · effort S

**Problem.** marker() treats `matches!(first, b'-' | b'*' | b'+') && bytes.get(1) == Some(&b' ')` as a bullet, so the CommonMark thematic breaks "* * *" and "- - -" count as list items and list_enter returns Continue("* ") or Continue("- "). heading() counts '#' only from column 0 (84), so toggle_lines(&["  ## Title"], Heading(2)) finds no heading, takes `line.trim_start()` = "## Title" (119) and produces "## ## Title".

**Impact.** Pressing Enter after a "* * *" or "- - -" rule starts a bullet list. Toggling H2 on a heading indented by 1–3 spaces doubles the hashes.

**Fix.** In marker(), return no marker for a line made only of three or more of the same marker character plus spaces. In heading() and toggle_lines, strip up to three leading spaces before counting hashes. Add test cases for both.

**Verifier note.** Impact is narrow. The most common rule spelling, "---", is not affected, because marker() requires a space after the first char. Spaced rules and headings indented by 1-3 spaces are uncommon in hand-written notes.

#### RA-489 · Every notify.* event while the popover is open sends a fresh notify.list and rebuilds every row, and each ack reloads twice

`apps/relay-native/src/notification_center.rs:115` · **low** · Performance · confirmed · effort S

**Problem.** `pub(super) fn changed() { if let Some(center) = center().filter(|c| c.popover.is_visible()) { center.load(); } }`. load() bumps the revision and always sends a request (128-142). The ack handlers call `center.load()` themselves (88, 268), and their own notify.changed event then triggers changed() again. For every notify.* event, app.rs:1196-1200 calls changed() and refresh_notification_count, and sounds::notify adds a notify.settings.get per notify.new (sounds.rs:89-105).

**Impact.** An agent looping on a refused command creates one notification and one notify.new per attempt (handlers/guardrail.rs:538-541). With the popover open, each attempt sends a notify.list (limit 100) on the shared serial connection and rebuilds every row, losing hover and keyboard focus. The revision check then discards all but the last result.

**Fix.** Coalesce the reloads as refresh_notes does: a pending flag plus a single in-flight load that runs once more if events arrived meanwhile. Drop the explicit load() after acks, since the event already triggers one.

**Verifier note.** Only matters while the popover is open. Each load is one indexed query of up to 100 rows, so the cost is wasted bus round-trips and a visible row rebuild (lost hover and focus) during a refusal burst, not a freeze. Dropping the explicit load() after acks and coalescing with a pending flag, as proposed, is the right fix.

#### RA-491 · Following a guardrail-hold notification opens the Guardrails page, and also switches the hidden agent wall to focus mode and saves that layout

`apps/relay-native/src/notification_center.rs:301` · **low** · Bug · confirmed · effort S

The claim that link-less notifications get an 'Open' affordance holds: row() always builds the open button (notification_center.rs:203-205). That is minor doc drift. #### RA-492 · Onboarding pre-fills the workspace with the GUI's raw cwd, bypassing the engine's 'use the parent of the enclosing checkout' suggestion

`apps/relay-native/src/onboarding.rs:75` · **low** · Bug · confirmed · effort S

**Problem.** `workspace_path: gtk::Entry::builder().text(std::env::current_dir().map(|p| p.to_string_lossy().into_owned()).unwrap_or_default())` (73-79). `discover` and `submit` always send this non-empty text (327-330, 518-521). The engine applies its protection only when the path is empty: `canon_workspace` calls `suggested_workspace()` only for empty input (workspace.rs:54-56, 115-116). Its doc says: "When that directory lives inside a Git checkout, use the checkout's parent so discovery presents the repository itself as a project instead of cloning another copy into its source tree" (69-71). That function also reads the engine process's cwd, not the GUI's. The returned `v["path"]` is never read by the client.

**Impact.** If relay-native is started from inside a checkout (`cargo run` in the repo, or any shell cd'ed into a project), the workspace becomes the checkout itself. Discovery then lists only that repo, and a later GitHub clone into this workspace lands inside that repo's working tree (`clone_destination` = workspace/name). Started from a subdirectory, discovery finds nothing. The engine's fix for exactly this case never runs for the native client.

**Fix.** Compute the suggestion client-side from the GUI cwd: walk up the ancestors for .git and use its parent. Alternatively, add a cwd hint to workspace.discover so the engine applies `suggested_workspace_from` to the caller's directory and returns it in `path`, then fill the entry from the returned `path`.

**Verifier note.** Downgraded to low. This is first-run onboarding only. The 'Workspace directory' field is visible and editable, with a Scan button (onboarding.rs:154-158), so the user sees the path before committing. The usual desktop-launcher cwd is $HOME, which the engine heuristic would not change anyway. The trigger is mostly a developer running `cargo run` in the repo. Simplest fix: send an empty path (or omit it) on first discover and fill the entry from the returned `path`.

#### RA-494 · An older workspace scan's error overwrites the result of a newer scan

`apps/relay-native/src/onboarding.rs:360` · **low** · Bug · confirmed · effort S

**Problem.** `discover` bumps `discovery_generation`, and the Ok branch checks `if current != path || setup.discovery_generation.get() != generation { return; }` (340-347). The Err branch has no such check: `Err(e) => setup.message.set_text(&e.to_string()),` (360).

**Impact.** The user scans a slow or unreadable directory, then a good one. The second scan lists its repositories, then the first scan's failure arrives, and the dialog shows an error for a directory that is no longer selected.

**Fix.** Apply the same generation and path check before reporting the error.

**Verifier note.** Mechanism: replies on one connection arrive in request order, so the newer scan's list never arrives before the older error. The stale message stays because discover never clears `self.message` when a new scan starts or when the Ok branch succeeds. A generation check on Err alone only covers the case where the error is still in flight when the user rescans. Fix: clear the message at the start of discover and in the Ok branch, and also apply the same path/generation check to Err. A related engine issue makes this error more common: discover_repositories's walk uses `fs::read_dir(path)?` and `entry?` (workspace.rs:398-401). One unreadable subdirectory within depth 4, such as a root-owned directory under $HOME, therefore fails the whole scan with workspace.discover_failed instead of skipping that directory.

#### RA-495 · Board refresh makes a second, serial module.list call only to label cards. It omits archived modules, so cards in completed modules show as "No module"

`apps/relay-native/src/pages.rs:67` · **low** · Bug · confirmed · effort S

**Problem.** After awaiting task.list, the board branch awaits a second call, `if let Ok(modules) = ui.call("module.list", json!({"project_id":project})).await {` (pages.rs:67). It then joins with `modules.iter().find(|module| module["id"] == task["module_id"])` per task, and keeps only `module["name"]` (pages.rs:68-76). module.list is a locked `register` handler that runs `summary()` (a per-module counts query) for every module, plus `header()`, which runs three aggregate queries (handlers/module.rs:75-104, 145). Without `include_archived` it uses `... AND completed_at IS NULL` (module.rs:145). So a task whose module is completed never gets `_module_name`. board_view then falls back to `unwrap_or("No module")` when grouping (board_view.rs:119), excludes it from the module-name search text (board_view.rs:111), and labels the filter `Module #{id}` (board_view.rs:1411).

**Impact.** Every board refresh pays a second round trip on the serialized control connection, which runs N+3 SQL queries under the store mutex just to look up names. Refreshes fire on every task event and every session.changed event (native-tasks#8). In normal use, completing a module that still has tasks makes those cards lose their module chip and show up under "No module" when grouped by module. Searching for the module name no longer finds them.

**Fix.** Have task.list return `module_name` through a LEFT JOIN on modules, regardless of completed_at. Then drop the module.list call and the per-task linear find. Short of that, pass `include_archived: true`.

**Verifier note.** The main impact is mislabeling, not cost. The extra serialized round trip is real but small. Completing a module is a normal action, but what goes wrong is cosmetic and filtering behavior, so this stays low. The fix is fine: a LEFT JOIN that returns module_name from task.list. #### RA-502 · Sidebar drag reorder rewrites every sibling's order with N sequential updates; a mid-way failure leaves the order half-applied

`apps/relay-native/src/shell.rs:106` · **low** · Performance · confirmed · effort M

**Problem.** 105-126: `for (order, item) in items.into_iter().enumerate() { ... ui.call(if workspace {"workspace.update"} else {"project.update"}, payload).await ... Err(e) => { ui.show_error(..); break; } }`. Every item in the group is sent, including those whose order did not change. Each update emits project.changed or workspace.changed, and each event sets registry_dirty and calls refresh (app.rs:1223-1225). Each update also records its own undo entry (workspace.rs:281-285).

**Impact.** Dragging within a workspace of N projects means N round trips with the sidebar insensitive, N events, several full re-lists, and repeated tree rebuilds (each of which leaks, per the other findings). If a call fails part-way, some items are renumbered and others are not, which leaves duplicate order values and an order scrambled by id tie-breaks.

**Fix.** Send only the items whose order changed (usually a contiguous range). Better: add a single reorder op that writes all orders in one transaction and emits one event.

**Verifier note.** There is also a user-visible cost the finding leaves out. One drag records N undo entries, so undoing a drag takes N undos, each one restoring a single item. The claim that each tree rebuild leaks rests on other findings and was not checked here. Fix: send only the items whose order changed. Better, add one reorder op that writes all orders in a single transaction with one undo entry and one event.

#### RA-509 · Shortcut matching compares the layout-translated character: no shortcuts on non-Latin layouts, and shifted punctuation never matches

`apps/relay-native/src/shortcuts.rs:44` · **low** · Bug · confirmed · effort M

**Problem.** `key.to_unicode().and_then(|c| c.to_lowercase().next()) == Some(letter)`. Under a Cyrillic or Greek layout, Ctrl+K produces the Cyrillic keyval, so no chord matches. For a chord such as "Ctrl+Shift+,", holding Shift produces the keyval `less` ('<') rather than ',', yet `valid()` accepts the chord.

**Impact.** Users with a non-Latin layout active get no shortcuts at all, and some chords the settings page accepts can never fire.

**Fix.** Use GTK's trigger matching (`gtk::ShortcutTrigger::parse_string` with `gdk::KeyEvent::matches`, which falls back across layout groups), or compare the hardware keycode translated in group 0. Reject shifted punctuation in `valid()`.

**Verifier note.** Shifted digits are affected as well as punctuation. A simple fix: when to_unicode does not match, compare against the keyval translated from the keycode in group 0 (the display's map_keycode or translate_key), or use gtk::ShortcutTrigger matching.

<a id="ra-511"></a>

#### RA-511 · refresh_status runs adb and usage.get on the shared, sequential control connection for every device/run/usage event, without coalescing, and never retries a failed device count

`apps/relay-native/src/status.rs:72` · **low** · Performance · confirmed · effort M

**Problem.** refresh_status (:66-85) always runs render_status_counts, refresh_usage(false), and a new `ui.call("device.list")` with no in-flight guard. It runs on every usage.changed, device.changed and run.changed (app.rs:1188-1193), and at connect before the first project/session load (app.rs:1158 vs 1162). device.list runs `adb devices -l` with a 2 s timeout (device.rs:32-34, :577). The engine serves one connection strictly one request at a time: it reads the next line only after `spawn_blocking(..).await` and `out_tx.send` (socket.rs:335, :742-744). The device watcher emits one device.changed per adb output line (device.rs:377). The Devices page already calls device.list itself (tools_devices.rs:11). On failure the label is left as it was (`if let Ok(v) = devices`).

**Impact.** At startup, device.list is probably queued ahead of project.list, workspace.list and session.list. With a cold adb server it takes the full 2 s, delaying the first sidebar and wall load. It then times out, so the strip shows 'No device' with a phone plugged in, and nothing retries until a device or run event arrives (device.changed only flows while the Devices page is open). A hot-plug with N devices sends N adb subprocesses plus a useless usage.get on the window's only control connection, stalling every other UI request. Each run state change spends an adb call as well.

**Fix.** Split refresh_status by event:
- device events: one coalesced device.list, or reuse the Devices page result;
- usage events: refresh_usage only;
- run events: neither.
Retry device.list once after a timeout. Consider sending these status reads on a separate short-lived connection, as lifecycle_request already does.

**Verifier note.** Severity is lower than claimed. Terminal panes use their own connections (terminal.rs:476), so keystrokes are never stalled. refresh_usage is already coalesced through busy/queued (status_usage.rs:321-324), so usage.get is not repeated per event. With a hot adb server each device.list takes tens of milliseconds. The device.changed bursts happen only while the Devices page, which also lists devices, is open. That adb takes longer than 2 s on a cold start is likely but was not measured. Fix: send the connect-time device.list after the first refresh, or on its own connection. Skip device.list on usage.changed, retry it once after device.adb_timeout, and coalesce in-flight calls.

Rebuilding the rows only when the set of sessions or worktrees changes would remove most of the churn.

<a id="ra-513"></a>

#### RA-513 · A failed read of the usage display preferences is never retried, and the options panel is built from preferences that may not be loaded and is never resynced

`apps/relay-native/src/status_usage.rs:356` · **low** · Bug · confirmed · effort S

**Problem.** Discovery runs only when `installed.is_none_or(|(seen, _)| *seen != generation)` (:320-321). `installed` is stamped as soon as provider.list succeeds (:348-355), but prefs are replaced only `if let Some(Ok(v)) = prefs` (:356-358). usage_options builds its switches and chips once from `self.usage.prefs.borrow().clone()` (:671, :680, :693). For Value::Null, enabled() defaults to true and interval() to 0. After a refused settings.set, reload_usage_prefs (:423) re-renders only the strip.

**Impact.** If the settings.get inside discovery fails (for example a timeout behind the connect burst) while provider.list succeeds, later automatic refreshes never read the preferences again. Hidden meters reappear in the strip, and a configured auto-refresh interval is ignored until the user presses refresh or a settings event arrives. If the popup opens before the preferences load, or after a refused write, the switches show defaults or the rejected value. For example, with Codex hidden its switch shows on, so the first click changes nothing.

**Fix.** Track whether the preferences have loaded separately from `installed`, and keep discovering until both reads succeed. Update the option widgets from render_usage_popup, blocking their handlers while doing so, instead of building them only once.

**Verifier note.** Prefs survive a reconnect (they are never reset per generation), so only the very first load can leave Null. The simplest fix is to stamp `installed` only when both reads succeed, or to track prefs-loaded separately. Resyncing the switches in render_usage_popup needs signal blocking, because the handlers write settings.

**Problem.** `confirm_inline_if(&discard, "Confirm discard", move || pending.dirty() || pending.unsent_message.get(), move |_| { if !d.busy.get() { *d.base.borrow_mut() = (d.snapshot)(); d.close(); } })` (199-204). Because of the unsent-message condition it asks for confirmation. On confirm it overwrites base and calls close(). close() calls can_close(), which returns false while `unsent_message` is set ("Send or clear your message before closing.", 131-136). By then base already holds the snapshot: only the 8 editable keys, with the user's edited values.

**Impact.** With text in the Messages tab composer, confirming Discard and close only shows "Send or clear your message" and the panel stays open. If the form also had edits, base now equals those edits. dirty() becomes false, so a later Back silently drops the edits. A later Save compares the engine's values against the user's edits and reports "This item changed elsewhere" for every edited field, so that draft can never be saved.

**Fix.** Add a `Draft::discard()` that clears the message buffer and `unsent_message`, then closes without going through can_close. Only overwrite base once the close actually happens. Alternatively, refuse up front with "clear your message first" without touching base.

**Verifier note.** Downgraded to low. The trigger needs text in the composer plus a confirmed discard, and the save failure only matters if the user then changes their mind about discarding. The claim that 'a later Back silently drops the edits' is not a separate harm: the user explicitly asked to discard them. Fix: clear the composer and unsent_message, or refuse before the confirmation, and assign base only once the close actually proceeds.

**Also at:** `apps/relay-native/src/task_pages.rs:131`, `apps/relay-native/src/task_pages.rs:1012`

The engine answers it through the same `out_tx` mpsc (capacity 1024 lines, socket.rs:295, 744) that carries the pane's frames (488-489); the client reader handles lines in order and blocks on the 64-slot notices channel while GTK feeds VTE (client.rs:179, 232-255).

<a id="ra-529"></a>

#### RA-529 · Wallpaper rotation re-downloads and re-hashes the whole library on every appearance change, so each tick loads everything twice

`apps/relay-native/src/wallpaper_rotation.rs:92` · **low** · Performance · confirmed · effort S

**Problem.** refresh() fetches `appearance.wallpaper_rotation` and the whole `appearance.wallpapers` library, which can be up to 1.5 MB of base64 (tools_settings.rs:1012). signature() serialises the full library to a String in order to hash it (61-62). refresh() runs from load_appearance (shell.rs:1117) on every `settings.changed` under `appearance.`, for `terminal.font_size`, or for the root (app.rs:1257-1262). That includes the `appearance.wallpaper` change each rotation makes itself. So one tick fetches the library twice (151-158, then refresh) and the current image twice, and load_appearance decodes the image on the GTK thread (shell.rs:1230 `Texture::from_bytes`).

**Impact.** Every rotation, and every font-size or opacity change, moves several MB over the single control socket and through the engine's store lock. It also re-serialises and hashes up to 1.5 MB and decodes a full image on the GTK thread, causing a frame hitch.

**Fix.** Call refresh only for `appearance.wallpaper_rotation`, `appearance.wallpapers` or root changes. Build the signature from the config plus image count and ids instead of the whole library. Decode the texture off the main thread and hand the result back.

**Verifier note.** The impact is smaller than claimed. Rotation runs at most once a minute (default every 15 minutes, interval clamped to 1-1440 min), so the redundant transfer is roughly 1.5 MB of library plus one image per tick, not 'several MB'. The appearance sliders (tools_settings.rs:291-325) do not write live; they are saved on Save, so the redundant work happens once per saved appearance field, not per slider movement. The cost per event is one extra round trip of up to 1.5 MB over the local socket, a 1.5 MB to_string plus hash, and one JPEG decode (at most 1280x900, about 10 ms) on the GTK thread. That is a minor hitch, not a recurring freeze. The most useful fix is to run refresh only when the path is `appearance.wallpaper_rotation`, `appearance.wallpapers` or empty, and to leave it out of the general load_appearance path. Moving the texture decode to ui.rt.spawn_blocking, as the add-wallpaper flow already does, is a secondary improvement. The relay-native crate cannot be compiled in this environment.

**Also at:** `apps/relay-native/src/shell.rs:1117`, `apps/relay-native/src/shell.rs:1230`, `apps/relay-native/src/app.rs:1257`, `apps/relay-native/src/wallpaper_rotation.rs:61`, `apps/relay-native/src/wallpaper_rotation.rs:151`, `crates/relay-core/src/handlers/settings.rs:217`, `apps/relay-native/src/tools_settings.rs:606`, `apps/relay-native/src/wallpaper_rotation.rs:83`, `apps/relay-native/src/tools_settings.rs:1022`

<a id="ra-530"></a>

#### RA-530 · relay-editor.xml inherits Adwaita-dark's language-specific styles, so Rust attributes, macros, paths and lifetimes (and CSS/XML/diff/Python tokens) bypass the Relay palette

`apps/relay-native/resources/relay-editor.xml:3` · **low** · Bug · confirmed · effort S

**Problem.** The scheme declares `parent-scheme="Adwaita-dark"`. GtkSourceView looks up a token's own style id (for example `rust:attribute`) in the scheme and then in its parent before it falls back to the language's `map-to` chain. rust.lang maps `attribute`, `macro` and `scope` to `def:preprocessor`, and `lifetime` to `rust:keyword`. Adwaita-dark defines `rust:attribute`, `rust:macro`, `rust:scope` and `rust:lifetime` itself (plus css:*, xml:*, diff:*, python:*, c:*, go:*), so those win over line 25's `def:preprocessor #c979d6`. Styles the scheme never defines also come from Adwaita-dark. I verified this with GtkSourceView 5.20 on the substituted relay-matte scheme: rust:attribute and rust:macro → #7D8AC7; rust:scope and rust:lifetime → #FFA348; def:constant → #7D8AC7; def:special-char → #F66151; def:heading → #33B2A4 bold; def:link-text → #ED333B; def:note → #3D3D3D on #F5C211; css:property-name → #FF7800; diff:added-line → #33B2A4.

**Impact.** In the Code editor (editor.rs:86-92, 199), every Rust file (the repo's main language) shows `#[derive]`, `format!`/`vec!`, `std::` paths and lifetimes in Adwaita periwinkle and orange. Those hues are absent from the SYN_MATTE palette that the header comment (line 2) promises. Markdown files get Adwaita's teal headings and red links, and TODO/FIXME notes get a yellow block background.

**Fix.** Add entries that re-point the parent's language styles, e.g. `<style name="rust:attribute" use-style="def:preprocessor"/>` (likewise for rust:macro and rust:scope) and `<style name="rust:lifetime" use-style="def:keyword"/>`. I verified this resolves to #c979d6. Do the same for the css/xml/diff/python ids, and define the def:* styles the palette should own: constant, special-constant, special-char, heading, link-text, inline-code, note, list-marker, preformatted-section and net-address. Alternatively, drop the parent and define the few global styles yourself (search-match, bracket-match).

**Verifier note.** The same `parent-scheme="Adwaita-dark"` inheritance is in NOTES_SCHEME (note_pages.rs:111-113). That scheme does override def:heading, list-marker and inline-code, but it still inherits the language-specific ids. Apply the same fix to both schemes.

**Also at:** `apps/relay-native/resources/relay-editor.xml:25`, `apps/relay-native/resources/relay-editor.xml:2`, `apps/relay-native/src/editor.rs:86`, `apps/relay-native/src/fonts.rs:41`, `DESIGN.md:140`
