#### RA-654 · 'during' cases wait a fixed 5 ms and never check the other op is still running; FIXES records a 470x win measured with no overlap at all

`crates/relay-core/examples/perf.rs:1251` · **low** · Test quality · confirmed · effort S

**Problem.** The other op starts on a thread, then `std::thread::sleep(Duration::from_millis(5))` (1250), then the measured request runs. There is no barrier, no start/end timestamps and no overlap check (1242-1257; during_session sleeps 2 ms at 1278). FIXES-2026-09-20.md:14 reports 'session.scrollback tail while a device.build runs 22.7 ms -> 48 us (470x)', while :27 shows device.build itself now takes 76 us. The build therefore finished about 5 ms before the measured read, and 48 us is an uncontended read. session_list.during_task_list (1266) cannot overlap either: task.list is 0.76 ms after the fixes. On a loaded machine the thread may not start within 5 ms at all.

**Impact.** The cases meant to make the store-mutex invariant 'a number' can report no contention when none was measured. That would hide a regression that puts slow work back under the lock, and the docs already contain an artefactual result.

**Fix.** Have the other op signal once it is inside its handler, or record its start and end Instants. Mark iterations whose measured request began after the other op finished, and report the overlap fraction. Drop or lengthen the task.list and device.build variants.

**Verifier note.** Severity lowered to low: this is a perf-harness accuracy problem with no effect on the app, and slow-under-lock regressions (the case that matters) would mostly still be caught. The fix is still sound: signal from inside the other op, or record its start and end Instants and report the fraction of iterations that overlapped. Drop or re-label the device.build and task.list variants.

**Also at:** `crates/relay-core/examples/perf.rs:1266`, `crates/relay-core/examples/perf.rs:1268`, `docs/perf/FIXES-2026-09-20.md:14`

<a id="ra-655"></a>

#### RA-655 · strace pass silently reports 0 syscalls under Yama ptrace_scope=1 (this machine's setting): strace cannot attach to its own parent

`crates/relay-core/examples/perf.rs:1360` · **low** · Test quality · confirmed · effort S

**Problem.** strace_start spawns `strace -f -c -o <file> -p <own pid>` as a child of the process it is meant to trace (1359-1366). /proc/sys/kernel/yama/ptrace_scope is 1 here, which is also the Ubuntu and Arch default. Under that setting a process may only ptrace its descendants, so the attach fails and strace exits. strace_start still returns Some after its 400 ms sleep. strace_stop (1372-1395) parses whatever the file holds and returns `{"total": 0, "top": []}`, without checking strace's exit status or that a 'total' row exists. In report.py:154-155, `st = ... or {}` treats that dict as truthy and prints `0.0` instead of '-'. The committed run was made as root on a Firecracker VM, where the attach succeeds.

**Impact.** With strace installed, baseline.py on this desktop writes 0 syscalls/iteration for every scenario into strace.jsonl and the report, presented as real data. The callgrind pass's callgrind_control/vgdb toggling also relies on ptrace to wake a valgrind process whose threads are all blocked (per the valgrind manual), so it may stall under the same setting. That part is unverified: valgrind is not installed here.

**Fix.** Call prctl(PR_SET_PTRACER, PR_SET_PTRACER_ANY) before spawning strace, or make strace the parent (`strace -f -c -o f -- perf run ...`). In strace_stop, treat a nonzero exit or a missing total row as failure and emit null. Have report.py render null as '-'.

**Verifier note.** Severity lowered to low: this is dev tooling only, and it is latent on this machine because strace is not installed, so baseline.py skips the pass. Drop the callgrind/vgdb speculation. Fix: call prctl(PR_SET_PTRACER, PR_SET_PTRACER_ANY), or the strace pid, before spawning strace. Alternatively, wait for strace's first output or check `child.try_wait()` after the sleep. Emit null when strace exited early or no 'total' row exists.

**Also at:** `crates/relay-core/examples/perf.rs:1372`, `scripts/perf/report.py:155`, `scripts/perf/baseline.py:633`

<a id="ra-656"></a>

#### RA-656 · strace pass counts each iteration's uncounted setup, cleanup and fixture git processes as the op's syscalls

`crates/relay-core/examples/perf.rs:1410` · **low** · Test quality · confirmed · effort M

**Problem.** strace attaches before the loop (1409) and detaches after it (1440). Inside the loop, every iteration runs `fx.drain_cleanup()` (1412) and `(case.prepare)(fx)` (1413), which is exactly the work the timer excludes, and `strace -f` (1360) also follows forked children. The committed strace.jsonl gives a fingerprint: one getrandom per bus request (its req_id UUID). op.task.update shows 50 getrandom for 50 iterations, but op.task.delete shows 150 (fresh_task's create, the measured delete, the cleanup delete), op.task.restore 200 and op.audit.get 100. op.task.delete is 125 syscalls/iter against 45 for task.update. op.project.add is 3,075 and op.project.remove 2,994 syscalls/iter, mostly rt_sigaction/openat from the five `git` commands small_repo runs in prepare. BASELINE-2026-09-19.md:375 then calls file.create/rename/move/delete 'a few hundred syscalls' each, which includes the prepare's file.create.

**Impact.** Per-op syscall counts are 2-4x too high for every case whose prepare creates rows, and wrong by orders of magnitude where prepare forks git. Conclusions in the analysis inherit the error.

**Fix.** Count only between markers: issue a distinctive marker syscall immediately before and after perf_measured, record with `strace -f -ttt -o`, and sum only the events between the markers. Alternatively, count raw_syscalls:sys_enter with perf stat toggled around the measured call. At minimum, subtract a calibrated no-op iteration that runs the same prepare and cleanup.

**Verifier note.** Severity lowered to low: the effect is limited to the accuracy of the perf report and does not touch the app. The marker or calibrated-baseline fix is reasonable. A simpler fix is to measure a no-op case that runs the same prepare and cleanup, and subtract it.

**Also at:** `crates/relay-core/examples/perf.rs:1412`, `crates/relay-core/examples/perf.rs:1360`, `docs/perf/BASELINE-2026-09-19.md:375`

<a id="ra-657"></a>

#### RA-657 · perf `run` treats every filter as a prefix, so baseline.py's exact-name shards run 19 cases twice under callgrind and add unlisted cases to the scale pass

`crates/relay-core/examples/perf.rs:1561` · **low** · Test quality · confirmed · effort S

**Problem.** perf.rs:1561: `.filter(|c| filters.is_empty() || filters.iter().any(|f| c.name == *f || c.name.starts_with(f.trim_end_matches('*'))))`. A plain name with no `*` still matches as a prefix. scripts/perf/baseline.py:266 splits exact names round-robin across jobs (`groups = [names[i::jobs] for i in range(jobs)]`) and passes each group as filters (line 273), and the scale pass passes the exact SCALE_OPS names (line 632). 21 case names prefix another case (op.session.list/op.session.list.all, op.task.list/.filtered, op.git.diff/.file/.staged, op.guardrail.gate/.hold/.refused, op.session.close/.created, op.settings.get/.path, ...). The checked-in run shows the effect. `cat docs/perf/runs/2026-09-19/callgrind/rows-*.jsonl | jq -r .name | sort | uniq -d` lists 19 names that ran in two shards. rows-extra-0.jsonl has 9 rows for 8 names passed. scale10.jsonl contains op.session.list.all@x10 and op.settings.get.path@x10, which are not in SCALE_OPS.

**Impact.** Each baseline run repeats about 19 scenarios under valgrind, the slowest pass at roughly 50x. The repeat happens in a different shard with different fixture state (see perf-harness#6). parse_callgrind keys profiles by name and keeps whichever dump sorts last (baseline.py:212-258), so the profile reported for those cases depends on which shard's pid sorts last. The scale pass also measures cases nobody chose. The numbers stay usable, but time is wasted and the selection does not match what was asked for.

**Fix.** Match exactly unless the filter ends in `*`: `c.name == *f || (f.ends_with('*') && c.name.starts_with(f.trim_end_matches('*')))`. Apply the same rule to baseline.py's `matches()` (line 110) so `--only` keeps working as a prefix only when given `op.git.*`. If bare-prefix behaviour should stay for interactive use, have baseline.py pass names with an `=` marker that means exact.

**Verifier note.** Line numbers match: perf.rs:1561, baseline.py:110, 211, 266, 273, 629-632. Only the callgrind shards run cases twice. Each single native or strace run filters cases once, so a case does not repeat within one run.

`crates/relay-core/tests/agent_features.rs:61` · **low** · Test quality · confirmed · effort S

**Problem.** agent_features.rs:60-61 inserts `VALUES (1,'Ship the thing','','','active','working',0,?1,?1)`, and awareness.rs:76-77 does the same. TaskState has only None/Dispatched/Running/Blocked/Failed/AwaitingReview (relay-bus types.rs:33-40), and parse_task_state maps anything else with `_ => TaskState::None` (task.rs:61-68). done_can_say_blocked_and_the_task_does_not_move reads `queued_state = task.get(1)["state"]` (line 215), which is "none", and then asserts `task["state"] == queued_state, "blocking the current task must not touch its queue"` (line 225).

The seeded row also holds a value no handler writes, so SQL filters such as `state='none'` and the API disagree about the same task.

That round-trip is a small product quirk in its own right: an unknown stored state is silently rewritten to 'none' on any body edit. Seed a real state such as 'dispatched' (task.update preserves it) and assert the literal value. awareness.rs:77 has the same seed.

#### RA-663 · Production code branches on Instance::Test, and two assertions describe behaviour production doesn't have

`crates/relay-core/tests/branch_cleanup.rs:110` · **low** · Test quality · confirmed · effort M

**Problem.** Production code changes behaviour under the test instance in four places. session.close skips the after-close cleanup: `if engine.instance != crate::Instance::Test { crate::branch_cleanup::after_close(…) }` (session.rs:1633-1635). git.pr.list skips after_merged_prs (git.rs:638). usage.get skips the provider file reads (provider.rs:60-71). Run commands use `sh` instead of `fish` (device.rs:1821). The tests then assert the test-only behaviour. branch_cleanup.rs:108-110 asserts that a merged branch survives session.close ("close alone keeps the branch for cleanup to judge"), but in production after_close deletes it on a background thread right away. phase9.rs:94-106 asserts usage.report → usage.get. Nothing in Relay sends usage.report on its own: the Claude status line writes ~/.claude/relay-usage.json instead (hooks.rs:576-578), although audit.rs:16 and BUS.md:883 still say the hooks call usage.report. In production, usage.get then overwrites the reported value with the file read regardless of age.

**Impact.** The paths users actually run have no engine-level test: the after-close cleanup thread with the real gh lookup, usage.get's file reads and precedence, and run commands under fish. Two assertions document behaviour production doesn't have.

**Fix.** Inject the dependency instead of branching on the instance: the gh path and cleanup trigger through Options or settings, the usage home through an env override like RELAY_SKILLS_HOME, the run shell through a setting. Test the production paths with fakes. Either give usage.report a real producer or remove it along with usage.changed.

**Verifier note.** The branches are documented as deliberate (session.rs:1632 comment, device.rs:1818-1820 comment), and the core logic they bypass is tested elsewhere: branch_cleanup::run is driven synchronously by branch_cleanup.rs, and usage::read_claude_file has unit tests (usage.rs:213). What is actually untested is thin glue: the thread spawn with the real gh, provider precedence in usage.get, and fish quoting of run commands. usage.report is not dead. Agents can call it as a builder/reviewer/docs op (settings.rs:36-38), and it is exposed as an MCP tool. It just has no automatic producer. The most concrete part is docs drift (audit.rs:16, BUS.md:519, BUS.md:883) plus the misleading assertion message at branch_cleanup.rs:110. Fix: reword that message to say the test instance defers cleanup, update the doc comments, and add one test of usage.get precedence with CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR pointed at a temp dir. That is cheaper than refactoring all four branches into injection.

**Problem.** No production code runs `adb exec-out` or `adb shell cmd input`; `exec-out` appears only in device_lease.rs's command classifier. On the test instance, device.mirror.start never starts the worker (handlers/device.rs:103-105). device.mirror.input goes to `MirrorRuntime::send_control`, which queues into `pending` when no control socket exists (device.rs:279-289). `crates/relay-core/tests/bus.rs:1033` · **low** · Test quality · confirmed · effort S

An unfiltered workspace.changed would come next and be swallowed by `sub.call(&...unsubscribe..., |_| {})` (1034), because Client::call hands events to on_event (socket.rs:810). The comment "the workspace event was filtered out" is never checked, and no unit test covers socket.rs's Filter. (b) "the signing password must not enter build output" (479-482) searches tasks.log. (d) The comment at 928 says the failed mutation "was audited as error", but the test only checks project.get.

#### RA-668 · mirror text-truncation tests never exercise the char-boundary backoff they claim to test

`crates/relay-core/tests/mirror.rs:233` · **low** · Test quality · confirmed · effort S

**Problem.** Both tests use `"é".repeat(151)` (302 bytes). 300 is even, so byte 300 is already a char boundary. The `while !s.is_char_boundary(end) { end -= 1; }` loops in `text` (src/mirror.rs:503-506) and `text_chunks` (532-535) therefore never run, and a naive `&s.as_bytes()[..300]` gives identical output. The test's own comment notes the cap 'would land on 300 exactly'. Because 300 = 2²·3·5², no repeated 2-, 3- or 4-byte char ever straddles it. set_clipboard_caps_on_a_char_boundary (mirror.rs:375-388) does this correctly.

**Impact.** Trigger: a refactor that drops or breaks the boundary loop. Consequence: INJECT_TEXT messages split a UTF-8 char, so the device types garbage (or the slice panics), while both tests stay green.

**Fix.** Offset the input by one ASCII byte, e.g. `format!("a{}", "é".repeat(150))` (301 bytes). Assert the first message carries 299 bytes and the chunks concatenate back to the input.

**Verifier note.** If the loop regressed, text_chunks would panic at `&rest[..end]` on a non-boundary rather than send garbage; text() would send invalid UTF-8. Either way it is uncaught. Fix: prefix one ASCII byte, e.g. `format!("a{}", "é".repeat(150))`, which is 301 bytes. Assert that the first message carries 299 bytes and that the chunks concatenate back to the input.

**Also at:** `crates/relay-core/tests/mirror.rs:259`, `crates/relay-core/src/mirror.rs:503`, `crates/relay-core/src/mirror.rs:532`

`crates/relay-core/tests/mirror.rs:864` · **low** · Test quality · confirmed · effort S

**Problem.** `serve_then_vanish` blocks in `listener.accept().unwrap()` twice (mirror.rs:816, 818) with no timeout. The helper then calls `worker.join().unwrap(); server.join().unwrap();` unconditionally (863-864). The worker can reach a terminal state without ever connecting: a push or forward failure calls `fail(...)` and returns (device.rs:768-780). The fake adb answers only the argv shapes it knows and exits 1 otherwise (`*) exit 1 ;;`, mirror.rs:679). The CI engine job sets no `timeout-minutes` (ci.yml:19-41), so GitHub's 360-minute default applies.

**Impact.** Trigger: any change to push_args/forward_args, a new adb step the fake doesn't recognise, or a failed exec of the freshly written script. Consequence: instead of failing with the worker's message, both worker tests hang in `server.join()`. `cargo test` never finishes, and CI burns hours before timing out with no diagnosis.

**Fix.** Accept with a deadline (set_nonblocking plus polling, or a channel with recv_timeout). Join the server only after the worker has connected; if the worker ends without connecting, fail with `runtime.status()`. Add `timeout-minutes` to the CI job.

**Verifier note.** Hang site: mirror.rs:864 (`server.join()`), with the blocking accepts at 815 and 817 (the finding says 816/818). An easy fix: after the status turns terminal, check whether the runtime ever reached Running or connected. If it did not, panic with `runtime.status()` before joining the server, or poke the listener with a throwaway `TcpStream::connect` so the accepts return. Separately, add `timeout-minutes` to the CI engine job.

**Also at:** `crates/relay-core/tests/mirror.rs:816`, `crates/relay-core/src/handlers/device.rs:768`, `.github/workflows/ci.yml:19`

<a id="ra-670"></a>

#### RA-670 · The phase12 AVD test can't fail on avd.create or avd.boot behaviour

`crates/relay-core/tests/phase12.rs:80` · **low** · Test quality · confirmed · effort S · rechecked after PR #30/#31: changed

**Problem.** The fake avdmanager is `if [ "$1" = "list" ]; then echo 'pixel_9'; fi\nexit 0` (phase12.rs:66), so `create avd` succeeds whatever arguments it gets. avd.create returns `list_avds(…).find(name).unwrap_or(Avd { name, device: p.device, package: Some(p.package), … })` (device.rs:339-340), and the fake emulator never lists New_API_35. So `assert_eq!(created["name"], "New_API_35")` (phase12.rs:79) only echoes the request back. avd.boot (phase12.rs:80) is checked only for Ok. The launch happens in after_commit and reports through an `avd.changed` event the test never reads.

**Impact.** Wrong --name, --package or --device arguments, a create that silently does nothing, or a broken `@name -no-snapshot-load` command line all pass the test.

**Fix.** Have each fake append its argv to a file and assert the exact invocations. Subscribe before avd.boot and assert avd.changed {state:"started"}. Make the fake emulator list New_API_35 after creation.

**Verifier note.** While verifying, I found a more important issue in the same code that the auditor missed. AvdCreate (device.rs:322) and AvdBoot (device.rs:345) are registered with plain Engine::register. AvdCreate runs avdmanager (a JVM tool that takes seconds) through spawn + wait_with_output, with no proc::output_with_timeout, while holding the store transaction and mutex. Both handlers also call list_avds(ctx.tx()), which runs the emulator binary under the lock. AvdCatalog's `avdmanager list device -c` (device.rs:314) has no timeout either. This breaks two CLAUDE.md invariants and should be raised as its own invariant finding: a hung avdmanager freezes the bus. The fix the test finding proposes (argv log file, avd.changed subscription, fake emulator that lists the new AVD) is right.

**Recheck after PR #30/#31 note.** The finding now covers avd.create only. The boot command line, including the cold-boot `-no-snapshot-load` flag and the new `-no-window`, is now asserted exactly. avd.create can still pass with wrong --name, --package or --device arguments, or with a create that does nothing. The fix is narrower: have the fake avdmanager log its argv and assert the exact `create avd -n New_API_35 -k <package> -d pixel_9 ...` invocation, the same way boot_log already does for the emulator. Then make the fake emulator's -list-avds include New_API_35 after creation, so the test reads back the created AVD rather than the request echoed through the fallback.

**Also at:** `crates/relay-core/src/handlers/device.rs:339`, `crates/relay-core/src/handlers/device.rs:353`, `crates/relay-core/tests/phase12.rs:66`

#### RA-671 · git/call/ok/Fixture helpers are copy-pasted into 10-17 engine test files and have already diverged

`crates/relay-core/tests/phase7.rs:11` · **low** · Duplication · confirmed · effort M

**Problem.** phase7.rs:11-19 `git` runs `.status()` with a bare `assert!(...success())`, so a failure reports neither the args nor stderr. awareness.rs:12-20 runs `.status()` and reports only the args. agent_features.rs:13-16 and phase8.rs:20-33 capture and print stderr. The `ok()` panic formats differ ("{op} failed: ..." vs "{op}: ..."), and phase8 has no `ok()` at all, unwrapping BusError Debug instead. Fixture::new in agent_features.rs:41-71 and awareness.rs:39-109 is the same sequence: tempdir, ws/app, git init/config/commit, Store::open, Engine::new, workspace.create, project.add, a raw INSERT into tasks, two session.create calls. phase7.rs:48-75 and phase8.rs:34-58 repeat the repo half. Across crates/relay-core/tests, `fn git(` appears in 13 files, `fn call(` in 17 and `struct Fixture` in 10, and there is no tests/common module.

**Impact.** Any fixture change has to be repeated 10-17 times: hermetic git config (see the git-config finding), an Engine::new or Store::open signature change, a new NOT NULL column in the raw INSERTs. When a phase7 or awareness fixture git command fails, the panic carries no stderr; the child writes straight to the terminal, interleaved with the other parallel tests.

**Fix.** Add crates/relay-core/tests/common/mod.rs containing: a stderr-capturing git helper, call/ok/refusal/code, a repo() builder that writes hermetic local git config, and a Fixture builder that seeds tasks and sessions through the bus. Add `mod common;` to each test file.

**Verifier note.** Severity is low, not medium. The duplication is confined to test helpers, and the divergence so far is in panic-message quality rather than in behavior. The ongoing cost is real but modest: an Engine::new or Store::open signature change, or adding hermetic git config, means editing about 10-18 files. A tests/common/mod.rs with a stderr-capturing git helper and call/ok is the right fix. Pull in the Fixture only where the files truly share its shape, because their seeds differ (modules, tasks, sessions).

#### RA-672 · Fixtures and the engine's git calls inherit the developer's global git config (core.hooksPath, commit.gpgsign, push.default)

`crates/relay-core/tests/phase8.rs:196` · **low** · Test quality · confirmed · effort S

**Problem.** Only user.name and user.email are set locally (agent_features.rs:48-49, awareness.rs:46-47, phase7.rs:55-56, phase8.rs:39-40). No test pins commit.gpgsign, core.hooksPath, push.default or init.templateDir, and there is no .cargo/config.toml or GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL; phase12 sets GIT_CONFIG_COUNT for one subprocess only. install_git falls back to `git rev-parse --git-path hooks` (hooks.rs:98). In a scratch repo with git 2.55 and a global `core.hooksPath=/home/someone/.githooks`, that command returned the global directory, while `config --worktree --get core.hooksPath` returned nothing.

**Impact.** With a global core.hooksPath, the hook-chaining test chains to the developer's real global pre-commit hook, run_user_pre_commit executes it against the temp repo, and the assertion at phase8.rs:246 fails. With commit.gpgsign=true, every fixture commit, the engine's git commit and the integration merge commit invoke gpg (a pinentry prompt or a failure). The author's current global config sets none of these, so this is a portability and hermeticity gap rather than a present failure.

**Fix.** Have the shared repo fixture write local config that overrides global: commit.gpgsign=false, tag.gpgsign=false, core.hooksPath=.git/hooks, push.default=simple. Alternatively, run the fixture's own git commands with GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL=/dev/null and GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM=1.

**Verifier note.** Production behavior is correct here: chaining to the global hooks directory matches what git itself would run. The defect is in the test fixture only. The simplest fix is to run the fixture's git, and the test process, with GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL=/dev/null and GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM=1. Alternatively, set core.hooksPath=.git/hooks and commit.gpgsign=false locally in real_repo; the same pattern in the other test files (agent_features.rs, awareness.rs, phase7.rs) would need the same change.

#### RA-673 · The integration test allows only 2.5 s for a background merge, and the watcher test's negative checks rely on fixed 250/350 ms windows

`crates/relay-core/tests/phase8.rs:500` · **low** · Test quality · confirmed · effort S

**Problem.** phase8.rs:500-510: `for _ in 0..100 { ...integration.get...; if matches!(state, "passed"|"failed"|"conflict") { break; } sleep(25ms) } assert_eq!(state, "passed");`. That is 2.5 s in total for a background thread that does set_state, `git worktree add` (production allows that call 120 s, worktree.rs:214), an octopus `git merge` and another set_state, while the other 11 phase8 tests run git in parallel. filesystem_reads_do_not_retrigger_refresh_but_writes_do (603-662) sleeps 250 ms and 350 ms and then asserts that no file.changed arrived. The watcher emits from a per-burst thread that sleeps 125 ms (watch.rs:119-121), so these windows are only 2-3x the delay; the positive checks wait 3 s.

**Impact.** On a loaded CI runner, or a desktop where several agents run cargo builds and tests at once (the normal workload here), the integration test fails with state "merging" although nothing is wrong. When the notify or timer thread is delayed past the window, the watcher's "no refresh" assertions pass without testing anything.

**Fix.** Subscribe before integration.request and wait for the integration.result event with a 30-60 s deadline, or poll with a deadline of that size. In the watcher test, make the 125 ms delay a pub(crate) const and derive the quiet windows from it with a generous multiple.

**Verifier note.** The integration test can only flake under heavy load; it is not broken in normal runs, so low severity is correct. In the watcher test, the vacuous negative checks are a coverage gap and not a source of flakes: they never fail spuriously. For the fix, the integration poll should use a deadline of 30 s or more, or wait on the integration.result event subscribed before the request. A pub(crate) debounce constant for the watcher windows would also help.

#### RA-674 · phase9's app.resources.watch check asserts only Ok, and its sampler never starts outside a tokio runtime

`crates/relay-core/tests/phase9.rs:119` · **low** · Test quality · confirmed · effort S

**Problem.** phase9.rs:119-124 turns app.resources.watch on and off and asserts only that both calls return Ok. The handler starts its sampler in after_commit with `let Ok(handle) = tokio::runtime::Handle::try_current() else { return };` (app.rs:98-99). The plain #[test] thread has no runtime, so the loop never starts and nothing is sampled.

**Impact.** The watch loop, its 2 s sampling, the epoch and client bookkeeping, and the off switch are all untested. The test passes whether they work or not.

**Fix.** Run the test under #[tokio::test(flavor = "multi_thread")], subscribe, and assert that a resource.sample arrives after on and none after off. Alternatively, move the tick into a sync function and test that directly.

**Verifier note.** The impact is overstated. Client counting, the epoch bump, and the off switch are covered by socket.rs:835 (resource_watch_leases_stop_on_disconnect_and_preserve_other_clients, a multi-thread tokio test). It asserts resource_watch_clients counts, resource_watch true/false transitions, and the epoch increasing on re-enable. What remains untested is the loop body: that resource.sample events actually arrive every 2 s while on, stop after off, and that the disk refresh fires every 15th tick. Fix: in the existing socket test, or a tokio test, subscribe and assert a resource.sample arrives within about 3 s after on and none after off. Or extract the tick body into a sync function and test that directly.

#### RA-675 · The write-roots launch test computes its expected roots with the code under test and never checks the configured root

`crates/relay-core/tests/sessions.rs:260` · **low** · Test quality · confirmed · effort S

**Problem.** The test sets `guardrails.allowed_write_roots = [extra]` (251). It then derives the expected list from the same production function the launch uses: `let roots = relay_core::guardrail::write_roots(&cfg, &worktree);` (259-260; the launch calls it at handlers/session.rs:453). It asserts each element appears as `--add-dir` and gets an allow verdict (263-269). `extra` is never named in an assertion. `extra` is f.root.join("agent notes"), which is under the system temp dir, and write_roots always ends with `roots.push(std::env::temp_dir());` (guardrail.rs:617). write_target treats anything under a non-worktree root as Scratch (guardrail.rs:645), so extra/note.md is allowed whether or not the setting is honoured. No other test exercises allowed_write_roots.

**Impact.** If cfg.allowed_write_roots stopped reaching write_roots (guardrail.rs:616), through a settings-path rename or a serde default for example, the expected list would shrink in step and the /tmp root would still satisfy the verdict check, so the test would stay green. Users' configured roots would silently stop reaching the providers' `--add-dir` and the guardrail.

**Fix.** Assert explicitly that args contain ["--add-dir", extra] and that an unlisted sibling directory is refused. Place `extra` outside the temp dir, e.g. under env!("CARGO_TARGET_TMPDIR"), so the always-present temp root cannot satisfy the verdict.

**Verifier note.** Severity lowered to low. A regression would fail closed: configured roots get refused, which a user notices, and no guardrail is bypassed. The test still provides real coverage of the memory roots and of --add-dir plumbing. Fix as proposed: assert ["--add-dir", extra] explicitly, put extra outside temp_dir, and add a refused-sibling case. The reverse direction is untested too: a relative entry must be dropped (guardrail.rs:616 filters is_absolute).

#### RA-676 · session_lifecycle_over_socket frame loops spin for 10 s on EOF or a decode error, then fail with a misleading 'no greeting'/'no echo' message

`crates/relay-core/tests/sessions.rs:391` · **low** · Test quality · confirmed · effort S

**Problem.** Both loops only act on one arm: `while !String::from_utf8_lossy(&seen).contains("hello-from-pty") { assert!(Instant::now() < deadline, "no greeting; got {:?}", ...); if let Ok(Ok(Some(Line::Frame(fr)))) = tokio::time::timeout(Duration::from_secs(2), term.next()).await { ... } }` (389-399), and the same pattern for "echo:ping" (404-410). `Client::next` (crates/relay-core/src/socket.rs:855-858) returns `Ok(None)` as soon as `next_line()` hits EOF, and returns `Err` for an I/O or JSON/serde decode error. Both are dropped silently by the `if let`, while `Client::call` in the same file treats `None` as `bail!("connection closed")` (878).

**Impact.** If a regression makes the engine close the attach stream (a server task panics, the door disconnects a lagging client) or send a frame that fails to decode, every `term.next()` after that returns at once. The loop busy-spins at full CPU until the 10 s deadline, then fails with "no greeting; got \"\"" or "no echo", which points the reader at the PTY child or session.input rather than at the closed or corrupt stream. That costs debugging time on the one integration test that covers attach over the real socket.

**Fix.** Match all arms: `match tokio::time::timeout(..., term.next()).await { Ok(Ok(Some(Line::Frame(fr)))) => {...}, Ok(Ok(None)) => panic!("attach stream closed; got {:?}", ...), Ok(Err(e)) => panic!("attach stream error: {e}"), _ => {} }` in both loops, or factor the two loops into one `read_until(&mut term, needle, &mut seen)` helper that does this.

**Verifier note.** Line numbers: the loops are at 388-398 and 402-408. The busy-spin only happens on EOF. A JSON or serde decode error uses up just that one line, so the next call blocks normally. In that case the frame is silently dropped (its bytes never reach `seen`), which can still end in the same misleading timeout, but without a spin. An I/O error from next_line may or may not repeat. The suggested fix (match the Ok(Ok(None)) and Ok(Err) arms and panic with a stream-specific message, ideally in one shared read_until helper used by both loops) is sound.

**Also at:** `crates/relay-core/tests/sessions.rs:404`, `crates/relay-core/src/socket.rs:855`

#### RA-677 · Three session-test assertions claim behaviour the test cannot observe: mid-turn injection, survival of a partial launch, and detach

`crates/relay-core/tests/sessions.rs:976` · **low** · Test quality · confirmed · effort S

**Problem.** (a) `assert!(!...scrollback...contains(&next_prompt), "Done must not inject into its own unfinished provider turn")` (914-915) runs immediately after session.done returns. An injected prompt only shows up once the fake provider reads and echoes it, so a regression usually lands after the check. Later, `contains` (924-930) cannot distinguish one injection from two. (b) The 'partial launch' is a session.create of a different session with `"worktree":"invalid-relative-worktree"` (1127-1134), refused in prepare before anything is allocated (handlers/session.rs:878-882). Only `!...ok` is asserted, so any error passes, and the session under test is never partially launched. (c) `// detach stops frames on term2` is followed by an unchecked `term2.call(... "session.detach" ...)` (431-432). Nothing verifies that frames stop, although the socket door implements it (socket.rs:514).

**Impact.** Regressions in Done-turn assignment injection, in launch-prompt preservation across a failed spawn, and in socket detach all pass, while the test names and comments say they are covered.

**Fix.** (a) After the trailing Stop, wait and assert the next-task echo appears exactly once, and keep the negative check only after a bounded wait. (b) Make the same session's spawn fail (point providers.claude.path at a missing file), restore it, respawn, and assert the stored assignment and the provider.not_installed code. (c) After detach, send input and assert term2 receives no frame within ~500 ms while `term` does.

**Verifier note.** For (a), the finding overstates it. Duplicate deferred assignment is partly covered: mail_count == 1 (sessions.rs:931-934) catches duplicated assignment mail, and the agent_done count and state checks (sessions.rs:919-922) cover the trailing-Stop marker logic. What stays uncovered is a double PTY injection, or an injection into the unfinished turn. These are weak assertions that don't match their comments, not missing coverage of whole features. Severity stays low.

#### RA-678 · The backup-retention test's 'newest first' check is guaranteed by the sort it tests and cannot tell which five backups were kept

`crates/relay-core/tests/store.rs:74` · **low** · Test quality · confirmed · effort S

**Problem.** `assert!(b[0]["created_at"].as_str().unwrap() >= b[4]["created_at"].as_str().unwrap(), "newest first");` (74). list_backups already sorts on that field: `v.sort_by(|a, b| b.created_at.cmp(&a.created_at));` (src/store.rs:607). `b[0]["reason"] == "manual"` (75) holds for all seven backups. The `path` returned by each app.backup.now is never compared with the list.

**Impact.** If the prune in backup_to pruned from the wrong end (`all.remove(0)` instead of `all.pop()`, src/store.rs:569), every manual or pre-upgrade backup would be deleted as soon as it was made, and this test would still see five sorted entries and pass.

**Fix.** Collect the path from each app.backup.now. Assert the listed paths equal the last five returned and that the first two no longer exist on disk.

**Verifier note.** The prune is at store.rs:567-572. The proposed fix is right and cheap: collect each returned `path`, assert the listed paths equal the last five returned, and assert the first two no longer exist on disk. A secondary weakness: the 2 ms sleeps rely on millisecond timestamp resolution to give each file a distinct name.

#### RA-690 · Every launch choice is a row of toggle buttons mirrored into a hidden DropDown or SpinButton, implemented three times and already diverged

`apps/relay-native/src/launch.rs:52` · **low** · Overengineering · confirmed · effort M

**Problem.** `choice_cards` (3-50), `segments` (52-86) and the provider-card loop in `Profile::new` (160-207) each build a grouped ToggleButton row bound to an invisible gtk::DropDown: mode (420), role (215), effort (248), task_filter (293), provider (207) and builders (450). The count is mirrored twice, in a hidden `count_select` DropDown and a hidden `gtk::SpinButton::with_range(1.0, 11.0, 1.0)` (433-447). Two comments record a bug this pattern caused: launch.rs:438-440 ("Segmented keys hold weak references to their backing control. Keep it owned by the form") and roadmap_smoke.rs:198-199 ("An unowned backing DropDown used to be destroyed, silently leaving the count at one"). The provider copy has already diverged: there is no `provider.connect_selected_notify` that updates the cards. After `provider.set_selected(1)` (as roadmap_smoke.rs:155 does), the Claude card still shows as selected.

**Impact.** About 40 hidden widgets per form exist only to hold integers. Each must be parented in the widget tree or its row silently stops working. The three copies of the binding logic drift apart (the provider cards already do not follow their model), and every new choice row repeats the trap.

**Fix.** Add one small `Choice` helper that owns its ToggleButtons and an `Rc<Cell<u32>>`, with `selected()`, `set_selected()` and `connect_changed()`, and read the count as `selected()+1`. This removes the hidden DropDowns, the SpinButton, the reverse-binding closures and the ownership pitfall.

**Verifier note.** The provider-card divergence cannot be reached in production. The cards are the only thing that changes `provider` there. Only roadmap_smoke.rs:154-157 calls provider.set_selected directly, and it never checks the cards, so the stale card state shows up only in the test. The hidden DropDowns also act as test handles: smoke tests find them by widget name (launch-provider-N, launch-effort-N, launch-count-control, launch-mode, launch-builders), so a Choice helper must keep a way for tests to reach them. That makes the payoff modest: low, not medium. The redundant SpinButton is the clearest piece to remove (read count_select.selected()+1 instead).

#### RA-693 · glyphs.rs copies the icons.rs SVG painter but not its render cache, re-parsing an SVG on every hover, focus or window-focus change

`apps/relay-native/src/mirror/glyphs.rs:43` · **low** · Duplication · confirmed · effort S

**Problem.** `glyphs::image` (34-49) is the same painter as `icons::image_with_stroke` (icons.rs:222-233): same SVG template, `connect_map` plus `connect_state_flags_changed`. It calls `gtk::Svg::from_bytes(...)` directly (43) instead of icons.rs's `rendered()` cache (icons.rs:6-26), whose comment says the cache exists because icons "repaint on map and on every state change". Geometry is duplicated too: "device", "close", "check" and "chevron-down" are identical in both tables, and the glyph "retry" is icons.rs "refresh".

**Impact.** Each mirror view has about 20 glyphs. Every state-flag change (hover, press, focus, and the BACKDROP flag on every window focus change) parses a new SVG for each glyph, the overhead icons.rs already removed. The two shape tables can also drift apart.

**Fix.** Expose a geometry-taking painter from icons.rs, e.g. `icons::image_from_geometry(shape, size, stroke)` that uses the same cache, and keep only the mirror-specific shapes in glyphs.rs.

**Verifier note.** The impact is mostly maintainability, with a minor parse overhead, not a measurable slowdown. Fix: have icons.rs expose `image_from_geometry(shape: &'static str, size, stroke)` that goes through `rendered()`, keep only the mirror-specific shapes in glyphs.rs, and map retry, close, check, chevron-down and device to the icons.rs names. This is native-client code that cannot be compiled in this environment.

#### RA-695 · Doc builds a Draft only to dismantle its layout, and Draft::close then reports refusals on a status label that is no longer on screen

`apps/relay-native/src/note_pages/doc.rs:301` · **low** · Code quality · confirmed · effort M

**Problem.** After `Draft::new_note(ui, "Note", …)`, build() calls `draft.layout.remove(&draft.status); draft.layout.remove(&draft.footer);`, unwraps Draft's ScrolledWindow and zeroes its margins. Doc uses only base, busy, snapshot, dirty, close and on_close from it; Draft::controls, its own save with different conflict logic, goes unused. When Draft::close refuses, can_close() writes `self.status.set_text("Save your changes or choose Discard and close.")` (task_pages.rs:131-144) to the detached label.

**Impact.** Example: request_close → Save, and the user keeps typing while the save is in flight. The `then` callback calls draft.close(), can_close() refuses, the message goes to the invisible label, and the tab silently stays open. Every note also builds and throws away a ScrolledWindow, Viewport and footer, and there are two save implementations to maintain.

**Fix.** Give notes a small struct with base, busy, dirty and on_close. Register it in ui.note_drafts behind a minimal dirty/busy interface for the quit guard. Show close refusals in the Doc's own notice bar.

**Verifier note.** The payoff is modest. Throwing away three widgets per tab is negligible, and the only user-visible effect is a silent non-close in a race. The cheaper fix is to give Draft an optional refusal callback, or have Doc check can_close itself and show the message in its notice bar, without splitting the struct. The category is code-quality, with a small UX bug in it, rather than overengineering.

#### RA-696 · Save as new note and both duplicate actions store the clipped display name as the new title, and their suffixes differ ('(copy)' vs ' copy')

`apps/relay-native/src/note_pages/doc.rs:1203` · **low** · Duplication · confirmed · effort S

**Fix.** Use one helper, e.g. copy_title(Option<&str>) -> Option<String>, in all three places. It should keep a null title null, so display_title still derives the name from the body, and otherwise append one agreed suffix.

The deleted-elsewhere path (no suffix) also turns the derived name of an untitled note into a stored title. A shared copy_title helper that keeps a null title null fixes all three call sites.

#### RA-697 · glyphs.rs is a second copy of icons.rs's SVG painter and cache, has already drifted from it, and defines three glyphs nothing uses

`apps/relay-native/src/note_pages/glyphs.rs:54` · **low** · Duplication · confirmed · effort S

**Problem.** glyph() re-implements icons::image_with_stroke. It has its own `static RENDERED: RefCell<HashMap<String, gtk::Svg>>` (7-9, vs icons.rs:13), the same `<svg ... color="{color}" stroke="{color}" ...>` document, the same cache lookup and the same `image.connect_map(paint); image.connect_state_flags_changed(...)` hookup (60-77, vs icons.rs:213-232). It has drifted: no `#141416` -> @console substitution and a hard-coded 1.5 stroke. No glyph() call ever requests the "rule" (41), "calendar" (46-48) or "goto" (49) geometry. Both copies repaint only on map and state-flag changes, so after a palette switch (load_appearance, shell.rs:1135-1146) glyphs keep the old stroke colour until they are hovered or remapped.

**Impact.** Every painter fix, for example repainting on a palette change, has to be made twice and kept in sync. The dead geometries are maintained for nothing.

**Fix.** Expose `icons::from_geometry(geometry: &'static str, size: i32, stroke: f64) -> gtk::Image`, or add these names to icons.rs's match. Then reduce glyphs.rs to its geometry table or delete it, and drop the unused rule, calendar and goto entries.

**Verifier note.** The claimed drift is overstated. No glyphs.rs geometry contains #141416, so the missing @console substitution changes nothing, and the hard-coded 1.5 stroke equals icons::image's default. The duplication is wider than reported, though: apps/relay-native/src/mirror/glyphs.rs:34-49 is a third copy of the painter, with no cache at all. Better fix: expose one icons.rs painter that takes a geometry string (e.g. icons::from_geometry), have both glyphs modules supply only geometry tables, and drop the unused rule, calendar and goto entries. The palette-switch staleness claim was not verified and affects all three copies alike.

#### RA-707 · settings::refresh is one 555-line function, and Save reads values back by parsing widget names

`apps/relay-native/src/tools_settings.rs:33` · **low** · Code quality · confirmed · effort L

**Problem.** One async fn (33-587) fetches 14 values with sequential awaits (41-58), builds seven categories, and wires Save and search. Save serializes by walking the widget tree and parsing names (606-692): `setting:` names with a `=value` suffix for the mode buttons, `notify:` and `notify:category:`, and `guardrail:` (dead). Special cases keyed on path strings are repeated: `terminal.font_size` is fractional both at 624 and at 801; empty becomes null except under `keybindings.` (643); the sound ids appear at 464 and 660 (and again in sounds.rs:109); every category title is in both CATEGORIES and its `category(&stack, name, title)` call; the nav hints sit in a separate match (187-195). The same widget names also serve as smoke-test lookup hooks.

**Impact.** Nothing ties a field to its value, which is how the dead guardrail branch survived. Save cannot diff (see the Save finding), adding a setting means edits in 2-3 places, and the page waits for 14 round trips one after another.

**Fix.** Fill a list of fields (path, initial value, read closure) as each control is built. Save then sends settings.set only for fields that changed, with no widget-name parsing. Split out one builder function per category, and fetch the initial values together with a single join.

**Verifier note.** The 14 sequential awaits run over a local Unix socket, so the latency cost is small. The concrete costs are the dead guardrail branch and the duplicated sound and font-size special cases. A field registry (path, initial value, reader) built while the controls are built would remove the name parsing and make diff-on-save possible. A smaller cleanup is to delete the guardrail branch and the guardrails variable.

#### RA-709 · The client parses SKILL.md front matter itself with rules that differ from the engine's, and shows wrong descriptions

`apps/relay-native/src/tools_skills.rs:57` · **low** · Duplication · confirmed · effort M

**Problem.** `if body.trim_start().starts_with("---") { lines.next(); for line in lines.by_ref() { let line = line.trim(); if line == "---" { break; } if let Some(value) = line.strip_prefix("description:") ...` (54-74). The engine has its own parser, plugins::frontmatter (plugins.rs:162-178): the first line must be `---`, keys must start at column 0, and it already supplies `description` for plugin skills.

**Impact.** A body with a blank line before `---`: lines.next() consumes the blank line, the loop stops at `---`, and the fallback returns the first front-matter line, so the card shows 'name: foo'. An indented `description:` nested under a key such as `metadata:` is chosen over the top-level one. Block scalars (`description: >`) show '>'. The same text drives search.

**Fix.** Add `description` to the bus Skill type, computed with the engine's single frontmatter() parser, and delete the client copy.

**Verifier note.** The block-scalar case (`description: >`) is not caused by the duplication. plugins::frontmatter also returns '>' for it, so moving the client to the engine parser does not fix that. The real cost is three diverged parsers: client description, plugins::frontmatter, and github::frontmatter_name. Computing `description` once in the engine and putting it on the bus Skill or summary type (see native-tools#2) removes the client copy. github::frontmatter_name should use the same helper.

**Also at:** `crates/relay-core/src/plugins.rs:162`, `crates/relay-core/src/github.rs:218`

#### RA-710 · Colour literals bypass the @define-color tokens: a second status palette in git_files.css, matte-only copies in theme.css, and a fixed Notes paper colour duplicated in Rust

`apps/relay-native/src/css/git_files.css:35` · **low** · Code quality · confirmed · effort M

**Problem.** git_files.css repeats literal status colours instead of tokens. #f0786f appears 5 times (35 `.git-conflict`, 92 `.image-hover-meta.error`, 139 `button.branch-delete:hover`, 212 `.scm-tag.pr-closed`, 246 `.diff-minus`), #73c991 3 times (32, 209, 245), #c9a24c 3 times (9, 222, 239) and #6c6c70 twice (36, 38). Its error red and success green differ from @held (#e5382e) and @live (#2ec469), and the PR chips mix both systems in one widget: `.scm-tag.pr-open { background: alpha(@live, 0.16); color: #73c991; }`, `.pr-closed { background: alpha(@held, 0.16); color: #f0786f; }`. theme.css hard-codes the matte token values: `.statusbar separator { background: #37373c }` (81, = @strong), `.lamp { border: 1px solid #77777a }` (83, = @faint) and `.task-card:hover { border-color: #37373c }` (95). notes.css:4 `@define-color notes_paper #0c0c0e` is the same in every appearance mode and is copied 4 times into NOTES_SCHEME (note_pages.rs:113-119). notes.css:16 colours the Notes close key #c42b1c/white, while the main window uses @held/@ink (theme.css:316). tools.css:73 uses #c4c4c2. relay-editor.xml repeats token values as literals (#ececea ink, #77777a faint, #a5a5a3 secondary, #e5382e held), and its per-mode backgrounds live in fonts.rs:36-40, separately from shell.rs:1141-1153's palettes. Conversely, shell.rs:1206 defines `@backbox`, which no stylesheet references.

**Impact.** Dark and OLED modes swap the tokens (shell.rs:1141-1153) but not these literals. Separators, lamp rings, the Notes paper and the editor's line numbers and cursor keep their matte values. Changing one status colour means finding up to five copies across CSS and Rust. Two different error reds appear side by side: an image-preview error in #f0786f next to notices in @held.

**Fix.** Add tokens in theme.css (e.g. `@define-color git_added #73c991; @define-color git_removed #f0786f; @define-color git_sha #c9a24c;`) and use them everywhere. Replace the theme.css literals with @strong/@faint. Derive notes_paper and the NOTES_SCHEME/relay-editor backgrounds from the active palette in one place. Drop the unused `backbox` definition.

**Verifier note.** The visual impact is smaller than claimed. The per-mode differences for the theme.css literals are a few RGB units (#37373c vs #33363d/#333336; #77777a is identical in oled). So 'keep their matte values' is technically true but barely visible. #c9a24c at git_files.css:9 is the `.ft-json` file-type tint, not a git or status colour, so it does not belong in the status-palette count. The Notes scheme's comment says it deliberately uses 'the Code editor's matte palette'. A fixed Notes paper may be intended; only the duplication is clearly a cost. The cheap, clear wins are to drop the dead `backbox` definition and replace theme.css:81/83/95 with @strong/@faint.

#### RA-712 · Three diverged copies of the square switch style; the other three GtkSwitches fall back to the desktop theme

`apps/relay-native/src/css/tools.css:159` · **low** · Duplication · confirmed · effort S · rechecked after PR #30/#31: still present

**Problem.** Three scoped rule sets each restyle switches within one area. tools.css:159-167 (`.ext-page switch`): 32×16, off ground @screen, slider @faint, radius 2/0. workspace.css:72-75 (`.registry-editor switch`): 34×18, @screen, slider @secondary, radius 2/1. usage.css:75-78 (`.usage-options switch`): 30×16, @slab, slider @faint, radius 2/2. theme.css has no `switch` rule, so the switches at agent_menu.rs:510, guardrail_settings.rs:498 and shell.rs:858 keep the system theme's rounded switch.

**Impact.** On/off controls differ from page to page in size, off colour and knob colour, and three of the six use the desktop theme's look, against DESIGN.md's square-plate rule. Every new switch needs another scoped copy.

**Fix.** Move one square-switch rule set into theme.css (`switch`, `switch:checked`, `switch > slider`, `switch > image`) and delete the three scoped copies.

**Verifier note.** DESIGN.md does not name a switch rule. #### RA-717 · Fixed sleeps stand in for synchronization throughout the harness and are followed by hard asserts, so a loaded machine produces false failures

`apps/relay-native/src/smoke.rs:162` · **low** · Test quality · confirmed · effort M

**Problem.** - smoke.rs:162: `glib::timeout_add_local_once(Duration::from_millis(900), ...)` then `assert!(ui.pages["settings"].is_sensitive(), "Settings save must finish")`. The Settings save issues one sequential `settings.set` per `setting:` widget (tools_settings.rs:143-149), with the guardrail save running alongside.
- smoke.rs:477: every roadmap part starts after a fixed 2 s. smoke_registry.rs:48 then does `ui.workspaces.borrow()[0]`, which panics if the initial refresh hasn't landed; roadmap_smoke.rs:69 calls `.expect("Fixture workspace")`.
- smoke.rs:350: 700 ms before unwrapping the launch form or task/note editors.
- smoke.rs:554/557, 578, 601, 632/642/652/661: 100/700, 700, 700, 100/500/250/1000 ms before asserting setup, launch and device controls.
- smoke.rs:705: `verify_burst(false)` asserts all 11 panes are attached 500 ms after navigation (app.rs:1634, terminal.rs:316-321).
- smoke.rs:712: `verify_save` asserts `!self.busy` 500 ms after the README read started.
- smoke_registry.rs:24-26 `settle()` sleeps 400 ms. The drop needs ui.projects refreshed, and the order check needs the drop handler's sequential project.update calls to have finished (shell.rs:104-127).
- smoke_notes.rs:227: 500 ms for a 300 ms debounce plus settings.set (notes_window.rs:123-124).
- smoke_project_files.rs:151-165: the coalescing check waits 1250 ms after the save, against a 125 ms engine debounce (watch.rs:120) and a 1000 ms client debounce (editor.rs:514).

**Impact.** Coalescing check: the save's own file.changed timer fires about 1125 ms plus the event-delivery lag after the write, and the measurement window opens about 1250 ms plus the file.read RTT after the save is observed. If event delivery lags by roughly 130-380 ms, the 20 invalidates coalesce into the save's pending timer and `tree_revision` moves before the 250 ms check. The run then fails with 'File events must not rebuild multiple times per second' although the product is fine.

Likewise:
- 'Settings save must finish' panics whenever the saves take more than 900 ms;
- a slow first refresh aborts every roadmap part with an index or unwrap panic;
- project-launch's close at 5 s is refused while `launch_busy` (app.rs:1033-1036), failing 'Native close blocked'.

The smoke usually runs on the same machine as the user's many live agents, so load is normal.

**Fix.** Replace each delay with a bounded poll, using the existing `wait_for` helper, on the condition the next step needs:
- `ui.pages["settings"].is_sensitive()` plus the guardrail status reading 'Saved';
- `ui.project.get() != 0 && !ui.workspaces.borrow().is_empty()` before any roadmap part;
- `ui.projects_box.is_sensitive()` after a registry drop;
- each pane's verify_ready condition before pasting;
- for coalescing, take `revision` only once no invalidate is pending (expose `invalidate_pending` as pub(crate)).

**Verifier note.** Downgraded to low. The harness cannot build or run in CI (CLAUDE.md), and runs by hand on the developer's machine, so the cost is an occasional false failure and a re-run. Nothing in the git history shows a flake actually happening, and the timing margins (for example 900 ms for a few local settings.set calls) are usually generous. Poll the same way the existing wait_for helper does, as the finding suggests.

`apps/relay-native/src/smoke.rs:426` · **low** · Test quality · confirmed · effort S

**Problem.** verify_confirmations is `glib::spawn_future_local(async move { for accept in [false, true] { ... assert_eq!(panel.response("Confirm").await, accept); ... } println!("In-app confirmation accept and cancel verified"); })` (smoke.rs:426-448).

The screenshot timer at `duration` (smoke.rs:724-808) closes the window regardless. The main close handler (app.rs:1032-1072) tears everything down and the app exits 0, dropping pending futures.

edit_fixture's loop over toplevels (smoke.rs:369-420) silently does nothing if the editor field hasn't appeared after 700 ms.

#### RA-721 · Several negative checks wait less time than the behaviour they rule out, so they cannot fail

`apps/relay-native/src/smoke_notes.rs:171` · **low** · Test quality · confirmed · effort S

**Problem.** - smoke_notes.rs:171-179: `glib::timeout_future(Duration::from_millis(850)).await;` then `require(stored["body"] == "Ordinary Plan fixture", "Plan was silently autosaved")`, but the autosave timer is `Duration::from_millis(1500)` (note_pages/doc.rs:606).
- smoke_notes.rs:242-247 checks 'Refresh reopened a deliberately closed tab' 200 ms after `refresh_notes`, instead of waiting for `owner.renders` to increment as lines 208-210 do.
- tools_devices.rs:284-292, called from roadmap_smoke.rs:256, does `window.present()`, waits 100 ms, then `assert!(window.width() <= 430, ...)`. An unallocated window reports 0.
- smoke_project_files.rs:122-126 checks the window did not widen 80 ms after a click.
- smoke_project_files.rs:166-170 calls a 1.1 s sample 'must not poll when idle'.
- roadmap_smoke.rs:282-283 reads back `split.set_position(position + 40)` from GTK's own property.

**Impact.** Each of these passes regardless of the regression it targets:
- If the `!super::prefs().autosave` guard in schedule_autosave (doc.rs:601) is dropped, the dirty Plan autosaves at 1500 ms, after the 850 ms check.
- If the Notes refresh takes more than 200 ms, the reopen check runs before the refresh lands.
- If the transient picker window is not allocated within 100 ms (a Wayland configure round trip under load), width() is 0 and the overflow assert holds whatever the content width.
- Any poll interval longer than 1.1 s goes unseen.
- The Paned read-back can only test GTK's setter.

**Fix.** - Wait past the debounce (≥1.7 s), or assert the doc's autosave timer is unset.
- Wait for `owner.renders` to increase before the reopen check.
- Measure the picker with `picker.widget.measure(Horizontal, -1).0`, as roadmap_smoke.rs:301 does, rather than the window width.
- Assert the Paned allocation after a frame, or drop the read-back.

**Verifier note.** 'Cannot fail' is overstated for several items.
- The 200ms wait after refresh_notes (smoke_notes.rs:241-247) races only if notes.list on a local fixture engine takes more than about 200ms. That is unlikely, so it is weak rather than vacuous. Waiting on owner.renders, as at :208-210, is still the right fix.
- The 80ms width check and the 1.1s 'no idle poll' sample are bounded samples that could still catch a regression; they are not tautologies.

#### RA-723 · Duplicated serve, accept and transport code that has already diverged

`crates/relay-cli/src/remote.rs:142` · **low** · Duplication · confirmed · effort M

**Problem.** `sigterm()` (remote.rs:142-149) is a verbatim copy of relay-core serve.rs:55-62, and the quit/ctrl-c/SIGTERM select and shutdown (remote.rs:127-139) copy serve.rs:44-52. The accept loops (direct.rs:37-53 vs rendezvous.rs:69-85) and the peek-and-answer HTTP responders (direct.rs:73-87 vs rendezvous.rs:125-144) are the same code. The phone-reader loops have already diverged: direct.rs:112-116 forwards Binary frames, while rendezvous.rs:273 silently drops them, so a client that sends binary works on the LAN but not through the rendezvous. `serve_with_door` (88-126) and `RemoteCommand::Serve` (181-206) repeat the bind/registry/tunnel/print sequence with different error handling. `connect_once` repeats its lane and writer teardown three times (tunnel.rs:82-85, 100-103, 155-158).

**Impact.** Fixes such as the timeouts, limits and keepalives above must be made in two places and will drift, as the Binary handling already has. The triple teardown makes it easy for a future early return to leak lane tasks.

**Fix.** Make relay-core's `sigterm`/wait-for-quit public, or add `serve_until_quit(served, extras)`. Extract a shared `accept_loop(listener, handler)` and HTTP-probe helper, and one ws pump used by both the direct door and joins. Add one `open_door(ctx, addr, registry) -> (door, tunnel)` used by both serve paths. Move the lane teardown into a drop guard.

**Verifier note.** The payoff is modest. The two serve paths differ in error handling on purpose: `relay serve --remote` tolerates a failed door bind, while `relay remote serve` must fail. A single `open_door` helper would therefore need a policy parameter and is not a pure simplification. The two HTTP probe responders also differ in path and in CORS header. The Binary divergence has no known engine-side consequence, since the bridge protocol is line-based text. The worthwhile parts are to expose relay-core's wait-for-quit/sigterm so the shutdown code is not copied, and to put the tunnel lane teardown in a drop guard.

`crates/relay-remote/tests/remote.rs:277` · **low** · Test quality · confirmed · effort M

#### RA-730 · CI pins Rust 1.94, but the workspace declares no rust-version while local and agent builds use 1.98

`Cargo.toml:7` · **low** · Code quality · confirmed · effort S

This machine builds with the distro package rust 1:1.98.1 (no rustup, so a rust-toolchain.toml would not be honoured either). CLAUDE.md tells agents to run `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` locally.

**Impact.** Code that uses a std API stabilized in 1.95-1.98 builds and passes clippy locally and in agent sessions, then fails CI on 1.94. In the other direction, lints added in clippy 1.95-1.98 fail local -D warnings runs that CI would pass, so agents change code that CI never asked about.

**Fix.** Add `rust-version = "1.94"` to [workspace.package] and `rust-version.workspace = true` to each member. Clippy's incompatible_msrv lint then flags newer std APIs on the local 1.98 toolchain. Bump it in the same PR as ci.yml's pin.

**Verifier note.** `rust-version` plus clippy's incompatible_msrv lint only covers the 'newer std API' direction. It does nothing about lints that are new in the 1.95-1.98 clippy firing locally but not in CI. Telling the two toolchains apart for that direction needs a note in CLAUDE.md, or a toolchain the agent image can actually select.

The file lives under target/, so `cargo clean` silently deletes the only diagnostics.

#### RA-732 · The scripts put the actions they verify inside assert statements, so python -O or PYTHONOPTIMIZE turns them into no-ops

`scripts/native-pointer-click.py:56` · **low** · Test quality · confirmed · effort S

**Problem.** native-pointer-click.py:56 `assert translate(display, window, root, int(sys.argv[2]), int(sys.argv[3]), ...)` performs the coordinate translation only inside the assert. native-smoke.py:135, 164 and 196 use `assert native.wait(timeout=...)==0`. Every check in native-smoke.py, native-setup-smoke.py and test-launcher*.py is an assert, including native-setup-smoke's call() error check (66).

**Impact.** With PYTHONOPTIMIZE set (or python3 -O), the pointer driver clicks at (0,0) of whatever display it is on. native-smoke kills every client immediately, because the wait is skipped and the finally block terminates the process, then skips every check. It still prints the success summary at line 209, claiming that saves, bursts and paste echoes were verified.

**Fix.** Perform side effects outside asserts and fail explicitly, e.g. `rc = native.wait(timeout=30); if rc: raise SystemExit(...)` and `if not translate(...): sys.exit(...)`. Alternatively, refuse to run when sys.flags.optimize is set.

**Verifier note.** The trigger is uncommon, since a developer has to have PYTHONOPTIMIZE set or run with -O. The concrete harm is a false pass from a verification script, not a product bug. The cheapest fix is a one-line guard at the top of each script, `if sys.flags.optimize: raise SystemExit('run without -O')`, rather than rewriting every assert.

#### RA-734 · The fixture-engine harness is copy-pasted across three scripts and has diverged in teardown, env scrubbing and error checking

`scripts/native-setup-smoke.py:110` · **low** · Duplication · confirmed · effort M

**Problem.** native-smoke.py:29-81 and 210-218, native-setup-smoke.py:16-67 and 107-110, and test-launcher-real.py:12-28 and 45-51 each re-implement temp XDG dirs, env scrubbing, engine start, the connect loop, call() and teardown. They have diverged in four ways. (a) native-smoke kills the engine when `wait(timeout=10)` times out (213-217). native-setup-smoke just calls `engine.wait(timeout=5)` (110), so a slow shutdown raises TimeoutExpired from `finally`, masking the original failure, and leaves the engine and its PTY children running while TemporaryDirectory deletes their store and socket. test-launcher-real sends SIGTERM (49) and never waits. (b) native-smoke pops RELAY_SESSION/RELAY_TOKEN/RELAY_BRIEF from the client env (115-116). native-setup-smoke builds the client env from raw os.environ (77). test-launcher-real pops a different set, without RELAY_BRIEF (27). (c) native-smoke sets RELAY_BIN and NO_COLOR for the fixture engine (35); native-setup-smoke does not. Run from inside a Relay session, its fixture sessions therefore use the parent's RELAY_BIN (hooks.rs:32-37 prefers it) instead of the build under test. (d) call() raises RuntimeError in native-smoke (79-80) but uses `assert result["ok"]` in native-setup-smoke (66), which `python -O` strips.

**Impact.** Each fix lands in only one copy, as the kill fallback and the env scrubbing already have. A failing setup smoke can leak an engine plus fixture providers and report TimeoutExpired instead of the real assertion.

**Fix.** Extract one scripts/fixture_engine.py: a context manager that creates temp XDG dirs, scrubs the env (including RELAY_BIN), starts the engine, connects with a deadline, provides a call() that raises on error, and tears down with terminate, wait, then kill. Add a native_env() helper for the client. Import both from the two smoke scripts and from test-launcher-real.py.

**Verifier note.** Lower to low. These are developer smoke scripts that need GTK and a display. CI does not run them and no user ever runs them, so the cost is limited to the developer's own verification runs. Divergence (b) is mostly harmless. relay-native/src never reads RELAY_SESSION or RELAY_TOKEN, and the client is pointed at the fixture explicitly with RELAY_NATIVE_SOCKET. So native-setup-smoke.py:77 building runenv from raw os.environ does not change behavior today. Smallest worthwhile fix: in native-setup-smoke.py, add the terminate/wait/kill fallback, set RELAY_BIN to the built binary, and raise instead of assert in call(). The shared fixture module in the finding is optional, with modest payoff for three scripts of about 100 lines each.

#### RA-735 · baseline.py burst phase measures its own byte-at-a-time Python reader, and any 1 s gap before BURST-END crashes the run

`scripts/perf/baseline.py:520` · **low** · Test quality · confirmed · effort S

**Problem.** `stream = sub.makefile("rwb", buffering=0)` (520), then `stream.readline()` (531). readline on a raw SocketIO does one recv per byte. A scratch test here measured 2.2 MiB/s unbuffered against 820 MiB/s buffered. The engine drops frames for a lagging subscriber (socket.rs:491-493). The committed process.json shows 1,194,990 payload bytes received of about 5.0 MB, 1.78 MB on the wire and mib_per_s_to_client 0.4. BASELINE-2026-09-19.md:488-496 reads this as what 'an attached reader that cannot keep up sees' and concludes that bursts leave terminal gaps. Second problem: `sub.settimeout(1.0)` (523). After the first timeout, SocketIO refuses further reads with OSError('cannot read from timed out object') (verified in a scratch test on Python 3.14), and `except socket.timeout` (532) does not catch that. The 'keep waiting' path after a failed scrollback check (546-549) therefore raises out of run_process, process.json (594) is never written, and main() aborts before the callgrind pass and report.py.

**Impact.** seconds_until_stream_quiet, mib_per_s_to_client, frames and payload_bytes_received describe the harness, not the engine, and they drove a product conclusion. On a loaded machine, a stall of 1 s or more before BURST-END reaches the scrollback kills the whole baseline run.

**Fix.** Read with select/selectors plus `sub.recv(1 << 16)` into a bytearray and split lines yourself, with no socket timeout under a makefile. Count dropped frames from seq gaps explicitly. Use a buffered reader in Engine.call (347) as well.

**Verifier note.** Lowered to low: this is a dev-only perf harness, and the BASELINE doc already frames the result as what 'an attached reader that cannot keep up sees'. The doc's point about the native client's 256 KiB catch-up does not depend on this measurement. The crash needs a stall of 1 s or more before the burst ends. Fix: read with select plus recv into a buffer, split lines yourself, and count dropped frames from seq gaps.

#### RA-738 · native-baseline.py points the GTK client's XDG_RUNTIME_DIR at a temp dir, so on Wayland GDK cannot reach the compositor and silently falls back to XWayland

`scripts/perf/native-baseline.py:204` · **low** · Test quality · confirmed · effort S

**Problem.** desktop_env sets `XDG_RUNTIME_DIR=str(runtime)` for the client (203-204). The client only needs that variable to exist, because RELAY_NATIVE_SOCKET is given (app.rs:309-319). libwayland resolves a relative WAYLAND_DISPLAY (here 'wayland-0') under $XDG_RUNTIME_DIR, so GDK's Wayland backend fails and GDK falls back to X11 through DISPLAY=:0 (XWayland); without DISPLAY the client cannot start. Sibling scripts that override XDG_RUNTIME_DIR set GDK_BACKEND=x11 explicitly (scripts/test-launcher-real.py:21-23, scripts/native-setup-smoke.py:79). run.sh launches the real client without the override. This was not run, because relay-native cannot be built here.

**Impact.** On the user's Wayland session the baseline profiles the XWayland path, with a different frame clock, presentation and GL path, and with XWayland's own CPU not counted. That is not the native Wayland client the user actually runs. On a Wayland-only session every page fails.

**Fix.** Leave XDG_RUNTIME_DIR alone for the client, since RELAY_NATIVE_SOCKET already selects the fixture engine. Or set WAYLAND_DISPLAY to the absolute path under the original runtime dir. Record the GDK backend in native.json.

**Verifier note.** Part of the evidence is wrong. scripts/native-setup-smoke.py does not override XDG_RUNTIME_DIR for the client: its runenv (line 77) is built from os.environ, and GDK_BACKEND=x11 at line 79 applies only to the pointer-driver mode. The right precedent is native-smoke.py:114, which leaves XDG_RUNTIME_DIR alone for the client. Fix: drop XDG_RUNTIME_DIR from desktop_env, since RELAY_NATIVE_SOCKET already selects the engine, and record GDK_BACKEND or the display type in native.json. Rated low, not medium: this dev-only harness has never been run and still produces numbers, just for a different display path.

**Also at:** `apps/relay-native/src/app.rs:313`, `scripts/test-launcher-real.py:23`, `scripts/native-setup-smoke.py:79`

`scripts/test-launcher.py:11` · **low** · Test quality · confirmed · effort S

**Problem.** Line 11 copies only run.sh into the fixture root. run.sh:18, added in 54e6bbc after this test was written in 073019a/34802a7, then runs `python3 scripts/install-native-desktop.py` relative to that root. I reproduced this with an isolated copy (TMPDIR in the scratchpad, same fakes). The first launch() returns 2 with stderr `python3: can't open file '.../relay launcher w4gqrrfu/scripts/install-native-desktop.py': [Errno 2] No such file or directory`, so `assert launch().returncode == 0` (line 42) fails. docs/VERIFICATION.md:34 still reports '`python3 scripts/test-launcher.py` | Passed'. What is actually lost is the headless coverage of the failure paths: build exit code passthrough, rejecting an invalid instance, engine start failure, and that no window opens after a failure. The proposed fix is right. The simplest version puts a fake `python3` (or a stub scripts/install-native-desktop.py) in the fixture and sets XDG_DATA_HOME to a temp dir. Because the test needs no GTK or cargo, adding it to the CI engine job is cheap. Also correct the stale VERIFICATION.md row.

#### RA-740 · User-only ops with no caller anywhere: file.import, file.restore_head and git.branch.clean_merged

`crates/relay-core/src/handlers/git.rs:693` · **low** · Dead code · plausible · effort S

**Problem.** None of them is referenced by native, remote, CLI or tests, and agents are refused at layer 1. file.import (file.rs:262-297) recursively copies whole trees (copy, 612-627) inside the transaction and gates only the top-level entry. file.restore_head (253-261) runs git checkout under the lock. git.branch.clean_merged (git.rs:693-720) re-implements git.branch.delete's eligibility rules (445-489) and runs `git worktree list` plus one `git branch -d` per branch under the lock; it is superseded by the staged git.branch.cleanup.

Retiring it, or making it an alias of cleanup, is the real cleanup. For file.import and file.restore_head, the actionable point is that if they are wired into the UI as BUS.md intends, they must be registered staged or unlocked, because they copy trees and run git under the store lock. Deleting them would drop documented features.

**Why only plausible.** The claim of no caller in native, remote or CLI holds, and all three are UserOnly (ops/file.rs:32-37; BUS.md:449 lists clean_merged as user_only). Each also does slow work under the lock: RestoreHead runs `git checkout` (file.rs:253-261), Import recursively copies whole trees (file.rs:262-297, copy at 612-627), and CleanMerged runs list_with_dirty plus one `git branch -d` per branch (git.rs:693-720). However, the evidence is wrong that tests do not reference them: crates/relay-core/tests/phase8.rs:419 exercises git.branch.clean_merged, and examples/perf.rs:924, 977 and 981 benchmark all three. All three are also documented bus API in BUS.md:830, 851 and 852. file.import is the specced 'OS drag-in' and file.restore_head is the specced 'one-click answer to a post-hoc guardrail.violation' (§9.3), so they are unwired features rather than plainly dead code.
